Previously 2026-05-24, **Slice CP.1 — ComparisonPlotDialog layout-recovery + animation-cursor polish shipped** — closes two user-reported UX bugs on the AT.3 ComparisonPlotDialog: (1) **collapsed-panel recovery** — the outer `m_splitter` (series tree ↔ charts) had its default `setChildrenCollapsible(true)` left as-is, so dragging the handle all the way left snapped the left pane to 0 px and the now-zero-width handle was un-grabbable. Fix: `m_splitter->setChildrenCollapsible(false)` + `m_leftHost->setMinimumWidth(60)` so the handle always has a grab area, AND new **View → Series Panel / Range Slider / Stats Panel** toolbar toggles (3 checkable QActions + master "Charts Only" with Ctrl+Shift+F) that hide/show each pane explicitly. Each toggle snapshots the current splitter sizes before hiding so re-show restores the user's prior width/height instead of resetting to defaults; the master "Charts Only" drives the three independent toggles in lockstep. (2) **bottom stats panel collapsibility** — `m_statsPanel->setMinimumHeight(160)` was preventing the user from dragging the handle below that height; relaxed to 60 so the user can shrink-to-sliver via drag and full-collapse via the new View toggle. (3) **animation-cursor vertical line not appearing in the time-series chart** — root cause: `rebuildCharts()` called `onAnimationCursorToggled` for visibility but never re-fired `applyAnimationCursorToCharts()` to set the line's `(t, ymin)→(t, ymax)` endpoints, so on first render the cursor line was empty until the AnimationController's next tick (which doesn't happen until the user starts playback). Fix: call `applyAnimationCursorToCharts()` at the end of `rebuildCharts()` so the cached `m_curAnimTime` is applied to fresh rows. (4) **animation cursor in legend** — line was previously `setName(QString())` with its legend marker explicitly hidden; renamed to `tr("Current time")`, pen width bumped 1.0 → 1.5 for visibility, and legend markers now track the master `m_showCursor` toggle so the user can see which dashed line is the cursor. **Files**: [include/ui/dialogs/comparisonplotdialog.h](../include/ui/dialogs/comparisonplotdialog.h) (4 new QAction members, 2 new QList<int> for splitter-size caches, 2 new QWidget members for the toggle targets, 4 new slot decls) + [src/ui/dialogs/comparisonplotdialog.cpp](../src/ui/dialogs/comparisonplotdialog.cpp) (toggle build in `buildToolBar`, slot impls, cursor-name + legend-marker fix, post-rebuild cursor re-apply). This section is the handoff log between sessions. Each completed slice lists its
phases, the files it touched, the QtTests added, and the manual chapters
co-authored. **An agent picking up this work should scan this section first**,
then consult the corresponding phase sections for unchanged design intent.

> Status legend: ✅ shipped & verified (build + tests green) · 🔧 in progress · ⏳ not started

### Completed slices

#### ✅ Slice A — Bootstrap (Phase 0 + 0.4 + 1.1–1.2)

- **Phase 0 — Project Bootstrap**: File menu (New / Open / Save / Save As), dirty-state
  tracking with `*` title marker, status-bar Flow Units combo, in-app Message Log dock,
  recent-files persistence in `QSettings`.
- **Phase 0.4 — Welcome / Start Tab**: MDI-tab welcome page with recent files panel,
  examples gallery (auto-discovered from `<install>/examples/`), New / Open buttons,
  Help links via `QDesktopServices::openUrl`, "Show on startup" toggle persisted to
  `QSettings`.
- **Phase 1.1–1.2 — Model loading**: `SWMMModelLayer::loadModel()` calls
  `swmm_engine_open` and builds a geometry cache (nodes via bulk API, links via
  per-link vertex queries with from/to-node endpoint reconstruction, subcatchment
  polygons, gages); `SWMMVisProjectWindow::loadModel()` delegates and triggers a
  reliable zoom-to-extent on first show via a self-rescheduling 50 ms timer.
- **Rendering pipeline (Phase 0.7 architecture)**: dual-layer compositing —
  `MapRenderJob` background worker for raster basemaps, `QGraphicsScene` for
  vectors. Worker lifetime decoupled from `MapRenderJob` via lambda value-capture
  + `shared_ptr<atomic<bool>>` cancel flag + `QPointer` finished signal so the
  job can be `deleteLater`'d without blocking the GUI. QGIS-style stale-buffer
  transform during pan/zoom (`m_mapBufferExtent` tracked separately from
  `m_extent`) eliminates the mouse-up flash. Direct `QGraphicsScene::render()`
  blit on the canvas (overlay `QGraphicsView` removed because its hidden
  `QOpenGLWidget` viewport prevented `QWidget::render` from working).
- **CMake**: `add_subdirectory("../openswmm.engine")` (the engine's exported
  `*Config.cmake` is incomplete); link target is `openswmm_engine`;
  `HAVE_OPENSWMMENGINE` is defined globally.

#### ✅ Slice B — Per-tab options (Phase 0.5 + 0.6)

- **Phase 0.5 — UnitSystem as delegating facade**: `UnitSystem::instance()` is now a
  facade whose accessors forward to whichever per-project instance is currently
  active. `setActiveProject(UnitSystem*)` rebinds the target and re-broadcasts
  `unitsChanged` so existing label-bearing call sites refresh on tab switch
  without per-callsite work. Per-project instances hold their own `mFlowUnits`
  state and `setFlowUnits()` writes through `swmm_options_set(engine, "FLOW_UNITS")`.
- **Phase 0.6 — Per-tab project options rebinding**: each `SWMMVisProjectWindow`
  owns a `UnitSystem*` and an `mElevationOffsetMode` bool (read from `LINK_OFFSETS`
  after load, written via `setElevationOffsetMode()`). `SWMMVis::onActiveSubWindowChanged`
  rebinds the `UnitSystem` facade target and syncs the **Flow Units** combo and
  **Offset Mode** checkbox (with `QSignalBlocker` to avoid write-back loops),
  disabling both when no project is active. After `loadModel` succeeds the
  handler is re-invoked because `subWindowActivated` may fire before
  `loadModel` runs.

#### ✅ Slice C — CRS change reproject prompt (Phase 0.7)

- **Phase 0.7 — CRS change after model load**: `CRSChangeDialog` (two radios
  Reproject / Re-render, OK / Cancel) is shown when the user picks a different
  CRS while a model is loaded. **Reproject** runs `CRSReproject::reprojectModel()`,
  which builds an `OGRCoordinateTransformation` once and rewrites every node
  (bulk), every link vertex chain, every subcatchment polygon + centroid, then
  writes the new CRS via `swmm_spatial_set_crs`. **Re-render only** keeps stored
  coordinates and just swaps the canvas SRS for on-the-fly display reprojection.
  Source-Local models disable the Re-render choice (no transform can be built).

#### ✅ Slice D-fix — Categorised layer tree, main-toolbar wiring, resource icons (Phase 0.8 polish)

User feedback after Slice D drove three follow-up changes:

1. **De-duplicated layer-add actions.** The main application toolbar already
   exposes *Add Vector Data*, *Add Raster Data*, *Add WMS Data*, *Add Basemap*,
   and *Add SWMM Output*. Vector / Raster / SWMM-Output were unwired; they now
   route through new `SWMMVis::onAddVectorLayer`, `onAddRasterLayer`, and
   `onAddSWMMResultsLayer` slots that build the layer + push onto the active
   canvas. The dock's own toolbar is **gone** — adding layers is now a single
   path through the main toolbar. The dock is purely a tree; per-layer
   operations (Zoom To, Properties, Move Up/Down, Show/Hide, Remove) live on
   the right-click context menu.
2. **Categorised tree.** `LayerTreeModel` is now a 2-level tree: root → category
   → layer. Categories are derived from `OpenSWMMVisLayerType`:
   *SWMM Model*, *SWMM Results*, *Vectors*, *Rasters*, *Basemaps*, *Tabular*,
   *Sub-projects*, *Other*. Empty categories are hidden; counts appear in the
   header (`Vectors (3)`). Within a category, layers list in canvas-stack order
   (top-of-stack first). Drag-drop reorder is intra-category only;
   cross-category is intentionally a no-op (categories reflect type and
   wouldn't make semantic sense to mix).

   > **Amendment 2026-05-16 (Slice BA decision):** The *SWMM Model* category will be upgraded to a **3-level tree** when Slice BA lands: `SWMM Model` category → `SWMMModelLayer` row → `SWMMResultsLayer` children. Results layers that reference a given model layer appear as children of that model row rather than as a sibling category. This makes the results↔model relationship immediately visible and supports future multi-model projects. The primary (active) results layer is rendered **bold** (`Qt::FontRole`). Right-click on a results-layer row gains **"Set as Active Results Layer"** action (calls `SWMMVis::setActiveResultsLayer`). The flat *SWMM Results* category is removed once Slice BA lands.
3. **Per-type icons from the existing resource bundle.** `Qt::DecorationRole`
   now returns `QIcon(":/swmmvis/<alias>")` per layer type — `AddVector`,
   `AddRaster`, `AddWMS`, `AddBasemap`, `Layers`, `Chart`, `TableView`,
   `Globe` — using the SVGs already shipped under `resources/images/`. The
   placeholder Qt-standard-icon mapping from Slice D is gone.

#### ✅ Slice K — About dialog with license browser (Phase: License and About)

User-driven slice: open-source distribution wants license transparency baked
into the app, not buried in a packaged `LICENSE` file.

- **`AboutDialog`** is a two-pane modal with a header strip (app version,
  build date+time, Qt version, OS / arch, plus a *Copy environment* button
  for bug reports). Left pane is a category-grouped tree of every shipped
  dependency with a search box; right pane shows the focused component's
  metadata (version, role, SPDX id, provenance, homepage link) and the
  full license text in a monospace `QPlainTextEdit`. **Copy License**,
  **Open Homepage**, and **Open Source** buttons act on the focused row.
- **Declarative manifest** at [resources/about/components.json](../resources/about/components.json)
  describes every component (category / name / version / role / homepage /
  source / SPDX / provenance / licenseFile path). Adding or updating a
  dependency is a JSON edit + one license file checked in — no recompile of
  the dialog needed.
- **License texts** under [resources/licenses/](../resources/licenses/) —
  one `.txt` per component, embedded via [resources/about.qrc](../resources/about.qrc).
  The 1.0 set covers OpenSWMMCore, Triangle, Qt 6, QPropertyModel, GDAL,
  PROJ, GeoTIFF, SQLite, Expat, libxml2, SUNDIALS/CVODE, and the OpenMP
  runtime. Each shipped file currently carries the canonical
  copyright/grant text or a clear pointer to the upstream `LICENSE` plus a
  note that packaging-time substitution should drop in the verbatim file.
- **Help → About** now opens the new dialog (replacing the placeholder
  `QMessageBox::about` blurb).

#### ✅ Slice D-2 — LayerPropertiesDialog + Layers search (Phase 0.8.5 / 0.8.6) + focus-loss fix

Two pieces in one slice:

**Bug fix (focus-loss):** [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp)
`onActiveSubWindowChanged` was clearing the Layers dock and status-bar
widgets whenever focus moved away from the MDI area (e.g. clicking a dock
widget) because `QMdiArea::subWindowActivated(nullptr)` fires on any focus
shift, not just when projects close. Fix: cache the active project pointer
in `mActiveProjectWindow`; on a null event, only clear when there are no
project sub-windows left in the area; on a non-null event, no-op when the
project hasn't actually changed. `activeProjectWindow()` returns the
cached value so toolbar actions ("Add Vector", etc.) keep targeting the
right project even when focus is on a dock. Cache invalidation wired to
`QObject::destroyed` on each project window.

**Phase 0.8.5 — LayerPropertiesDialog**: 3 tabs, mutates the layer on
**Apply** / **OK** so the user can cancel uncommitted edits.

- **General** — editable name, read-only type label, CRS row with a
  *Change…* button (delegates to `CRSSelectionDialog`; setting a new SRS
  on the layer is the *layer's stored CRS* update — coordinate
  reprojection still goes through the canvas-CRS button + `CRSChangeDialog`
  per Phase 0.7).
- **Rendering** — visibility checkbox + paired opacity slider / spinbox
  (kept in sync via `QSignalBlocker`).
- **Metadata** — read-only summary built by the static
  `LayerPropertiesDialog::metadataSummary(layer)` helper: UUID, type,
  visibility, opacity, CRS, extent, child count.

**Phase 0.8.6 — search box**: a `QLineEdit` above the tree that drives a
`QSortFilterProxyModel` (`setRecursiveFilteringEnabled(true)` so category
headers are hidden when no contained layer matches). The panel now owns
`m_proxy` between the model and the view; all index handoffs route
through `toSourceIndex(const QModelIndex&)` so context-menu, drag-drop,
and current-selection lookups still talk to the source model.

  flags, plus the six `IGNORE_*` checkboxes (Rainfall / Snowmelt /

  with calendar popup, plus `REPORT_STEP` / `DRY_STEP` / `WET_STEP` /

  buf, len)`; every write through `swmm_options_set(key, value)`.
  `writeToEngine()` diffs against the last-read value and only writes
  changed keys, so Apply is cheap and `setHasChanges` is only flagged when
  something actually changed.

  active project's engine. Added programmatically in `initializeMenus`

##### ⚠️ Tab 7 (Files / Output / Plugins) — deferred, engine API gaps

All four planned sub-features need engine-side work before they can
ship. Recording the gap precisely so a continuing agent can either close
the gap in OpenSWMMCore or skip Tab 7 cleanly:

| Sub-feature | Missing engine surface |
|-------------|------------------------|
| Rain file list | No C ABI for the `[FILES]` section. Need `swmm_files_count` + `swmm_files_get(i, kind, path)` + `_set` + `_add` + `_remove`. The handler is internal (`FilesHandler.cpp`). |
| Output format selector | Output backend is selected at `swmm_engine_open(..., out_path)` time and isn't queryable / changeable from C. Need either `swmm_options_set("OUTPUT_FORMAT", "GeoPackage")` extension key or a runtime toggle API. |
| `[PLUGINS]` editor | No C ABI to read/write the `[PLUGINS]` list once the engine is open. Plugins are passed as a single library path to `swmm_engine_open(..., input_plugin_lib)`. Need `swmm_plugin_count` / `swmm_plugin_get` / `_set` / `_add` / `_remove` plus a way to surface init-arg key=value tokens. |
| `[REPORT]` controls | No C ABI for `REPORT_INPUT`, `REPORT_CONTROLS`, `REPORT_NODES`, `REPORT_LINKS`, `REPORT_SUBCATCHMENTS`, `REPORT_STATUS`. The handler exists internally. Need `swmm_report_get_flag(name)` / `_set_flag` / `_get_subset(name, ids[])`. |

Recommended path: ship these four engine APIs as a small dedicated batch,
then Tab 7 becomes mechanical (form + `QListWidget` + spin/check
controls). Tracked in *Known follow-ups* below.

#### ✅ Slice G-4 — Simulation Options Tab 7: Files / Output / Plugins (Phase 3.9 + 3.10 close-out)

**Shipped 2026-05-22.**  Tab 7 — *Files / Output / Plugins* — is now in
place.  The single legacy "Files" page was split into a nested
`QTabWidget` with three sub-tabs (Phase 3.10.2 + 3.10.3) so the
unrelated `[FILES]`, output / `[REPORT]`, and `[PLUGINS]` concerns no
longer fight for vertical space in a single scrolled page.  A
validation pass (Phase 3.10.4) gates Apply / OK on the same blocking
errors a Save As round-trip would catch silently.

Sub-tab layout (all three reachable inside the top-level **Files /
Output / Plugins** tab):

| Sub-tab | Engine surface | Notes |
|---------|----------------|-------|
| **Files**   | `[FILES]` rainfall / runoff / RDII / inflows / outflows / hot-start USE; `swmm_hotstart_saves_*` for the multi-row scheduled-saves table | Replaces the legacy single SAVE HOTSTART field (Slice BV-01). |
| **Output**  | Writer / container combos (per role plugin id); `RPT_*` options API (six bool flags + three NONE/ALL/Selected selectors); per-project `.rpt` / `.out` override paths persisted to `QSettings`. | Single-container check box auto-locks the output + report combos to the input writer when the chosen plugin is tri-role (e.g. GeoPackage). |
| **Plugins** | `swmm_plugins_count` / `swmm_plugin_get` / `swmm_plugin_set` raw `[PLUGINS]` table editor. | The first input-capable row is also the writer used by File → Save As when picking a non-`.inp` extension. |

The deferred engine prerequisites at Slice G-3 are resolved without
adding a separate `swmm_report_*` family: the existing
`swmm_options_get` / `swmm_options_set` keyspace was extended with
nine `RPT_*` keys (`RPT_DISABLED`, `RPT_INPUT`, `RPT_CONTINUITY`,
`RPT_FLOWSTATS`, `RPT_CONTROLS`, `RPT_AVERAGES`, `RPT_SUBCATCHMENTS`,
`RPT_NODES`, `RPT_LINKS`).  Bool keys take YES / NO / TRUE / FALSE /
1 / 0; selector keys take `ALL`, `NONE`, or a comma- or
whitespace-delimited name list (engine normalises to comma-joined on
the way out).  Covered by
[tests/unit/engine/test_report_options_api.cpp](../../openswmm.engine/tests/unit/engine/test_report_options_api.cpp)
(defaults, round-trip, alternate boolean tokens, garbage rejection,
selector NONE / ALL / SOME round-trip incl. whitespace, empty token
skipping, empty-string collapse, unknown-key rejection).

**Phase 3.10.4 validation gate.**  `validateFilesTab(QString *warn)`
runs from both `onApply` and `onAccept`:

- **Blocking** (Apply / OK refuses, row highlighted red):
  - `[PLUGINS]` row with empty plugin id (column 0).
  - Scheduled hot-start save row with empty path (column 0).
- **Non-blocking warnings** (surfaced as Yes/No prompt):
  - `[REPORT]` selector with **Selected** radio chosen but the name
    list empty → silently collapses to NONE on write.
  - `.rpt` / `.out` override path whose parent directory does not
    exist on disk.

The blocking errors mirror what the engine writers would reject
silently at Save As; the warnings give the user a chance to confirm
edits that would otherwise produce a surprising round-trip.

##### Historical context — pre-ship spec (kept for archaeology)

The original Slice G-4 design assumed a dedicated
`swmm_report_*` C ABI family. We instead piggy-backed on
`swmm_options_get` / `swmm_options_set` with the `RPT_*` keyspace
(simpler, no new headers, reuses the existing dialog
get/set plumbing). The historical spec below is retained verbatim
because it still describes the intended *UI* layout group-by-group:

Implements **Tab 7 — Reporting & Output** once the engine-side C ABI gaps
above are closed. This tab consolidates reporting item selection (matching
the legacy EPA SWMM 5.x `[REPORT]` section) with browseable file paths
for the `.rpt` report file and the `.out` binary output file.

##### Tab 7 layout — three group boxes

**Group 1 — Report Items** (mirrors legacy `[REPORT]` section behaviour)

| Control | Engine key | Notes |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| `REPORT_INPUT` checkbox | `REPORT_INPUT` | Echo the `.inp` contents at top of report |
| `REPORT_CONTROLS` checkbox | `REPORT_CONTROLS` | List all control actions taken |
| `REPORT_STATUS` checkbox | `REPORT_STATUS` | Print simulation status messages |
| `REPORT_SUBCATCHMENTS` | `REPORT_SUBCATCHMENTS` | `ALL` / `NONE` / pick list |
| `REPORT_NODES` | `REPORT_NODES` | `ALL` / `NONE` / pick list |
| `REPORT_LINKS` | `REPORT_LINKS` | `ALL` / `NONE` / pick list |

For `REPORT_SUBCATCHMENTS`, `REPORT_NODES`, and `REPORT_LINKS` the UI
presents a three-state combo (`All` / `None` / `Selected`) followed by
an expandable `QListWidget` of item IDs (populated from the live engine
via the object-count / get-by-index family of APIs). When `Selected` is
active the list is enabled and individual items can be checked.
Round-trip: a space-separated list of IDs is written as the option value;
`ALL` and `NONE` map to the combo states without touching the list.

**Group 2 — Report File**

- `QLineEdit` pre-filled with the input file path stem + `.rpt`
  extension (e.g. `~/projects/model.rpt` when the open input is
  `~/projects/model.inp`).
- **Browse…** `QPushButton` opens a `QFileDialog::getSaveFileName`
  filtered to `Report files (*.rpt);;All files (*)`. The selected path
  is written back to the line-edit and to `swmm_options_set("REPORT_FILE",
  path)` on Apply.
- Default derivation: `QFileInfo(inputPath).absoluteDir().filePath(
  QFileInfo(inputPath).completeBaseName() + ".rpt")`.

**Group 3 — Output File**

- `QLineEdit` pre-filled with the input file path stem + `.out`
  extension.
- **Browse…** button opens `QFileDialog::getSaveFileName` filtered to
  `Output files (*.out);;All files (*)`. Written to
  `swmm_options_set("OUTPUT_FILE", path)` on Apply.
- Default derivation: same stem swap as report file but `.out`.
- A read-only note below the edit reminds users that changing this path
  affects where post-processing tools (charts, tables) look for results.

##### Engine API prerequisites (OpenSWMMCore work items)

Before Slice G-4 can ship the following C ABI surface must exist in the
engine (to be tracked in the engine's ROADMAP):

```c
/* [REPORT] flag access */
int  swmm_report_get_flag(SWMMEngine *engine, const char *name, int *value);
int  swmm_report_set_flag(SWMMEngine *engine, const char *name, int  value);

/* Subset lists (space-separated IDs or "ALL"/"NONE") */
int  swmm_report_get_subset(SWMMEngine *engine, const char *kind, char *buf, int len);
int  swmm_report_set_subset(SWMMEngine *engine, const char *kind, const char *ids);

/* Output / report file paths (queryable at runtime) */
int  swmm_options_get_report_path(SWMMEngine *engine, char *buf, int len);
int  swmm_options_set_report_path(SWMMEngine *engine, const char *path);
int  swmm_options_get_output_path(SWMMEngine *engine, char *buf, int len);
int  swmm_options_set_output_path(SWMMEngine *engine, const char *path);
```

##### IPlugin output-format discovery (future extension)

Once the `[PLUGINS]` C ABI is available, the **Output File** group will
be extended to support plugin-provided output formats. The `IPlugin`
interface will be extended with:

```cpp
// Declared in include/engine/iplugin.h (OpenSWMMCore)
struct PluginArgDescriptor {
    const char *key;          // option key (e.g. "OUTPUT_FILE")
    const char *displayName;  // human-readable label
    const char *fileFilter;   // Qt file-dialog filter string, or nullptr if not a file arg
    const char *defaultValue; // may reference "$INP_STEM" macro
};

// New virtual — default impl returns empty span (no extra args)
virtual std::span<const PluginArgDescriptor> outputArgDescriptors() const;
```

The GUI will call `swmm_plugin_arg_count(engine, pluginIdx)` and
`swmm_plugin_arg_get(engine, pluginIdx, argIdx, &descriptor)` (the C
wrappers for the above) to discover what file-path arguments each loaded
plugin needs, then render one browse-row per descriptor inside a
**Plugin Output Files** sub-group below the core Output File row. File
filters come directly from `descriptor.fileFilter`; defaults expand
`$INP_STEM` to the current input file base name. This makes the dialog
generically extensible for any future output format (GeoPackage,
HDF5, NetCDF, etc.) without modifying the GUI code.

#### ✅ Slice H — Redraw / Invalidation Policy (Phase 0.9 first cut)

Adds the per-channel dirty-flag system the plan specifies. Existing
`refresh()` / `refreshLayerItems()` callers are preserved untouched —
they keep working via the legacy 50 ms timer. New callers use the
typed `invalidate()` entry point; a follow-on slice migrates legacy
sites incrementally so no one operation moves tens of files at once.

- **API on `MapCanvas`**:
  - `enum DirtyChannel { NoChannel, Raster=0x1, Scene=0x2, Overlay=0x4, Extent=0x8 }`
    + `Q_DECLARE_FLAGS(DirtyChannels, DirtyChannel)` +
    `Q_DECLARE_OPERATORS_FOR_FLAGS`.
  - `void invalidate(DirtyChannels channels, const QString &reason = {})` —
    single entry point. Routes Overlay/Extent through immediate paths
    (`update()` and `applyExtentToOverlay()` + extent/scale signals)
    and arms two per-channel debounce timers for Raster (150 ms) and
    Scene (50 ms). Coalesces bursts so 50 quick `invalidate(Scene)`
    calls fire once.
  - `void suspendRefresh()` / `void resumeRefresh()` — reference-counted
    bracketing for batch operations (e.g. loading a project with many
    layers). On the matching `resumeRefresh()` that returns the count
    to zero, any pending channels fire.
- **Per-channel timers** are *lazy-initialised*: a `MapCanvas` that
  never calls `invalidate()` allocates zero extra `QTimer`s.
- **Diagnostics — `SWMMVIS_LOG_REDRAW=1`** env var: when set, every
  `invalidate()` call and every channel firing emits a `qDebug()` line
  with the channel mask (`Raster|Scene`) and the caller's `reason`
  string. The lookup is done once per process (`qEnvironmentVariableIntValue`),
  so the gating cost is a single `bool` load. The plan's verification
  steps for Phase 0.9 now have a real instrumentation hook to assert
  against in CI.
- **Backward compat**: `refresh()` and `refreshLayerItems()` are
  unchanged — they still arm the existing 50 ms `m_refreshTimer` and
  drive the legacy combined raster+scene path. Callers can migrate to
  `invalidate(channels, "reason")` over time. Mixed use during the
  migration is safe: each channel's pending state is tracked
  independently.
- **Files**: [include/map/mapcanvas.h](../include/map/mapcanvas.h)
  (DirtyChannel enum + flags, invalidate / suspend / resume decls,
  per-channel timer + state members, `Q_DECLARE_OPERATORS_FOR_FLAGS`
  out of class), [src/map/mapcanvas.cpp](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp)
  (~150 lines for `invalidate`, `suspendRefresh`, `resumeRefresh`,
  `fireRasterChannel`, `fireSceneChannel`, `channelsToString`,
  `redrawLogEnabled`).
- **Tests**: parked. Same `MapCanvas` → OGR/GDAL snowball as the
  layertreepanel test; the Q_DECLARE_FLAGS / QTimer machinery being
  exercised is stock Qt. Will land alongside the broader
  `swmmvis_core` extraction. **Total active GUI tests: 5 binaries,
  32 cases, all passing.**
- **Manual**: chapter [docs/manual/21_redraw_policy.md](manual/21_redraw_policy.md)
  added — explains the four channels, when to use which, the
  suspend/resume bracket, and the SWMMVIS_LOG_REDRAW env var for
  troubleshooting performance regressions.
- **Test regression note**: the Slice G-3 split that put the dialog's
  pure helpers in `simulationoptionshelpers.cpp` worked when the moc
  vtable only needed the (now-inlined) destructor. After Slice G-3
  added the Tab 5 spatial slots, moc references those slot bodies
  too, so compiling only the helpers no longer satisfies the linker.
  Test re-parked; helpers split is preserved as-is for the eventual
  `swmmvis_core` extraction. No production code change.

#### ✅ Slice L — Object Browser + AttributePanel wire-up (Phase 0 / Phase 6.2 first cut)

Two panels shipped together to deliver the **"navigate model → see
properties"** loop on top of the Slice E SelectionManager bus.

**L-1 — Object Browser Panel** (new):
- `ObjectBrowserPanel` is an embeddable QWidget hosting a categorised
  `QTreeWidget` that mirrors the legacy Delphi browser's per-type
  groups: Rain Gages, Subcatchments, Junctions, Outfalls, Storage
  Units, Dividers, Conduits, Pumps, Orifices, Weirs, Outlets. Each
  group hides when empty; counts appear in the header
  (`Junctions (1205)`).
- `setProject(layer, selMgr)` rebinds on every MDI tab switch. On
  bind the tree is populated by iterating the engine's
  `swmm_node_count` / `swmm_link_count` / `swmm_subcatch_count` /
  `swmm_gage_count` and dispatching by
  `swmm_node_get_type` / `swmm_link_get_type`.
- **Two-way bus integration**: selecting tree rows calls
  `SelectionManager::select(..., Replace)`; the panel subscribes to
  `selectionChanged` so map clicks scroll the matching tree row into
  view and highlight it. A reentrancy flag prevents bounce-back.
- **Search box** at the top filters by name live (case-insensitive),
  hides entire groups when no child matches.
- Per-type icons come from the existing `:/swmmvis/Junction` /
  `Conduit` / `Orifice` / etc. resource bundle — no new assets.

**L-2 — AttributePanel wire-up** (existing class, wired for the
first time):
- The panel already existed as a QDockWidget class but was never
  instantiated. `initializeAttributePanelDockWidget()` adds it to
  the right dock area.
- On every tab switch, the project's `SelectionManager::selectionChanged`
  is connected (with `Qt::UniqueConnection` + a `pw ==
  mActiveProjectWindow` guard so a stale lambda can't fire on a dead
  project). The handler queries the active model layer's new
  **`SWMMModelLayer::identifyByName(name)`** helper and feeds the
  attribute map into the existing `showIdentifyResults()` path.
- `identifyByName` returns an `elementType / Name / coordinates /
  sub-type` map today — read-only. Per-type Property Editor dialogs
  (Phase 3) are a future slice; this provides immediate visibility into
  the picked object without that infrastructure.

**End-to-end behavior**:
1. Click a node on the map (map tool → SelectionManager::Replace)
2. Object Browser scrolls to and highlights the row
3. AttributePanel populates with the object's attributes
4. Click a different row in the Object Browser (ObjectBrowser →
   SelectionManager::Replace)
5. Map highlights the new selection; AttributePanel re-populates

#### ✅ Slice M — Run Simulation + Time Series Plot (Phase 4.1 + Phase 5.2 first cuts)

Closes the **edit → run → view results** loop. Two paired slices.

**M-1 — Run Simulation** (Phase 4.1 first cut):
- Wires the toolbar's existing `actionExecute` to a new
  `SWMMVis::onRunSimulation` slot. Auto-saves the project if dirty
  (the engine reads from disk), derives sibling `.rpt` and `.out`
  paths from the `.inp` filename, then runs `swmm_engine_run` on a
  worker thread via `QtConcurrent::run` + `QFutureWatcher` so the
  GUI stays responsive.
- On completion, the `.out` file is auto-loaded as a
  `SWMMResultsLayer` attached to the same project's canvas — so any
  subsequent results-view feature (e.g. M-2's plot) finds it
  without an extra "Add SWMM Output" step.
- Status-bar progress bar enters busy mode for the duration; log
  messages report start, success path, or engine error code.
- **Cancel deferred** — engine doesn't yet expose a clean cancel API.
  When that lands the `actionCancelExecution` button can be wired.

**M-2 — Time Series Plot** (Phase 5.2 first cut):
- New `TimeSeriesPlotDialog` reads the project's `.out` via
  `swmm_output_open` / `_get_*_series`, plots with `QChart` +
  `QLineSeries`. Variable combo populated by object class:
  - **Node**: depth / head / volume / lateral inflow / total inflow / overflow
  - **Link**: flow / depth / velocity / volume / capacity
  - **Subcatchment**: rainfall / snow depth / evaporation / infiltration / runoff
- X axis is **hours since simulation start** (numeric `QValueAxis`).
  Calendar-based `QDateTimeAxis` is deferred — `swmm_output_get_start_date`
  returns a Julian-date double whose epoch convention isn't documented
  uniformly across SWMM forks. Hours-from-start is unambiguous and
  immediately useful; calendar-time follow-up is a one-method change.
- **Wired via right-click → Plot Time Series…** in the Object Browser
  (Slice L). The dialog is non-modal (`Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose`) so users
  can keep multiple plots open against the same `.out`.

**End-to-end loop now works**:
1. Edit options (Tools → Simulation Options…)
2. Click toolbar Execute → engine runs in background → `.out` loads
3. Right-click any object in the Object Browser → Plot Time Series…
4. Switch variables in the dialog dropdown to inspect different metrics

#### ✅ Slice F — Interactive map editing: Move / EditVertex / AddNode + auto-length (Phase 2 first cut)

Closes the **load → edit geometry → run** loop. Delivers the three most
common geometry edits (move a node, edit link vertices, add a node)
fully undoable, with conduit length auto-recalculating from the polyline
when the status-bar toggle is on.

**Engine-side expansion** — the user asked for add / remove to be
guarded by lifecycle state rather than recorded as a deferred gap:

- **`CHECK_EDITABLE(ctx)` macro** added to
  [openswmm_api_common.hpp](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_api_common.hpp)
  — allows BUILDING or OPENED, explicitly forbids INITIALIZED /
  STARTED / RUNNING / ENDED.
- **`_add` APIs relaxed to OPENED**:
  [swmm_node_add](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_nodes_impl.cpp),
  [swmm_link_add](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_links_impl.cpp),
  [swmm_subcatch_add](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_subcatchments_impl.cpp),
  [swmm_gage_add](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_gages_impl.cpp)
  now accept both BUILDING (programmatic construction) and OPENED
  (interactive editing) states. SoA push + NameIndex::add is safe in
  either state — solver data hasn't been cached yet.
- **Narrow `_pop_last` APIs added**:
  [swmm_node_pop_last](../../openswmm.engine/include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_nodes.h) and
  [swmm_link_pop_last](../../openswmm.engine/include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_links.h)
  tombstone the most-recently-added object (verifying the expected id
  before pop). This is the minimal surface needed for AddNodeCommand /
  AddLinkCommand undo without the deeply-invasive renumbering that a
  general-purpose `swmm_node_remove(idx)` would require.
  [NameIndex::pop_back()](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/data/NameIndex.hpp)
  added to support it.
- **Doc headers updated** to reflect OPENED-editable semantics on
  `swmm_node_add`, `swmm_link_add`, `swmm_subcatch_add`, `swmm_gage_add`.

**GUI-side expansion**:

- New pure-logic module: [core/editgeometry.h](../include/core/editgeometry.h) +
  [.cpp](../src/core/editgeometry.cpp) — `polylineLength`,
  `replacedAt`, `insertedAt`, `removedAt`, `distanceToPolyline`.
  No Qt-GUI / OGR / engine deps, so it lives in a standalone QtTest
  binary.
- `SWMMModelLayer` gained `nodeIndex / linkIndex`, `cachedNodeCoord`, `cachedLinkPolyline`,
  `cachedLinkInteriorVertices`, `engineLinkLength`, `isConduit`,
  `linksAttachedToNode`, `linkEndForNode`, `applyNodeMove`,
  `applyLinkLength`, `applyLinkInteriorVertices`, `applyNodeAdd`,
  `rollbackTailNodeAdd`. Every mutator writes engine state first, then
  cache, then flags `m_needsRebuild` + emits `repaintRequested` so the
  canvas picks up the change through the existing invalidate path.
- New `MoveNodeCommand` (id 10) merges consecutive moves of the same node (cuts rapid-drag
  stack bloat); redo/undo through `applyNodeMove` + per-link `applyLinkLength` from a
  `QVector<LengthRec>` captured at commit.
- New `EditVertexCommand` (id 11) records old / new interior vertex vectors plus an
  auto-length snapshot when enabled.
- New `AddNodeCommand` (id 12) redo calls `applyNodeAdd`, undo calls `rollbackTailNodeAdd`.
  Undo only succeeds while the added node is still the engine's tail — subsequent edits
  can invalidate it, which is the expected cost of the narrow `_pop_last` primitive.

**GUI-side — tools** *(original Slice F implementation; superseded by Slice UI-1 item 3 — see below)*:
- `MapToolMoveNode` (**removed** — functionality merged into `OpenSWMMVisMapToolSelect` inline edit mode) — original: left-click a node to drag via MoveNodeCommand; Escape cancels.
- `MapToolEditVertex` (**removed** — functionality merged into `OpenSWMMVisMapToolSelect` inline edit mode) — original: click a link, interior vertex handles as overlay paint; drag/right-click to move/delete/insert vertices via EditVertexCommand.
- `MapToolAddNode` — one class parameterised by `nodeType` + `namePrefix`; four instances (J / O /
  S / D) live on the project window and wire to
  `actionAddJunction` / `actionAddOutfall` / `actionAddStorage` in
  the .ui, plus a programmatic **Add Divider** action (the .ui lacks
  one). Name generation walks `<prefix>1`, `<prefix>2`, … until the
  engine's `nodeIndex` returns -1.

**Auto-length status-bar toggle**:
- Per-project bool on `SWMMVisProjectWindow` persisted to
  `QSettings("SWMMVis/autoLength")`.
- Status-bar checkbox `mCheckBoxAutoLength` parallels
  `mCheckBoxLevelOffsetMode` — enabled only when a project is active,
  rebinds in `onActiveSubWindowChanged`.
- Published to the canvas via `setProperty("autoLength", bool)` so tools
  can read it without a back-pointer to the project window.
- Tools consult the property at commit time; conduit length is
  recomputed from the resulting polyline via
  `EditGeometry::polylineLength`.

**CRS caveat (documented in tool headers)**: the tools compute
layer-CRS coordinates from canvas-pixel coordinates by treating the
canvas as sharing the layer's CRS. When the canvas is reprojecting the
layer (Phase 0.7 Re-render mode), the transform is non-trivially
invertable; the tools still commit edits using the canvas coord as the
layer coord, which will cause a visible jump unless the user first runs
the Phase 0.7 Reproject (which rewrites engine coords + clears the
transform). A future slice could build the inverse transform once and
route scene↔layer through it; for now the tools are safe to use in the
common "canvas CRS == layer CRS" configuration.

**Engine gap — arbitrary-index `swmm_node_remove(idx)` deferred to
Slice F-2**:

The general-purpose remove would renumber every reference to node
indices >= the removed idx across ~56 sites (links.node1 / node2,
subcatch.outlet, controls, reports, divider_link, hotstart writer,
interface file writer, and the plotter subsystem). That work needs its
own session with a regression pass against the legacy model suite; the
GUI's MapToolDelete is held back until it lands. Today the user
edits by: Add + EditVertex + Move + undo for newly-placed objects;
for permanent removal of pre-existing objects, the workflow is "save
to a new .inp with the section omitted, reload" until the API lands.

Precise engine work needed for Slice F-2:
1. `NameIndex::remove_at(idx)` — erase + renumber every map entry
   with a larger index (already O(N), matches current add-cost profile).
2. `NodeData::erase_at(idx)` (and `LinkData::erase_at`, etc.) — per-row
   vector erase on all ~20 SoA arrays.
3. Renumber cross-references: a sweep pass over links /
   subcatchments / dividers / controls / reports / interface file /
   hotstart metadata that decrements any index > removed_idx and
   flags a `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM` for any index == removed_idx that
   isn't already cascade-scheduled.
4. C ABI entry points `swmm_node_remove(idx)`,
   `swmm_link_remove(idx)`, `swmm_subcatch_remove(idx)`,
   `swmm_gage_remove(idx)` — all `CHECK_EDITABLE`.
5. `MapToolDelete` + `DeleteObjectCommand` in the GUI — cascade-delete
   attached links before the owning node; undo restores in the
   reverse order.

Junction → Outfall → **Divider** → Storage.
The `.ui` `toolBarEdit` already lists `actionAddJunction` / `actionAddOutfall` /

`MapToolMoveNode`, `MapToolEditVertex`, and the dead `actionSelectEdit` toolbar button are

**Double-click activates edit mode on the feature under the cursor:**

- **Node** (junction / outfall / storage / divider): a circle+crosshair handle appears at
  the node position. Drag to move. On release, a "Recalculate conduit length?" dialog
  appears if the node has attached conduits; Yes/No applies or skips the length update.

- **Link** (conduit / pump / orifice / weir / outlet): the full polyline highlights in blue

  types appear:

  - **Vertex handles** (white circles, indices 1..N): dragging one moves just that polygon
    corner; the centroid handle updates in real time to track the new centroid.

affected. Answering **No** clears the `LengthRec` list so `MoveNodeCommand` /
`EditVertexCommand` records the geometry change without touching the stored length.

**Exit edit mode:** double-click the same feature again (toggle), double-click empty space,

#### ✅ Slice N — Simulation Status MVC (Phase 4.1 — `SimulationRunner` + `SimulationStatusModel`)

Replaces the fire-and-forget `swmm_engine_run` worker in `onRunSimulation` with a
proper Model-View-Controller that surfaces live progress, warnings, and continuity
errors in the **Simulation Status** dock (the `dockWidgetSimulationStatus` /
`treeViewSimulationStatus` that already exists in the `.ui` but was unpopulated).

**Model — `SimulationStatusModel`** (`QAbstractItemModel`):

Two-level tree:
- **Level 0 — job rows**: one row per simulation run (persists across the session
  so users can compare multiple runs). Columns:

  | # | Header | Content |
  |---|--------|---------|
  | 0 | Name | Project file name (e.g. `Example1.inp`) |
  | 1 | Status | `Running` / `Success` / `Failed` / `Cancelled` |
  | 2 | Progress | `"45.2 %"` while running; `"100 %"` on completion |
  | 3 | Sim Time | Current decimal-day value (updates every step); blank when not running |
  | 4 | Runoff Err (%) | Populated after `swmm_engine_end`; blank while running |
  | 5 | Routing Err (%) | Same |
  | 6 | Duration | Wall-clock seconds once finished; live stopwatch while running |

- **Level 1 — warning rows**: expandable children under each job row; one child
  per warning the engine emits. Col 0: `"[code] message"` text; other columns blank.

Public mutators (called from the GUI thread via queued signals from `SimulationRunner`):
- `int addJob(const QString& instanceName, const QString& inpPath)` → returns job id
- `void updateProgress(int jobId, double fraction, double simTimeDays)`
- `void addWarning(int jobId, int code, const QString& message)`
- `void finishJob(int jobId, bool success, int errCode, const QString& errMsg, double runoffErrFrac, double routingErrFrac)`

**Controller — `SimulationRunner`** (`QObject`, lives on GUI thread):

Runs the full SWMM step loop (`create → open → initialize → start → step-loop →
end → report → close → destroy`) on a worker thread via `QtConcurrent::run`.
Uses the full lifecycle (not the convenience `swmm_engine_run_with_callback`) so
both `SWMM_ProgressCallback` and `SWMM_WarningCallback` can be registered.

Static C callbacks post back to the GUI thread via
`QMetaObject::invokeMethod(runner, λ, Qt::QueuedConnection)`.

Signals:
- `void started(int jobId)`
- `void progressChanged(int jobId, double fraction, double simTimeDays)`
- `void warningReceived(int jobId, int code, QString message)`
- `void finished(int jobId, bool success, int errorCode, QString errorMessage, double runoffErrFrac, double routingErrFrac)`

Cancel is guarded by `std::atomic<bool> m_cancel`; `cancel()` sets it and the step
loop exits early. Engine state is still torn down cleanly (end/close/destroy) after
cancellation so file handles aren't leaked.

**View**: the existing `QTreeView` (`ui->treeViewSimulationStatus`) — no `.ui` change
needed. `initializeSimulationStatusDockWidget()` sets the model, configures column
widths, and enables `uniformRowHeights` for painting performance.

**Integration in `onRunSimulation()`**:
1. Call `mSimStatusModel->addJob(instanceName, inpPath)` → `jobId`.
2. `new SimulationRunner(jobId, instanceName, inpPath, rptPath, outPath, this)`.
3. Wire runner's 4 signals → model mutators + (on `finished`) load `.out` results
   layer + `deleteLater` the runner.
4. Call `runner->start()`.
5. Remove the old `onSetProgressBarBusy` / `QFutureWatcher<int>` block (the status
   dock now carries progress; the main-window progress bar can still be toggled for
   the busy-mode visual but is no longer the primary status channel).

| [include/simulation/simulationrunner.h](../include/simulation/simulationrunner.h) | New — `SimulationRunner` class declaration |
| [src/simulation/simulationrunner.cpp](../src/simulation/simulationrunner.cpp) | New — step-loop implementation + C callback statics |
| [include/simulation/simulationstatusmodel.h](../include/simulation/simulationstatusmodel.h) | New — `SimulationStatusModel` + `SimulationJobRecord` |
| [src/simulation/simulationstatusmodel.cpp](../src/simulation/simulationstatusmodel.cpp) | New — `QAbstractItemModel` implementation |
| [CMakeLists.txt](../CMakeLists.txt) | Add 4 new sources (2 headers + 2 .cpp) |
| [include/swmmvis.h](../include/swmmvis.h) | Add `SimulationStatusModel* mSimStatusModel`; add `initializeSimulationStatusDockWidget()` decl |
| [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) | `initializeSimulationStatusDockWidget()` impl; refactor `onRunSimulation()` |

standalone QtTest once the existing `swmmvis_core` extraction lands. Parked for
now (same blocker as LayerTreeModel / MapCanvas tests). End-to-end verification
via running the app.

**Verify**: Open Example1.inp → Execute → Simulation Status dock shows a running row
with live progress %; on completion row turns green with "Success", continuity errors
populated, warnings listed as children.

#### ✅ Slice O — Layer Tree + Object Browser UX: visibility toggle, double-click zoom, object zoom (Phase 0.8 polish + Phase 6.2 polish)

Two paired UX enhancements across the **Layer Tree Panel** and the **Object Browser Panel**:
toggle visibility and zoom-to-location from both panels, accessible via the tree's
context menu and by double-clicking.

---

**O-1 — Layer Tree Panel changes** (`LayerTreePanel` / `LayerTreeModel`):

*What already works (no change needed):*
- Checkbox (`Qt::CheckStateRole`) on every layer row toggles `layer->setVisible(…)` —
  wired via `LayerTreeModel::setData`. Checking / unchecking a layer in the dock
  immediately shows or hides it on the canvas.
- Right-click context menu already includes **Zoom to Layer** (`actZoom`) which calls
  `onZoomToSelectedLayer()` → `m_canvas->setExtent(layer->extent())`.

*Change — double-click behavior:*

Currently `onLayerDoubleClicked(index)` emits `layerPropertiesRequested(layer)`, which
opens the Layer Properties dialog. Change: double-click should **zoom to the layer's
extent** instead (same action as "Zoom to Layer" in the context menu).

Implementation:
1. In `onLayerDoubleClicked`: replace `emit layerPropertiesRequested(layer)` with a
   call to `onZoomToSelectedLayer()`.
2. Change `m_treeView->setEditTriggers(QAbstractItemView::DoubleClicked)` →
   `QAbstractItemView::NoEditTriggers` so the opacity column is not accidentally
   opened for inline editing on double-click. (Opacity editing moves to the
   Properties dialog, already accessible via the context menu.)

*No header change* — `onLayerDoubleClicked` signature is unchanged; only the body
differs.

---

**O-2 — Object Browser Panel changes** (`ObjectBrowserPanel`):

Currently the Object Browser has no visibility toggles and no per-object zoom. Three
additions:

**a) Per-category visibility toggle (checkboxes on group header items)**

Each group header item (`Rain Gages`, `Junctions`, etc.) gains a checkbox
(`Qt::ItemIsUserCheckable` flag, default `Qt::Checked`). When a header is
checked/unchecked the state propagates to all its child leaf items (cosmetic,
to give visual feedback) and the panel emits a new signal:

```cpp
void objectTypeVisibilityChanged(int objectTypeFlag, bool visible);
```

`SWMMVis` connects this signal to a new `SWMMModelLayer` method:

```cpp
void setObjectTypeVisible(int typeFlag, bool visible);
```

`typeFlag` is one of a new bitmask enum on `SWMMModelLayer`:

```cpp
enum ObjectTypeMask {
    Gages         = 1 << 0,
    Subcatchments = 1 << 1,
    Junctions     = 1 << 2,
    Outfalls      = 1 << 3,
    StorageUnits  = 1 << 4,
    Dividers      = 1 << 5,
    Conduits      = 1 << 6,
    Pumps         = 1 << 7,
    Orifices      = 1 << 8,
    Weirs         = 1 << 9,
    Outlets       = 1 << 10,
    AllObjects    = (1 << 11) - 1
};
```

`SWMMModelLayer::populateScene` (or `refreshScene`) checks the visibility mask
before drawing each `QGraphicsItem` group. The mask is stored as an `int
m_objectTypeMask` member (default `AllObjects`).

**b) Context menu — Zoom to Object**

`onContextMenuRequested` gains a new `actZoom` entry: **Zoom to Object**.
When picked, the handler calls a new `ObjectBrowserPanel::zoomToCurrentObject()`
helper:

1. Query the object's location via `m_layer->identifyByName(name)` which already
   returns a coordinate map.
2. Build a small `MapExtent` centred on the coordinate (e.g. ± 100 m buffer, or
   the layer extent's diagonal × 0.005 as a fraction, whichever is larger).
3. Call `m_canvas->setExtent(zoomBox)`.

`m_canvas` is stored on `ObjectBrowserPanel` (passed in via
`setProject(layer, selMgr, canvas)` — add `MapCanvas *canvas` parameter).

**c) Double-click — Zoom to Object**

Connect `QTreeWidget::itemDoubleClicked(QTreeWidgetItem *, int)` to a new slot
`onItemDoubleClicked`. For leaf items, call `zoomToCurrentObject()`. For group
header items, ignore.

#### ✅ Slice R — Batched map rendering (Phase 1 of "millions of points")

Companion plan: [~/.claude/plans/gui-map-millions-of-points.md](../../../../.claude/plans/gui-map-millions-of-points.md).

- **Problem.** One `QGraphicsItem` per SWMM object (a `NodeGraphicsItem` /
  `LinkGraphicsItem` / `CatchmentGraphicsItem` / per-gage item) doesn't scale.
  Paint time and memory both break down well before 1M objects because
  `QGraphicsScene`'s BSP index, per-item hover/selection state, vtables, and the
  ~300-byte per-item overhead dominate. Target: stay interactive with
  **1–5 M nodes + links**.
- **Approach.** Collapse all rendering for one `SWMMModelLayer` into a
  single **batched `QGraphicsItem`** that iterates the layer's SoA once per
  paint and issues bucketed `QPainter` calls. The legacy per-object items stay
  in the scene as invisible hit-targets for the existing edit tools
  (`QGraphicsItem::ItemHasNoContents` = skipped by paint but still enumerated
  by `QGraphicsScene::items()` for hit-testing). Ripping the per-object items
  out entirely is Phase 3 of the sub-plan, once tools are retargeted at a
  layer-owned spatial index.
- **`SWMMLayerItem`** ([include/map/swmmlayeritem.h](../include/map/swmmlayeritem.h),
  [src/map/swmmlayeritem.cpp](../src/map/swmmlayeritem.cpp)):
  - Friend of `SWMMModelLayer` — reads `m_nodes`, `m_links`, `m_catchments`,
    `m_gages`, the `m_transform` GDAL reprojection, `m_hiddenObjects`, and
    `m_selectedNames` directly without public-accessor round-trips.
  - `ItemUsesExtendedStyleOption` on, so `option->exposedRect` in `paint()` is
    the actual dirty tile → viewport culling via `QRectF::intersects()` on each
    polyline's bbox and each marker's expanded halo.
  - `NoCache` — the layer is dynamic (edits, result animation, selection), so
    `DeviceCoordinateCache` would just churn.
  - `boundingRect()` is cached (scene-space extent + 16 px pad for marker halos)
    and recomputed via `refreshBoundingRect()` after SoA mutations.
  - Paint buckets:
    1. **Subcatchments** — one pen+brush, `drawPolygon` loop with a yellow fill
       override on selected rows.
    2. **Links** — one pen, assemble every visible polyline's segments into a
       single `QVector<QLineF>`, one `drawLines` call; selected links go into a
       second vector painted with the highlight pen (yellow, +2 px).
    3. **Nodes** — four buckets keyed on `nodeType` (0=Junction circle,
       1=Outfall triangle, 2=Storage square, 3=Divider diamond). Each bucket
       owns its symbology pen+brush, painted with `drawEllipse` / `drawRect` /
       `drawPolygon`. Selected nodes painted yellow in a separate sub-pass per
       bucket.
    4. **Gages** — diamond glyph, matches the legacy rendering.
    5. **Labels** — only drawn when `painter->transform().m11() >= 0.5` (LOD
       threshold). Skipped entirely at wider zooms.
  - `ownerLayer()` getter so `SWMMModelLayer::depopulateScene` can identify its
    batched item among multiple `SWMMModelLayer` instances in the same scene.
- **`SWMMModelLayer`** ([include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h),
  [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)):
  - `populateScene` now allocates one `SWMMLayerItem` at `baseZ + 4` (above
    per-object items), then flags every per-object
    `NodeGraphicsItem` / `LinkGraphicsItem` / `CatchmentGraphicsItem` with
    `QGraphicsItem::ItemHasNoContents` so they no longer paint. Tools that call
    `scene->items(scenePos)` still find them — Qt skips the flag for hit-testing.
  - `depopulateScene` picks up the batched item by back-pointer
    (`SWMMLayerItem::ownerLayer() == this`) so multi-layer scenes tear down
    cleanly.
  - `m_batchedItem` pointer tracked so future geometry edits can
    `refreshBoundingRect()` without a full depopulate/populate cycle. Not yet
    exercised in Phase 1 because every mutation path already sets
    `m_needsRebuild = true` and relies on `refreshScene` to rebuild.
  - Added `friend class SWMMLayerItem;`.
- **Selection contract preserved.** The Object Browser + Attribute Panel's
  `selectionChanged(QStringList)` signal contract is unchanged — the batched
  pass reads `m_selectedNames` and paints a yellow fill / highlight pen overlay
  over each bucket, so the visual result matches the legacy per-item
  highlight.
- **Phase 3 shipped (2026-04-24).** Tools now hit-test through the
  layer's `pickAt` and the per-object `NodeGraphicsItem` /
  `LinkGraphicsItem` / `CatchmentGraphicsItem` placeholders are gone.
  Memory per loaded layer drops from one QGraphicsItem-per-object
  (~300+ bytes × N) to a single `SWMMLayerItem` + the SoA that was
  always there. This is where the Slice R memory goal actually
  lands; Phase 1 only fixed paint time. Details:
  - **New layer API** ([include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h),
    [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)):
    `PickResult pickAt(sceneX, sceneY, tolerance)` returns a typed
    `(Category, soaIndex, name)` triple so tools don't have to
    second-lookup after `identifyAt`. `bool previewNodeMove(idx,
    newX, newY)` mutates cached coords + attached link endpoints
    and emits `repaintRequested` without touching the engine —
    MoveNode uses it for live drag preview.
  - **Tool retargets**:
    [src/map/tools/maptoolmovenode.{h,cpp}](../src/map/tools/maptoolmovenode.cpp) —
    `hitTestNode` → `pickNode` returning `(layer*, nodeIdx, name)`;
    drag state is a map-CRS coord pair, not a `NodeGraphicsItem*`.
    [src/map/tools/maptooleditvertex.{h,cpp}](../src/map/tools/maptooleditvertex.cpp) —
    `hitTestLink` → `pickLink` returning a `LinkHit`.
    Both tools no longer `#include "map/graphicsitems.h"`.
  - **Placeholder removal**:
    `SWMMModelLayer::populateScene` no longer constructs
    `NodeGraphicsItem` / `LinkGraphicsItem` / `CatchmentGraphicsItem`
    — just the batched `SWMMLayerItem`. `depopulateScene` sweep
    simplified to a single `dynamic_cast<SWMMLayerItem *>` +
    `ownerLayer()` check. `#include "map/graphicsitems.h"` dropped
    from the layer. The per-object-item classes themselves are still
    compiled (scale-bar / coord display / GIS vector feature items
    share the file); only the SWMM-side usage is retired.
- **What's deferred to Phases 2, 4, 5 of the sub-plan.**
  - **Phase 2** — spatial index (uniform grid or R-tree) + layer-owned
    `queryInRect(sceneRect)`. Not a prerequisite any more (Phase 3
    shipped against the linear-scan identifyAt), but still worth doing
    for true 1 M-scale interactive perf. `pickAt` becomes O(log n)
    instead of O(n) when the grid lands.
  - **Phase 3** — SHIPPED 2026-04-24. See the Phase-3-shipped block
    above; memory wins landed with the placeholder deletion.
  - **Phase 4** — SHIPPED 2026-04-24. Hover tooltip + cursor feedback:
    - **Tooltip** — [src/map/mapcanvas.cpp](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp)
      overrides `event(QEvent*)` to intercept `QEvent::ToolTip`.
      Walks visible `SWMMModelLayer`s via `pickAt`, builds a small HTML
      tooltip from `identifyByName` attributes (name, kind, node /
      link subtype, coord, vertex count as applicable), shows via
      `QToolTip::showText`. `setMouseTracking(true)` was already on
      the canvas so no extra plumbing.
    - **Cursor feedback** —
      [src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp](../src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp)'s
      `mouseMoveEvent` now does a lightweight `pickAt` when no button
      is held and flips the canvas cursor to `PointingHandCursor` when
      hovering a SWMM object, back to the tool's default cursor
      otherwise. Gives users a "this is clickable" cue without clicking.
  - **Phase 4 (orig text)** — hover state + tooltip wiring (override
    `QGraphicsView::viewportEvent` for `QEvent::ToolTip`, build tooltip from
    the SoA on demand).
  - **Phase 5** — `Tools → Debug → Generate N Nodes` synthetic benchmark
    action at N ∈ {10 k, 100 k, 1 M, 5 M}; lock in the perf target (≥ 30 fps
    pan/zoom at 1 M, ≥ 15 fps at 5 M on an M-series laptop).
- **Files**:
  - [include/map/swmmlayeritem.h](../include/map/swmmlayeritem.h) (new)
  - [src/map/swmmlayeritem.cpp](../src/map/swmmlayeritem.cpp) (new)
  - [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h)

#### ✅ Slice S — Virtualised Object Browser tree (companion to Slice R)

**Motivation.** Slice R scaled the map canvas to millions of objects, but the
Object Browser dock still uses a `QTreeWidget` that allocates one
`QTreeWidgetItem` per SWMM object. At the scales Slice R now targets the
browser becomes the bottleneck — building 1 M `QTreeWidgetItem`s takes seconds,
consumes hundreds of MB, and stalls the UI thread on every refresh. This slice
swaps the backing widget for a fully **virtualised `QTreeView + QAbstractItemModel`**
so only the ~30 rows currently on screen ever materialise.

**Approach (option 2 — virtualised model).** Replace `QTreeWidget` with
`QTreeView` + a custom `SWMMObjectTreeModel` backed by the
`SWMMModelLayer`'s SoA. No per-leaf heap allocation. `QSortFilterProxyModel`
above the source model supplies the existing "Filter by name…" box.

##### Layer-side additions — [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h), [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)

Category-aware API keyed on a new `enum Category` (Junctions, Outfalls,
Storage, Dividers, Conduits, Pumps, Orifices, Weirs, Outlets, Subcatchments,
RainGages):

```cpp
int             categoryCount(Category c) const;              // O(1)
QString         objectNameAt(Category c, int row) const;      // O(1)
void            setObjectVisibleAt(Category c, int row, bool);// O(1) + signal
void            setCategoryVisible(Category c, bool);         // O(n) per category
Qt::CheckState  categoryCheckState(Category c) const;         // O(1)
```

Backed by two new lazy caches built in `buildGeometryCache` (and cleared in
`closeEngine`):

- `QVector<int> m_nodesByType[4]` and `QVector<int> m_linksByType[5]` — row
  → underlying SoA index, one bucket per SWMM sub-type. Lets the model
  answer `rowCount(cat)` and `objectNameAt(cat, row)` in O(1) without
  scanning `m_nodes` / `m_links`.
- `int m_hiddenCountByCategory[NumCategories]` — decremented/incremented
  in every `setObjectVisibleAt` / `setCategoryVisible` call so
  `categoryCheckState` returns Checked / Unchecked / PartiallyChecked in
  O(1) rather than scanning the category's hidden set.

Existing `setObjectVisible(name, bool)` stays as a convenience for
call sites that only hold a name (map-tool tooltips, command-line paths).
Internally it reroutes through a name→(category, row) lookup built at
cache time (`QHash<QString, QPair<Category, int>> m_objectLocation`) so
the name variant is still O(1) after a small constant hash-probe cost.

##### `SWMMObjectTreeModel` — [include/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.h](../include/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.h), [src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp) (new)

Two-level `QAbstractItemModel`:

| Level | Row id encoding                       | Data                                 |
|-------|---------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 0 (category) | `internalId == kRootMarker`    | One row per `Category` with children |
| 1 (leaf)     | `internalId == parent-row`     | Synthesised on demand from layer SoA |

- `index(row, col, parent)` / `parent(child)` use `internalId` to thread
  the two-level hierarchy without allocating any per-row helper objects.
- `rowCount(parent)` returns `NumCategories` at root and
  `layer->categoryCount(cat)` inside a category. Empty categories are
  omitted from the visible row set via a `QVector<Category> m_visible`
  mapping so the view doesn't render headers for types the current model
  doesn't contain.
- `data(idx, role)`:
  - Category row: `DisplayRole` = `"Junctions (1 234 567)"`,
    `DecorationRole` = `iconForGroup`, `CheckStateRole` =
    `layer->categoryCheckState(cat)`, `UserRole + Category` = `int(cat)`.
  - Leaf row: `DisplayRole` = `layer->objectNameAt(cat, row)`,
    `DecorationRole` = `iconForType`, `CheckStateRole` = `Checked` iff
    `layer->isObjectVisible(name)`, `UserRole + ObjectType` = int(type),
    `UserRole + ObjectName` = QString(name). The "Object" header is
    column 0; no other columns.
- `flags(idx)`:
  - Category: `Qt::ItemIsEnabled | Qt::ItemIsUserCheckable | Qt::ItemIsAutoTristate`.
  - Leaf: `Qt::ItemIsEnabled | Qt::ItemIsSelectable | Qt::ItemIsUserCheckable`.
- `setData(idx, value, CheckStateRole)`:
  - On leaf: call `layer->setObjectVisibleAt(cat, row, checked)`, then
    emit `dataChanged` on the leaf and its parent category (so the
    parent's tri-state re-renders). The layer internally updates
    `m_hiddenObjects` and the per-category count; the map's batched
    renderer re-reads both on next paint.
  - On category: call `layer->setCategoryVisible(cat, checked)`, then
    emit `dataChanged` on the entire child range so every leaf
    checkbox redraws.
- `beginResetModel` / `endResetModel` are wired to the layer's
  `modelLoaded` signal so opening / reloading a project reshapes the
  tree safely.

##### `ObjectBrowserPanel` — [src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp)

- `QTreeWidget` swapped for `QTreeView`; owns a `SWMMObjectTreeModel`
  and wraps it in a `QSortFilterProxyModel` with
  `setRecursiveFilteringEnabled(true)` so the search box filters
  leaves but keeps category headers visible whenever any child
  matches.
- Selection bridge goes through `view->selectionModel()`:
  - `selectionChanged` collects selected source-model indexes (mapped
    via proxy), reads `(Category, name)` from their
    `UserRole+Category / ObjectName` roles, pushes into the existing
    `SelectionManager`.
  - Reverse direction converts `SWMMObjectRef` → source-model index
    using `m_objectLocation` on the layer, maps through proxy,
    updates the selection model.
- Zoom-to-object / Plot Time Series actions move to the view's
  `doubleClicked` and `customContextMenuRequested` slots; the logic
  in `zoomToObject(SWMMObjectRef)` is unchanged.
- Existing `objectVisibilityChanged` / `objectsVisibilityChanged`
  signals become dead code — the model calls the layer directly.
  They are removed from the panel's public surface; the
  main-window wiring in [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) drops
  its two `connect`s because the layer now drives
  `setObjectVisible*` from inside `setData`.

##### Performance expectations

- **Refresh time**: from O(N) `new QTreeWidgetItem` allocations to
  O(NumCategories) model-reset. On a 1 M-object model the refresh goes
  from multi-second stall to < 10 ms.
- **Memory**: from ~300 B × N (QTreeWidgetItem) to ~ 30 KB total
  (the model itself + per-category index arrays stay on the layer,
  already needed for the batched renderer; the model adds no
  per-leaf state).
- **Scrolling / search**: virtualised — only visible rows call
  `data()`; `QSortFilterProxyModel` keeps a sparse index of accepted
  rows. Sub-millisecond filter response up to ~5 M.

##### Files

- [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h)
  — `enum Category`, `categoryCount` / `objectNameAt` /
  `setObjectVisibleAt` / `setCategoryVisible` / `categoryCheckState`,
  per-category caches.
- [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp) —
  implement the above; wire into `buildGeometryCache`, `closeEngine`,
  `setObjectVisible`.
- [include/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.h](../include/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.h) (new)
- [src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp) (new)
- [include/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.h](../include/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.h)
  — drop `QTreeWidget`, add `QTreeView` + model members.
- [src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp)
  — rewrite UI + bus wiring.
- [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) — remove the two panel-visibility
  `connect()`s (the model now calls the layer directly).
- [CMakeLists.txt](../CMakeLists.txt) — register new sources.

##### Tests (parked, alongside Slice R)

- Unit tests for `SWMMObjectTreeModel::rowCount / data / setData`
  (CheckStateRole round-trip, tri-state on mixed-child toggle).
- Unit tests for `SWMMModelLayer::categoryCheckState` counter
  invariants under sequences of `setObjectVisibleAt` +
  `setCategoryVisible`.

##### Verify

- Open a real `.inp`; Object Browser populates as before (groups with
  counts, leaves with checkboxes, icons).
- Toggle a leaf checkbox → dot/line disappears from the map, category
  header becomes partially-checked.
- Toggle a category header → all leaves toggle; map refreshes once.
- Search "J1" → only matching leaves + their group headers remain.
- Click a leaf → SelectionManager fires; Attribute Panel updates.
- Right-click leaf → Zoom to Object / Plot Time Series still work.
- Synthetic 500 k-node model (pending Slice R Phase 5 benchmark
  action) populates the browser in < 50 ms.

##### Follow-up fix (2026-04-24) — Zoom to Object now works for every kind

The initial Slice S ship relied on `identifyByName()` to return X/Y for
zoom. That map only carries X/Y for nodes and rain gages, so
subcatchments (and multi-vertex links without a centred X/Y attribute)
silently fell through without zooming. Fixed by adding
`SWMMModelLayer::objectExtent(name)` — a unified layer-CRS bounding-box
lookup that returns a point bbox for nodes/gages, the polyline bbox
for links, and the polygon bbox for subcatchments. Unknown names
return a NaN-sentinel extent so callers can reliably distinguish "not
found" from a node at the origin. `ObjectBrowserPanel::zoomToObject`
now drives the canvas from this bbox (with a 25 % pad for areal
features, an extent-proportional buffer for point features), so
double-click and right-click → Zoom to Object both work on every SWMM
object type.

**Files**: [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h),
[src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)
(new `objectExtent`), [src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp)
(rewritten `zoomToObject`).

#### ✅ Slice U — UX round-up: welcome close, log filter, default CRS, options MVC, click-select

Six small-but-visible quality fixes that stabilise the shell around
Slices R / S and unlock the rest of Phase 0 UX.

##### U.1 Welcome-page close regression — [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp)

Previous scheme (delete-on-close + reparent inside `eventFilter`) was
fragile: reopening via Help → Show Welcome sometimes left the tab X
inactive. Switched to a **hide-on-close lifecycle**:

- Welcome sub-window is created by `setupUi` and kept alive —
  `WA_DeleteOnClose = false`, never destroyed.
- `eventFilter` still catches `QEvent::Close` but only to pick the next
  visible sibling sub-window (via `QMetaObject::invokeMethod
  Qt::QueuedConnection`) so the next project tab auto-activates
  after welcome closes. With no siblings the MDI area just goes blank,
  which is exactly what the user wants.
- `onShowWelcomeScreen` becomes a one-liner: `if (!sub->isVisible())
  sub->show(); setActiveSubWindow(sub);`. No reparenting, no
  destruction, no re-creation.

Result: Close X always works, and the follow-up focus behaviour
matches "close showing the next project document in the MDI area,
blank if none."

##### U.2 Message-log filter — [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp)

`onLogMessage` entries in the dock are supposed to be user-facing
modelling events. The shell was also emitting GUI-lifecycle chatter
("Workspace initialized.", "Reading settings", "Finished reading
settings", "New Project: opens the Welcome tab…", "Recent files
cleared."). Those are gone — the dock now only carries
modelling-relevant messages (load warnings/errors, Save / Save As
results, simulation cancel requests, tool "not yet implemented"
hints, and anything surfaced by the engine).

qDebug output was never in the UI (no `qInstallMessageHandler` was
installed), so the fix is purely an audit of explicit
`onLogMessage` call sites — no runtime pipeline change.

##### U.3 Default CRS — WGS 84 when .inp has no CRS — [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)

Resolution order on load:
1. CRS stored in the .inp via `swmm_get_crs`.
2. **EPSG:4326 (WGS 84)** — the new default.
3. `SpatialReferenceSystem::untitled()` — only if EPSG:4326 lookup
   fails (missing PROJ data etc.).

Matches the convention most GIS-derived SWMM models assume and lets
WMS/WMTS basemaps reproject correctly without a manual CRS pick.

##### U.4 Simulation-options MVC wire — [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h), [src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp](../src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp)

New surface on `SWMMModelLayer`:

```cpp
QString getOption(const QByteArray &key, const QString &fallback = {}) const;
bool    setOption(const QByteArray &key, const QString &value);
int     setOptions(const QMap<QByteArray, QString> &values);
// Signal
void    optionsChanged(const QStringList &keys);
```

- `SimulationOptionsDialog::setOption` now routes through the layer
  when a layer is bound (engine direct for engine-only tests). Every
  key write fans out through `optionsChanged({key})` on the layer.
- Main window listens to `optionsChanged` per-tab: if the key set
  includes `FLOW_UNITS`, it re-syncs the status-bar combo via
  `UnitSystem::syncFromEngine`. If it includes `LINK_OFFSETS`, it
  calls `SWMMVisProjectWindow::reloadElevationOffsetModeFromEngine()`
  (new method) and updates the Offset Mode checkbox.
- Adding a new observer of options is one `connect(layer,
  &SWMMModelLayer::optionsChanged, …)` — no more polling on
  `subWindowActivated` to sync dialogs to engine edits.

##### U.5 Click-selection on SWMM objects — [src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp](../src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp), [src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp](../src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp)

- `OpenSWMMVisMapToolSelect::selectAtPoint` previously only walked
  `GISVectorLayer`s. Extended to `SWMMModelLayer` via
  `identifyAt(mapX, mapY, tol)` → grabs the `"Name"` attr → pushes
  into `layer->setSelectedElementNames()`. Shift = add, Ctrl =
  remove, no-mod = replace. A miss with no modifier clears the SWMM
  layer's selection so the Attribute Panel empties out.
- Project window now sets `mSelectTool` as the default active tool
  on construction (was `mPanTool`). Matches legacy EPA SWMM's
  defaults so users can click objects immediately after opening a
  model.
- The existing `SelectionManager` bridge in the project window picks
  up the layer's `selectionChanged(QStringList)` signal, so
  Attribute Panel / Object Browser / Layer Tree all respond
  automatically.

##### U.6 Legacy defaults audit — deferred, documented

Audit of `SimulationOptionsDialog` defaults vs legacy EPA SWMM 5.2
(FLOW_UNITS=CFS, INFILTRATION=HORTON, FLOW_ROUTING=KINWAVE,
START=JAN-01-2002, END_TIME=06:00:00, REPORT_STEP=00:15:00,
WET_STEP=00:05:00, DRY_STEP=01:00:00, ROUTING_STEP=0:00:30, etc.):
**the dialog reads whatever the engine returns**, so any
mis-alignment lives in `src/engine/core/SimulationOptions.hpp`
defaults on the engine side. Tracked as a follow-up — needs
engine-side verification and a single-PR alignment pass once the
matrix is confirmed. The earlier investigation (see conversation
history) already flagged `start_date = 2453006.0` (Jan 1, 2004) in
the refactored engine vs legacy's Jan 1, 2002 as one concrete
divergence.

##### Files

- [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) — welcome lifecycle simplified; log chatter removed; options-listener per tab.
- [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h) + [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp) — `getOption` / `setOption` / `setOptions` / `optionsChanged`; WGS 84 default CRS.
- [include/swmmvisprojectwindow.h](../include/swmmvisprojectwindow.h) + [src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp](../src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp) — `reloadElevationOffsetModeFromEngine`; default active tool = Select.
- [src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp](../src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp) — `setOption` routed through layer when bound.
- [src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp](../src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp) — `SWMMModelLayer` branch in `selectAtPoint`; miss-with-no-mod clear.

##### Follow-ups

- Full legacy-defaults alignment (U.6) — engine work, plan-tracked.
- Slice T (reorderable drawing order) — next up per the prior plan slice.
- Rubber-band rect select for SWMM layers — stub exists in
  `selectInRect` (GIS-only today); extend with `SWMMModelLayer`
  range-query once Slice R Phase 2 lands a spatial index.

#### ✅ Slice W — Selection UX pass + CRS-aware picking + on-the-fly reprojection

Consolidated record of the selection / CRS work done immediately after
Slice U shipped. Individual fixes went in as small iterations in
response to user testing; this entry is the single authoritative
description so follow-on slices (T / V) don't accidentally regress
them.

##### W.1 Unified object-extent API — [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h), [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)

- `MapExtent objectExtent(const QString &name) const` — returns a
  layer-CRS bbox for any SWMM object kind (point bbox for nodes /
  gages, polyline bbox for links, polygon bbox for subcatchments).
  Unknown name → NaN-sentinel (callers use `std::isfinite` to test;
  zero-bbox is ambiguous with a node at the origin so zero is
  reserved).
- `bool findObjectLocation(name, &cat, &row)` — O(1) hash lookup
  backing the tree model's `SelectionManager`→index bridge.
- Fixes subcatchment zoom-to-object (used to silently no-op because
  `identifyByName` didn't return X/Y for polygons).

##### W.2 On-the-fly CRS reprojection — [src/map/mapcanvas.cpp](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp)

- `MapCanvas::insertLayer` now:
  1. Connects `layer::srsChanged` → rebuild the layer's transform
     against the current canvas SRS, `refreshScene`, then
     `zoomToFullExtent` so the view actually shifts to where the
     reprojected content is. Previously `setSRS` emitted
     `srsChanged` into the void — `m_transform` never rebuilt,
     features stayed at raw layer coordinates.
  2. Seeds the transform at insert time via one
     `onCanvasCRSChanged` call — first-frame correctness when the
     layer's SRS differs from the canvas's at load.
- New static `layerExtentInCanvasCRS()` reprojects the 4 corners of
  a layer's extent through its SRS → canvas SRS transform. Used by
  `fullExtent()` so a UTM layer's extent doesn't get unioned with a
  4326 layer's extent as if they were the same CRS.
- Default layer CRS fallback = EPSG:4326 when `.inp` has no CRS
  (set in `loadModel`).

##### W.3 CRS-aware `identifyAt` — [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)

The core bug behind "nodes impossible to click after reprojecting".
`identifyAt` was comparing layer-CRS SoA coords to canvas-CRS click
coords — meaningless when the two CRSes differ.

Fix: inverse-transform the click (and a tolerance-offset point) into
layer coords at the top of `identifyAt`. `tolerance` is also
converted to layer units so the comparison is apples-to-apples. All
subsequent tiers operate in layer CRS.

##### W.4 Tiered identifyAt priority — [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)

Previous "nearest-wins-across-all-kinds" logic let a conduit near a
junction steal the click. New priority:

1. **Nodes + Rain Gages** with full tolerance. If any within
   tolerance, return nearest and bail — links/subcatchments cannot
   compete.
2. **Links** with tolerance ÷ 3. Tightened because users reported
   links were "too easy"; now the click must be close to the
   drawn stroke.
3. **Subcatchments** point-in-polygon only. No tolerance — click
   must land inside.

Per-segment distance (not midpoint) for link hit-testing so long
conduits are clickable anywhere along the drawn stroke. `m_hiddenObjects`
filter applies to every tier so invisible features never hit.

##### W.5 Render-bounds tolerance floor — [include/map/tools/maptoolselect.h](../include/map/tools/maptoolselect.h), [src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp](../src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp), [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)

- `SWMMModelLayer::maxMarkerHalfBoundPx()` — returns the largest
  visible-glyph half-bound in pixels across every node + gage
  symbology. Circles use radius; squares / triangles / diamonds use
  `size/2 × sqrt(2)` so the corner reaches the bound.
- Select tool computes effective pick radius as
  `max(userPrefTol, markerFloor + 4 px halo)`. Guarantees any click
  inside the visible glyph picks it regardless of the user's
  tolerance preference.
- Default `m_pixelTol = 16`, drag threshold `m_dragThreshPx = 8`.

##### W.6 Right-click context menu on canvas — [src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp](../src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp), [include/map/tools/maptoolselect.h](../include/map/tools/maptoolselect.h)

- Right-click on a SWMM object pops a menu: **Zoom to Object** +
  (for Node / Link / Subcatchment) **Plot Time Series…**.
- Mirrors the Object Browser right-click menu; right-clicks also
  promote the hit object to the current selection so the
  Attribute Panel follows the menu target.
- New signal `plotTimeSeriesRequested(SWMMObjectRef)` on the tool.
- Main-window `openTimeSeriesPlotFor(ref)` factored out so Object
  Browser and Select tool both drive the same dialog through one
  slot.

##### W.7 Rubber-band select for SWMM layers — [src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp](../src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp)
