#### ✅ Slice T — User-reorderable drawing order (layers, categories, objects)

**Status (2026-04-24):** shipped with `.oswp` persistence deferred
to Phase 12. Working summary:

- **T.1 Layer drawing order** — [src/map/mapcanvas.cpp](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp):
  `moveLayer` now rebuilds every vector layer's scene items so new
  `layerZValue` takes effect visually on the first frame (the
  existing drag-drop path already shuffled `m_layers` + emitted
  `layerOrderChanged`; the visible stacking just stayed stale
  because `setZValue` was frozen at `populateScene` time).
- **T.2 Category order in Object Browser** — `SWMMModelLayer`
  gains `m_categoryOrder` + `setCategoryOrder` /
  `categoryOrderChanged`; `SWMMObjectTreeModel::m_visible`
  reads the ordered vector, implements
  `supportedDropActions` / `mimeTypes` (`application/x-swmm-category-row`)
  / `mimeData` / `canDropMimeData` / `dropMimeData`; Object
  Browser panel enables `InternalMove` on the QTreeView.
- **T.3 Intra-category object order** — sparse
  `QHash<Category, QVector<int>> m_objectOrderOverrides` on the
  layer; `setObjectOrder` validates a permutation against
  `defaultObjectOrder`; `objectNameAt` prefers override over
  default bucket; `m_objectLocation` rewritten for the reordered
  category so the selection bridge still returns visible rows.
  Second mime type `application/x-swmm-leaf-row` in the tree model
  handles leaf-row drags; cross-category drops rejected.
- **Persistence**: deferred — see T's open items at the end of
  this entry and Phase 12.

**Files touched in the Slice T ship:**

- [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h)
  + [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)
  (`m_categoryOrder`, `m_objectOrderOverrides`, `setCategoryOrder`,
  `setObjectOrder`, `clearObjectOrder`, `objectOrder`,
  `defaultObjectOrder`, `categoryOrderChanged` signal).
- [include/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.h](../include/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.h)
  + [src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp)
  (drag-drop quartet + both mime types).
- [src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp)
  (QTreeView drag-drop flags).
- [src/map/mapcanvas.cpp](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp)
  (`moveLayer` rebuilds scene).

---

**Original design (kept for reference to `.oswp` persistence +
future sort-by / keyboard-move follow-ups):**

**Motivation.** Three reorder-related UX gaps:

1. **Layer draw order.** Canvas Z-order today is driven by
   `layerZValue()` offsets hard-coded at `populateScene` time. The
   Layer Tree already has `setDragEnabled` / `setDragDropMode(InternalMove)`
   ([src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp:597-600](../src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp#L597)) and a
   `MapCanvas::moveLayer(from, to)` hook used by the panel, but the
   drop handler isn't fully reliable (group categories can trap drops,
   persistence across session reload is missing). Formalise drag-and-drop
   layer reordering as a supported workflow and persist the order.
2. **Object Browser category order.** Category enumeration in
   [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h)
   is frozen (Junctions → Outfalls → …). Users who want "Conduits"
   at the top can't put it there. Expose a per-project category
   ordering that the tree model consumes, with drag-and-drop in the
   panel.
3. **Object order within a category.** The virtualised tree model
   (Slice S) exposes leaves in SoA-index order. Users who rearrange
   them expect the new order to stick across tab switches and
   sessions. Needs a per-layer override map and drag-and-drop plumbing.

None of these change the on-disk `.inp`: SWMM has no concept of
layer/category/object presentation order. Order state is a GUI artifact
persisted in the project's `.oswp` sidecar.

**Approach.**

##### T.1 Layer drawing order — [src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp), [src/map/mapcanvas.cpp](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp)

- Audit the existing `dropEvent` / `moveLayer` path. Confirm the drop
  indicator resolves to a legal target (can't drop above the SWMM
  Model / Results category headers, can't drop into a leaf). Block
  invalid drops with `dragMoveEvent` + `event->ignore()` at the target.
- Every successful drop calls `MapCanvas::moveLayer(src, dst)`, which
  shuffles the `m_layers` vector and reassigns `layerZValue()` in
  stride order so the batched + legacy items repaint in the new
  stack. Emit a new `canvas::layerOrderChanged()` signal so the
  Object Browser / Attribute Panel re-bind if the active layer
  changed position.
- **Persist** the final order in `.oswp`: append
  `layerOrder: [layer-id, …]` to the project file and replay on
  session restore. Layers missing from the saved list append at
  the bottom (newly-imported layers).

##### T.2 Category order — [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h), [src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp)

- `SWMMModelLayer` gains a `QVector<Category> m_categoryOrder` seeded
  at cache time with the default enum order. Two public methods:
  `setCategoryOrder(QVector<Category>)` and
  `Category categoryAtVisibleIndex(int i) const`. Existing code
  stops referencing the `Category` enum ordinal directly for tree
  positioning — reads go through the new lookup.
- `SWMMObjectTreeModel::m_visible` becomes a filtered view of
  `m_categoryOrder` (drop empty categories in the current order
  rather than the enum order). `reload()` picks up order changes.
- `QTreeView::setDragEnabled(true)` + `setDragDropMode(InternalMove)`
  on category rows. `SWMMObjectTreeModel` implements
  `supportedDropActions` (`MoveAction`), `mimeData` (encodes source
  category ordinal), `dropMimeData` (reorders `m_categoryOrder`,
  emits `layoutChanged`).
- **Persist** the category order in `.oswp` per project:
  `{layerId}.categoryOrder: [int,...]` — a round-trip round-trip on
  project reload reapplies the sequence.

##### T.3 Intra-category object order — [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h), [src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp)

- Per-category override: `QHash<Category, QVector<int>>
  m_objectOrderOverrides`. Key: category. Value: ordered list of SoA
  indices. If the category has no override, reads fall back to the
  existing `m_nodesByType[type]` / `m_linksByType[type]` arrays. So
  default-ordered categories carry zero extra memory.
- `objectNameAt(cat, row)` reads the override table first, then the
  default bucket. `setObjectOrder(cat, QVector<int> soaIndices)`
  installs an override; `clearObjectOrder(cat)` reverts.
- Tree view's `setDragDropMode(InternalMove)` on leaves emits the
  source/target row pair. `SWMMObjectTreeModel::dropMimeData` reorders
  the override vector and emits `dataChanged` + `layoutChanged` so
  the view animates the swap. Category headers reject object drops
  (drop only accepted when source and target are siblings under the
  same category).
- New objects (AddNode, etc.) append at the tail of both the override
  (if present) and the default bucket.
- **Persist** in `.oswp`:
  `{layerId}.objectOrder.{categoryOrdinal}: [soaIndex, …]` — only
  emitted for categories with a user override. Round-trips across
  tab switches and session restarts.

##### Risks and follow-ups

- **Name collisions on reload**: if the underlying SoA changed
  (add/remove between save and load), override vectors can reference
  stale indices. Validate at load: drop indices outside `[0, count)`,
  append missing indices at the end, log a single warning.
- **Drag-drop UX with millions of rows**: at 1 M leaves in a category,
  drag-and-drop is the wrong UI for anything but small nudges. Defer
  "sort by…" (name / count / last-modified) + "move up/down" keyboard
  commands — both reuse the same override vector — to a follow-up
  if users ask.
- **Interaction with category hide**: a hidden category's leaves
  stay in the override vector; un-hiding restores them in the saved
  order.
- **.oswp schema**: Slice T is the first slice whose state belongs in
  the project file but has no `.inp` counterpart. This is the first
  concrete driver for the project-file schema work in Phase 12 — the
  reorder payloads shape the minimum project serializer.

##### Files

- [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h)
  + [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)
  — `m_categoryOrder`, `m_objectOrderOverrides`,
  `setCategoryOrder` / `setObjectOrder` / `clearObjectOrder`, override
  fallback in `objectNameAt`, persistence hooks.
- [include/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.h](../include/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.h)
  + [src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/swmmobjecttreemodel.cpp)
  — `supportedDropActions`, `mimeTypes`, `mimeData`, `dropMimeData`;
  route category vs leaf drops; `m_visible` derivation switches from
  enum to `m_categoryOrder`.
- [src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp)
  — `setDragEnabled(true)` + `setDragDropMode(InternalMove)` +
  `setDropIndicatorShown(true)` on the `QTreeView`.
- [src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp)
  — tighten `dropEvent` validation, emit persistence signal.
- [src/map/mapcanvas.cpp](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp) +
  [include/map/mapcanvas.h](../include/map/mapcanvas.h) — new
  `layerOrderChanged()` signal; `moveLayer` reshuffles z-values
  densely.
- [src/project/openswmmvissession.cpp](../src/project/openswmmvissession.cpp)
  (or whichever file owns `.oswp` I/O once Phase 12 ships) — serialize
  the layer order + per-layer category order + per-category object
  overrides.

##### Verify

- Layer Tree: drag the SWMM Outputs layer above the SWMM Model layer →
  results raster now draws on top of the network. Save project,
  reopen → order persists.
- Object Browser: drag the Conduits category to the top →
  `setDragDropMode(InternalMove)` accepts the drop; leaves reparent
  correctly; tab-switch away and back → category order persisted.
- Drag a single conduit leaf within the Conduits category →
  re-ordered; cross-category drop rejected.
- Add a new node via map tool → appears at the end of the Junctions
  category (default override behaviour for tail inserts).
- Delete a node while its category has a user override →
  override vector compacts; subsequent scrolls render without gaps.
- 1 M-object stress: drag-drop interactive (<50 ms per drop), memory
  overhead under 8 MB per category with full override installed.

#### ✅ Slice V — Settings & Preferences infrastructure

**Status (2026-04-24):** first cut shipped. App scope only today;

**Open follow-ups**

- Thread-safety: the singleton reads `QSettings` synchronously.
  The Select tool's `preferenceChanged` lambda and the simulation
  runner snapshot are both GUI-thread entries, so no race today.
  When a background `SWMMLayerItem::paint` starts reading live
  manager state (currently reads the LOD lazily inside `paint` which
  runs on the GUI thread too), re-audit.
- "Per-field indicator" + "project override checkbox next to each
  setting" from the original design — defer with the

- Debug `[select]` + `[crs]` qDebug traces have been removed now

**Original design (kept for reference to Phase 12 hand-off):**


Motivation. Configuration state is scattered today: some lives in
`QSettings`, some is hard-coded (Select-tool pixel tolerance was
8 px at source, now 12 px at source — with no UI to tune it), some is
implicit in source defaults (symbology colours / sizes), and some
belongs to the project (symbology overrides for a specific model)
but there's no project file yet. A single Preferences dialog + a
typed accessor layer unifies the story and gives users the click
tolerance / LOD / default-tool knobs they keep asking for.

The slice's main design decision is the **two-level split**: which
settings follow the **user** across every project they open (app
scope), and which follow the **project** when it's shared with
someone else (project scope). Getting this split right now avoids
breaking changes when Phase 12 lands `.oswp` project files.

##### V.0 Two-level settings model

| Scope        | Store       | Lifetime                  | Examples                                                   |
|--------------|-------------|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| **App**      | `QSettings` | Per-user / per-installation | click tolerance, default tool, theme, recent-files size, auto-save interval, engine thread count, label LOD threshold, welcome-on-startup, WMS/WMTS endpoint list |
| **Project**  | `.oswp`     | Per-project (shipped with the model) | per-layer symbology overrides, layer/category/object order (Slice T), per-view bookmarks, project-specific CRS preference, per-project basemap choice, per-project measurement unit override |

Guiding rule: **if changing the setting alters what a collaborator
sees when they open the same `.oswp`, it belongs in the project
scope**. Everything else is app scope. Follows QGIS / AutoCAD
conventions.

Project-scope settings always fall back to the app-scope value at
load time so a missing key is never fatal — project file just
inherits the user's default. Changing an app-scope default doesn't
invalidate any project's stored override.

##### V.1 Typed accessor layer — new `PreferencesManager`

New class [include/core/preferencesmanager.h](../include/core/preferencesmanager.h) (singleton like `UnitSystem`):

```cpp
class PreferencesManager : public QObject {
public:
    // Typed accessors per key group. Each getter reads:
    //   1. active project override (if any)  — project scope
    //   2. app-scope QSettings               — app scope
    //   3. compiled-in default                — fallback
    //
    // Setters write to the appropriate scope. Each emits
    // `preferenceChanged(group, key)` so live-binding UI refreshes.

    struct Selection {
        int    clickTolerancePx;     // default 12
        int    dragThresholdPx;      // default 8
        bool   clearOnMiss;          // default true
    } selection;

    struct Rendering {
        bool   antialiasAtFarZoom;   // default false
        qreal  labelLodM11Min;       // default 0.5
        int    maxVisibleLabels;     // default 500
    } rendering;

    struct Canvas {
        QString defaultTool;         // "Select" / "Pan" / "Zoom"
        QString defaultCrsAuth;      // "EPSG"
        int     defaultCrsCode;      // 4326 (WGS 84)
    } canvas;

    struct Log {
        enum Verbosity { Errors, Warnings, Modelling, Verbose };
        Verbosity uiVerbosity;       // default Modelling
        bool      copyToFile;
        QString   logFilePath;
    } log;

    struct Simulation {
        int     engineThreads;       // 0 = auto
        int     progressTickMs;      // 1000
        bool    autoLoadResults;
    } simulation;

    struct Appearance {
        QString theme;               // "system" / "light" / "dark"
        QString monoFontFamily;
        int     mapLabelPointSize;
    } appearance;

signals:
    void preferenceChanged(const QString &group, const QString &key);
};
```

The main window holds a `QPointer<OpenSWMMVisWorkspace>`-driven
binding that pushes the active project's override table into the
singleton on tab switch (same pattern Slice B uses for
`UnitSystem::setActiveProject`).

##### V.2 Preferences dialog — `PreferencesDialog`

New [include/ui/dialogs/preferencesdialog.h](../include/ui/dialogs/preferencesdialog.h) +
[src/ui/dialogs/preferencesdialog.cpp](../src/ui/dialogs/preferencesdialog.cpp).

`QDialog` with a left-side `QListWidget` category list and a
`QStackedWidget` of pages on the right — macOS Preferences / VSCode
Settings style. Accessed from the menu (Tools → Preferences… on
Linux/Windows, auto-routed to the Application menu on macOS via
`QAction::setMenuRole(PreferencesRole)`). Opens against the app
scope by default with a "Project overrides" toggle at the top of
each page; toggling it on reveals per-key checkboxes next to the
existing controls ("Use project override for this setting").

Pages:

1. **General**
   - Default tool on project open (Select / Pan)
   - Welcome screen on startup (checkbox)
   - Auto-save interval (seconds)
   - Recent files size cap
2. **Canvas & CRS**
   - Default CRS when `.inp` has none (EPSG authority + code)
   - Zoom sensitivity (wheel step multiplier)
   - Show rulers / grid (deferred)
3. **Selection**
   - Click tolerance (px)
   - Drag threshold (px)
   - Clear selection on background click
4. **Rendering**
   - Anti-aliasing (off / on / auto-by-zoom)
   - Label LOD threshold (view-scale m11 minimum)
   - Max labels per frame
5. **Symbology** — project-scope only
   - Per-element-type colour pickers + marker-size spins
   - "Copy to application defaults" button to push a project palette up to app scope
6. **Simulation**
   - Engine threads (0 = auto)
   - Progress tick interval (ms)
   - Auto-load results after run
7. **Logging**
   - UI log verbosity
   - Copy log to file (path + browse)
8. **Plugins** (placeholder for Phase 12.0 plugin registry)

Apply / OK / Cancel buttons at the bottom.
Apply writes immediately (so live-bound UI refreshes);
Cancel discards the dialog's pending diffs. Each changed setting
fires `PreferencesManager::preferenceChanged`; listeners
(`SelectTool` for tolerance, `SWMMLayerItem` for LOD, etc.) read
through the manager's typed accessors.

##### V.3 Migration — existing QSettings keys

`SWMMVis/autoLength`, `SWMMVis::RecentFiles`,
`SWMMVis::ShowWelcomeOnStartup`, `SWMMVis::MainWindow/*` stay in
their current keys (no migration needed); they read through
`PreferencesManager` getters that fall through to the same
`QSettings` group. New keys land under `SWMMVis/Preferences/<group>/<key>`.

Existing scattered hard-coded constants get swapped for manager
reads in one pass:

- `OpenSWMMVisMapToolSelect::m_pixelTol` →
  `PreferencesManager::selection().clickTolerancePx`
- `OpenSWMMVisMapToolSelect::m_dragThreshPx` →
  `dragThresholdPx`
- `SWMMLayerItem::paint` m11 LOD gate →
  `rendering().labelLodM11Min`
- `SimulationRunner` 1 s tick → `simulation().progressTickMs`
- `SWMMVisProjectWindow` default tool (`mSelectTool` vs `mPanTool`)
  → `canvas().defaultTool`

All of the above rebind through `preferenceChanged` so a
Preferences dialog Apply takes effect without a restart.

##### V.4 Project-scope override mechanism

Each `OpenSWMMVisWorkspace` gains a `QMap<QString,QVariant>
m_overrides` keyed as `"group/key"`. `PreferencesManager` reads via:

```cpp
QVariant PreferencesManager::effective(const QString &grp, const QString &key) const {
    if (m_activeProjectOverrides && m_activeProjectOverrides->contains(grp+"/"+key))
        return m_activeProjectOverrides->value(grp+"/"+key);
    return m_qsettings.value("SWMMVis/Preferences/"+grp+"/"+key,
                              compiledDefault(grp, key));
}
```

Serialising the override map is the responsibility of Phase 12's
project-file serializer. Until `.oswp` ships, the override map
exists in-memory only and is lost on close — acceptable for this
slice since the primary user demand is app-scope tuning.

##### V.5 UX touches

- **Search box** at the top of the dialog filters the left-side
  category list by label + key name (`QSortFilterProxyModel` on a
  `QStandardItemModel` with one row per preference).
- **"Reset to defaults"** at the bottom of each page — restores
  everything on the page to its compiled-in default.
- **Per-field indicator**: a small inline icon next to any setting
  that has a non-default value, click to clear back to default
  (matches VSCode's gear icon).

#### ✅ Slice X — `.oswp` sidecar + ProjectSerializer (Phase 12 first cut)

**Motivation.** Slice T's layer / category / object reorderings and a
handful of Slice U / V settings (layer CRS override, canvas extent,
hidden-object set) can't round-trip through the `.inp`. Without a
project file they were lost on close. This slice adds a minimal
JSON sidecar next to each `.inp` that persists exactly what the GUI
needs today.

**What ships:**

- [include/project/projectserializer.h](../include/project/projectserializer.h)
  + [src/project/projectserializer.cpp](../src/project/projectserializer.cpp):
  `ProjectSerializer::saveToFile(oswpPath, pw)` /
  `applyFromFile(oswpPath, pw)` /
  `sidecarPathFor(inpPath)` returning `<basename>.oswp` in the same
  directory. JSON schema versioned (`schemaVersion = 1`); pre-Slice-X
  format (v0 — `{ layers: [{ path: ... }] }`) parsed as a no-op so
  older files don't error out.

  **Relative-path convention (applies to all schema versions ≥ 2):**
  All file-path fields written by `ProjectSerializer` (`"inpPath"`,
  future layer `"path"` entries, `.gpkg` references, etc.) are stored
  as paths **relative to the `.oswp` file's parent directory**. This
  makes the project folder self-contained and shareable — moving or
  copying the folder preserves all references. When saving a new
  project via Save As, the GUI places all companion files (`.inp`,
  `.gpkg`, any auxiliary inputs declared by the active IO plugin) in
  the same directory as the chosen `.oswp` path.

  `ProjectSerializer` exposes two helpers:
  ```cpp
  // Returns path of p relative to the directory containing oswpFile.
  // Falls back to p's absolute path when they are on different volumes.
  static QString toRelativePath(const QString &p, const QString &oswpFile);

  // Resolves a stored path (relative or legacy-absolute) against the
  // directory containing oswpFile.  Absolute paths are returned as-is
  // for backward compatibility with v1 sidecars.
  static QString resolveStoredPath(const QString &stored, const QString &oswpFile);
  ```

  At **save time** every path written to JSON goes through
  `toRelativePath(…, oswpPath)`. At **load time** every path read from
  JSON goes through `resolveStoredPath(…, oswpPath)` — so v1 files
  (which stored absolute paths) continue to work without migration.

- Save path — [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) `onSaveProject` +
  `onSaveProjectAs`: after the `.inp` writes, emit the `.oswp`
  sidecar. Serializer failure logs at Warning — the `.inp` itself
  already saved so the project is recoverable.  When saving a **new
  (untitled) project**, `onSaveProjectAs` places the `.inp` (and any
  `.gpkg` or other engine-declared companion file) in the same
  directory the user chose for the `.oswp`, ensuring all relative
  path references in the sidecar resolve to the same folder.
- Open path — [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) `openSingleINP`:
  after the layer loads, look for `<basename>.oswp` next to the
  `.inp` and `applyFromFile` if present. Missing sidecar is not an
  error.

**v1 schema — what's persisted (absolute `inpPath` — legacy):**

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "inpPath": "/abs/path/to/model.inp",
  "layer": {
    "crsAuthority": "EPSG",
    "crsCode": 26910,
    "categoryOrder": [4, 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10],
    "objectOrder":   { "4": [3, 1, 0, 2, …] },
    "hiddenObjects": ["J1", "C47"]
  },
  "canvas": {
    "crsAuthority": "EPSG",
    "crsCode": 4326,
    "extent": [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax]
  }
}
```

- `categoryOrder` and `objectOrder.N` (where N is the Category
  enum ordinal) drive Slice T persistence.
- `hiddenObjects` drives the Object Browser leaf-checkbox round-trip.
- `canvas.crs` + `canvas.extent` restore the user's working view.

**Shipped extension (2026-05-15) — duplicate-open guard + result-layer round-trip + auto-discover:**

- **Duplicate-open guard** (`openSingleINP`): before creating a new `SWMMVisProjectWindow`,
  scan all MDI sub-windows for an existing project window whose `modelLayer()->modelFilePath()`
  resolves to the same `QFileInfo` as the requested path. If found, activate that window and
  return immediately — no second load, no duplicate window.

- **Result layer serialization** (`projectserializer.cpp`):
  - `serializeSession()` now collects every `SWMMResultsLayer` on the canvas and writes their
    paths as `"resultLayers": ["rel/path/to/model.out", …]` (relative to the `.oswp`) inside
    the session object.
  - `applySession()` reads `"resultLayers"`, resolves each path via `resolveStoredPath`, checks
    the file exists, constructs a `SWMMResultsLayer`, adds it to the canvas (no undo push), and
    calls `openResults()`. Errors are silently swallowed (file may have been moved); the sidecar
    itself still applies successfully.

- **Auto-discover sibling output files** (`openSingleINP`): after the sidecar is applied, if the
  canvas still has no `SWMMResultsLayer` (i.e. the sidecar was absent or had no persisted result
  paths), the code queries `FileFilterRegistry::patternsFor(ResultsRead)` +
  `patternsFor(ResultsWrite)` for glob patterns (e.g. `*.out`), derives the sibling candidate
  `<basename>.<ext>` in the `.inp`'s directory, and loads the first existing match as a
  `SWMMResultsLayer`. Logs "Auto-loaded results: <filename>" at Info level. At most one file is
  loaded automatically (the first pattern match) to avoid flooding the canvas.

**Schema note:** `"resultLayers"` is added to the session object inside `"sessions"[0]`. v1/v2/v3
legacy sidecars omit the key — `applySession` treats its absence as "no result layers to restore"
(no-op), so backward compatibility is preserved.

**Deferred (still open under Phase 12):**

- **Schema v2 — relative-path migration**: bump `schemaVersion` to 2
  and switch `"inpPath"` (and any future file-reference fields) from
  absolute to relative storage. `saveToFile` already calls
  `toRelativePath`; the version bump just formalises the contract.
  `applyFromFile` must handle both: detect absolute paths via
  `QDir::isAbsolutePath` and pass them through unchanged (v1 backward
  compat); resolve relative paths against the sidecar's parent dir.
  New unit test: `relativePath_roundTrip` — save with a relative path,
  reload from a different `cwd`, assert the resolved absolute path
  matches. Schema v2 also standardises that all companion files (`.inp`,
  `.gpkg`, auxiliary engine outputs) land in the same directory as the
  `.oswp` on first save; `onSaveProjectAs` enforces this by placing the
  engine-declared output files next to the chosen sidecar path.
- Project-scope **preference overrides** (Slice V's `m_overrides`
  map on `OpenSWMMVisWorkspace`). Easy to add — bolt on a
  `"preferences": { "Selection/ClickTolerancePx": 30, … }` object
  under root and have `PreferencesManager::effective()` consult it.
  Pending the manager's project-scope wiring.
- **Multi-layer projects** — the schema only covers one SWMM model
  layer per file. Phase 12.1 extends to a `"layers": [...]` array
  and includes GIS imports / WMS / WMTS registrations. All `"path"`
  entries in the `"layers"` array are stored as relative paths
  (relative to the `.oswp` directory), consistent with the
  relative-path convention above.
- **Recent bookmarks**, **simulation history**, **themes** — all
  Phase 12.2+ items.
- **IO plugin registry** (Phase 12.0) — totally untouched; input
  plugins still load via `swmm_engine_open`'s hard-coded path.
- **Old-sidecar cleanup on Save As** — when the user renames via
  Save As, the old `.oswp` is left behind. Fine for now (small JSON
  file); polish later.

**Risks / follow-ups:**

- `setObjectOrder` validates permutations strictly. If the underlying
  SoA changes between save and load (add/remove node), the override
  silently rejects — leaving the category at default order. Not a
  data loss; just a visible revert. A future polish could log a
  warning when that happens.
- The sidecar JSON is git-friendly (small, stable, diffable). Users
  who want to share a project can ship the `.inp` + `.oswp` together.

**Verify:**

1. Open an `.inp`, drag a category in the Object Browser, File → Save.
   Check that `<basename>.oswp` appeared next to the `.inp` with a
   `categoryOrder` array.
2. Close the project, reopen the `.inp` — categories appear in the
   saved order.
3. Change the layer CRS via Properties dialog, Save, close, reopen —
   CRS is restored from the sidecar.
4. Hide an object via Object Browser checkbox, Save, close, reopen —
   the object is still hidden.

#### ✅ Slice Y — New SWMM model: synthetic-`.inp` instantiation + New-Project workflow (first cut, 2026-04-25)

**Motivation.** Today the only way into the app is opening an
existing `.inp`. `File → New Project` currently re-opens the
Welcome tab (stub behaviour from Slice A). Engine-side Slice F
exposed `swmm_node_add` / `swmm_node_pop_last` so the GUI can
mutate an opened model — but there's no path for "start with an
empty model, then build it up". This slice closes that loop:
create a fresh `SWMM_Engine` with legacy-compatible defaults, wire
it into a new `SWMMVisProjectWindow`, and let the user add nodes /
links / subcatchments via the existing map tools, saving out as
`.inp` + `.oswp`.

**Three pieces to the story:**

##### Y.1 Engine-side: a minimum blank-engine primitive

Current engine flow is `create → open(inp, rpt, out) → initialize →
…`. For a new model we need `create → open-empty → initialize` so
the engine is in a valid state with NO nodes / links / etc. and
legacy defaults for OPTIONS. Two ways this can happen:

1. **Preferred — engine `swmm_engine_open_empty(eng)`** that
   skips the input reader and just installs
   defaults-from-`SimulationOptions.hpp`. Needs a ~30-line
   engine-side addition; ties into the Slice U.6 legacy-defaults
   audit (both want the same default matrix).
2. **Fallback — GUI writes a bare-minimum synthetic `.inp`** to
   a temp file (just `[OPTIONS]` + the minimum required blocks)
   and opens that. Works today without engine changes. The temp
   path is renamed to the user's chosen location on Save As.

First cut ships **option 2** (this slice). Engine `swmm_engine_open_empty`
remains a Y.5 follow-up on the engine repo (no engine change required for
the GUI to ship today). The synthetic `.inp` writes the legacy default
matrix from the dialog inputs (`FLOW_UNITS`, `INFILTRATION`,
`FLOW_ROUTING`, `START_*`/`END_*`, plus the boilerplate
`REPORT_STEP` / `WET_STEP` / `DRY_STEP` / `ROUTING_STEP` and `[REPORT]`
defaults).

##### Y.2 GUI state machine — untitled project (shipped)

`SWMMVisProjectWindow` gains:
- `bool mUntitled = false` + `QString mTempInpPath` members.
- `void markUntitled(const QString &tempInpPath)` setter; called by
  `SWMMVis::onNewProject` after `openSingleINP` returns.
- `bool isUntitled() const` getter.
- `updateWindowTitle()` formats as `"Untitled [*]"` while
  `mUntitled` is true (overriding the temp path's basename).
- `save()` short-circuits with the "use Save As" hint when
  `mUntitled` is true; the existing `onSaveProject` slot routes
  through to `onSaveProjectAs()` on that signal.
- `saveAs()` deletes the temp `.inp` on first success, clears
  `mUntitled`, refreshes the title.
- `closeEvent()` deletes the temp file on Discard / no-changes
  paths; cancels the close with an info box if the user picks
  Save on an untitled project (synchronous Save As from inside
  closeEvent is risky — user is told to trigger it manually).
- Recent-files list: `SWMMVis::onNewProject` removes the temp path
  immediately after `openSingleINP` registers it, so untitled
  projects don't pollute Recent.

##### Y.3 New-Project dialog (shipped)

Single-page dialog
([include/ui/dialogs/newprojectdialog.h](../include/ui/dialogs/newprojectdialog.h)
+ [.cpp](../src/ui/dialogs/newprojectdialog.cpp)) driven from
`File → New` (Welcome-tab button still wires through
`SWMMVis::onNewProject`). Fields:

- **Name** — becomes `[TITLE]` in the synthetic `.inp`.
- **Flow units** — CFS / GPM / MGD / CMS / LPS / MLD → bakes into
  the `.inp`'s `FLOW_UNITS` (no `swmm_options_set` round-trip
  needed; engine reads from the file).
- **Infiltration model** — HORTON / MODIFIED_HORTON / GREEN_AMPT
  / MODIFIED_GREEN_AMPT / CURVE_NUMBER.
- **Flow routing** — STEADY / KINWAVE / DYNWAVE.
- **Simulation window** — `QDateTimeEdit` pair, defaulting to
  legacy SWMM5 (Jan 1 2002 00:00 → 06:00). Validated on accept.
- **CRS** — read-only line + `Choose…` button → `CRSSelectionDialog`.
  Default seeded from `PreferencesManager::defaultCrs*`; falls back
  to `EPSG:4326` when prefs are unset.

**Template** (Blank / Residential / Combined Sewer) deferred to a
Y-follow-up — needs bundled template `.inp`s under
`resources/templates/`, separate from this slice's scope.

The dialog has no Apply button — engine creation happens when the
user clicks OK and the synthetic `.inp` is written + opened.

##### Y.4 Map-tool wiring for empty canvases

Current `MapToolAddNode` assumes there are ALREADY nodes (for
snapping to endpoints, link auto-length). An empty canvas needs:

- Add-node tools draw on empty scene (checked — no regression needed
  since the SoA is allowed to be empty).
- Canvas extent starts at a sensible default (EPSG:4326 world
  bounds if CRS is geographic; a 1-km square centred on origin
  for projected CRSes). Users add the first node and the extent
  auto-fits.
- Save As prompts when the user tries to close an untitled project
  with unsaved work; offers "Save / Discard / Cancel".

##### Y.5 Follow-up: promote option 1 (engine `open_empty`)

Once the engine-side change lands, swap the temp-inp path for a
direct `swmm_engine_open_empty(eng)` call. Eliminates the temp
file round-trip. Tracked alongside Slice U.6 (legacy defaults
audit) since both touch `SimulationOptions.hpp` defaults.

##### Files (this slice)

- [include/swmmvisprojectwindow.h](../include/swmmvisprojectwindow.h)
  + [src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp](../src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp)
  — `mUntitled` flag, `mTempInpPath`, `markUntitled()`,
  `isUntitled()`, title formatter, save/closeEvent updates.
- [include/ui/dialogs/newprojectdialog.h](../include/ui/dialogs/newprojectdialog.h)
  + [.cpp](../src/ui/dialogs/newprojectdialog.cpp) — new dialog.
- [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) — `onNewProject` rewritten
  (was a stub showing the Welcome tab); anonymous-namespace
  `synthesizeBlankInp()` helper.
- [CMakeLists.txt](../CMakeLists.txt) — `newprojectdialog.{h,cpp}`
  added to `PROJECT_SOURCES`.

##### Files (deferred follow-ups)

- **resources/templates/** — `blank.inp`, `residential.inp`,
  `combined-sewer.inp` bundled; accessed via `QResource`. Adds the
  Template combo back to the dialog.
- **Engine-side Y.5** — `src/engine/core/openswmm_engine_impl.cpp`
  in `openswmm.engine`: new `SWMM_ENGINE_API int
  swmm_engine_open_empty(SWMM_Engine)`. Replaces the temp-file
  round-trip with a direct in-memory init.

##### Verify

- File → New Project → dialog opens → defaults (CFS, HORTON,
  DYNWAVE, EPSG:4326) are pre-selected.
- OK creates a project window titled "Untitled *". Canvas is
  blank at a sensible extent.
- Select Add Junction from toolbar, click on canvas → a node
  appears; the ObjectBrowser lists one Junction.
- File → Save prompts for a path; typing `newmodel.inp` saves
  the `.inp` + `newmodel.oswp` sidecar; title updates to
  `newmodel`; dirty marker clears.
- Reopen `newmodel.inp` — the single node survives.

##### Risks / follow-ups

- **Engine default drift**: the audit the GUI does today to match
  legacy defaults might not perfectly match what the engine picks
  internally. Keep a small "what we wrote" map and re-assert after
  `swmm_engine_open_empty` returns.
- **Temp-file cleanup**: the fallback path creates a temp `.inp`
  that must be deleted on project-window close if `m_untitled` is
  still true (user closed without saving). Wire into the close
  handler with a confirmation dialog.
- **Multi-project templates**: the first cut bundles three `.inp`
  templates. Long-term these should move to a user-extensible
  directory (`~/.config/SWMMVis/templates/`) so teams can add
  standard starting points.

### Demo prep (2026-04-26) — off-plan

User pulled forward demo work outside the recommended sequence. Items
landed:

- **CRS hard-sync** between SWMM model layer and project canvas: when
  `SWMMModelLayer::srsChanged` fires, the project window drags the
  canvas via `MapCanvas::setCanvasSRS` + `zoomToFullExtent`. Connected
  before `addLayer` so it runs before MapCanvas's per-layer
  `srsChanged` listener — the canvas SRS is updated first, then the
  layer's `refreshScene + zoomToFullExtent` runs against the correct
  canvas CRS. Removes the old "layer reprojected, view stuck at old
  coordinates" drift. Other (non-SWMM) layers reproject on-the-fly
  via the existing `applyCRSInternal → onCanvasCRSChanged` fan-out.
- **File → New simplified**: `NewProjectDialog::exec()` no longer
  blocks the new-project flow. `SWMMVis::onNewProject` now writes a
  synthetic `.inp` with hard-coded legacy defaults (CFS / HORTON /
  DYNWAVE / Jan 1 2002 → 06:00) and routes through `openSingleINP`;
  the layer adopts the `PreferencesManager` default CRS via
  `loadModel`, the canvas follows via the hard-sync, no GUI
  interruption. The `NewProjectDialog` class stays in the codebase
  for a future "New From Template…" entry.
- **Dead `onSetLayerCRS` slot** removed (declared, defined, never
  wired — confused readers).
- **2D module as a project toggle** in the Simulation Options dialog:
  new "Modules" group on the Models tab with **1D Hydraulics
  (always-on)** + **2D Surface Routing (CVODE)** checkbox. Toggle
  enables/disables the existing "2D Surface Routing" tab so the
  parameters are previewable but uneditable when off. State persists
  per-`.inp` under `QSettings: SWMMVis/Project/<inpPath>/Module2DEnabled`.
  Compile-time gate: when `OPENSWMM_HAS_2D` is undefined (SUNDIALS
  not available in the current vcpkg manifest), the checkbox is
  disabled with a tooltip pointing at `-DOPENSWMM_BUILD_2D=ON +
  SUNDIALS`. Engine 2D code paths stay opt-in.
- **Default option values audited** against the legacy SWMM-GUI
  (`SWMM-GUI/Epaswmm5/Doptions.pas`, `objprops.txt`,
  `Uupdate.pas`). Current `readFromEngine` fallbacks already match
  the legacy factory defaults: `INFILTRATION=HORTON`,
  `FLOW_ROUTING=DYNWAVE`, `SURCHARGE_METHOD=EXTRAN`,
  `FORCE_MAIN_EQUATION=H-W`, `NORMAL_FLOW_LIMITED=BOTH`,
  `INERTIAL_DAMPING=PARTIAL`, `MAX_TRIALS=8`,
  `HEAD_TOLERANCE=0.0015`, `LAT_FLOW_TOL=5%`, `SYS_FLOW_TOL=5%`,
  steps `REPORT_STEP=900s` / `WET_STEP=300s` / `DRY_STEP=3600s` /
  `ROUTING_STEP=30s`. No changes needed.

**Demo-blocker bug logged 2026-04-26**:

- **Shapefile + raster layers don't render when loaded** — user-reported
  during the 2D mesh discussion. Add Vector / Add Raster paths place
  the layer on the layer tree but the canvas stays blank. Suspected:

  for the 2026-04-26 demo** — the mesh-generation flow needs working

**Visualisation / theming layer (next plan expansion):** the existing
[Slice AC](#) sketch ("Animation + theming") only listed
animation-toolbar wiring. For the demo the visualisation surface
needs more depth: per-layer style editor (color ramp, opacity,
stroke), per-attribute theming for SWMM objects (depth / head /
flow heatmap), and a 2D mesh-specific theme that follows the same

controller), AC.2 (Per-layer style editor), AC.3 (Theme registry +

**Follow-ups recorded for after the demo:**

#### ⏳ Slice Z — Attribute tables + SQL-like query (original spec)

**Motivation.** The legacy GUI's table reports (table-by-object,
table-by-variable) and its query dialog are the two surfaces users
reach for when "click on the map" doesn't scale. Today the new GUI
has only the read-only Attribute Panel showing one selected object
at a time. This slice adds:

1. A persistent **Tables** dock with a `QTableView` of model rows.
2. Three driving sources for that view:
   - **SWMM attribute table** (per element type — Junctions, Conduits,
     Subcatchments, etc.). Backed by the layer's SoA + identify
     attributes.
   - **Feature-layer attribute table** (any `GISVectorLayer` — exposes
     OGR feature attributes via GDAL).
   - **Tabular file layer** (CSV / TSV / Excel uploaded as a non-spatial
     "table layer"). Read via QXlsx or csv parser; new layer kind
     `TabularDataLayer` so it appears in the Layer Tree without
     producing scene items.
3. A SQL-like **query bar** above the table for filtering on the
   underlying attributes.
4. **Selection ops**: New Selection / Add to Selection / Remove from
   Selection / Intersect with Selection / Invert — operating on the
   filtered row set.

##### Z.1 — Table dock + view + Cross-view MVC

- New `AttributeTablePanel` (QDockWidget) holding a `QTableView`
  driven by category-specific `QAbstractItemModel` subclasses
  (e.g. `SWMMAttributeTableModel<Category>`,
  `OGRFeatureAttributeTableModel`,
  `TabularDataModel`). All three implement the same row interface so
  the dock can host any of them via a category combo at the top.
- Cross-view selection: the table's `QItemSelectionModel` is bound
  to the project window's `SelectionManager` (Slice E). Two-way
  sync — picking 50 rows in the table highlights them on the
  canvas, and rubber-band-selecting on the canvas scrolls the table
  to the first match and highlights the rows.
- View toolbar: **Show selected only** toggle, **Zoom to selected**
  button, **Export to CSV** button.

##### Z.2 — SQL-like query bar (shipped 2026-05-11)

- New module
  [include/core/queryparser.h](../include/core/queryparser.h) +
  [src/core/queryparser.cpp](../src/core/queryparser.cpp) — pure
  Qt, recursive-descent.  Supports `< <= = != > >= AND OR NOT
  LIKE IN`, parenthesised sub-expressions, `[bracket]` /
  `"quoted"` identifiers (so column keys with spaces like
  `[Invert elev]` work), `'string'` literals, numeric values.
  18-test unit suite at
  [tests/unit/test_queryparser.cpp](../tests/unit/test_queryparser.cpp)
  covers each operator + composition + LIKE wildcards + IN list +
  missing-field semantics.
- New `FilteringProxy` subclass of `QSortFilterProxyModel` inside
  [src/ui/panels/attributetablepanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/attributetablepanel.cpp)
  composes the existing "show selected only" regex filter with a
  query predicate: a row passes when both filters pass.
- Query bar UI: line-edit + Apply / Clear buttons + status label
  ("`47 of 1205 matched`" / `Error col N: …`).  Enter in the line
  edit triggers Apply.  Parse errors paint the line edit pink and
  surface the column / message in the status label.  Switching
  categories clears the query automatically (column keys change).
- Future Z.3 selection ops feed off the matched row set, not the
  full table — same predicate, applied to the full row population.

##### Z.3 — Selection ops (shipped 2026-05-11)

Five `QPushButton`s on a "Selection:" row above the query bar:

| Button       | Effect                                              | How              |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| New          | Replace `SelectionManager` with matched refs        | `select(refs, Replace)`    |
| Add          | Union matched refs into selection                   | `select(refs, Add)`        |
| Remove       | Subtract matched refs from selection                | `select(refs, Subtract)`   |
| Intersect    | Keep only refs in both matched ∩ selection          | panel computes ∩ → `Replace` |
| Invert       | Replace with (all in category) \ selection          | panel computes \ → `Replace` |

Implementation in
[src/ui/panels/attributetablepanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/attributetablepanel.cpp):

- `matchedRefs()` walks `m_model` (source rows, not the proxy-
  filtered subset) and evaluates the current Z.2 query predicate
  against each row's identify-map.  Empty query == every row in
  the current category matches.  Bad-query parse error == empty
  set (so a malformed query is a no-op rather than a surprise).
- `allCategoryRefs()` short-cut for the Invert op.
- Each button binds to one slot that calls
  `SelectionManager::select(refs, mode)`.  No engine round-trip;
  selection changes ripple through the existing E/O/S cross-view
  binding (canvas highlights + Object Browser + Attribute Table
  rows all flash yellow together).

Notes:

- **No new `SelectionManager::Mode`** was needed.  Intersect /
  Invert are pure set operations done panel-side; the manager
  receives the final ref set with `Replace`.  Keeps the bus API
  small.
- The buttons operate on the **full population** (source-model
  rows) not the **visible** subset (proxy-filtered).  So an
  un-applied "show selected only" filter doesn't change the input
  set of the op — exactly what the spec demanded.
- An empty query + **New** is the natural "Select all
  Junctions" — discoverable via empty-query semantics, no
  dedicated button needed.

##### Z.4 — Tabular file uploads (shipped 2026-05-11)

**Z.4.1 — `TabularDataLayer`**: new layer subclass at
[include/layers/tabulardatalayer.h](../include/layers/tabulardatalayer.h)
+ [.cpp](../src/layers/tabulardatalayer.cpp).  Inherits
`OpenSWMMVisLayer` with `layerType() == SWMMTabularDataLayer`
(the enum value was already declared but un-instantiated until
this slice).  Stores `QStringList m_headers` + `QVector<QVariantMap>
m_rows`.  `render()` and `populateScene()` are explicit no-ops —
the layer participates in the Layer Tree (visibility / order /
properties) but produces no scene items.

CSV / TSV loading is RFC-4180-ish, with double-quote field
escaping and CRLF / LF tolerance.  Numeric columns are auto-
promoted (failed-parse cells stay strings), so the Z.2 query
predicate sees the right types without manual coercion.  XLSX
short-circuits with "QXlsx not yet enabled" — landing it is a
plug-in scope question, not core engine work.

**Z.4.2 — `File → Add Delimetered Data` action wired**:
[forms/swmmvis.ui](../forms/swmmvis.ui) had `actionAddDelimeteredData`
declared but disconnected.  Slice Z.4 wires it to a new
`SWMMVis::onAddTableLayer` slot that:

1. Opens `QFileDialog` filtered via `FileFilterRegistry`'s
   `TabularRead` kind (CSV / TSV / xlsx).
2. Constructs `TabularDataLayer` and calls `loadFromFile(path)`.
3. On success, adds the layer to the active canvas (which routes
   through `LayerTreePanel` so visibility / order UI gains the
   new entry automatically).
4. On failure, surfaces the loader's error in a QMessageBox so the
   user knows what's wrong with the file rather than getting a
   silent no-op.

**Z.4.3 — Attribute Table panel integration**: deferred to a
follow-up cut.  Today the loaded TabularDataLayer appears in the
Layer Tree but the AttributeTablePanel's category combo only
surfaces SWMM categories.  When the next round lands, the panel
will need:

- A polymorphic source-model holder so the proxy can swap between
  `SWMMAttributeTableModel` and a new `TabularDataTableModel`.
- Category-combo entries grouped by source: SWMM (Junctions,
  Conduits, …) and "Table layers" (loaded CSV / TSV files).
- Delegate installation gated on SWMM source (no engine setters
  for tabular layers — they're inert observation data).
- Change-Type / cross-view selection short-circuited on tabular
  source.

##### Z.5 — Inline editing + shared edit delegates (original DRAFT, awaiting approval)

**Motivation.** Z.1 displays attributes; users expect to **edit**
them in place.  Today the only editing surface is the
AttributePanel (Property Browser), which inherits QPropertyModel's
auto-generated spinbox/checkbox/line-edit set — no enum dropdowns,
no name-reference pickers, no compound sub-editors.  Z.5 fixes that
gap for **simple attributes** (those the engine already exposes a
`swmm_*_set_*` setter for); compound editors (inflows, RDII RTK,
DWF, patterns, curves, timeseries) move to Slice AG.

**Architecture decision (confirmed with user 2026-05-11):** both
the Attribute Table and the Property Browser bind to a shared set
of edit delegates so the two surfaces stay in lockstep.  One
codebase, two presentations.

###### Z.5.1 — Shared edit-delegate module

New files:
- `include/ui/panels/attributedelegates.h` + `.cpp` — pure-Qt
  delegates with no engine deps; the schema (which delegate to
  install on which column) lives in `SWMMAttributeTableModel`.

Delegate set (first cut):

| Delegate                   | Editor              | Use cases                                              |
|----------------------------|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `NumericDelegate`          | `QDoubleSpinBox`    | invertElev, maxDepth, length, roughness, slope, …      |
| `IntegerDelegate`          | `QSpinBox`          | maxTrials, threads, vertex counts (read-only)          |
| `EnumDelegate`             | `QComboBox`         | NodeType, OutfallType, LinkType, ConduitShape, …       |
| `NameRefDelegate`          | `QComboBox` + "…"   | Timeseries name, Pattern name, Curve name, Outlet node |
| `BoolDelegate`             | `QCheckBox`         | flapGate, ignoreLid, …                                 |
| `ButtonCellDelegate`       | "Edit…" QPushButton | Inflows / DWF / RDII (delegates to Slice AG sub-dialogs) |

`EnumDelegate` is configurable: at install time it takes a
`QList<QPair<QString /*label*/, QVariant /*data*/>>` and shows the
combo accordingly.  Engine enums (`SWMM_NodeType`, `SWMM_LinkType`,
`SWMM_OutfallType`, etc.) are mirrored as static const tables in
`include/ui/panels/attributedelegates.h` so the model can pick the
right one without dragging in the engine SDK headers.

`NameRefDelegate` populates its combo from the layer's registry
of named objects (timeseries, patterns, curves) plus a literal
"" entry for "no reference".  The trailing "…" button opens the
matching Slice AH editor dialog (when AH lands) or, for now, a
read-only listing.

###### Z.5.2 — Editable column schema on `SWMMAttributeTableModel`

Today the schema is just `{keys, labels}`.  Z.5 extends it to:

```cpp
struct ColumnSpec {
    QString    key;          ///< identifyByName-map key
    QString    label;        ///< Header label
    EditorKind editor;       ///< Numeric / Integer / Enum / NameRef / Bool / Button / ReadOnly
    QString    setter;       ///< swmm_*_set_* function name (empty == read-only)
    QString    getter;       ///< swmm_*_get_* function name (when distinct from key)
    QVariantList enumValues; ///< For Enum: pre-baked label/data pairs
    double     minValue = -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
    double     maxValue =  std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
    int        decimals = 4;
};
```

`SWMMAttributeTableModel`:
- `flags(idx)` returns `Qt::ItemIsEditable` for columns with non-empty
  `setter` (and the row's underlying object is editable per engine
  lifecycle).
- `setData(idx, val, EditRole)` resolves the column spec, validates
  the value (`minValue` / `maxValue` clamp, type cast), calls the
  engine setter via a function-pointer table, returns true on
  `SWMM_OK`.  On failure logs to the message dock and reverts the
  visible cell.
- Cache invalidation: writes invalidate `m_rowCacheValid[row]` so
  the next `data()` re-fetches via `identifyByName`.

###### Z.5.3 — AttributePanel (Property Browser) hookup

The AttributePanel today uses QPropertyModel with `setEditTriggers
(AllEditTriggers)` — every `Q_PROPERTY` is auto-editable.  Z.5
replaces the generic auto-editors with the same delegates the table
uses:

- For each per-type adapter (e.g. `JunctionPropertyAdapter`, which
  Slice AG will introduce in full), the property tree installs
  delegates per-property using the same `ColumnSpec` schema.
- A small `AttributeDelegateInstaller` helper walks the tree once
  on `setObject(ref)` and matches delegates to property names.
- For properties driven by engine getters that already exist (e.g.
  `Q_PROPERTY(double invertElev …)`), no engine change is needed —
  the delegate's `setModelData` calls the same Q_PROPERTY setter the
  QPropertyModel was already using.

###### Z.5.4 — Attribute coverage (no engine changes needed)

Wave-1 attributes that become inline-editable in both surfaces:

- **Junction**: invertElev, maxDepth, initDepth, surchargeDepth,
  pondedArea.
- **Outfall**: outfallType (enum), fixedStage, tidalCurve (NameRef),
  stageTimeseries (NameRef), flapGate, routeTo.
- **Storage**: maxDepth, initDepth, surchargeDepth, pondedArea,
  evapFactor, storageCurve (NameRef), functionalCoeffs (3 numeric).
- **Divider**: maxDepth, initDepth, dividerType (enum), divertedLink
  (NameRef), cutoffFlow, weirCoeff, weirHt, weirCd.
- **Conduit**: length, roughness, initialFlow, maxFlow, offset1,
  offset2, flapGate, culvertCode (enum).
- **Pump**: pumpCurve (NameRef), initialStatus (enum: ON/OFF),
  startDepth, shutoffDepth.
- **Orifice / Weir / Outlet**: type (enum), offsets, discharge
  coefficients, flapGate, geometry parameters.
- **Subcatchment**: area, imperv%, width, slope, NLat, NImperv,
  NPerv, SImperv, SPerv, pctZero, raingage (NameRef), outlet
  (NameRef).
- **Rain gage**: format (enum), interval, SCF, dataSource (enum),
  timeseries (NameRef), filename + station + units.

Each listed attribute already has a `swmm_*_set_*` C-API setter in
the engine — no engine work required.

###### Z.5.5 — UX details

- **Validation**: NumericDelegate enforces `[minValue, maxValue]`
  at commit; out-of-range edits show a tooltip with the bounds
  and revert.
- **Atomic edits**: each cell commit is a single engine call; no
  multi-cell transactions in this slice.  Z.3 selection-ops still
  feed the bulk-modify pipeline (a future small slice) but bulk
  edit is **not** in Z.5.
- **Undo**: each commit pushes a tiny `EditCommand` onto the
  project's `QUndoStack` (the same one Slice T uses for category
  reorder).  Undo restores the previous value via the inverse
  engine setter.
- **Concurrency with running simulation**: the model blocks edits
  when the engine is in `SWMM_STATE_RUNNING` (CHECK_EDITABLE macro
  on the engine side); the table dims editable columns and shows
  a "Simulation running — pause to edit" tooltip.

#### ✅ Slice AA — File format plugin registry + Save As submenu + Plugins dialog (first cut, 2026-04-25)

**Motivation.** Today Save / Save As only writes `.inp` (with the
new `.oswp` sidecar from Slice X). Open accepts `.inp` and `.oswp`.
The legacy GUI exports to `.map`, `.emf`, `.dxf`, hot-start files,
and supports user-installable I/O plugins. The engine ships a
plugin SDK (Phase 12.0). This slice exposes it through the GUI:

1. A `FileFilterRegistry` that aggregates every reader / writer
   plugin's declared filters by **kind** (Input, Results,
   Project, Vector, Raster, Tabular, Map-Export, Hot-Start).
2. Save / Save As filter list driven by writers for the **active
   object kind** (e.g. saving a project shows "Project (`.oswp`)
   *.oswp" + every writer plugin that handles "Project").
3. Open filter list driven by readers across all kinds, defaulting
   to "All supported" with a category breakdown below.
4. A **Plugins** dialog (Tools → Plugins…) that lists installed
   plugins with enable / disable / remove + an **Add Plugin**
   button that file-picks a `.dylib` / `.dll` / `.so` and copies
   it into `~/.config/SWMMVis/plugins/`.

##### AA.1 — Registry (shipped)

The placeholder
[include/plugins/filefilterregistry.h](../include/plugins/filefilterregistry.h)
became a concrete `FileFilterRegistry` singleton. **Implementation
diverged from the original sketch**: rather than a standalone
GUI-side `FileFilter::Kind` enum, the registry now layers a GUI
`FilterKind` enum over the engine's pre-existing
`openswmm::PluginRole`. Engine-backed kinds proxy
`openswmm::discover_all_filters()`; GUI-only kinds (Project, Vector,
Raster, Tabular, MapExport) come from a built-in static table.

```cpp
namespace openswmmvis {

enum class FilterKind {
    InputRead,        // engine-backed (PluginRole::INPUT_READ)
    ResultsRead,      // GUI-only — engine writes, GUI reads .out
    ResultsWrite,     // engine-backed (PluginRole::OUTPUT_WRITE)
    ReportWrite,      // engine-backed (PluginRole::REPORT_WRITE)
    StateRead,        // engine-backed (PluginRole::STATE_READ)
    StateWrite,       // engine-backed (PluginRole::STATE_WRITE)
    ProjectRead, ProjectWrite,        // GUI-only (.oswp)
    VectorRead, RasterRead,           // GUI-only (GIS)
    TabularRead,                      // GUI-only (.csv/.tsv)
    MapExportWrite                    // GUI-only (.png/.svg/.dxf)
};

class FileFilterRegistry : public QObject {
    Q_OBJECT
public:
    struct Entry {
        QString     description; QStringList patterns;
        FilterKind  kind;        QString     pluginId;   // empty = built-in
        bool        canRead = false; bool canWrite = false;
        bool        enabled = true;  // for AA-2 disable feature
    };
    static FileFilterRegistry *instance();
    QString     filterFor(FilterKind kind) const;
    QStringList patternsFor(FilterKind kind) const;
    QString     filterFor(openswmm::PluginRole role) const;   // back-compat shim
    QStringList patternsFor(openswmm::PluginRole role) const;
    QList<Entry> allEntries() const;
    QList<Entry> entriesFor(FilterKind kind) const;
    void         rescan();
    static const char *kindLabel(FilterKind kind) noexcept;
    static bool        isWriteKind(FilterKind kind) noexcept;
signals:
    void entriesChanged();
};

} // namespace openswmmvis
```

Built-in filters registered at startup (see
[src/plugins/filefilterregistry.cpp](../src/plugins/filefilterregistry.cpp) `registerBuiltinFilters()`):

- ProjectRead/Write: `*.oswp`
- ResultsRead: `*.out`
- VectorRead: ESRI Shapefile, GeoJSON / JSON, GeoPackage, KML, GML
- RasterRead: GeoTIFF, ERDAS Imagine, ESRI ASCII Grid, NetCDF, HDF
- TabularRead: CSV, TSV (`.xlsx` deferred to QXlsx-backed module)
- MapExportWrite: PNG, SVG, DXF, EMF, EPA SWMM Map

Engine-backed filters arrive via `discover_all_filters()` (existing
mechanism; covers `DefaultInputPlugin` → `*.inp`,
`GeoPackagePluginInfo` → `*.gpkg`, plus any third-party engine
plugins).

**Why this shape, not the standalone `FileFilter::Kind` enum from
the original plan?** The engine SDK already has `PluginRole` with
five values (INPUT_READ / OUTPUT_WRITE / REPORT_WRITE / STATE_READ /
STATE_WRITE), and three call sites in
[swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) already used it via
`filterFor(PluginRole)`. Layering the GUI enum on top keeps the
engine surface unchanged, gives back-compat shims to existing
callers, and adds the GUI-only kinds without touching cross-repo
code.

##### AA.2 — Plugin discovery (deferred to AA-2)

GUI-side discovery of `~/.config/SWMMVis/plugins/` and
`<bundle>/Resources/plugins/` for an `IGuiFileFilterPlugin`
interface stays open. Engine plugins are discovered today via
`openswmm::discover_all_filters()` and surface in the registry
automatically. AA-2 will add:

- A new `IGuiFileFilterPlugin` Qt-side interface (separate from
  engine `IInputPlugin` / `IOutputPlugin`) for filters the engine
  doesn't care about (CSV observed-data readers, custom raster
  drivers, etc.).
- `~/.config/SWMMVis/plugins/` + `<bundle>/Resources/plugins/`
  scan at startup; load via `QPluginLoader`.
- ABI-version int validated at load (`extern "C"` factory + plain
  POD `init()` struct) to keep the symbol surface stable.
- Errors during load surface in the Message Log dock and in the
  Plugins dialog's status column.

#### ✅ Slice AA-2 — Plugin icon, GeoPackage by default, Save As INP writers, Output/Report plugin preferences (2026-05-01)

> **⚠ Superseded in part by Slice AA-4 (2026-05-11):** The `Preferences → Output` page and the four `PreferencesManager` `Output` group accessors (`defaultReportPluginId`, `defaultOutputPluginId`, `defaultReportFilePath`, `defaultOutputFilePath`) were removed. Output/report path overrides are now per-project in the SimulationOptions Files tab. Only the app-scope Preferences content from this slice remains.

**Motivation.** Four polish / usability improvements that build
directly on the Slice AA plugin registry:

1. **Plugin menu-item icon** — `actionPlugins` in the Tools menu
   showed no icon; the existing `images/plugin.svg` asset was not
   registered in the QRC.  
   → Added `Plugin` alias to `resources/swmmvis.qrc` and wired an
   `<iconset>` block onto `actionPlugins` in `forms/swmmvis.ui`.

2. **GeoPackage compiled by default** — `FetchOpenSWMMEngine.cmake`
   previously left `OPENSWMM_WITH_GEOPACKAGE OFF`. The engine's
   GeoPackage plugin registers `*.gpkg` under `InputRead` and
   `ResultsWrite` via `discover_all_filters()`, so turning it on
   makes the GeoPackage format appear automatically in:
   - **File → Open** (InputRead filter)
   - **File → Save As → Input File…** (InputRead write-capable entries)
   - **File → Save As → Project…** (InputRead write-capable entries)
   - **Tools → Plugins…** (all entries table)
   - **Preferences → Output** plugin combos  
   → `set(OPENSWMM_WITH_GEOPACKAGE ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)` added
   to `cmake/FetchOpenSWMMEngine.cmake`.

3. **Save As INP / GeoPackage** — `File → Save As → Input File…`
   (`onSaveAsInputFile`) already uses
   `FileFilterRegistry::filterFor(InputRead)` for its `QFileDialog`
   filter. With GeoPackage compiled in the engine, the filter list
   now includes `GeoPackage (*.gpkg)` alongside the default
   `SWMM Input File (*.inp)`. The engine's plugin handles the
   actual write when the user picks `.gpkg`.  
   No new code needed; the existing AA.3 integration
   (`filterFor(InputRead)`) covers it automatically once the plugin
   is compiled in.

4. **Preferences → Output page** — a new page was added to
   `PreferencesDialog` (Preferences → Output) that lets users choose:
   - **Report format** — combo of `FilterKind::ReportWrite` entries
     from the registry; "Default (.rpt text report)" is always first.
   - **Report file path** — optional absolute path override (blank =
     derive sibling file from the `.inp` path using the selected
     plugin's extension). Browse button opens a `QFileDialog` with
     the `ReportWrite` filter.
   - **Results output format** — combo of `FilterKind::ResultsWrite`
     entries; "Default (.out binary output)" is always first.
   - **Output file path** — optional absolute path override. Browse
     button uses the `ResultsWrite` filter.
   
   Selections are persisted to `QSettings` via four new
   `PreferencesManager` accessors:
   `defaultReportPluginId` / `defaultOutputPluginId` /
   `defaultReportFilePath` / `defaultOutputFilePath`
   (group: `Output`, keys under `SWMMVis/Preferences/Output/`).

   `SWMMVis::onRunSimulation` was updated to honour these preferences
   when deriving the `rptPath` / `outPath` for `SimulationRunner`:
   - If an override path is set, it is used verbatim.
   - Otherwise, the extension is derived from the first matching
     pattern of the selected plugin entry (falling back to `.rpt`
     / `.out` when no plugin is selected or no matching entry
     exists in the registry).

##### Writer / Container combos (shipped 2026-05-10)

The original AA-3.5 combo-driven design landed on top of the MVP
table editor:

- **Three writer combos** at the top of the Files tab — Input /
  Output / Report.  Each combo is populated from the
  `FileFilterRegistry` entries that advertise the matching
  `FilterKind` (`InputRead` + `canWrite` for Input;
  `ResultsWrite` for Output; `ReportWrite` for Report).  The
  first item is always "(built-in: …)" with an empty
  `pluginId` — the engine default.
- **"Single container" checkbox** — enabled only when the chosen
  Input writer plugin advertises all three of `INPUT_READ`,
  `OUTPUT_WRITE`, `REPORT_WRITE` (detected via the engine's
  `discover_plugins_by_id()` grouped facade).  Toggling on forces
  the Output and Report combos to the Input plugin's id and
  disables them.  Toggling off re-enables them at their previous
  values.
- **Read** — on dialog open, `readWriterCombosFromEngine()` walks
  the engine's `[PLUGINS]` rows and, for each role, picks the
  first plugin id that advertises that role per
  `discover_plugins_by_id()`.  Single-container is auto-checked
  when all three resolve to the same non-empty id.
- **Write** — on Apply, `writeWriterCombosToEngine()` runs **after**
  the `[PLUGINS]` table editor; it is **additive-only** (uses
  `swmm_plugin_set` to ensure the chosen plugin ids exist as
  `[PLUGINS]` rows but never removes rows).  This means the table
  view stays the canonical way to delete a plugin row, and the
  combos can never destroy user-managed args.  Documented on the
  Files tab.
- The MVP `[PLUGINS]` table from the earlier AA-3.5 cut stays as
  the power-user view immediately below the combos.

With this, the original user-stated requirement —
*"individual SWMM instances may be saved to different formats"* and
*"GeoPackage can contain both input, report, and output"* — is now
fully wired through the GUI.  Picking GeoPackage as the Input
writer enables the Single Container toggle; checking it routes
input + output + report into the same `.gpkg`.

##### Multi-row hot-start + `[FILES]` relative paths (shipped 2026-05-11)

The two follow-ups from the previous round both landed:

- **Multi-row `SAVE HOTSTART`** — `FilesSpec::hotstart_save_path` /
  `_datetime` was lifted to `std::vector<HotstartSaveEntry>` with
  `{path, datetime}` per entry.  Parser appends per row; writer emits
  one line per entry, with the optional `MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS` tail
  when `datetime > 0`.  The C API's singular
  `HOTSTART_SAVE_PATH` / `_DATETIME` keys are now slot-0 sugar
  (clearing both removes the entry), and a new read-only
  `HOTSTART_SAVE_COUNT` key reports the vector size.  Three new tests
  in `test_engine_files_section.cpp` cover the parser append,
  round-trip write-grep, and slot-0 clear semantics.
- **`[FILES]` relative paths** — `SimulationOptionsDialog::writeFilesSectionToEngine`
  now routes absolute path strings through
  `ProjectSerializer::toRelativePath(rawPath, inpPath)` before
  calling `swmm_files_set`.  Relative paths pass through unchanged
  (the engine resolves them against the `.inp` directory at run
  time, legacy behaviour).  Result: typing an absolute path in a
  Files-tab field stores it relative so moving the project folder
  keeps the references valid.
- **GUI smoke-test** — app launched cleanly after the changes
  (basemap tiles load, no errors / crashes in the run log).

**Motivation.** Five concrete defects/gaps in today's IO:

1. **Save As → Input File → `*.gpkg` silently corrupts the file.**
   `SWMMVisProjectWindow::saveAs(path)` unconditionally calls
   `swmm_model_write(engine, path)` which only writes `.inp`-format
   text. Picking GeoPackage in the filter writes `.inp` content into
   a file with `.gpkg` extension. ([src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp:425](../src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp#L425))
2. **`.oswp` paths are still absolute.** Slice X promised v2
   relative-path schema (`toRelativePath` / `resolveStoredPath`
   helpers) but only the *intent* shipped — the helpers don't exist
   in [src/project/projectserializer.cpp](../src/project/projectserializer.cpp);
   schema v3 still writes `inpPath` as absolute. Projects can't be
   moved/zipped/shared as a folder.
3. **No project-level multi-instance concept.** One
   `SWMMVisProjectWindow` = one `.inp` = one `.oswp`. The user-stated
   model is "a project = one or more SWMM instances + GUI state",
   each instance independently dirty-tracked and savable. **File →
   Save Project** today saves only the active window.
4. **No per-instance IO overrides.** PreferencesManager carries
   app-scope `defaultReportFilePath` / `defaultOutputFilePath` /
   `defaultReportPluginId` / `defaultOutputPluginId` (Slice AA-2)
   but there is no per-model surface in the Simulation Options
   dialog — Tab 7 was deferred at Slice G-4 on engine-API gaps.
5. **GeoPackage as a one-file container is unsupported.** The
   engine ships GeoPackageInputPlugin + GeoPackageOutputPlugin +
   GeoPackageReportPlugin (tri-role for the same `.gpkg`), but the
   GUI treats input / report / output as three separate paths. No
   "single container" toggle exists.

**Architecture decisions (confirmed with user 2026-05-08):**

- A *project* (`.oswp`) references **one or more SWMM model
  instances**. This is Phase 13's redesign brought forward into
  the IO layer. UI changes to support multiple windows-per-project
  remain Phase 13's concern; this slice ships the *persistence*
  side (schema array of length ≥ 1) and the *Save Project* loop.
- **Default IO is the legacy triplet** `.inp` + `.rpt` + `.out`.
  Single-GeoPackage-container is **opt-in**, set per-instance from
  the Simulation Options dialog Tab 7 (or the New Project dialog).
- **Per-instance IO settings live in the `.inp` itself**:
  - `[FILES]` section → input/report/output paths (legacy parity)
  - `[REPORT]` section → report knobs (already there)
  - `[PLUGINS]` section → writer/report/output plugin id + args
    (engine already parses this on read; GUI needs API to mutate)
- The `.oswp` carries only **project-level state**: the list of
  instance references, GUI-only state (themes, layer order, hidden
  objects, canvas view), and project-scope preference overrides.
  No path or plugin choice that belongs in the `.inp` is duplicated
  in the `.oswp`.
- **All file references in `.oswp` are stored as paths relative to
  the `.oswp` directory.** Same convention extends to the `[FILES]`
  section of each instance `.inp` when the GUI writes them — but
  only because the engine already resolves `[FILES]` paths
  relatively to the `.inp` directory; this is legacy SWMM behaviour.
- **Defaults chain:** `[FILES]`/`[PLUGINS]` in instance `.inp`
  (if present) → project-scope override in `.oswp` (if present) →
  app-scope `PreferencesManager` default → engine hard-coded
  default. First non-empty wins.

##### AA-3.1 — Engine API gaps (block remaining sub-slices)

These items belong in `openswmm.engine`, not the GUI. Filing them
as a coordinated batch so the GUI can land in one cut:

| Symbol | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `swmm_model_write_with_plugin(engine, path, output_plugin_id)` | Replace hard-coded `.inp`-only `swmm_model_write`. Routes through `IInputPlugin::write()` of the named plugin. NULL/empty → existing default `.inp` writer. |
| `swmm_plugins_count(engine, *count)` | Number of `[PLUGINS]` entries currently registered on the engine (for GUI listing). |
| `swmm_plugin_get(engine, idx, *role, *id, *args_buf, args_buf_sz)` | Read one `[PLUGINS]` row by index. |
| `swmm_plugin_set(engine, role, id, args)` | Add or replace a `[PLUGINS]` row by `(role, id)` key. Engine re-serializes on next `swmm_model_write*`. |
| `swmm_plugin_remove(engine, role, id)` | Remove a `[PLUGINS]` row. |
| `swmm_files_get(engine, kind, *path_buf, sz)` / `swmm_files_set(engine, kind, path)` | Read/write `[FILES]` section entries (`SAVE OUTFILE`, `USE OUTFILE`, hot-start, etc.). Already partly there for hot-start (Slice AM); extend to outfile/report-file. |
| `openswmm::DiscoveredFilter::roles` (extended) | Today `DiscoveredFilter` has one role per entry. Add `roles_advertised: bitmask<PluginRole>` so the GUI can detect tri-role plugins (GeoPackage's three components share a `plugin_id`). Or expose a grouping API: `discover_plugins_by_id()` returning `{id, version, caption, roles[]}` aggregates. |

**Open** on the engine side: whether `swmm_model_write_with_plugin`
should also flush the report and output via the chosen plugin (one
call writes everything to the same `.gpkg`), or whether that stays
a separate concern (`swmm_engine_open` already takes the plugins
that handle writes during simulation, not at save-time). Resolution
TBD with engine team.

##### AA-3.2 — `.oswp` schema v4 (sessions array + relative paths)

[include/project/projectserializer.h](../include/project/projectserializer.h)
+ [src/project/projectserializer.cpp](../src/project/projectserializer.cpp).
Bump `kCurrentSchemaVersion` from 3 → 4. New shape:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 4,
  "title": "My Project",
  "sessions": [
    {
      "id": "session-1",
      "title": "Base Scenario",
      "inpPath": "models/base.inp",
      "engineVersion": "5.3.0",
      "layer": { "crsAuthority": "EPSG", "crsCode": 26910,
                 "categoryOrder": [...], "objectOrder": {...},
                 "hiddenObjects": [...] }
    }
  ],
  "canvas": { "crsAuthority": "EPSG", "crsCode": 4326,
              "extent": [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax] },
  "basemaps": [...],
  "preferences": { "Selection/ClickTolerancePx": 30, ... }
}
```

Implementation notes:
- All `inpPath` (and any future `gpkgPath`, `*.aux` references)
  go through new helpers `toRelativePath(p, oswpFile)` /
  `resolveStoredPath(stored, oswpFile)`. Helpers are in the public
  header so future slices reuse them.
- `applyFromFile` accepts schema 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 and migrates in-memory
  on load. v1–v3 had a single root-level `inpPath` + `layer` block;
  v4 lifts those into a `sessions[0]` entry.
- Multi-session save (when more than one window/instance exists in
  the project) iterates `mProject->sessions()` and writes one
  `sessions[N]` block per instance.
- `preferences` block is the long-deferred Slice V project-scope
  override map. Loaded into the workspace's override layer on
  open; written back on save.

##### AA-3.3 — Plugin-aware Save / Save As (the actual GeoPackage write)

[src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp](../src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp)
`save()` / `saveAs(path)`:

1. Determine the writer plugin id for `path`:
   - If the path's extension matches the *active* writer plugin
     (the one currently set in the `[PLUGINS]` `INPUT` row, or
     `""` for built-in `.inp`), use it.
   - Else, look up the first registry entry of `FilterKind::InputRead`
     with `canWrite=true` whose patterns include `path`'s extension.
     If found, route through that plugin.
   - Else, error: "No writer plugin handles `*.X` files." (Sim
     Options dialog has a writer combo so users hit this rarely.)
2. Call `swmm_model_write_with_plugin(engine, path, pluginId)`.
3. On a Save As that changes the writer (e.g. `.inp` → `.gpkg`),
   update the `.inp [PLUGINS]` row via `swmm_plugin_set` so the
   project remembers its preferred container on next open.

[src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) `onSaveAsInputFile`: no change
to the dialog logic — just the call into `pw->saveAs(path)` now does
the right thing for `*.gpkg`.

##### AA-3.4 — Save Project iterates dirty instances

[src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) `onSaveProject` /
`onSaveProjectAs` rewritten:

```cpp
void SWMMVis::onSaveProject() {
    auto *proj = activeProject();          // owning workspace
    if (!proj || proj->oswpPath().isEmpty()) { onSaveProjectAs(); return; }

    QStringList errors;
    for (auto *inst : proj->dirtyInstances()) {
        QString err;
        if (!inst->save(&err)) errors << err;
    }
    QString sidecarErr;
    if (!ProjectSerializer::saveToFile(proj->oswpPath(), proj, &sidecarErr))
        errors << sidecarErr;

    if (!errors.isEmpty()) showSaveErrorsDialog(errors);
}
```

Today there is exactly one `SWMMVisProjectWindow` per project so
the loop iterates once. When Phase 13 lands and a project owns
N windows, the loop's body is unchanged.

`onSaveProjectAs` additionally:
- Asks "Move all instance files into the new project folder?"
  (Yes / Keep in place). Yes: copies `.inp`/`.gpkg`/aux files
  next to the chosen `.oswp`, rewrites `[FILES]` paths to bare
  basenames, clears any `.oswp` absolute references.
- Old `.oswp` cleanup is now in scope (was deferred at Slice X).
