##### Verify (acceptance criteria)

- **GeoPackage round-trip:** New Project → pick GeoPackage container.
  Add a junction. Save. The chosen `model.gpkg` exists and contains
  the SWMM model schema; no `.inp` text file is written. Reopen
  `model.gpkg` from File → Open — the junction survives.
- **Triplet round-trip (default):** New Project → default container
  (`.inp`). Save. Files at `model.inp` only (no `.rpt`/`.out` until
  simulation runs). Reopen — model survives.
- **Single container toggle:** open `model.inp`, Sim Options →
  Files, switch input writer to GeoPackage and check "Single
  container". Save. `model.gpkg` exists; the `[FILES]` section in
  the in-memory model now points all three (input/report/output)
  to that path. Run simulation — report and output land inside the
  same `.gpkg`.
- **Per-instance overrides:** open two `.inp`s in two windows,
  configure each with a different output writer in Sim Options.
  Run both — outputs land at the per-window paths, not at the
  app default.
- **Relative paths:** save a project to `~/work/proj/`. Move
  the entire `~/work/proj/` directory to `/tmp/proj/`. Open
  `/tmp/proj/proj.oswp` — references resolve, model loads.
- **Save As → moves instance files:** project at
  `~/A/proj.oswp` referencing `~/A/models/x.inp`. Save As to
  `~/B/proj.oswp` → "Move instance files?" → Yes → `~/B/x.inp`
  exists, `[FILES]` paths in the new `.inp` are bare basenames,
  the `.oswp` references `x.inp` (not `models/x.inp`).
- **Old sidecar cleanup on Save As:** the old `.oswp` at the
  source path is deleted (deferred from Slice X).
- **Misuse guard:** Save As → `model.xyz` (extension with no
  registered writer) shows an error dialog, doesn't write anything.
- **Backward compat:** open a v1/v2/v3 `.oswp` from before this
  slice — it loads and the next save upgrades to v4 silently.

##### Decisions resolved (2026-05-08)

1. **Multi-instance UI surface for today** → ship the thin
   `SWMMVisProject` wrapper now. Schema writes a `sessions[]` array
   of length 1; class plumbing is in place for Phase 13 to add the
   second instance without a schema migration.
2. **Plugin args grammar** → free-form `QLineEdit` per `[PLUGINS]`
   row in this slice. Argspec metadata + typed widgets parked for a
   future Slice AA-4 gated on user demand.
3. **Autosave on Run Simulation** → preserve current behaviour
   (save the running instance only). Other dirty instances stay
   dirty across runs.
4. **Recent files** → list both `.oswp` and `.inp` paths,
   distinguished by icon, with `.oswp` preferred on save and `.inp`
   registered on open-without-sidecar. Opening an `.oswp` rehydrates
   the full project; opening a bare `.inp` creates a single-instance
   project as today.
5. **Hot-start files** → stay in Slice AM (deferred). Sim Options
   Tab 7 ships without hot-start UI in this slice.

##### Sequencing

1. Engine team: AA-3.1 ships first (no GUI work blocked on each
   other). Estimated 1–2 weeks engine-side.
2. AA-3.2 (schema v4 + relative paths) — independent of engine
   work; can land today. Provides forward-compat entry point.
3. AA-3.3 (plugin-aware save) — needs AA-3.1.
4. AA-3.4 (save loop) + AA-3.5 (Sim Options Tab 7) — needs AA-3.1
   for the plugin/files mutators.
5. AA-3.6 (menu reshape) + AA-3.7 (New Project combo) — pure GUI,
   parallel.

##### Risks

- **Engine API churn.** AA-3.1 is six new functions; bikeshedding
  on names/signatures could delay 1–2 weeks. Mitigation: present
  the full list to the engine team upfront, get sign-off before
  GUI changes start.
- **`.inp` → `.gpkg` content fidelity.** The GeoPackage
  InputPlugin's `write()` must produce a file whose subsequent
  `read()` reconstructs the exact same SimulationContext, including
  user flags (Slice AW), tags, and plugin specs. Add a round-trip
  property test in `tests/integration/`.
- **Schema migration regressions.** v1 → v4 covers four schema
  versions. Add fixture `.oswp` files at every version under
  `tests/fixtures/oswp/` and a parametric test that loads each
  and checks no data loss on save.
- **Symbolic-link / case-insensitive filesystems.** Relative-path
  helpers must canonicalise without resolving symlinks (otherwise
  the user's `~/work` symlink becomes an absolute path on save).
  Use `QDir::cleanPath` + `QDir::relativeFilePath`, not
  `QFileInfo::canonicalFilePath`.

#### ⏳ Slice AG — Compound property editors (DRAFT 2026-05-11, awaiting approval)

**Motivation.** Slice Z.5 (above) makes **simple** attributes
inline-editable in both the Attribute Table and the Property
Browser via shared delegates.  That doesn't cover the structurally
complex SWMM concepts a real model needs:

- **Inflows** at a junction — zero-to-many entries each with type
  (`FLOW` / `CONCEN` / `MASS`), constituent / pollutant, baseline,
  scale factors, optional timeseries + pattern.
- **Dry-weather flow (DWF)** at a junction — average value + up to
  four pattern slots (monthly / daily / hourly / weekend).
- **RDII / unit hydrographs** — a hydrograph **group** with up to
  three response sets (short / medium / long), each holding R/T/K
  (ratio / time-to-peak / recession ratio).  Junctions reference a
  group by name with an associated area.
- **Curves, patterns, timeseries** — referenced by name from many
  places; need their own table editors.

Slice AG closes the gap with **sub-dialogs reached from "Edit…"
buttons** in the per-row Attribute Table and the Property Browser
(user-confirmed UX, 2026-05-11).

##### AG.0 — Engine API prerequisites (blocks the rest)

These belong in `openswmm.engine` and need to ship first.  Filing
them as a coordinated batch like the AA-3.1 spec.

**Inflows** (`openswmm_inflows.h`):

```c
int swmm_inflow_count(SWMM_Engine, int node_idx, int* count);
int swmm_inflow_get(SWMM_Engine, int node_idx, int inflow_idx,
                    int* type, char* constituent_buf, int constituent_sz,
                    char* ts_name_buf, int ts_sz,
                    double* baseline, double* m_factor, double* s_factor,
                    char* pattern_buf, int pattern_sz);
int swmm_inflow_set(SWMM_Engine, int node_idx, int inflow_idx,
                    int type, const char* constituent,
                    const char* ts_name, double baseline,
                    double m_factor, double s_factor,
                    const char* pattern);
int swmm_inflow_remove(SWMM_Engine, int node_idx, int inflow_idx);
```

**Dry-weather flow** — same shape: `swmm_dwf_count/get/set/remove`.

**RDII / unit hydrographs** (`openswmm_hydrographs.h`, new):

```c
int swmm_hydrograph_count(SWMM_Engine, int* count);
int swmm_hydrograph_get(SWMM_Engine, int idx,
                        char* name_buf, int name_sz,
                        char* raingage_buf, int rg_sz);
int swmm_hydrograph_create(SWMM_Engine, const char* name,
                           const char* raingage);
int swmm_hydrograph_remove(SWMM_Engine, const char* name);

/* RTK for one (hydrograph, response, month) cell.
 * response: 0=short, 1=medium, 2=long.
 * month:    0..11 (or -1 for "all months" default row). */
int swmm_hydrograph_get_rtk(SWMM_Engine, const char* name,
                            int response, int month,
                            double* r, double* t, double* k);
int swmm_hydrograph_set_rtk(SWMM_Engine, const char* name,
                            int response, int month,
                            double r, double t, double k);

/* Junction-side RDII slot. */
int swmm_node_rdii_get(SWMM_Engine, int node_idx,
                       char* hydrograph_buf, int hg_sz, double* area);
int swmm_node_rdii_set(SWMM_Engine, int node_idx,
                       const char* hydrograph, double area);
int swmm_node_rdii_clear(SWMM_Engine, int node_idx);
```

**Object type conversion** (added 2026-05-11 after user feedback):

```c
/* Convert a node from one of {JUNCTION, OUTFALL, STORAGE, DIVIDER}
 * to another, preserving the node's name + coordinates + connectivity
 * (the connected links keep their endpoints) and the shared
 * attributes (invert_elev, max_depth, init_depth, surcharge_depth).
 * Type-specific state (storage curve, outfall boundary, etc.) is
 * reset to defaults for the new type. */
int swmm_node_change_type(SWMM_Engine engine, int idx, int new_type);

/* Same for links — convert between {CONDUIT, PUMP, ORIFICE, WEIR,
 * OUTLET} preserving name + endpoints + xsection + offsets where
 * applicable. */
int swmm_link_change_type(SWMM_Engine engine, int idx, int new_type);
```

Without these, the conversion has to be implemented GUI-side as
*read all shared attrs → save connections → swmm_*_remove old →
swmm_*_add new type → restore attrs + connections* which is
fragile and loses attributes the engine doesn't yet expose.

The GUI surfaces the affordance today as a placeholder **Change
Type…** entry in the Attribute Table's right-click menu
(`AttributeTablePanel::onChangeTypeTriggered`) — the menu opens a
QMessageBox documenting this gap so the affordance is visible even
before the engine API lands.  Inline type-editing in the table /
property browser is **explicitly prohibited** per user rule
(2026-05-11): changing what an object IS must be a deliberate
context-menu action, not a casual cell edit.

**Patterns, curves, timeseries** — Slice AH already covers the
table editors for these; AG just needs **NameRef pickers** that
can reach them, which the existing `swmm_pattern_count/get`,
`swmm_curve_count/get`, `swmm_ts_count/get` C-API already supports
in read-only form.  Write-side covered by AH.

A standalone engine-API request doc lives at
[`openswmm.engine/docs/AG_GUI_API_REQUEST.md`](../../openswmm.engine/docs/AG_GUI_API_REQUEST.md)
— filed 2026-05-11 alongside Z.5.5 shipping; six sections (type
conversion, inflows, DWF, RDII / hydrographs, missing node
getters, divider type) totalling 16 new symbols + three matching
getters.  Lifts the existing AA-3.1 request-doc shape.

##### AG.1 — Inflows sub-dialog

Triggered by an `Edit…` button cell in the Junction row's
**Inflows** column (Z.5.1 `ButtonCellDelegate`).  Modal dialog:

- Top: junction name (read-only).
- Tabbed:
  - **External Inflows** — `QTableView` with columns:
    `Constituent (NameRef pollutant)`, `Type (combo)`, `Time series
    (NameRef)`, `Baseline`, `Scale factor`, `Mass factor`,
    `Pattern (NameRef)`.  Add / Remove buttons; Save commits
    all rows via `swmm_inflow_set` (existing rows by idx) and
    `swmm_inflow_remove` (for deleted rows).
  - **Dry-Weather Flow** — same table shape but with
    `Constituent`, `Average value`, `Monthly pattern`, `Daily
    pattern`, `Hourly pattern`, `Weekend pattern`.
- OK applies; Cancel reverts via the same `EditCommand` undo
  stack Z.5.5 introduces.

##### AG.2 — RDII / Unit Hydrograph sub-dialog

Triggered by `Edit…` in the junction's **RDII** column.  The
dialog is split into:

- **Hydrograph group picker** — combo of hydrograph names (via
  `swmm_hydrograph_count/get`).  Buttons: New… (prompts for name +
  raingage), Rename…, Delete.
- **RTK matrix** — 3 × N table.  Rows are `Short` / `Medium` /
  `Long` response; columns are `R` (response ratio), `T` (time to
  peak, hr), `K` (recession ratio).  One column per "month" tab —
  default tab is "All months" (`month = -1`), with per-month
  override tabs added on demand.
- **Junction binding** — area field (`swmm_node_rdii_set`) and
  Clear button (`swmm_node_rdii_clear`).

##### AG.3 — Per-type Property Browser overhaul

The existing `AttributePanel` is generic; AG.3 introduces typed
adapters so the property tree shows category-appropriate
properties + sub-groups.  New files:

```
include/ui/properties/swmmpropertyadapter.h   — base interface
include/ui/properties/junctionpropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/outfallpropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/storagepropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/dividerpropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/conduitpropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/pumppropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/orificepropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/weirpropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/outletpropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/subcatchmentpropertyadapter.h
include/ui/properties/raingagepropertyadapter.h
```

Each adapter:

1. Declares `Q_PROPERTY` per attribute with `READ` / `WRITE` going
   to the matching engine setter/getter (no extra storage —
   adapter is a thin façade over `swmm_*_set/get`).
2. Includes a **sub-group** property for compound editors —
   `Inflows` / `DWF` / `RDII` show as group nodes in the tree
   whose value is an `Edit…` button (Z.5.1 `ButtonCellDelegate`
   re-used) opening the AG.1 / AG.2 dialogs.
3. Picks the right delegate per property using the shared schema
   from Z.5.

The existing QPropertyModel binding stays — adapters just expose
typed `Q_PROPERTY` instead of the current generic identify-map.

##### AG.4 — Outfall / Storage / Divider conditional sub-editors

These categories have **type-dependent** parameter sets that
Z.5's flat schema can't express:

- **Outfall**: `FIXED` → fixed-stage spinbox; `TIDAL` → curve
  picker; `TIMESERIES` → timeseries picker; `FREE` / `NORMAL` →
  no extra params.
- **Storage**: `FUNCTIONAL` → 3 coeffs; `TABULAR` → curve picker;
  `PYRAMIDAL` / `CONICAL` / `CYLINDRICAL` → dimensions.
- **Divider**: `OVERFLOW` → nothing; `CUTOFF` → cutoff flow;
  `TABULAR` → curve picker; `WEIR` → coefficient, height, Cd.

Adapter `Q_PROPERTY`s are dynamically gated via property
visibility flags exposed on the QPropertyModel side; the property
browser hides/shows them as the type combo's value changes.  The
Attribute Table column for the type field installs a `setData`
hook that triggers the same hide/show.

##### AG.5 — Curve / pattern / timeseries pickers reach Slice AH

When `NameRefDelegate` (Z.5.1) opens the trailing "…" button:

- For now (Z.5 ship), opens a read-only listing dialog.
- When Slice AH ships, the same button opens AH's full editor for
  the active reference type.

- Select a Junction in the Object Browser.  Property Browser
  shows typed properties (invertElev, maxDepth, …) AND the

- Click `Edit…` in the Inflows row → modal opens with existing

- Click `Edit…` in the RDII row → modal opens.  Create a new

##### AG — Sequencing

1. **AG.0 (engine work)** ships first.  Estimated 1-2 weeks
   engine-side; no GUI work blocked on each other.
2. **AG.1 + AG.2** (Inflows / RDII dialogs) — primary user-visible
   value; ~1 week GUI work.
3. **AG.3** (per-type adapters + Property Browser overhaul) — bulk
   of the GUI work, ~1.5 weeks.
4. **AG.4** (conditional sub-editors for Outfall / Storage /
   Divider) — ~3 days.
5. **AG.5** wires up when AH ships; no AG-side blocker.

##### AG — Risks

- **Engine round-trip fidelity.** Inflow / RDII edits must
  round-trip through `swmm_model_write` so saved `.inp` reproduces
  the same model on reopen.  Existing tests for `[INFLOWS]` /
  `[HYDROGRAPHS]` writers cover the format; round-trip property
  tests in `tests/integration/` exercise the edit path.
- **Multi-month RTK UI density.** The RTK matrix can blow up to
  12 month-tabs × 3 response rows × 3 columns = 108 cells per
  hydrograph.  Default to "All months" only; per-month tabs
  added on user demand.
- **Pollutant constituents.** The Constituent combo in AG.1 needs
  the model's pollutant list (`[POLLUTANTS]`).  Engine already
  exposes `swmm_pollutant_count/get`; no new API needed.

#### ⏳ Slice AT — Multi-pane Time Series + 1v1 Comparison Plot Dialog

Replaces the single-series, single-session
[`TimeSeriesPlotDialog`](../include/ui/dialogs/timeseriesplotdialog.h)
from Slice M with a comparison / analysis surface. Absorbs Slice M's
deferred follow-ups (multi-series, calendar X axis, Δ derived
series), the time-series portion of Slice AD ("Time Series Plot
extends to add series / legend / styling"), and the plot-based
two-session comparison referenced by Phase 13.4.

##### Goals (user-stated, 2026-04-25)

1. **Multiple series per chart.** Add / remove series freely; series
   come from any open `.out` (multiple project windows / runs) plus
   imported observed-data files.
2. **Calendar X axis.** Real `QDateTime` labels driven by
   `swmm_output_get_start_date` (Julian → QDateTime), not hours-
   since-start.
3. **Attribute grouping (Nx1 stack).** One chart **per attribute**
   (Flow, Depth, Velocity, Rainfall, …), stacked vertically. A
   series can only land on the chart whose attribute matches.
4. **Per-series styling.** Color, line on/off, line width, line dash
   pattern, marker on/off, marker shape, marker size, opacity,
   legend name — all editable.
5. **Animation cursor.** When the global animation controller
   (Slice AC) is playing, each chart shows a dashed vertical line at
   the current sim time with a label showing the timestamp.
6. **Two-output / two-model 1v1 comparison.** Pick a baseline run
   and a comparison run; for each attribute row, a **scatter plot**
   appears in column 2 (X = baseline, Y = comparison) with a 45°
   identity line dashed; goodness-of-fit metrics (NSE / R² / RMSE /
   PBIAS) printed in the row title.
7. **Layout: Nx2.** Column 0 = time-series; column 1 = 1v1 scatter
   (visible only when ≥2 runs are loaded). Column 1 collapses to
   zero width when only one run is plotted, so the dialog falls
   back gracefully to multi-series time-series only.
8. **Δ derived series (B − A)**, opt-in via per-row toolbar toggle
   `Δ`: adds a derived `(comparison − baseline)` series rendered
   in the same time-series chart with a distinct dashed style and
   a separate right-side Y axis. Useful when a 1v1 scatter
   collapses temporal information the user wants to keep.

##### UI layout

```
┌─ Series panel (left dock) ────────────────────────────┐
│ ▾ Run A  (Project: foo.inp)         [● baseline]     │
│   ▾ Junction J1                                      │
│     ☑ depth        [ ── ●  blue   ]                  │
│     ☑ head         [ ──    teal   ]                  │
│   ▾ Conduit C5                                       │
│     ☑ flow         [ ── ●  red    ]                  │
│ ▾ Run B  (Project: foo_calibrated.inp)               │
│   ▾ Junction J1                                      │
│     ☑ depth        [ ─ ─    green  ]                 │
│ ▾ Observed (file: observed.csv)                      │
│   ▾ Junction J1                                      │
│     ☑ depth        [    ●   black, no line ]         │
│ [Add Series…]  [Remove]                              │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Time-series                  │  1v1 scatter (vs A)   │
│ ┌──── Depth (NSE=0.87) ──┐    │ ┌──── Depth ────────┐ │
│ │ y(t)                   │    │ │  Y=B  /           │ │
│ │ (J1 A, J1 B, J1 obs)   │    │ │      / 45°        │ │
│ │  ┊ animation cursor    │    │ │     /  • • •      │ │
│ └────────────────────────┘    │ └───────X=A─────────┘ │
│ ┌──── Flow ──────────────┐    │ ┌──── Flow ─────────┐ │
│ │ y(t) (C5 A only)       │    │ │ (empty — C5 only  │ │
│ │                        │    │ │  in run A)        │ │
│ └────────────────────────┘    │ └───────────────────┘ │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Layout: outer `QSplitter` (horizontal) — series panel | charts area.
Charts area is a `QGridLayout` with N rows × 2 columns. Each row
owns two `QChart`s; rows are added/removed dynamically as the user
adds series whose attributes don't yet have a row. Vertical scroll
when more than ~4 rows.

##### Architecture (MVC)

**`ComparisonPlotModel`** (new, `include/plot/comparisonplotmodel.h`):
- `QList<RunSource>` — each is one of three kinds:
  - `Output` — `.out` from an **open project window** (preferred —
    inherits the project's unit system / label automatically); or
  - `Output` — `.out` from a **standalone load** via
    `Tools → Comparison Plot → Load Run…` (no project window
    required; user supplies a label). Both forms produce the same
    `RunSource::Output` record after construction.
  - `Observed` — observed time-series file (`.csv`, `.tsv`,
    `.dat`, `.xlsx`) loaded through Slice AA's
    `FileFilterRegistry` (`FileFilter::Kind::Tabular`, `canRead`)
    so plugins can register custom observed-data formats. Falls
    back to a built-in CSV reader (column-mapping dialog —
    timestamp column + value column + unit) when no plugin
    matches the suffix. Slice AA's existing `Tabular` kind covers
    this; no new enum value required.
  - One run is flagged `isBaseline()` for the 1v1 column.
- `QList<SeriesSpec>` — `{ runIndex, objectRef, attribute, style }`.
  Series with the same `attribute` land in the same row.
- `QHash<PlotAttribute, AttributeRow>` — derived per-attribute:
  series rendered, axis ranges, fit metrics for the column-1
  scatter.
- Signals: `seriesAdded`, `seriesRemoved`, `styleChanged`,
  `baselineChanged`, `animationTimeChanged`,
  `runSourceAdded/Removed`.

**Calendar X axis.** Convert SWMM Julian (SWMM5 epoch =
1899-12-30 00:00 — same as Excel "1900 system" minus 2 leap-day
quirks; `swmm5/datetime.c::DateTimeFromYMD` is the canonical source)
to `QDateTime`:
```cpp
inline QDateTime swmmJulianToDateTime(double julian) {
    static const QDate kEpoch(1899, 12, 30);
    const double days = std::floor(julian);
    const double frac = julian - days;
    return QDateTime(
        kEpoch.addDays(static_cast<qint64>(days)),
        QTime(0, 0).addMSecs(
            static_cast<qint64>(frac * 86'400'000.0)),
        Qt::UTC);
}
```
Charts use `QDateTimeAxis`; format auto-adapts to span (>30 d → date
only; 1–30 d → date + hour; ≤1 d → date + h:mm).

**Attribute identity.** `PlotAttribute` enum (Depth, Head, Volume,
LateralInflow, TotalInflow, Overflow, Flow, Velocity, Capacity,
Rainfall, SnowDepth, Evap, Infil, Runoff, …) with
`PlotAttribute::units(UnitSystem)` so series on the same row share
a Y axis. A category is omitted when no run has data for it.

**Per-series styling.** `SeriesStyle` struct: `QColor color`,
`bool showLine`, `qreal lineWidth`, `Qt::PenStyle dash`,
`bool showMarkers`, `MarkerShape shape`, `qreal markerSize`,
`qreal opacity`, `QString legendName`. Defaults auto-assigned from
a 12-color cycle on first add. Edits persist via QSettings under
the dialog's geometry key, scoped per `(runLabel, objectRef,
attribute)`.

**Animation cursor.** Each time-series chart owns a dashed
`QLineSeries` whose X is bound to
`AnimationController::currentTimeChanged(QDateTime)` (Slice AC).
When AC isn't shipped, the cursor stays hidden; the slot is
pre-wired so it lights up automatically when AC lands. Label is a
`QGraphicsSimpleTextItem` overlay anchored to the plot-area top.

**1v1 scatter (column 1).** For each attribute row that has ≥2 runs
sharing ≥1 `objectRef`, build a scatter where X = baseline sample,
Y = comparison sample, paired by timestamp. When report steps
differ, the comparison run is **resampled to the baseline's
timestep** by linear interpolation (boundary clipped). 45° identity
line is a `QLineSeries` from `(min, min)` to `(max, max)` with a
dashed pen. Optional best-fit regression line + R² annotation
toggled in the row's tiny toolbar.

**Δ derived series.** Per-row toolbar `Δ` toggle adds a
`DerivedSeriesSpec { baselineRunIdx, comparisonRunIdx, objectRef,
attribute }` whose values at each baseline timestep are
`comparison(t) − baseline(t)` (resampled). Rendered on a secondary
Y axis (right side of the time-series chart) so its scale doesn't
distort the absolute series. Style defaults: dashed, half-width,
desaturated colour of the comparison run.

**Goodness-of-fit.** `FitMetrics::compute(obs, sim)` →
`{ nse, r2, rmse, pbias }`. Shown in the column-1 chart title and
in the series-panel tree's tooltip.

##### Engine plumbing

- `swmm_output_get_start_date(handle, double *julianOut)` — already
  used by Slice M for X-range. This slice converts to `QDateTime`
  and uses it as the axis base.
- `swmm_output_get_pollut_count` + name lookup — minor extension
  for pollutant attributes (deferred sub-item; ship with the
  variables Slice M already exposes).
- No new engine surface for the comparison itself — each
  `RunSource::Output` opens its `.out` independently.

##### Behaviour edge cases

- **Different report steps.** Comparison run resampled to baseline's
  timestep via linear interpolation (boundary clipped). Series gets
  a small `[resampled]` badge in the legend.
- **Run A has J1 but Run B doesn't.** `(J1, attribute)` series
  renders only for Run A; column-1 scatter for that row hides when
  no pairs exist.
- **NaN / missing values.** Dropped before metric computation;
  rendered as gaps in the time series.
- **Animation cursor with no current time.** Hidden when
  `AnimationController` is null or stopped.
- **Single run.** Column 1 width set to 0 — grid degenerates to
  Nx1. This is the requested Nx1 fallback.
- **Observed CSV with mismatched units.** A unit mismatch banner
  appears at the top of the affected row; user can either pick a
  conversion in the per-row toolbar or remove the series.

##### Verification

1. **Calendar axis.** Open a real `.out`; X axis shows
   `2026-01-01 00:00 → 2026-01-02 12:00` style labels (not
   `0 → 36 h`). Zoom: labels switch density appropriately.
2. **Multi-series.** Add three series (J1 depth, J1 head, J5 depth)
   from one run. Lands on two rows: Depth (J1 + J5) and Head (J1).
3. **Per-series styling.** Toggle markers, change color, change
   line width — chart updates immediately.
4. **Two runs.** Open a second project window with a perturbed
   model. Drag-add J1 from Run B to the same `(J1, depth)` slot.
   Column-1 scatter appears with 45° dashed line and NSE label.
5. **Observed overlay.** Import a CSV via Slice AA's plugin filter
   set; add it as a series — renders on the same Depth row as
   markers-only. Column-1 scatter pairs observed × baseline.
6. **Animation cursor.** After Slice AC, hit Play in the animation
   toolbar; dashed vertical line sweeps across all time-series
   rows in lockstep with the canvas.
7. **Backwards compat.** Object-Browser right-click → Plot Time
   Series… (Slice M path) opens the new dialog populated with one
   series; user-facing behaviour matches today.

##### Sequencing & cross-references

- Depends on **Slice AC** for the animation cursor (cursor is
  optional — slice ships without AC, lights up later).
- Depends on **Slice AA** when observed-data import surfaces via
  the plugin filter set.
- **Subsumes** Slice M's deferred follow-ups (multi-series,
  calendar axis, Δ derived series — Δ now native via 1v1 scatter
  or a planned "Δ" derived attribute on a row).
- **Narrows** Slice AD: AD now scopes to Status / Summary / Profile
  only (no time-series extensions there — those move here).
- **Hosts** the plot-based comparison referenced by Phase 13.4.
- **Feeds into** Slice AK (calibration) — calibration data files
  add an `Observed` `RunSource`; the calibration UI is a thin
  preset on this dialog.

#### ⏳ Slice AT.2 — Toolbar, map-picking, system attributes, linked X axis

Surgical interaction-surface upgrade to the existing Slice AT
`ComparisonPlotDialog`. AT defined the Nx2 grid + series model; AT.2
brings the dialog up to parity with `ProfilePlotDialog` in terms of
interactive controls and removes six rough edges that surfaced once
users started exercising the dialog on real models (2026-05-22):

1. No chart toolbar — zoom, pan, fit-to-data, export, display
   options, animation-cursor toggle.
2. Series objects could only be added by typing object names — no
   point-and-click selection from the map canvas.
3. System-level results (`swmm_output_get_system_series`'s 14
   `SWMM_OUT_SYS_*` quantities) had no GUI entry point.
4. Per-row X axes were independent — no way to slew time across all
   charts together.
5. Charts lived inside a `QScrollArea + QGridLayout` with default
   size hints; the first chart didn't fill the dialog.
6. Map background right-click was dead.

##### Goals

- **Profile-style chart toolbar** mirroring `ProfilePlotDialog`'s
  `QActionGroup` mode pattern (Select / Pan / ZoomIn / ZoomOut),
  plus Fit, Export PNG…, Display Options…, and an Animation Cursor
  toggle. Right-click on any chart → context menu (Copy as Image,
  Save PNG, Reset Zoom, Hide/Show Cursor, Remove Row, Options).
- **`AttributePickerMenu`** widget — `QMenu` factory keyed off
  `ObjectRef::Kind`. Reused by every place the user picks an
  attribute (object right-click, map-pick tool, Add System Series
  button).
- **Map context menu attribute submenu** — replaces the current
  single "Plot Time Series…" entry in
  `OpenSWMMVisMapToolSelect::showContextMenu` with a submenu of
  attributes valid for the hit object's kind (incl. an "All
  attributes" entry). Background-hit right-click opens "Plot System
  Variable…" with the 14 system attributes.
- **`OpenSWMMVisMapToolPlotPick`** — transient `OpenSWMMVisMapTool`
  pushed onto the canvas when the user clicks the dialog's "Add
  from Map…" toolbar action. Each click hit-tests via `identifyAt`,
  pops the attribute submenu at the cursor, and emits
  `objectPicked(SWMMObjectRef, PlotAttribute)`. Tool stays active
  across clicks; Esc / right-click / un-checking the toolbar action
  exits and restores the previous map tool.
- **System attributes** — extend `PlotAttribute` with 14 `System*`
  enumerators (values 22–35) mirroring `SWMM_OUT_SYS_*`; add
  `ObjectRef::Kind::System` + `forSystem()` factory; route the new
  kind through `SwmmOutRunLayer::getSeriesAt` to
  `swmm_output_get_system_series`. **No engine work** — the
  output-reader API already ships.
- **Linked X axis** — Qt Charts won't let one `QAbstractAxis` cross
  charts, so each row keeps its own `QDateTimeAxis` and the dialog
  manually mirrors range changes on `rangeChanged` via a recursion-
  guarded loop (`m_syncingX` flag). Display Options gains a "Sync X
  axis" master toggle (default on).
- **Vertical-splitter chart layout** — replace `QScrollArea +
  QGridLayout` with `QSplitter(Qt::Vertical)` whose children are
  per-row widgets. On add: `setSizes(QList<int>(N, total / N))` for
  equal stretch; user-draggable handles take over from there.
  `setChildrenCollapsible(false)` so rows can't disappear. With a
  single row, splitter fills the chart pane — the first-chart-
  stretches-to-fill requirement is met implicitly.
- **Animation cursor toggle** — already wired via
  `onAnimationTimeChanged` → per-row `cursorLine`. AT.2 adds a
  toolbar toggle (`Ctrl+Shift+C`, persisted in QSettings) plus a
  per-row override in the chart context menu.

##### Files (new)

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `include/ui/widgets/interactivechartview.h` / `.cpp` | `QChartView` subclass intercepting mouse events for Select/Pan/ZoomIn/ZoomOut; drives `QChart::zoomIn(QRectF)`, `chart->scroll(-dx,-dy)`, `chart->zoomReset()`. Owns the chart context menu. |
| `include/ui/widgets/attributepickermenu.h` / `.cpp` | `QMenu` factory keyed off `ObjectRef::Kind`. |
| `include/map/tools/maptoolplotpick.h` / `.cpp` | Transient `OpenSWMMVisMapTool` that emits `objectPicked(SWMMObjectRef, PlotAttribute)` after each click + attribute pick. Stays active until Esc. |
| `tests/gui/test_comparisonplot_toolbar.cpp` | Programmatic ZoomIn / Pan / Fit / Reset on a populated dialog. |
| `tests/gui/test_comparisonplot_xaxis_link.cpp` | `rangeChanged` on row 0 propagates to rows 1+; recursion-guard fuzz under a 50 ms storm of `setRange`. |
| `tests/gui/test_comparisonplot_system_attrs.cpp` | `ObjectRef::forSystem(SystemRunoff)` lands on its own row with correct units; engine resolver receives the matching `SWMM_OUT_SYS_*` enum. |

##### Behaviour edge cases

- **Pan mode + horizontal scroll wheel.** Wheel scrolls X only;
  modifier-less wheel zooms about the cursor (matches profile
  dialog convention).
- **Map-pick mode with no active results layer.** Dialog raises a
  status-bar warning and refuses to add the series. Map tool stays
  active.
- **System attribute on an `Observed` RunSource.** Not allowed —
  observed CSVs are object-scoped. Add Series dialog grays out the
  System pseudo-object when the selected RunSource is Observed.
- **`m_xAxisLinked` off + zoom.** Zoom affects only the row the
  user is interacting with. Re-enabling reapplies the most recent
  row's range to all rows.
- **Splitter row count > 6.** Outer `QScrollArea` activates with a
  per-row minimum height of ~200 px so tall stacks remain
  scrollable.
- **Animation cursor toolbar off + per-row override on.** Per-row
  override wins (lets users compare with the cursor on one row only
  while keeping it off elsewhere).

Follow-up batch after AT.2 went green on manual verification
(2026-05-22). Closes the gap between "the dialog renders" and "the
dialog is a real interactive exploration surface". Eight items, all
landing inside the existing `ComparisonPlotDialog` (no new top-level
surface).

##### Goals

1. **Series-tree show/hide checkboxes.** Each series row in the
   left-pane tree gets a `Qt::ItemIsUserCheckable` flag. Toggling
   the checkbox flips `SeriesStyle::showLine` on the underlying
   spec via `ComparisonPlotModel::updateStyle`; the existing
   incremental `onStyleChanged` slot already restyles the
   `QLineSeries` without a full chart rebuild.
2. **Series-tree right-click context menu.** Right-click a series
   row → `Plot This Only` (hides all other series in the same row),
   `Edit Style…` (existing double-click flow), `Remove Series`.
   Right-click a run row → `Add Series…`, `Remove Run`.
3. **SVG icons on the toolbar.** Replace text-only `QAction`s with
   `QIcon(":/swmmvis/svg/<name>.svg")` for Select, Pan, Zoom In,
   Zoom Out, Fit, Export, Cursor, AddSystem, AddFromMap. Lucide /
   Material outline-style; ship as `resources/svg/*.svg` and add to

6. **Per-chart `Chart Properties…` (QPropertyModel-backed).** New

7. **Hover-tooltip.** `InteractiveChartView::mouseMoveEvent` in
   `Mode::Select` walks visible `QLineSeries` on the chart, finds
   the sample with X closest to the cursor's data-x, and shows a
   `QToolTip` at the cursor with
   `<seriesName>\n<date-time>: <value> <units>`. Throttled to
   ~20 Hz to avoid tooltip flicker. Disabled in Pan / Zoom modes
   so it doesn't interfere with drag operations.
8. **Statistics Summary tab.** New `StatsSummaryPanel`
   (`include/ui/widgets/statssummarypanel.h`) docked under the
   chart splitter as a collapsible second `QSplitter` pane.
   `QTabWidget` with one tab per `PlotAttribute` row; each tab is a

   Default columns: `count / mean / median / stddev / min / max /

#### ⏳ Slice AU — 2D Mesh Generation (Shewchuk Triangle, embedded source)

**Motivation.** The engine's 2D module ([2dModelStrategy.md](../../openswmm.engine/docs/2dModelStrategy.md),
[two_dimensional_model.md](../../openswmm.engine/docs/two_dimensional_model.md))
ingests a triangular mesh through `[2D_VERTICES]` / `[2D_TRIANGLES]` /
`[2D_VERTEX_NODE_MAP]` / `[2D_TRIANGLE_NODE_MAP]` sections in the `.inp`
(or in an external `.2dm` linked via `[2D_MESH_FILE]`). The engine has
no runtime mesh-set API — meshes are baked into the input file at write
time. The GUI needs a workflow that takes a Digital Terrain Model + the
SWMM 1D network as input and produces those sections, with **vertices
and triangles tagged so the engine can wire 1D↔2D coupling without
post-processing**.

##### AU.1 — Shewchuk Triangle source (vendored, not full TriangleComponent)

- Vendor a **stripped `triangle.c` / `triangle.h`** from Shewchuk's
  distribution into [vendor/triangle/](../vendor/triangle/) (~1500 LOC
  after dropping `showme`, X11, file-I/O, and CLI driver). Keep only
  the constrained Delaunay + Steiner-point refinement + the
  `triangulate()` C entry. License text already shipped at
  [resources/licenses/triangle.txt](../resources/licenses/triangle.txt)
  and listed at [resources/about/components.json](../resources/about/components.json#L15).
- **Why not the HydroCouple `TriangleComponent`** ([…/HydroCouple/TriangleComponent](../../HydroCouple/TriangleComponent)):
  it pulls in the HydroCouple framework + Qt plugin glue + UI and is
  too heavy for an embedded mesher. We just need the algorithmic core.
- **Why not GEOS / CGAL**: GEOS has triangulation but only unconstrained;
  CGAL is GPL-poison for our MIT distribution. Triangle (MIT) is the
  right floor.

##### AU.2 — `MeshGenerator` (`src/mesh/`)

- Inputs:
  - **Domain**: a closed polygon (`QPolygonF`) defining the mesh boundary.
  - **Constraint segments**: list of polylines that must be honoured as
    edges (conduits, levees, buildings).
  - **Steiner points**: list of 2D points that must appear as mesh
    vertices (junctions, outfalls, storage units, gauges).
  - **Hole points**: interior points marking holes (buildings, blocked
    areas) — Triangle removes any triangle reachable from these.
  - **Quality knobs**: max triangle area, min angle (default 28°),
    Steiner-allowed flag.
- Output: `MeshResult { QVector<MeshVertex>, QVector<MeshTriangle>,
  QHash<int, QString> vertexTags, QHash<int, QString> triangleTags,
  QVector<MeshSegment> boundarySegments }` where each `MeshVertex`
  carries `(x, y, marker)` and `MeshSegment` carries `(v0, v1,
  marker)` — the marker is what Triangle propagates from input
  segment markers to output edges.
- Integration: thin C wrapper around `triangulate("pzqaq28DQ", ...)`
  (p = read PSLG, z = zero-based, q = quality, a = max area,
  D = use Delaunay, Q = quiet). Boundary tagging works because Triangle
  preserves segment markers from the input PSLG to the output edge
  list — we set markers when constructing the input.

##### AU.3 — Tagging rules (the seamless-coupling glue)

Three tag categories, all written into `[2D_VERTICES]` / `[2D_TRIANGLES]`
TAG columns and reflected in `[2D_VERTEX_NODE_MAP]` / `[2D_TRIANGLE_NODE_MAP]`:

| Tag carrier   | Source (1D side)              | Mesh-gen rule                                         | Engine section emitted |
|---------------|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| **Vertex**    | Junction / outfall / storage  | Add as Steiner point at exact (x,y); TAG = node ID    | `[2D_VERTEX_NODE_MAP]` |
| **Edge**      | Conduit polyline              | Add interior vertices of polyline as Steiner points + segments between them with marker = conduit ID | (Marker preserved on output edges; future `[2D_BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS]` can consume) |
| **Triangle**  | Subcatchment polygon          | After meshing, point-in-polygon test on each triangle's centroid; matches → TAG = `subcatch_<id>`, link to subcatchment outlet | `[2D_TRIANGLE_NODE_MAP]` |
| **Edge**     | Domain boundary               | Marker code → `outflow` / `wall` / `tidal` per user-assigned region tag | Future `[2D_BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS]` |

Junction/outfall/storage **inside** the domain → guaranteed to land at
exact 1D coords (Triangle never moves Steiner points). Junction
**outside** the domain → not in the mesh; the corresponding conduit's
endpoint is clipped at the domain boundary and that boundary vertex
inherits the conduit endpoint's coupling tag.

##### AU.4-toolbar+tab — Generate Mesh entry point + Mesh tab (shipped 2026-04-26)

Two preparatory pieces shipped ahead of the dialog itself, so the demo
flow has visible affordances even before AU.4 lands:

1. **Editing-toolbar action** `actionGenerateMesh` with the
   `:/swmmvis/CreateMesh` icon ([resources/images/create_mesh.svg](../resources/images/create_mesh.svg))
   appended after the rain-gage / climate group on
   [forms/swmmvis.ui](../forms/swmmvis.ui#L728-L734). Click currently
   logs "MeshGenerationDialog under construction"; the slot becomes
   the dialog launcher in AU.4.
2. **New "Mesh" tab on the Simulation Options dialog**
   ([include/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.h](../include/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.h)
   `buildMeshTab` / `refreshMeshList`) — **purely a selector** for
   existing mesh configurations. Lists every `.2dm` next to the active
   `.inp`; shows the search directory + the currently-active
   `[2D_MESH_FILE] FILE …` reference parsed from the `.inp`. Buttons:
   **Set Active / Remove / Refresh**. Refresh + the list view are wired
   today; Set Active / Remove become live alongside AU.4.
3. **Mesh generation lives entirely in the dedicated dialog** reached
   from the toolbar's Generate Mesh action — never on the options
   dialog. The Simulation Options dialog's role for 2D is **solver
   configuration + mesh selection**, nothing more (user-clarified
   2026-04-26).
4. **Tab visibility tied to the 2D-module toggle** on the Models tab:
   when 2D Surface Routing is checked the Mesh tab is interactive,
   when unchecked the tab stays present but disabled (so the user
   can still see what's there). Mesh tab is **always built** (not
   gated by `OPENSWMM_HAS_2D`) because file selection is a pure GUI
   concern — independent of whether SUNDIALS is available.

Why a separate tab and not a section on the existing 2D Surface
Routing tab: mesh **selection** is file-level (browse, pick); the 2D
Surface Routing tab is reserved for engine-side CVODE / dry-depth /
limiter knobs that need `OPENSWMM_HAS_2D`. Keeping these separate
means the user can pick a mesh without SUNDIALS being available.

##### Mesh boundary: SWMM subcatchments option (shipped 2026-04-26)

In addition to "(none)" → model-bbox fallback and a vector-layer
polygon, the boundary picker has a built-in **"Use SWMM subcatchment
polygons"** option. When chosen the pipeline:

1. Iterates `SWMMModelLayer::cachedSubcatchVertices(idx)` for every
   subcatchment (`cachedSubcatchCount()` rows).
2. Builds an `OGRMultiPolygon` (each subcatchment becomes one
   `OGRPolygon` with a closed exterior `OGRLinearRing`).
3. Calls `OGRGeometry::UnaryUnion()` to merge touching / overlapping
   subcatchments into a single polygon (or `OGRMultiPolygon` when
   subcatchments are disjoint).
4. Picks the largest-area polygon and extracts its exterior ring as
   the meshing domain `QPolygonF`.

Avoids requiring a separate domain shapefile when the catchment is
already represented in the SWMM model — common in demo workflows.
Fails cleanly with a dialog message when the model has no
subcatchments / no subcatchment polygons.

##### AU.5 — DTM elevation sampling

For each generated mesh vertex, sample the DTM raster via GDAL
`RasterIO` with bilinear interpolation. Out-of-raster vertices clamp
to nearest-edge value with a warning. Sampled `Z` is written to the
`[2D_VERTICES]` section's third column.

Triangle-centroid roughness defaults to `0.03` (Manning's n for grass)
unless a roughness raster is also provided — that's a follow-up.

##### AU.5b — Recursive normal-dot-product DTM thinning

**Goal.** Sample the DTM at native resolution where curvature matters,
but place fewer mesh-influence points where the surface is flat. The
mesh remains driven by the user's max-area / min-angle knobs (AU.4),
but the **candidate Steiner-point pool** harvested from the DTM is
recursively decimated so flat regions don't carry redundant points
that would otherwise force unnecessarily fine triangles.

**Inputs.**
- DTM raster at full resolution (no upstream downsampling).
- A neighborhood radius `r` (in DTM cells; default 1 = 8-connected).
- A flatness tolerance `τ ∈ (0, 1]` (default 0.999). Larger τ keeps
  more points; smaller τ thins more aggressively.
- Max iterations (default 5).

**Algorithm.**

```
points := every cell centre inside the meshing domain (full DTM res).
for iter in 1..maxIter:
    removed := 0
    for each candidate point p in points:
        N(p) := unit-normal at p, estimated from a local plane fit
                 over the rxr neighbourhood (least-squares).
        nbrs := still-present points in the rxr neighbourhood.
        if nbrs is empty: continue
        m := min over q in nbrs of dot(N(p), N(q))
        if m >= τ:
            mark p for removal     # flat — its normal aligns with all nbrs
    points -= marked
    if removed == 0: break
return points
```

The dot-product test is **per-pair-minimum**, so a candidate survives
as long as at least one neighbour has a meaningfully different
normal — i.e. some local feature (ridge, channel, slope break) needs
representation. Plateaus collapse round by round; ridges, swales,
and channel banks are preserved.

**Post-processing.**
- The thinned point set is fed to `MeshGenerator::addSteinerPoint` (or
  fed as additional region density seeds) **only inside the meshing
  domain**, and only outside the buffer of any existing
  SWMM-derived Steiner / segment / region — those win because they
  carry coupling tags (AU.3).
- DTM elevation at every retained point is sampled by `DTMSampler`
  and written into `[2D_VERTICES]` Z.
- The user controls trade-off via two dialog knobs: the flatness
  tolerance τ and the max iterations (AU.4 expansion).

**Files.**
- `include/mesh/dtmthinner.h`, `src/mesh/dtmthinner.cpp` (new) —
  pure compute, GDAL-only dependency for the source raster.
- Unit tests at `tests/gui/test_dtmthinner.cpp`:
  - flat surface → almost all points removed
  - pure ramp (constant slope) → almost all points removed
  - quadratic bowl → ridges around centre retained
  - real-world DTM tile → reasonable thinning ratio
    (assertion: ≥40% reduction at τ=0.999, no edge-band loss)

**Why this approach.** Fixed-grid downsampling loses sharp features
(flood-relevant curbs, levees, building footprints). Recursive normal
dot-product thinning is the same idea behind hierarchical mesh
simplification (e.g. Garland-Heckbert quadrics) but cheap to
implement and tunable per project. The user keeps full DTM resolution
on disk; only the **mesh density** adapts.

##### AU.6 — `SWMM2DMeshLayer` (visualization)

New layer type rendering the engine-side mesh:

- **Vertices**: small dots; coupled vertices (those listed in
  `[2D_VERTEX_NODE_MAP]`) drawn as filled markers in the SWMM-node
  colour for that node type (junction red, outfall blue, etc.) and
  labelled with node ID.  Deferred to Slice AC.4 (theming).
- **Triangles — default: elevation-coloured fill + ghost wireframe
  (shipped 2026-04-28).**  When the mesh carries DTM-sampled z values
  (any `MeshVertex::z != 0`) each triangle is painted with a solid fill
  colour derived from the centroid elevation using a 5-stop terrain
  ramp (deep blue → sea green → yellow-green → golden → near white).
  A semi-transparent wireframe overlay (50% opacity) is drawn on top so
  triangle boundaries remain legible.  When no DTM was sampled (all
  z == 0) the layer renders wireframe-only as before.
  - **Implementation:** `MeshGraphicsItem` in
    [`src/layers/swmm2dmeshlayer.cpp`](../src/layers/swmm2dmeshlayer.cpp)
    stores `QVector<SceneTri>` (scene-space triangle vertices + centroid
    z).  `rebuildSceneGeometry()` (renamed from `rebuildSceneEdges`)
    populates the triangle list alongside the deduplicated edge list and
    tracks `m_zMin` / `m_zMax` for the normalisation.  `MeshGraphicsItem`
    draws fills when `m_zMax > m_zMin`; otherwise falls back to
    wireframe.
  - **Future override (Slice AC.4 — theming):** the built-in terrain
    ramp and opacity are the hard-coded default.  The theming slice will
    add a `MeshLayerStyle` struct (colour-ramp enum/custom stops,
    wireframe-on-top toggle, opacity, variable to map — elevation /
    depth / velocity) whose active instance is passed to
    `MeshGraphicsItem` at paint time.  When results are loaded the
    mapped variable switches automatically to `swmm_2d_get_depths_bulk`
    and the ramp transitions to the depth colour scheme.
- **Triangles — results mode (Slice AC.4):** switch to **depth heatmap**
  when results are loaded — colour ramp from `swmm_2d_get_depths_bulk`
  (or `swmm_2d_get_heads_bulk` per user choice) updated each animation
  step.  The same `SceneTri` vector is reused; only per-triangle z values
  are replaced with the bulk depth query result.
- **Boundary edges**: highlighted with marker-derived colour
  (free-outflow green, wall black, tidal blue).  Deferred to Slice AC.4.
- Live during a sim: subscribes to the animation controller's
  current-time tick; pulls the bulk depth array; updates the colour
  buffer.

Extends [`OpenSWMMVisLayer`](../include/layers/openswmmvislayer.h);
batched rendering via a single `QGraphicsItem` (same pattern as Slice R
shipped for the 1D network).

> **Theming hook (Slice AC.4).** The `SceneTri` struct, `m_zMin`,
> `m_zMax`, and the `elevationColor()` ramp function in
> `swmm2dmeshlayer.cpp` are the seam the theming slice targets.  Add

##### AU.7 — `InpMeshWriter` + engine round-trip (shipped 2026-04-26)

[`mesh::InpMeshWriter`](../include/mesh/inpmeshwriter.h) renders the four
2D sections + handles the round-trip into the `.inp` (or external file).

**Output modes** — caller picks via `MeshOutputMode`:

- **`External` (default).** Writes a sibling `<basename>.2dm` next to
  the `.inp` containing the four sections. Patches the `.inp` with
  `[2D_MESH_FILE]\nFILE <relpath>\n` so the engine pulls the mesh from
  the external file at parse time. **Why default**: keeps the user's
  `.inp` clean (the sections can be tens of thousands of lines for a
  realistic mesh), supports sharing one mesh across multiple SWMM
  models, and the `.2dm` is portable as a unit with the `.inp`. User-
  stated preference, 2026-04-26.
- **`Inline`** fallback writes the four sections directly into the
  `.inp` and strips any prior `[2D_MESH_FILE]` block so the engine
  reads inline data instead of a stale external reference.

Both modes use `QSaveFile` (atomic temp + rename). On failure the
original file is left intact.

**`CouplingMap` struct** carries the SWMM-aware tagging produced by
the dialog: `vertexToNode`, `triangleToNode`, `triangleMannings`. The
writer emits the vertex/triangle key as **its tag when present** (more
robust against renumbering) or as the index otherwise.

**Manning's n source extension** (planned, dialog-side):

The writer accepts a per-triangle `triangleMannings` map; how that map
is built is the dialog's job. Three sources surfaced in
`MeshGenerationDialog`:

1. **Constant** (default 0.035 — natural channel/grass).
2. **Categorical raster** — band stores integer category id per pixel
   (e.g. land-cover code). Caller samples raster at each triangle
   centroid + looks up `category → roughness` via a small
   `QHash<int, double>` editable in the dialog.
3. **Shapefile field** — caller spatially joins each triangle centroid
   against polygons in the shapefile, reads the chosen attribute (e.g.
   `Mannings_n` field) and stores per-triangle.

`mesh::ManningsSampler` (new — planned alongside the dialog) wraps the
per-source logic and produces a `QHash<int, double>` ready to drop
into `CouplingMap::triangleMannings`. The writer remains agnostic.

**Engine round-trip + run**:

- After Apply, the GUI calls `swmm_engine_close + swmm_engine_open` to
  re-read the `.inp` with the new 2D sections — same path File → Save
  As uses today.
- The existing **Run Simulation** button (Slice M) drives the engine
  step loop. Engine-side, 2D activates automatically when
  `[2D_VERTICES]` is present (no GUI flag needed) — works whether the
  data is inline or referenced via `[2D_MESH_FILE]`.
- During the run, the new `SWMM2DMeshLayer` polls
  `swmm_2d_get_depths_bulk` per animation tick (Slice AC) and recolours.

**Tests** ([tests/gui/test_inpmeshwriter.cpp](../tests/gui/test_inpmeshwriter.cpp))
— 7 cases covering: section text contents, omitted-section guards,
external vs inline mode, relative-path emission, idempotent rewrites
(stale `[2D_MESH_FILE]` cleared), empty-mesh failure path.

#### ✅ Slice AV — Pinch-to-zoom map gestures (touch + trackpad, first cut 2026-04-26)

Wire standard pinch gestures into the map canvas so a two-finger
pinch on a touchscreen (or a trackpad pinch on macOS / Windows
Precision touchpads) zooms the canvas in / out around the gesture
centre, matching the existing wheel-zoom semantics.

**Status (2026-04-26)**: AV.1–AV.4 shipped — code compiles and
links into `SWMMVis.app`. AV.5 manual verification still pending
the user's hands-on test on macOS trackpad / touch hardware.

##### AV.1 — Gesture grab + event plumbing

`MapCanvas` (the widget that already owns wheel / mouse / key
handling — [src/map/mapcanvas.cpp:1119](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp#L1119))
gains a single `grabGesture(Qt::PinchGesture)` call in its
constructor and an override of `bool event(QEvent*)` that
dispatches `QEvent::Gesture` to a new private
`gestureEvent(QGestureEvent*)` helper. All other event handlers
(`mousePressEvent`, `wheelEvent`, etc.) stay untouched so existing
tools keep working unchanged.

Why a separate `event()` override instead of folding pinch into a
tool: scroll-wheel zoom is already tool-independent
([mapcanvas.cpp:1121](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp#L1121) — "always
active, regardless of which tool is selected"). Pinch should
behave the same way — the user expects to pinch-zoom even while
the Select or Identify tool is active.

##### AV.2 — Pinch handler reuses `zoomAroundCursor`

`MapCanvas::zoomAroundCursor(double factor, const QPoint
&viewportPos)` ([mapcanvas.cpp:1379](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp#L1379))
already does the right math: anchors a scene point under a viewport
pixel, clamps scale to `[1e-9, 1e6]`, pre-expands the scene rect,
and emits `extentChanged` / `scaleChanged`. The pinch handler
delegates straight to it:

```cpp
void MapCanvas::gestureEvent(QGestureEvent *event)
{
    if (auto *g = static_cast<QPinchGesture *>(
            event->gesture(Qt::PinchGesture)))
    {
        if (g->changeFlags() & QPinchGesture::ScaleFactorChanged)
        {
            // QPinchGesture::scaleFactor() is the *incremental* factor
            // since the previous update — multiplies cleanly with our
            // existing zoom step semantics.
            const QPoint vp = mapFromGlobal(g->centerPoint().toPoint());
            zoomAroundCursor(g->scaleFactor(), vp);
        }
        event->accept();
    }
}
```

Two subtleties worth noting in code comments:
- `scaleFactor()` is the **incremental** factor since the last
  `gestureUpdated`, not the cumulative factor since gesture start —
  perfect for chaining through `zoomAroundCursor` which multiplies
  the current transform.
- `centerPoint()` is delivered in **global** screen coordinates;
  convert with `mapFromGlobal` before handing to
  `zoomAroundCursor` (which expects viewport pixels). Skipping the
  conversion is the most likely bug source on a multi-monitor
  setup.

##### AV.3 — Edge cases

- **Gesture cancelled** (`Qt::GestureCanceled`): no rollback needed
  — each `scaleFactor()` was already applied incrementally; the
  user just stops pinching.
- **Tiny scale factors**: `zoomAroundCursor` already early-outs on
  `qFuzzyCompare(factor, 1.0)`, so jitter near 1.0 is a no-op.
- **Clamp at extremes**: existing `qBound(1e-9, oldS * factor,
  1e6)` in `zoomAroundCursor` keeps a runaway pinch from blowing
  past sane limits.
- **Interaction with active map tools**: `QPinchGesture` does not
  consume mouse events, so a tool's mouse handlers continue to
  receive simulated single-touch input. macOS trackpad pinch fires
  *only* the gesture — no spurious mouse moves.

##### AV.4 — Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [include/map/mapcanvas.h](../include/map/mapcanvas.h) | declare `bool event(QEvent*) override` and private `void gestureEvent(QGestureEvent*)`; add `<QGestureEvent>` forward decl. |
| [src/map/mapcanvas.cpp](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp) | `grabGesture(Qt::PinchGesture)` in ctor; implement `event()` dispatcher + `gestureEvent()`; `#include <QGestureEvent>` and `<QPinchGesture>`. |

No new files, no new public API beyond the override — this is a
single-widget addition.

##### AV.5 — Verification

Programmatic gesture events are awkward to synthesise in QtTest
(the platform plugin normally produces them), so verification is
manual:

1. **macOS trackpad** (primary dev surface): two-finger pinch on
   the canvas → zooms around the gesture centre, matches wheel-zoom
   feel. Status-bar scale + coordinates update live during the
   gesture.
2. **Windows Precision touchpad**: same.
3. **Touchscreen** (if available): two-finger pinch on a Surface /
   touch monitor → same behaviour.
4. **Tool-independence**: works while Select / Pan / Zoom /
   Identify / Measure tools are active; tool's overlay (rubber
   band, measurement line) is not desynced after pinching.
5. **Extent + scale signals**: `extentChanged` and `scaleChanged`
   fire during the pinch (verified by the status-bar updating
   without releasing the gesture — same path as wheel-zoom).
6. **Wheel-zoom regression**: scroll-wheel still zooms exactly as
   before (pinch path is additive, not a replacement).

##### AV.6 — Sequencing

Independent of every other slice. Lands whenever — pure UX polish
on top of the existing zoom infrastructure. Good candidate to bundle
into the next map-UX slice rather than ship alone.

---

#### ⏳ Slice AW — User Flag Schema + Per-Category Attribute Tables + Object Tagging

**Motivation.** The engine already implements two parallel "annotate
an object with metadata" features that the GUI doesn't surface yet:

1. **Legacy `[TAGS]` section** — a single free-form string per
   object (SWMM 5.x parity). Stored in
   [SimulationContext.hpp:464-466](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/SimulationContext.hpp#L464-L466)
   as `node_tags` / `link_tags` / `subcatch_tags`. Parsed today,
   round-trips through `.inp`, but unreachable from any GUI control.
2. **InfoWorks ICM-style typed user flags** — a two-section design
   ([UserFlags.hpp](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/UserFlags.hpp)):
   `[USER_FLAGS]` declares the *schema* (name, `BOOLEAN` /
   `INTEGER` / `REAL` / `STRING` type, description); `[USER_FLAG_VALUES]`
   assigns concrete typed values to specific objects. Schema-level
   accessors already exist in
   [openswmm_model.h:227-265](../../openswmm.engine/include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_model.h#L227-L265);
   per-object value access and `[TAGS]` access do not.

The user wants this slice to deliver:

- **Define** custom flag schemas (name, type, description, applies-to)
  through a project-scoped editor.
- **Display** all objects of one category in an editable table on
  right-click — bulk-edit hundreds of rows at once.
- **Assign** typed flag values to objects (and the legacy single-string
  `[TAGS]` value) inline in that table and in the per-object property
  editors.
- **Persist** schema + values through `.inp` (engine sections) and
  `.oswp` (column ordering, hidden columns, last-used filters).

**Dependencies.**
- **Slice Z** (`AttributeTablePanel` + cross-view selection + query
  bar) is the substrate; AW.2 extends it with category-driven entry
  points and inline edit support.
- **Slice V** (`PreferencesManager`) provides typed accessors but is
  *not* the host for the schema editor — schemas are project state,
  not user prefs (see AW.1 risk).
- **Slice AG** (per-type property editors) hosts the per-object
  user-flag group box (AW.3); AW can ship without AG and pick up
  the property-editor surface later.
- **Engine ABI extension (AW.4)** must land in `openswmm.engine`
  before AW.1–AW.3 wire round-trip — same pattern Slice G-3 used to
  defer Tab 7 behind a documented C ABI batch.

##### AW.1 — User Flags dialog (`Tools → User Flags…`)

A new modeless `UserFlagsDialog` for editing the project's
`[USER_FLAGS]` schema. The user phrasing pointed to the Options
dialog; we host this as its own dialog instead because the schema
is *project state* (round-trips through the saved `.inp`), not a
user preference. A future "default schema for new projects"
preference under Slice V is a clean follow-up.

- **Layout**: single `QTableView` over a new `UserFlagSchemaModel`
  (`QAbstractTableModel` mirroring `UserFlags::all_defs()`). Columns:

  | # | Column      | Editor                                                | Validation |
  |---|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------|------------|
  | 1 | Name        | `QLineEdit`, uppercased on commit                     | non-empty, unique, regex `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`; conflicts highlight red |
  | 2 | Type        | `QComboBox`: BOOLEAN / INTEGER / REAL / STRING        | required   |
  | 3 | Description | `QLineEdit`                                           | optional; tooltip surfaced everywhere the column appears |
  | 4 | Applies-to  | multi-select chip group (Node sub-types: Junction / Outfall / Storage / Divider; Link sub-types: Conduit / Pump / Orifice / Weir / Outlet; Subcatchment) | at least one chip on |
  | 5 | Default     | type-appropriate editor (checkbox / spin / line-edit) | optional; if set, AW.3 pre-fills values for newly created objects |

- **Toolbar**: Add Flag, Remove (confirms when assigned values exist),
  Move Up / Down (display order propagates to the attribute table
  column ordering and to the `.inp` writer), Import from `.inp`,
  Export to `.inp`.

- **OK / Apply / Cancel** mirror `SimulationOptionsDialog`.
  - Apply diffs against the engine-side `UserFlags::all_defs()`,
    pushing through the new
    `swmm_userflag_def_add` / `_remove` / `_update` ABIs (AW.4).
  - Removing a flag with extant values prompts:
    *"42 objects have a value for `INSPECTED`. Remove anyway?"* —
    Yes drops both the def and all its values; Cancel aborts the row.
  - Renaming a flag (in-place edit on the Name column) cascades:
    the engine's `UserFlags::rename(old, new)` (AW.4) walks the
    composite key table once.

- **Persistence**: schema is engine-state → round-trips through
  `[USER_FLAGS]` in the saved `.inp`. The dialog publishes a new
  signal `SWMMModelLayer::userFlagsChanged(QStringList changedFlagNames)`
  (mirrors `optionsChanged` from Slice W.9); the attribute table
  (AW.2) and Object Browser listen and rebuild affected columns.
  Display order, hidden columns, and last-used per-category sort
  are GUI-only and persist into `.oswp` (Phase 12) under
  `"userFlagsView": { "<category>": { "columnOrder": [...], "hidden": [...] } }`.

- **Menu wiring**: `Tools → User Flags…` (added to `initializeMenus`
  between `Simulation Options…` and the existing Plugins/Preferences
  group). Disabled when no project is open, with a clear log message —
  same pattern as Slice G-1.

- **Files**:
  - `include/ui/dialogs/userflagsdialog.h` (new) +
    `src/ui/dialogs/userflagsdialog.cpp` (new ~280 lines).
  - `include/ui/models/userflagschemamodel.h` +
    `src/ui/models/userflagschemamodel.cpp` (new ~150 lines —
    pure `QAbstractTableModel`; no Qt-widget deps so it compiles
    into the leaf test target without dragging GDAL in).
  - [include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h](../include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h) /
    [src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp) —
    pass-through helpers `userFlagDefs()` / `addUserFlagDef()` /
    `removeUserFlagDef()` / `updateUserFlagDef()` plus the new
    `userFlagsChanged` signal.
  - [include/swmmvis.h](../include/swmmvis.h) /
    [src/swmmvis.cpp](../src/swmmvis.cpp) — `onUserFlags` slot +
    Tools menu wiring.

- **Tests** (leaf binary `tests/gui/test_userflagschemamodel.cpp`):
  4 cases — name regex / uniqueness, applies-to round-trip, type-
  change diff detection, schema-rename composite-key migration.

##### AW.2 — Per-category attribute table on right-click

Three entry points all opening the same `AttributeTablePanel`
(Slice Z) filtered to one category:

1. **Object Browser group node right-click** —
   [src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp:163](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp#L163)
   already routes `customContextMenuRequested` through
   `onContextMenuRequested(QPoint)`. Extend it to detect when the
   indexed item is a category header (Junctions / Conduits / …)
   and add `Show Attribute Table` above the existing
   Plot / Zoom items. Emits a new signal
   `categoryAttributeTableRequested(SWMMObjectCategory)`.
2. **Layer Tree right-click on a category sub-row** under the SWMM
   model layer (Slice T's category nodes) —
   [src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp).
   Same item, same signal, routed through `LayerTreePanel`.
3. **Canvas right-click on empty space** —
   [src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp](../src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp)
   already pops a context menu (Slice W.6). Add an
   `Attribute Tables ▶` submenu listing populated categories;
   selecting one opens the panel.

The main window's new
`SWMMVis::openCategoryAttributeTable(SWMMObjectCategory)` slot is
the single sink — it raises the `AttributeTablePanel`, switches the
panel's category combo to the target, clears any leftover query
filter, and calls `selectColumn(0)` so the user lands on a clean,
focused table.

**Bulk edit support** in the existing
`SWMMAttributeTableModel<Category>` (Slice Z designed it but didn't
implement edit):

- `Qt::ItemIsEditable` per cell when the column maps to a writable
  engine field. Most do; computed columns (e.g., `slope` for non-
  conduit links) stay read-only and render in italic.
- `setData()` writes through the per-category C ABI
  (`swmm_node_set_*`, `swmm_link_set_*`, `swmm_subcatch_set_*`,
  …) and emits `dataChanged` for the row. `Name` column writes route
  through the engine's rename helper (with a duplicate-name check
  surfaced as an inline validator).
- **Multi-select bulk edit**: select N rows, right-click on a
  column header → `Set value for selected rows…` opens a small
  modal `BulkEditDialog` carrying a single editor of the column's
  type. Apply runs `setData` over the selection. Failures (rename
  conflicts, type-bound violations) are collected and shown in a
  summary at the end — partial-success is allowed (matches the
  engine's per-row validation).
- **Undo / redo**: each edit pushes a `BulkEditCommand` onto a
  per-project `QUndoStack` (new — minimal addition to
  `SWMMVisProjectWindow`). Single-cell edits push individually so
  Ctrl+Z reverses one cell; multi-cell bulk edits push as one
  composite via `QUndoCommand::beginMacro` so the entire bulk op
  reverses in a single Ctrl+Z. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y bind to the active
  project window's stack via `QApplication::focusWidget`.
- **Validation hook**: `SWMMAttributeTableModel::validate(row,
  column, value)` returns a `QValidator::State`; invalid values
  revert the cell with a status-bar warning. (Mirrors the
  `simulationoptionshelpers.cpp` pattern from Slice G-3 — pure,
  testable, no widget dependency.)
- **Performance**: bulk operations wrap the row span in
  `beginResetModel` / `endResetModel` to avoid `dataChanged`-per-
  cell; the QUndoStack pushes one composite. A 50,000-row bulk
  SET completes in a single repaint pass.

- **Files**:
  - [include/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.h](../include/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.h) /

    extend `onContextMenuRequested` + new
    `categoryAttributeTableRequested` signal.
  - [include/ui/panels/layertreepanel.h](../include/ui/panels/layertreepanel.h) /

##### AW.3 — User-flag values + Tag column in the attribute table & property editors

Once the schema (AW.1) and edit infrastructure (AW.2) exist, expose
*values*:

**In the attribute table (`AttributeTablePanel`)**:

- For each defined `UserFlagDef` whose `applies-to` includes the
  active category, the model adds one column. Header label is
  `flag.name`; **header tooltip is `flag.description`** so users
  can see the full prose without leaving the table. Editor delegate
  is type-driven via the new `UserFlagDelegate`:
  - **BOOLEAN** → tri-state checkbox (`Unchecked` = unset,
    `PartiallyChecked` is hidden in the editor — the only states
    a user can pick are `Unset` / `YES` / `NO`)
  - **INTEGER** → `QSpinBox`
  - **REAL** → `QDoubleSpinBox` (precision pulled from
    `PreferencesManager::rendering().displayPrecision`)
  - **STRING** → `QLineEdit`
- A first **"Tag"** column (always present, free-form string) maps
  to the engine's `[TAGS]` section via the new
  `swmm_node_tag_get` / `_set` / `swmm_link_tag_get` / `_set` /
  `swmm_subcatch_tag_get` / `_set` ABIs (AW.4). Header tooltip
  reads *"Free-form text tag (legacy `[TAGS]` section). For typed,
  schema-validated metadata, define a User Flag instead."* —
  this resolves the `[TAGS]` vs `[USER_FLAGS]` overlap question
  inline.
- Empty user-flag cells render gray-italic `(unset)` — matching
  the engine's `try_get_value()` returning `nullopt`. The cell
  rendering uses `Qt::ToolTipRole` to show the flag's
  type + description on hover, so the column header tooltip is
  duplicated per cell for users who scroll past the header.

**In the per-object property editor (Slice AG)**:

- A collapsible `User Flags` group box appears below the object's
  intrinsic properties when the active project has any user flags
  applicable to the object's category. Empty if no flags apply —
  group box is hidden in that case (no "this section is empty"
  visual noise).
- Same type-driven editors as in the table.
- Reads via `swmm_userflag_object_get_*` (new ABI in AW.4); writes
  via the matching `_set_*` family. Each edit pushes a
  single-cell `BulkEditCommand` so the property editor and the
  attribute table share one undo timeline per project.

**Cross-cutting**:

- `userFlagsChanged` (signal from AW.1) triggers a column-set
  rebuild in `AttributeTablePanel`. Existing in-flight edits commit
  first; the rebuild is wrapped in `beginResetModel` /
  `endResetModel` so the view's selection is cleanly reset.
- The query bar (Slice Z.2) gains awareness of user-flag column
  names so `INSPECTED = YES AND PRIORITY <= 2` is a valid `WHERE`
  clause. The `QueryParser` field-resolver (Slice Z) gets an
  injection point: `ResolverChain::addResolver(UserFlagFieldResolver)`.

- **Files**:
  - `include/ui/models/swmmattributetablemodel.h` /
    `src/ui/models/swmmattributetablemodel.cpp` — extend with
    user-flag columns + Tag column + the per-row composite-key
    lookup against `UserFlags::values_`.
  - `include/ui/delegates/userflagdelegate.h` +
    `src/ui/delegates/userflagdelegate.cpp` (new ~120 lines) —
    `QStyledItemDelegate` returning the right editor per
    `UserFlagType`; tri-state BOOLEAN handling.
  - `include/ui/widgets/userflagsgroupbox.h` +
    `src/ui/widgets/userflagsgroupbox.cpp` (new ~140 lines) —
    composes per-flag rows, drives via the same
    `userFlagsChanged` signal.
  - `include/core/queryparser.h` (Slice Z) — extend the
    field-resolver chain to look up user-flag names with their

    coercion.
  - [include/ui/dialogs/junctioneditor.h](../include/ui/dialogs/junctioneditor.h)
    *and the other Slice AG editors* — embed the

- **Tests**:
  - 3 cases in `test_userflagschemamodel.cpp` — column rebuild

##### AW.4 — Engine API prerequisites (`openswmm.engine` work items)

The schema-level user-flag accessors already exist
([openswmm_model.h:227-265](../../openswmm.engine/include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_model.h#L227-L265))
for BOOLEAN / INTEGER / REAL. The GUI needs the following additions
before AW.1–AW.3 can ship cleanly. Track as a single dedicated batch
in `openswmm.engine/ROADMAP.md` (same pattern as Slice G-3's Tab 7
list).

| Group | Missing surface | Implementation |
|-------|-----------------|---------------|
| Schema iteration / mutation | `swmm_userflag_def_count` / `_def_get` / `_def_add` / `_def_remove` / `_def_update` / `_def_rename` | Wraps `UserFlags::all_defs()` / `define()` / a new `remove_def(name, drop_values)` / a new `rename_def(old, new)` that walks the composite-key map once. |
| String schema-level accessors | `swmm_userflag_get_string` / `_set_string` | Stub — currently only BOOLEAN / INTEGER / REAL exist (gap noted in `openswmm_model.h:267`). |
| Per-object value access | `swmm_userflag_object_get_bool` / `_int` / `_real` / `_string` (each with `int* found`) and matching `_set_*` + `_clear` | Wraps `UserFlags::set` / `try_get_value` / the new `clear(object_type, object_name, flag_name)` helper. |
| `[TAGS]` section access | `swmm_node_tag_get` / `_set`; `swmm_link_tag_get` / `_set`; `swmm_subcatch_tag_get` / `_set` | Read/write directly into `SimulationContext::node_tags` / `link_tags` / `subcatch_tags`. Empty string clears the tag (no separate `_clear`). |

    dialog → 12 existing assignments migrate (composite-key rewrite
    in `swmm_userflag_def_rename`).
11. Tag column — type `URGENT` into J42's Tag cell, save → `.inp`
    contains `TAGS NODE J42 URGENT`. Reopen → cell still reads
    `URGENT`.

##### Risks / follow-ups

- **Schema editor location.** The user phrasing pointed at the
  Options dialog. Engine-side storage of `[USER_FLAGS]` makes the
  schema project state, not user pref, so AW.1 ships as
  `Tools → User Flags…` instead. If the user wants a *cross-project
  default schema* (preference-scope), add a small "Apply default
  schema to new projects" `PreferencesManager` key in a follow-up
  slice — `PreferencesDialog` already has the slot pattern.
- **Engine ABI churn.** AW.4 is a meaningful surface addition;
  track it as a single small PR in `openswmm.engine` before AW.1
  starts. Until then AW.1 can be developed against a thin
  `SWMMModelLayer`-side mock (in-memory map mirroring `UserFlags`)
  and disabled behind a `OPENSWMM_HAS_USERFLAGS_ABI` build flag —
  same pattern Slice G-3 used for `OPENSWMM_HAS_2D`.
- **Multi-row edit performance.** Verified above; the
  `beginResetModel` + composite `QUndoCommand::beginMacro` pair
  caps a 50,000-row bulk SET at one repaint.
- **`[TAGS]` vs `[USER_FLAGS]` overlap.** The legacy single-string
  tag is technically subsumable by a STRING-typed user flag named
  `TAG`. We keep `[TAGS]` as a distinct first-class column for
  `.inp` parity with SWMM 5.x; users wanting structure define a
  user flag instead. The Tag column tooltip explains the choice
  inline.
- **Sub-types as applies-to.** The chip group surfaces sub-types
  (Junction / Outfall / Storage / Divider; Conduit / Pump / …),
  but the engine's `UserFlagDef` only models the parent kind today.
  Storing the sub-type allowlist as a description metadata prefix
  (`[NODE,JUNCTION,OUTFALL] Has the object been …`) is a hack to
  avoid an engine schema change. If the engine adds
  `UserFlagDef::scope` natively (cleaner), AW.1 migrates to it;
  until then the prefix is the carrier and the prefix is hidden
  from the description tooltip.
- **`QUndoStack` ownership.** Putting the stack on
  `SWMMVisProjectWindow` matches the rest of the per-project
  state. Future map-tool edits (Slice AE / AF) plug into the same
  stack — covered by the existing edit operations the tools push
  through `SWMMModelLayer`.
- **Column hide / reorder persistence.** Stored in `.oswp` per
  category. If `.oswp` parity slips behind, the dialog still works
  but the user's column layout resets per session — acceptable
  short-term.

##### Sequencing

- AW depends on **Slice Z** (substrate) and benefits from
  **Slice AG** (property editors) for AW.3's group-box hookup.
  AW.1 can land independently right after AW.4 (engine ABI) ships.
- Insertion in the Recommended sequence: **AW slots between Slice
  Z and Slice AG** so Z's empty-attribute-table debuts already have
  category right-click + bulk edit + tag column from AW.2 / AW.3
  the day Z ships.

#### Slice AX — Layer Stack Reordering

**Motivation.** The layer panel currently displays layers in
add-order and the map composites them in that same fixed order.
Users need to move a basemap tile layer above SWMM network
layers for context, place a raster DEM behind a mesh result,
or put a GIS vector overlay on top of everything.  This is
standard GIS behaviour (QGIS, ArcGIS Pro); without it the layer
panel is decorative but not authoritative over what the map shows.

##### AX.1 — Data model: ordered layer list

`MapCanvas` already holds a `QList<OpenSWMMVisLayer *>` layer
stack.  Add the following surface changes:

```cpp
// MapCanvas
void moveLayerUp(OpenSWMMVisLayer *layer);
void moveLayerDown(OpenSWMMVisLayer *layer);
void moveLayerTo(OpenSWMMVisLayer *layer, int newIndex);
int  layerIndex(OpenSWMMVisLayer *layer) const;
// signals
void layerOrderChanged();
```

The render compositing loop in `MapCanvas::paintEvent` already
iterates the list in order — changing the list position is
sufficient; no render path changes needed.  Raster layers blit
their `m_mapBuffer` bottom-to-top; vector/SWMM items in
`OpenSWMMVisScene` must be Z-sorted to match: call
`QGraphicsItem::setZValue(stackIndex)` on each `SWMMLayerItem`
/ `GISVectorLayerItem` after every reorder.

##### AX.2 — LayerTreePanel drag-drop reorder

`LayerTreePanel` uses a `QTreeView` + `LayerTreeModel`.  Add:

- `LayerTreeModel::supportedDropActions()` returns
  `Qt::MoveAction`.
- `LayerTreeModel::flags()` adds `Qt::ItemIsDragEnabled |
  Qt::ItemIsDropEnabled` on layer rows.
- `LayerTreeModel::dropMimeData()` decodes the dragged row's
  layer pointer and calls `MapCanvas::moveLayerTo(layer, targetRow)`.
- `LayerTreeModel::mimeTypes()` registers
  `"application/x-openswmmvis-layerptr"` to prevent cross-widget
  drops.
- Drop indicator is shown between rows (not on rows) so the
  intent (insert before / after) is unambiguous.

**Important:** the Layer Tree shows layers top-to-bottom in the
same visual order as the render stack (top of tree = drawn last =
visually on top), matching the QGIS convention.  Index 0 in the
`QList` is therefore the *bottom* layer; the tree shows it last.
`LayerTreeModel::index(row, …)` maps `row 0` → `QList.last()`.

##### AX.3 — Context menu reorder actions

Right-click a layer row → context menu gains:

| Action | Shortcut |
|--------|---------|
| Move to Top | Ctrl+Shift+PgUp |
| Move Up | Ctrl+PgUp |
| Move Down | Ctrl+PgDown |
| Move to Bottom | Ctrl+Shift+PgDown |

These call the same `MapCanvas::moveLayer*` API as drag-drop.

##### AX.4 — Persistence

`ProjectSerializer` serialises the layer list in its current
order.  On load, layers are inserted in saved order so the
visual stack is restored exactly.  The `.oswp` `"layers"` array
is already ordered; no schema change needed — the serialiser
just must not sort the list alphabetically on write (audit the
current `toJson` path).

##### Files touched

```
include/map/mapcanvas.h          + moveLayerUp/Down/To
src/map/mapcanvas.cpp
include/ui/panels/layertreepanel.h
src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp
include/ui/models/layertreemodel.h
src/ui/models/layertreemodel.cpp + drag-drop support
src/project/projectserializer.cpp (audit write order)
tests/gui/test_layertreemodel_reorder.cpp
docs/manual/04_layers.md         (Reordering Layers section)
```

##### Verify

1. Load a project with a basemap (XYZ), a GIS raster, and a
   SWMM model layer.  Drag the XYZ tile row above the SWMM row →
   map repaints with tiles composited on top of the network.
2. Right-click the raster row → Move to Top → raster covers all
   other layers.
3. Save → reopen → layer order is identical to the saved state.
4. Undo / Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) restores the previous order
   (layer reorder pushed onto the per-project `QUndoStack`).
