#### Slice AY — SWMM Object Category Reordering in Object Browser

**Motivation.** The Object Browser lists SWMM object categories
(Junctions, Conduits, Subcatchments, …) in a fixed compile-time
order.  Users sometimes want subcatchments listed before nodes,
or rain gages at the top, to match their mental model or a
client report structure.  Additionally within a category the
display order of individual objects (by name / by manual sequence)
should be user-controllable — e.g., to match the order objects
appear in a report table.

##### AY.1 — Category-level reorder

`SWMMObjectTreeModel` currently hard-codes 11 `CatXxx` root rows
in a fixed sequence.  Change to:

```cpp
// SWMMModelLayer
QList<SWMMModelLayer::Category> categoryDisplayOrder() const;
void setCategoryDisplayOrder(const QList<Category> &order);
// signals
void categoryOrderChanged();
```

Default: existing compile-time order.  Persisted in `.oswp`
under `"objectBrowserCategoryOrder": ["CatJunctions", ...]`.

`SWMMObjectTreeModel::beginResetModel()` is called when
`categoryOrderChanged()` fires so the tree rebuilds its root
rows in the new sequence.

Drag-drop within the tree's root level (category rows only, not
leaf rows) triggers `SWMMModelLayer::setCategoryDisplayOrder()`
the same way AX.2 does for layer rows.  Right-click context menu
on a category row gains Move Up / Move Down / Reset to Default.

##### AY.2 — Per-category object reorder

`SWMMObjectTreeModel` virtualieses leaves from
`SWMMModelLayer::nodeNames(cat)` in insertion order.  Add:

```cpp
// SWMMModelLayer
QList<QString>  objectDisplayOrder(Category cat) const;
void            setObjectDisplayOrder(Category cat,
                                      const QList<QString> &order);
// shorthand: apply a permutation vector returned from the model
void            applyObjectPermutation(Category cat,
                                       const QVector<int> &perm);
```

In the Object Browser tree, leaf-level drag-drop within the same
category (intra-category only; cross-category is no-op) invokes
`setObjectDisplayOrder`.  This matches the existing Slice T.2
design note ("Slice T.2: intra-category drag to reorder within
category") — AY.2 is that sub-slice now fully specified.

Default order is insertion order from the engine (`swmm_node_count`,
`swmm_node_name` iteration); "Reset to Default" restores it.
Alphabetical sort is offered as a one-shot context menu action
("Sort A→Z") that calls `applyObjectPermutation` with a
sorted permutation — it does not lock future insertions to
alphabetical.

##### AY.3 — Persistence

Two keys added to the `.oswp` session object:

```json
"objectBrowserCategoryOrder": ["CatJunctions", "CatConduits", ...],
"objectBrowserObjectOrder": {
  "CatJunctions": ["J-101", "J-102", ...],
  "CatConduits":  ["C-10", "C-11", ...]
}
```

`ProjectSerializer` reads/writes these arrays.  On load,
`SWMMModelLayer::setCategoryDisplayOrder` and
`setObjectDisplayOrder` are called before any UI is shown.

2. Expand Junctions.  Drag leaf `J-102` above `J-101` → order

3. Right-click `Subcatchments` → Reset to Default → restores

#### Slice AZ — Mesh Layer Objects in Object Browser + Per-Feature Theming

**Motivation.** `SWMM2DMeshLayer` (Slice AU) renders the 2D
mesh on the map canvas but contributes nothing to the Object
Browser — users cannot inspect, select, or theme individual mesh
features (sub-areas, open-boundary edges, breaklines, tagged
triangles) from the panel.  Additionally, because the mesh is a
continuous triangulation, users need to colour individual
sub-areas or breakline groups differently (e.g., impervious roofs
one colour, channel triangles another) to verify geometry before
running a simulation.

##### AZ.1 — Mesh object categories

Define the mesh object domain.  A `SWMM2DMeshLayer` owns the
following named feature collections:

| Category | Source | Engine tag |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| `MeshSubAreas` | polygonal zones that map to SWMM subcatchments or 2D sub-areas | `[2D_SUBAREAS]` |
| `MeshBreaklines` | enforced polylines in the triangulation | `[2D_BREAKLINES]` |
| `MeshOpenBoundaries` | boundary edges with a head/flow BC | `[2D_OPEN_BOUNDARIES]` |
| `MeshClosedBoundaries` | no-flow boundary edges | `[2D_CLOSED_BOUNDARIES]` |
| `MeshNodeMappings` | mesh vertices linked to 1D SWMM nodes | `[2D_VERTEX_NODE_MAP]` |

These are read from the engine's `[2D_*]` tagged sections (already
parsed by `MeshINPWriter` / `MeshGenerator` in Slice AU) and
stored as named feature lists on `SWMM2DMeshLayer`:

```cpp
// SWMM2DMeshLayer
struct MeshFeature { QString name; int featureIndex; };
enum MeshCategory { MeshSubAreas, MeshBreaklines,
                    MeshOpenBoundaries, MeshClosedBoundaries,
                    MeshNodeMappings };

QList<MeshFeature> meshFeatures(MeshCategory cat) const;
int                meshFeatureCount(MeshCategory cat) const;
QString            meshFeatureName(MeshCategory cat, int row) const;
```

##### AZ.2 — Object Browser integration

`ObjectBrowserPanel` currently binds to `SWMMModelLayer`.
Generalise to a `IObjectBrowserSource` interface (or a union
variant approach — whichever fits the existing panel architecture
best) so `SWMM2DMeshLayer` can also populate the browser when it
is the active/selected layer.

The simplest approach: when the user clicks a
`SWMM2DMeshLayer` row in the Layer Tree, the Object Browser
switches to show the mesh's categories instead of (or alongside)
the SWMM network categories.  A toggle or tab in the Object
Browser header lets the user pin one source while browsing the
other.

`MeshObjectTreeModel` (new, analogous to `SWMMObjectTreeModel`)
provides the virtualised tree:

```
Root
├── Sub-Areas  (N)
│   ├── SA-1
│   └── SA-2
├── Breaklines (M)
│   └── BL-1
├── Open Boundaries (K)
└── Node Mappings (P)
    └── NM-J101
```

Selection in the mesh object tree highlights the corresponding
triangles / edges on the map canvas (via `SelectionManager`
extended to `MeshFeatureRef`).  Double-click zooms to the
feature's bounding box.

```cpp
// new
include/ui/models/meshobjecttreemodel.h
src/ui/models/meshobjecttreemodel.cpp

// extended
include/selection/selectionmanager.h  + MeshFeatureRef
src/selection/selectionmanager.cpp
include/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.h + source-switching logic
src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp
```

##### AZ.3 — Per-feature theming for mesh layer

Users assign a distinct `QColor` (fill + outline) to each named
mesh feature category or to individual named features.  This is
separate from the 2D results heat-map (Slice AC) which overrides
colours at simulation time; theming here applies at rest
(geometry-inspection mode).

**Symbol struct:**

```cpp
struct MeshFeatureSymbol {
    QColor  fillColor;
    QColor  outlineColor;
    double  outlineWidth = 1.0;
    float   opacity      = 1.0f;
    bool    showLabel    = false;
};
```

**Theming levels (coarser overrides finer only when finer is
unset):**

1. **Category default** — one `MeshFeatureSymbol` per
   `MeshCategory`; stored in `SWMM2DMeshLayer`.
2. **Named-feature override** — per `MeshFeature::name`; stored
   in a `QHash<QString, MeshFeatureSymbol>` on the layer.
3. **Selection highlight** — rendered by `SelectionManager` at
   draw time on top of any stored symbol (not persisted).

**Editing:**

- Right-click a category row in the mesh Object Browser →
  `Set Category Symbol…` opens a lightweight
  `MeshSymbolDialog` (colour pickers for fill + outline,
  width spinner, opacity slider).
- Right-click a named-feature leaf → `Set Feature Symbol…` →
  same dialog scoped to that feature.
- Right-click → `Reset to Category Default` clears the
  per-feature override.
- `Layer Tree → right-click SWMM2DMeshLayer → Layer Properties…`
  opens the existing `LayerPropertiesDialog` extended with a
  **Mesh Features** tab listing all categories with their current
  colours (same `MeshSymbolDialog` inline).

**Render integration:**

`SWMM2DMeshLayer::populateScene()` (or the batched
`MeshLayerItem::paint()`) resolves the effective symbol per
feature at paint time:

```cpp
MeshFeatureSymbol effectiveSymbol(MeshCategory cat,
                                  const QString &name) const;
// → per-feature override if set, else category default
```

Z-values within the mesh scene items: breaklines above
sub-area fills, open-boundary markers above breaklines —
consistent fixed within-mesh Z ordering, not user-configurable.

##### AZ.4 — Persistence

```json
// .oswp session → layers array → SWMM2DMeshLayer entry
"meshCategorySymbols": {
  "MeshSubAreas":       { "fill": "#c8e6c9", "outline": "#388e3c", "width": 1.0 },
  "MeshBreaklines":     { "fill": "#ffcc00", "outline": "#cc9900", "width": 2.0 },
  "MeshOpenBoundaries": { "fill": "#0000ff", "outline": "#0000aa", "width": 1.5 }
},
"meshFeatureSymbols": {
  "SA-rooftop": { "fill": "#ff5722", "outline": "#bf360c", "width": 1.0 }
}
```

`ProjectSerializer` reads/writes these under the layer's JSON
object.  If a category key is absent, the layer's compiled
default colour is used (no forward-compat breakage).

#### ✅ Slice H-3 — Measure Tool v2: CRS-accurate geodesics, area mode, per-vertex labels, unit panel

**Motivation.** The existing measure tool has four compounding
problems that make it unreliable in practice:

1. **Inaccurate geodesics for geographic CRS.** The distance
   formula uses a hard-coded spherical radius (6 371 000 m) via the
   Haversine formula, ignoring the WGS-84 oblate-spheroid ellipsoid
   (semi-major 6 378 137 m, 1/f ≈ 298.257).  For a 10 km segment
   at mid-latitude this introduces a ~50 m error (~0.5%).  Area
   uses a simplified spherical-excess formula with the same
   approximation.

2. **No UI for mode or unit selection.** `MeasureMode` and
   `MeasureUnit` exist in code but no visible control lets the
   user switch between Distance/Area or pick a unit; the tool
   silently defaults to Distance/Metres forever.

3. **Only the final total is labelled.** In Distance mode only
   one label is painted at the last vertex, showing the grand
   total.  The user cannot read off where the 2 km mark is, or
   how long each individual segment is.

4. **No finalisation state.** Double-click adds the terminal
   vertex but the tool remains open: subsequent left-clicks keep
   appending vertices to the existing measurement.  The user has
   no feedback that the measurement is "done".

##### H-3.1 — CRS-accurate distance calculation

Replace the hand-rolled Haversine sphere with a proper geodesic
path through GDAL:

**Strategy:**
- On `activate()` (and whenever `canvasSRS()` changes), build
  and cache an `OGRCoordinateTransformation *m_toWgs84` from the
  canvas CRS to EPSG:4326 using
  `canvasSRS()->createTransformationTo(*wgs84SRS)`.
  Destroy and rebuild the transform if the canvas SRS changes
  (connect to `MapCanvas::canvasSRSChanged` or rebuild lazily in
  `geodesicDistance`).

**Geographic CRS (canvas is already lon/lat):**
- Transform the two points to WGS-84 lon/lat (a no-op if the
  canvas CRS is already EPSG:4326, but correct if it is e.g.
  EPSG:4269 / NAD83 geographic).
- Compute the ellipsoidal geodesic distance using the
  `OGRSpatialReference::GetSemiMajor()` / `GetInvFlattening()`
  from the WGS-84 SRS and the Vincenty direct formula, or use
  GDAL ≥ 3.7's `OGRLineString::geodesicLength()` if available
  at compile time (guarded by `#if GDAL_VERSION_NUM >= GDAL_COMPUTE_VERSION(3,7,0)`).
- Fallback (older GDAL): apply the improved Haversine / Bowring
  iterative formula using the actual ellipsoid semi-axes rather
  than the spherical constant.

**Projected CRS:**
- Keep the existing `sqrt(dx²+dy²) × linearUnitsToMetres()`
  path — it is already accurate for projected planar systems.

**Local / undefined CRS:**
- Raw Euclidean, treat result as dimensionless (display "units"
  instead of a distance symbol); no conversion applied.

```cpp
// private cache in OpenSWMMVisMapToolMeasure
OGRCoordinateTransformation *m_toWgs84 = nullptr;  // owned
// rebuilt in activate() and on srsChanged()
void rebuildTransform();
double geodesicDistance(const QPointF &a, const QPointF &b) const;
```

##### H-3.2 — CRS-accurate area calculation

**Geographic CRS:**
- Transform all polygon vertices to WGS-84 lon/lat via
  `m_toWgs84` (same cached transform as H-3.1).
- Apply the standard spherical-excess formula with the correct
  WGS-84 mean-radius (`R = 6 371 008.8` m) rather than the
  current approximate constant.
- For higher accuracy when GDAL ≥ 3.7 is available, use
  `OGRPolygon::geodesicArea()`.

**Projected CRS:**
- Keep Shoelace × `linearUnitsToMetres()²` — already correct.

**Local CRS:**
- Raw Shoelace, display "units²".

##### H-3.3 — Separate distance and area unit selectors

The current `MeasureUnit` enum conflates distance and area units
into a single field.  Replace it with two independent properties
backed by `MeasurementUnitManager`:

```cpp
// Header changes — remove MeasureUnit enum entirely
MeasurementUnitManager::DistanceUnit distanceUnit() const;
void setDistanceUnit(MeasurementUnitManager::DistanceUnit);

MeasurementUnitManager::AreaUnit areaUnit() const;
void setAreaUnit(MeasurementUnitManager::AreaUnit);

// Remove:
//   MeasureUnit m_unit
//   static QString unitSymbol(MeasureUnit)
//   double convertDistance(double) const
//   double convertArea(double) const
// Replace with delegation to MeasurementUnitManager:
//   MeasurementUnitManager::formatDistance(metres, m_distanceUnit)
//   MeasurementUnitManager::formatArea(sqm, m_areaUnit)
```

The two units are independent: switching from Distance to Area
mode preserves both unit choices so returning to Distance mode
restores the user's last distance unit.

Default: `DistanceUnit::Metres`, `AreaUnit::SquareMetres`.

##### H-3.4 — Per-vertex cumulative distance labels

In **Distance mode**, paint a cumulative-distance label at each
committed vertex (not just the last):

```
[0.00 m]——[142.3 m]——[308.7 m]——[mouse: 400.1 m?]
    v0           v1           v2          (rubber-band)
```

- Each label shows the cumulative distance from `v0` to `vN`
  using `MeasurementUnitManager::formatDistance()`.
- The label for `v0` (start) shows `0.00 m` (or is omitted if
  space is tight — configurable by a const flag for now).
- A lightweight ghost label near the mouse cursor shows
  `+ΔsegLen / Σtotal` while rubber-banding (segment-delta /
  running total).
- Labels use the same pill background (translucent yellow) as
  the current total label, but 1–2 pt smaller font to reduce
  clutter.
- When the segment count exceeds a threshold (e.g., 20 vertices),
  labels on interior vertices are suppressed and only first,
  last, and every-N-th vertex labels are shown to avoid overlap
  (configurable const `kMaxLabelledVertices = 20`).

In **Area mode**, paint a single centroid label showing the
current polygon area (updating live as the mouse moves), plus
the vertex count in parentheses: `3 847.2 m²  (6 pts)`.
No per-vertex labels are needed in area mode.

##### H-3.5 — Area mode visual overlay

When in **Area mode** and ≥ 2 vertices exist:

- Draw a **semi-transparent fill** over the in-progress polygon
  formed by `[v0, v1, …, vN, mousePos]` using a pale blue
  (`QColor(100, 149, 237, 60)`).
- Rubber-band shows *two* dashed lines from the last vertex: one
  to the current mouse position, and one from the mouse position
  back to `v0` (closing the polygon preview).
- The outline is drawn as a solid red pen (same as Distance
  mode) after the polygon is closed.
- On double-click (finalise): fill becomes slightly more opaque
  (`alpha 100`) and the closing segment becomes solid rather
  than dashed to indicate the shape is locked.

##### H-3.6 — Finalisation state (double-click terminates)

Add `bool m_finalized = false` to the class.

Behaviour changes:

| Event | Not finalized | Finalized |
|-------|--------------|-----------|
| Left-click | Add vertex | Start new measurement (calls `clearMeasurement()` first, then adds first vertex) |
| Double-click | Finalise (`m_finalized = true`) | — (already finalized; no-op) |
| `Escape` | If ≥1 vertex: remove last vertex (same as Backspace); if 0 vertices: no-op | Clear measurement (`m_finalized = false`, `m_vertices.clear()`) |
| `Backspace` | Remove last vertex | No-op |
| `activate()` | — | Resets `m_finalized = false` |

**Double-click de-duplication:** Qt fires `mousePressEvent` for
the first click, then `mouseDoubleClickEvent` *instead of* the
second `mousePressEvent`.  The existing guard
`m_vertices.last() != QPointF(mx, my)` prevents the
double-click position from being added twice; that guard is
sufficient and should be retained.

**Visual indication of finalized state:** When `m_finalized`,
draw all committed segments with a slightly thicker pen (width 3
instead of 2) so the user can see the measurement is locked.

#### ✅ Slice H-4 — Scale bar CRS-accurate rendering

**Motivation.** `MapCanvas::renderScaleBar()` computes the bar
width as:

```cpp
double mapUnitsPerPixel = m_extent.width() / width();   // CRS units / pixel
double barMapUnits      = maxLen * mapUnitsPerPixel;     // ← CRS units, NOT metres
// …
m_scaleBarSettings->formatLabel(barMapUnits);           // expects metres
```

`MapExtent::width()` returns degrees when the canvas CRS is
geographic (WGS-84 / NAD83), so `barMapUnits` is in degrees.
`ScaleBarSettings::formatLabel()` always treats its argument as
metres (documented in the header comment), so the scale bar
displays nonsense: a 100-pixel bar that spans 0.01° is labelled
"0.01 m" instead of ~1.1 km.  For projected CRS (UTM, etc.) the
existing code happens to be correct only because the CRS linear
unit is already metres; a projected CRS whose linear unit is feet
(e.g. `EPSG:2263 — NY State Plane, feet`) would also be wrong.

The same bug exists in `ScaleBarItem::paint()` in
`graphicsitems.cpp`, though that class is not yet instantiated.

##### H-4.1 — `MapCanvas::metresPerPixel()` helper

Add a private `const` method that returns the ground distance
(in metres) represented by one horizontal pixel at the current
canvas centre:

```cpp
// mapcanvas.h — private
double metresPerPixel() const;
```

```cpp
// mapcanvas.cpp
double MapCanvas::metresPerPixel() const
{
    if (width() <= 0 || !m_extent.isValid())
        return 1.0;

    const double mapp = m_extent.width() / width();   // CRS units / pixel

    if (!m_canvasSRS)
        return mapp;   // local / unknown — treat as raw

    if (m_canvasSRS->isProjected())
        return mapp * m_canvasSRS->linearUnitsToMetres();

    if (m_canvasSRS->isGeographic())
    {
        // Convert longitude-degrees/pixel → metres/pixel at the
        // centre latitude of the current view.
        // Approximation: distance along a parallel at latitude φ is
        //   d = R · |Δλ| · cos(φ)
        // where R is the WGS-84 semi-major axis (6 378 137 m) and
        // Δλ is in radians.  Error < 0.05 % for view extents
        // < 10° wide, which is more than sufficient for a scale bar.
        constexpr double R = 6378137.0;
        const double lat   = qDegreesToRadians(m_extent.centerY());
        return mapp * (M_PI / 180.0) * R * std::abs(std::cos(lat));
    }

    return mapp;   // local CRS — no conversion
}
```

This helper is intentionally simpler than the measure tool's
full GDAL-geodesic path (H-3.1): a scale bar only needs the
local scale at the view centre, where the flat-earth cosine
formula is accurate enough.  The measure tool needs accuracy
over potentially long segments and therefore uses GDAL.

##### H-4.2 — Fix `MapCanvas::renderScaleBar()`

Replace the existing distance calculation with one that works
through `metresPerPixel()`:

```cpp
void MapCanvas::renderScaleBar(QPainter &painter) const
{
    const int margin = 10;
    if (width() <= 0 || !m_extent.isValid() || m_extent.width() <= 0)
        return;

    const int    maxLen   = m_scaleBarSettings->maxBarLength();
    const double mpp      = metresPerPixel();   // metres per screen pixel

    // Choose a "nice" bar length in metres
    double barMetres   = maxLen * mpp;
    double magnitude   = std::pow(10.0, std::floor(std::log10(barMetres)));
    double nice        = barMetres / magnitude;
    if      (nice < 2.0) nice = 1.0;
    else if (nice < 5.0) nice = 2.0;
    else                 nice = 5.0;
    barMetres = nice * magnitude;

    // Convert back to pixels for drawing
    int barPixels = static_cast<int>(std::round(barMetres / mpp));
    if (barPixels < 2) barPixels = 2;

    // … position, draw line + ticks, then:
    painter.drawText(barX, barY - 6,
                     m_scaleBarSettings->formatLabel(barMetres));
                     //                                ↑ metres — correct
}
```

The key change is:
- Input to `formatLabel` is now **metres** regardless of canvas CRS.
- `ScaleBarSettings::formatLabel()` already handles m ↔ km auto-
  switching and user-selected Feet / Miles / Kilometres.
- `barPixels` is derived from `barMetres / mpp` (round-trip via
  metres), so the drawn bar length is always self-consistent.

##### H-4.3 — Fix `ScaleBarItem::paint()` (graphicsitems.cpp)

`ScaleBarItem` is not yet instantiated but should be fixed in
the same pass to avoid a latent bug when it is wired up.

Add `m_metresPerPixel` alongside the existing
`m_mapUnitsPerPixel` and update `setMapUnitsPerPixel` to also
accept the metres value, OR add a new setter:

```cpp
// graphicsitems.h — ScaleBarItem
void setMetresPerPixel(double mpp) { m_metresPerPixel = mpp; }
// …
double m_metresPerPixel = 1.0;   // metres / screen pixel (CRS-aware)
```

In `ScaleBarItem::paint()` replace:

```cpp
double barMapUnits = maxLen * m_mapUnitsPerPixel;
```

with:

```cpp
double barMetres = maxLen * m_metresPerPixel;
```

and thread `barMetres` through the rest of the method, including
the `formatLabel` call.

When `ScaleBarItem` is eventually instantiated, its caller must
supply `metresPerPixel()` from the owning `MapCanvas`.

##### H-4.4 — Scale bar label for local / unknown CRS

When `m_canvasSRS` is null or `isLocal()`, the scale bar has no
real-world meaning.  Display the bar with a "units" suffix
rather than metres to avoid misleading the user:

```cpp
// ScaleBarSettings::formatLabel  — add a new overload or a flag
QString ScaleBarSettings::formatLabel(double value, bool rawUnits) const
{
    if (rawUnits)
        return QStringLiteral("%1 units").arg(value, 0, 'g', 3);
    // … existing switch on m_units …
}
```

`MapCanvas::renderScaleBar()` passes `rawUnits = true` when
`m_canvasSRS` is null or `isLocal()`.

## Phase 12 — Project File Persistence (.oswp + .inp)

### 12.0 IO Plugin Integration

The refactored engine ships a plugin SDK
([include/openswmm/plugin_sdk/](../../openswmm.engine/include/openswmm/plugin_sdk/)):
`IInputPlugin.hpp`, `IOutputPlugin.hpp`, `IReportPlugin.hpp`. Plugins ship as shared libs
and are passed to `swmm_engine_open(engine, path, rpt, out, input_plugin_lib)`. The GUI
treats the engine's plugin SDK as its IO substrate so file format support is extensible
without GUI code changes.

#### IOPluginRegistry

File: `include/io/iopluginregistry.h`, `src/io/iopluginregistry.cpp`.

- Discovers plugin libraries at app startup from `<install>/plugins/io/` plus any user-
  configured directories (Tools → Program Preferences → Plugins).
- Each plugin self-describes: name, version, supported extensions, read/write capability.
- `.inp` is itself a built-in InputPlugin so it routes through the same path; this keeps
  the GUI agnostic.
- File → Open and File → Save As dialogs build their format filter list from the registry —
  no hard-coded `*.inp` filter dispatch.
- **Files**: [src/io/iopluginregistry.cpp](../src/io/iopluginregistry.cpp),
  [include/openswmm/plugin_sdk/IInputPlugin.hpp](../../openswmm.engine/include/openswmm/plugin_sdk/IInputPlugin.hpp),
  [include/openswmm/plugin_sdk/IOutputPlugin.hpp](../../openswmm.engine/include/openswmm/plugin_sdk/IOutputPlugin.hpp),
  [include/openswmm/plugin_sdk/IReportPlugin.hpp](../../openswmm.engine/include/openswmm/plugin_sdk/IReportPlugin.hpp).

#### GeoPackage import / observed-data writes

File → Import GeoPackage uses the dual interface in
[openswmm_geopackage.h](../../openswmm.engine/include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_geopackage.h).
Model definitions are loaded into a session; observed-data writes (calibration import,
Phase 11.1) use the bulk-insert API for the 10–100x speedup vs. row-at-a-time inserts.

#### Plugins menu (Tools → Plugins)

- List discovered plugins, enable/disable, view metadata, open plugin documentation.
- `[PLUGINS]` `.inp` section is editable from the Simulation Options dialog (Phase 3.9
  Tab 7) so plugins can be wired into specific models.

**Verify:** Discover a sample IO plugin from `plugins/io/`; format appears in File → Open
filter; importing a `.gpkg` populates a session; observed-data write to `.gpkg` completes
in a single transaction.

### 12.1 SWMM .inp Read/Write
- `swmm_engine_open(engine, inp, rpt, out, nullptr)` handles all .inp reading
- `swmm_model_write(engine, path)` handles .inp writing (all standard sections)
- GUI-only sections (labels, profiles, calibration) appended as `[SWMMVIS_*]` custom sections or stored separately in `.oswp`

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "title": "My Project",
  "notes": "",
  "crs": "EPSG:32614",
  "extent": { "xmin": 0, "ymin": 0, "xmax": 5000, "ymax": 5000 },
```

### 12.3 ProjectSerializer
File: `include/project/projectserializer.h`

Serializes/deserializes all session, layer, theme, calibration, and display state.

### 12.4 Combine Projects
`CombineProjectsDialog`: load a second `.inp` file; select offset for coordinates; merges
all objects into the current project (calls `swmm_node_add()`, `swmm_link_add()`, etc.).

- **Copy** → clipboard for tables, charts, and map viewport.

## Slice W — WMTS Basemap Rendering Fix

### Problem summary

`WMTSLayer` failed to render tiles after being added from the `WMTSConnectionDialog`.
Three independent bugs conspired to produce a blank layer:

1. **`parseCapabilities` — `TileMatrixSetLink` nesting**
   The capabilities parser called `reader.readElementText()` on the container element
   `<TileMatrixSetLink>`, which with Qt's default `ErrorOnUnexpectedElement` behaviour
   raised an XML error as soon as it encountered the `<TileMatrixSet>` child element.
   This either aborted parsing entirely (error path) or appended an empty string
   to `tileMatrixSetIds` (skip-children path). Either way `m_activeTileMatrixSet`
   was never set, so `fetchCache()` returned immediately without requesting any tiles.

2. **`selectTileMatrix` — assumed ascending sort order**
   The zoom-level picker iterated matrices top-to-bottom and broke on the first matrix
   finer than the canvas scale. WMTS capabilities XML has no mandated ordering, so
   services that list finest-first (or in random order) produced a wrong zoom level,
   leading to tile-key mismatches between `fetchCache` and `render`.

3. **`TopLeftCorner` axis order for geographic CRS**
   OGC WMTS specifies that `TopLeftCorner` coordinates follow the axis order of the
   declared CRS. For EPSG:4326 that is *(latitude, longitude)* = *(Y, X)*, not *(X, Y)*.
   The old parser blindly assigned `parts[0] → topLeftX`, placing tiles at mirrored
   positions when the tile matrix set used a geographic CRS.

### Additional improvements shipped with the fix

- **`WMTSLayerInfo::styles`** — `parseCapabilities` now extracts style identifiers from
  `<Style><ows:Identifier>` inside each Layer element. The `WMTSConnectionDialog` style
  combo is populated from capabilities rather than hard-coded to `"default"`.
- **`WMTSLayerInfo::wgs84BoundingBox`** — `ows:WGS84BoundingBox` is now parsed so the
  layer extent is set correctly and `fullExtent()` can zoom to the layer's geographic
  coverage.
- **`isBasemapLayer() = true`** — `WMTSLayer` now overrides this virtual to match
  `XYZTileLayer`, so world-spanning WMTS services are excluded from `fullExtent()`
  calculations just like XYZ tile basemaps.
- **Duplicate toolbar button removed** — `actionAddWMSData` ("Add WMS/WMTS Data") was
  functionally identical to `actionAddBasemap` ("Add Basemap"). The former was removed
  from the toolbar and its action definition deleted from `swmmvis.ui`.

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/layers/wmtslayer.cpp` | Rewrote `parseCapabilities` with `inTMSLink`/`inBBox`/`inStyle` state tracking; post-process geographic CRS axis swap; rewrote `selectTileMatrix` to be sort-order independent |
| `include/layers/wmtslayer.h` | Added `WMTSLayerInfo::styles`; added `isBasemapLayer()` override |
| `src/ui/dialogs/wmtsconnectiondialog.cpp` | Style combo populated from parsed capabilities |
| `forms/swmmvis.ui` | Removed `actionAddWMSData` toolbar entry and action definition |
| `src/swmmvis.cpp` | Removed `connect(ui->actionAddWMSData, …)` |

### Verify

1. Connect to a standard OGC WMTS service (e.g. USGS National Map WMTS) — the layer list
   populates, style and tile matrix set combos show real values from capabilities.
2. Accept the dialog — tiles appear on the canvas within one or two refresh cycles.
3. Pan and zoom — tiles update correctly at all zoom levels.
4. Open a project with only a WMTS basemap — "Zoom to Full Extent" does NOT try to zoom
   to the entire world (isBasemapLayer guard respected).
5. The toolbar shows one basemap button ("Add Basemap"), not two.

## 🔧 Slice AB-2 — Add Basemap Dialog (XYZ Tiles / WMS·WMTS / ArcGIS REST, auth + serialisation)

**Status:** in progress.

**Motivation.** The current `actionAddBasemap` wires directly to
`WMTSConnectionDialog`, a single-protocol dialog with no authentication,
no saved connections, and no project persistence of basemap layers.
Users who need OSM/Google XYZ tiles, a corporate WMS, or an ArcGIS
Online/Enterprise REST service cannot configure them through the existing
UI.  This slice replaces the stub with a full-featured multi-tab "Add
Basemap" dialog modelled on QGIS's equivalent workflow (studied from
the QGIS source in the workspace at `../QGIS`), adapted to the
`XYZTileLayer` / `WMSLayer` / `WMTSLayer` stack already present in
OpenSWMMVis, and adds:

- Saved named connections with optional Basic-auth credentials stored
  encrypted in `QSettings` (no third-party keychain required — own
  AES-256-CBC implementation, matching QGIS's `QgsAuthCrypto` approach).
- Project persistence: basemap layer descriptions serialised into the
  `.oswp` sidecar so basemaps are restored on project re-open.
- ArcGIS REST tile service support via `XYZTileLayer` with `ZYX`
  axis order (no separate class needed — ArcGIS tiled MapServer URLs
  are structurally identical to XYZ tiles with swapped y/x indices).
- Arbitrary HTTP request headers (Referer, User-Agent, API keys, etc.)
  on all three connection types, matching QGIS's `QgsHttpHeaders` model.

---

### AB-2.0 — Data structures

All connection descriptors live in
`include/connections/basemapconnection.h` (new file, structs only,
no `Q_OBJECT`).

#### `BasemapHttpHeaders`

A thin alias for `QMap<QString, QString>` with one named constant:

```cpp
using BasemapHttpHeaders = QMap<QString, QString>;
static constexpr const char *kRefererKey = "referer";
```

`Referer` is always stored under the lower-case key `"referer"` for
compatibility with QGIS's `QgsHttpHeaders::KEY_REFERER` convention.
Arbitrary extra headers (e.g., `User-Agent`, `X-Api-Key`) are stored
alongside it in the same map.

In `QSettings` the map is written as individual values under an
`http-header/` sub-group:

```
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/http-header/referer      = "..."
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/http-header/User-Agent   = "..."
```

This mirrors the QGIS `PATH_PREFIX = "http-header/"` convention.

In the `.oswp` JSON the map is stored as a nested object under `"headers"`:

```json
"headers": { "referer": "https://mysite.com", "User-Agent": "OpenSWMM" }
```

#### `BasemapAuth`

```cpp
struct BasemapAuth {
    QString  username;   // HTTP Basic-auth username (may be empty)
    QString  password;   // plaintext at runtime; encrypted at rest
};
```

#### `XYZConnection`

Mirrors `QgsXyzConnection` (`src/providers/wms/qgsxyzconnection.h`).

```cpp
struct XYZConnection {
    QString           name;
    QString           urlTemplate;       // {z}/{x}/{y} or {z}/{y}/{x}
    int               zMin  = 0;
    int               zMax  = 19;
    // Tile pixel ratio: 0=Undefined, 1=Standard 96 DPI (256 px),
    // 2=HiDPI 192 DPI (512 px).  Matches QGIS TilePixelRatio enum.
    // @2x in a URL template is a literal string the user types;
    // this field is a DPI rendering hint only.
    int               tilePixelRatio = 0;
    TileAxisOrder     axisOrder = ZXY;   // ZXY=standard; ZYX=ArcGIS REST
    BasemapHttpHeaders httpHeaders;      // "referer" key = Referer header
    BasemapAuth        auth;
};
```

**`TileAxisOrder` enum:**

```cpp
enum TileAxisOrder { ZXY, ZYX };  // ZXY = standard OSM; ZYX = ArcGIS REST
```

#### `WMSConnection`

Mirrors QGIS `QgsOwsConnection` fields relevant to WMS/WMTS basemaps.
WMS vs WMTS is auto-detected from the URL (see AB-2.4 Tab 2).

```cpp
struct WMSConnection {
    QString  name;
    QString  url;
    QString  version;                    // "1.1.1"/"1.3.0"; empty=auto
    bool     ignoreAxisOrientation = false;  // skip CRS-declared axis order
    bool     invertAxisOrientation = false;  // force lat/lon swap
    bool     ignoreGetMapURI       = false;  // use base URL, not caps URI
    // DPI mode bitmask: 0=None,1=QGIS,2=UMN,4=GeoServer,7=All
    int      dpiMode = 7;
    // 0=Undefined,1=Standard 96DPI,2=HiDPI 192DPI
    int      tilePixelRatio = 0;
    bool     smoothPixmapTransform = true;
    BasemapHttpHeaders httpHeaders;
    BasemapAuth        auth;
};

// WMTS uses the same struct; protocol auto-detected from URL.
using WMTSConnection = WMSConnection;
```

#### `ArcGISRestConnection`

Mirrors `QgsArcGisConnectionSettings`.

```cpp
struct ArcGISRestConnection {
    QString  name;
    QString  url;
    QString  urlPrefix;         // optional proxy URL prefix
    // Portal/Enterprise API endpoints (empty = public ArcGIS Online).
    QString  contentEndpoint;   // e.g. .../sharing/rest/content
    QString  communityEndpoint; // e.g. .../sharing/rest/community
    BasemapHttpHeaders httpHeaders;
    BasemapAuth        auth;
};
```

These structs are value types (no `Q_OBJECT`, no signals).

---

### AB-2.1 — Encryption helper (`BasemapCrypto`)

`QCA` (Qt Cryptographic Architecture) is not a dependency of the
current project and adding it would be disproportionate.  Instead,
implement a minimal self-contained AES-256-CBC wrapper using
**Qt 6's built-in `QCryptographicHash` + XOR key stream** — or,
preferably, link `OpenSSL` (already required by `Qt6Network`) through
`EVP_*` APIs.  The interface mirrors QGIS `QgsAuthCrypto`:

```
include/core/basemapcrypto.h
src/core/basemapcrypto.cpp
```

```cpp
class BasemapCrypto
{
public:
    // Derive a 32-byte key from passphrase + salt using PBKDF2-SHA256
    // (100 000 iterations).  Returns hex-encoded salt + IV used.
    static QString encrypt(const QString &passphrase,
                           const QString &plaintext,
                           QString *saltAndIvOut = nullptr);

    // Decrypt a string produced by encrypt().
    // saltAndIv must be the value written by encrypt().
    static QString decrypt(const QString &passphrase,
                           const QString &ciphertext,
                           const QString &saltAndIv);

    // One-way hash for verifying the passphrase at load-time.
    static QString passwordHash(const QString &passphrase);
    static bool    verifyPasswordHash(const QString &passphrase,
                                      const QString &hash);
};
```

**Implementation choice — no extra dependency:**
Qt 6's `QSslKey` + `QSslCipher` live behind `Qt6Network` (already
linked).  However the simplest zero-dependency path that ships
on macOS, Linux, and Windows without QCA is:

1. Use `QCryptographicHash::hash(passphrase + salt, SHA256)` as the
   AES-256 key.
2. Use `OpenSSL`'s `EVP_EncryptInit_ex(EVP_aes_256_cbc(), ...)` —
   OpenSSL headers are available via Qt's private headers or vcpkg's
   `openssl` port (already in `vcpkg.json` via Qt dependencies).
3. If `OpenSSL` symbols are unavailable at link time, fall back to an
   XOR cipher with the SHA-256 key (obfuscation, not encryption) and
   log a warning.  Production builds on standard platforms will always
   have OpenSSL.

The passphrase used as the encryption key is a per-installation
**application secret** derived from:

```
appSecret = QCryptographicHash::hash(
    QSysInfo::machineUniqueId() + "OpenSWMM-BasemapStore-v1",
    QCryptographicHash::Sha256).toHex()
```

This binds stored credentials to the machine (matching the QGIS
approach of using the master password / keychain key).  Credentials
moved to another machine will fail to decrypt; the user re-enters
them.  This is the correct security model for local credential
storage without a system keychain dependency.

### AB-2.2 — Connection store (`BasemapConnectionStore`)

```
include/connections/basemapconnectionstore.h
src/connections/basemapconnectionstore.cpp
```

Singleton (`SWMMVis::initializeBasemapStore()` creates it on first use).
Wraps `QSettings` under `SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/`.
WMTS connections share the WMS list (same struct, auto-detected on load).

```cpp
enum class BasemapProvider { XYZ, WMS, ArcGIS };

class BasemapConnectionStore : public QObject
{
    Q_OBJECT
public:
    static BasemapConnectionStore &instance();

    QList<XYZConnection>          xyzConnections()  const;
    void addOrUpdate(const XYZConnection &c);

    QList<WMSConnection>          wmsConnections()  const;  // includes WMTS
    void addOrUpdate(const WMSConnection &c);

    QList<ArcGISRestConnection>   arcgisConnections() const;
    void addOrUpdate(const ArcGISRestConnection &c);

    void remove(const QString &name, BasemapProvider p);

signals:
    void connectionsChanged(BasemapProvider p);

private:
    // Passwords encrypted with BasemapCrypto; httpHeaders map written
    // as individual http-header/{key} QSettings entries.
    void saveXYZ(const XYZConnection &c);
    XYZConnection loadXYZ(const QString &name) const;
    void saveWMS(const WMSConnection &c);
    WMSConnection loadWMS(const QString &name) const;
    void saveArcGIS(const ArcGISRestConnection &c);
    ArcGISRestConnection loadArcGIS(const QString &name) const;
};
```

**Complete QSettings layout:**

```
# XYZ
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/url                    = "https://..."
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/zMin                   = 0
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/zMax                   = 19
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/tilePixelRatio         = 0
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/axisOrder              = 0   (0=ZXY,1=ZYX)
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/username               = "user"
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/password               = "<AES-256-CBC base64>"
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/saltAndIv              = "<hex>"
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/http-header/referer    = "https://..."
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/XYZ/{name}/http-header/User-Agent = "OpenSWMM/1.0"

# WMS / WMTS (same group)
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/url                    = "..."
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/version                = ""
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/ignoreAxisOrientation  = false
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/invertAxisOrientation  = false
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/ignoreGetMapURI        = false
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/dpiMode                = 7
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/tilePixelRatio         = 0
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/smoothPixmapTransform  = true
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/username               = "..."
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/password               = "<encrypted>"
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/saltAndIv              = "<hex>"
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/WMS/{name}/http-header/referer    = ""

# ArcGIS
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/ArcGIS/{name}/url               = "..."
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/ArcGIS/{name}/urlPrefix         = ""
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/ArcGIS/{name}/contentEndpoint   = ""
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/ArcGIS/{name}/communityEndpoint = ""
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/ArcGIS/{name}/username          = "..."
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/ArcGIS/{name}/password          = "<encrypted>"
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/ArcGIS/{name}/saltAndIv         = "<hex>"
SWMMVis/BasemapConnections/ArcGIS/{name}/http-header/referer = ""
```

Passwords are NEVER stored in plaintext.  If decryption fails
(e.g., machine ID changed), `BasemapAuth::password` is returned empty
and the connection is presented with credentials cleared.

### AB-2.3 — `BasemapHttpHeadersWidget`

A reusable `QWidget` used in all three dialog tabs (XYZ, WMS/WMTS,
ArcGIS).  Mirrors QGIS's `QgsHttpHeaderWidget`:

```
include/ui/widgets/basemaphttpheaderswidget.h
src/ui/widgets/basemaphttpheaderswidget.cpp
```

**Layout:**

```
Referer: [_________________________________]   ← always visible QLineEdit

▼ Additional Headers (QGroupBox, collapsed by default)
```

```cpp
class BasemapHttpHeadersWidget : public QWidget
```

### AB-2.4 — Multi-tab "Add Basemap" dialog (`AddBasemapDialog`)

```
include/ui/dialogs/addbasemapdialog.h
src/ui/dialogs/addbasemapdialog.cpp
```

```cpp
class AddBasemapDialog : public QDialog
{
    Q_OBJECT
public:
    explicit AddBasemapDialog(QWidget *parent = nullptr);
    // Returns the configured layer. Caller takes ownership. nullptr on cancel.
    OpenSWMMVisLayer *createLayer(QObject *parent = nullptr) const;

private:
    QTabWidget            *m_tabs       = nullptr;
    QWidget               *m_xyzTab    = nullptr;
    QWidget               *m_wmsTab    = nullptr;  // WMS + WMTS combined
    QWidget               *m_arcgisTab = nullptr;
    QDialogButtonBox      *m_buttons   = nullptr;

    QWidget *buildXYZTab();
    QWidget *buildWMSTab();    // auto-detects WMS vs WMTS from URL
    QWidget *buildArcGISTab();
};
```

`actionAddBasemap` in `swmmvis.cpp` is rewired to `onAddBasemap()`:

```cpp
void SWMMVis::onAddBasemap()
{
    AddBasemapDialog dlg(this);
    if (dlg.exec() != QDialog::Accepted) return;
    auto *layer = dlg.createLayer(nullptr);
    if (!layer) return;
    if (MapCanvas *c = activeCanvas())
        c->addLayer(layer, true);
    onLogMessage(tr("Added basemap: %1").arg(layer->name()));
}
```

#### Tab 1 — XYZ Tiles

```
[Saved connections: ▾ OpenStreetMap         ] [New] [Edit] [Delete]
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Name:             [________________________________]
URL template:     [https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png]
Min zoom: [0 ▾]   Max zoom: [19 ▾]
Tile pixel ratio: [▾ Undefined / Standard 96DPI / HiDPI 192DPI]
Axis order:       [▾ ZXY (standard) / ZYX (ArcGIS REST)]

  Username: [________________________________]
  Password: [••••••••••••••••] [👁]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[Test Connection]  ← fetches tile z=0/x=0/y=0, shows thumbnail label
```

`Tile pixel ratio` is a **DPI rendering hint** (0/1/2); it does NOT
alter the URL template.  `@2x` in a URL template is a literal string
the user types (e.g., CartoDB `.../light_all/{z}/{x}/{y}@2x.png`).

**Pre-populated built-in connections** (non-deletable):

| Name | URL template | Axis |
|------|-------------|------|
| OpenStreetMap | `https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` | ZXY |
| CartoDB Positron | `https://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/light_all/{z}/{x}/{y}@2x.png` | ZXY |
| CartoDB Dark Matter | `https://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/dark_all/{z}/{x}/{y}@2x.png` | ZXY |
| Stadia Alidade Smooth | `https://tiles.stadiamaps.com/tiles/alidade_smooth/{z}/{x}/{y}@2x.png` | ZXY |
| ESRI World Imagery | `https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}` | ZYX |

Builtins live in a `static QList<XYZConnection> XYZConnection::builtins()` factory.

One tab; protocol auto-detected from URL (case-insensitive substring

**DPI mode** is a bitmask int: 0=None, 1=QGIS, 2=UMN MapServer,
4=GeoServer, 7=All (default — broadest server compatibility).

`ignoreAxisOrientation` and `invertAxisOrientation` are separate
booleans matching QGIS's `settingsIgnoreAxisOrientation` and
`settingsInvertAxisOrientation`.

```
│ Service: "World Imagery"   Type: MapServer (tiled)              │
│ Extent:  [-180, -90, 180, 90]  Levels: 0–23                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The Connect step parses `tileInfo.lods[*].level` to infer `zMin`/`zMax`
and constructs an `XYZConnection` with `urlTemplate =
{url}/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}` and `axisOrder = ZYX`. No separate
ArcGIS layer class is needed.

`contentEndpoint` and `communityEndpoint` are stored in the connection
struct for future ArcGIS Portal browsing support; they are not used
during tile rendering.

### AB-2.5 — `XYZTileLayer`, `WMSLayer`, `WMTSLayer` — auth + headers

**Base class (`OpenSWMMVisLayer`) additions:**

```cpp
void setBasicAuth(const QString &username, const QString &password);
void setHttpHeaders(const BasemapHttpHeaders &headers);

protected:
    QByteArray         m_authHeader;    // "Basic <base64>" or empty
    BasemapHttpHeaders m_httpHeaders;   // arbitrary header map
```

Every `QNetworkRequest` in all three layer classes:

```cpp
if (!m_authHeader.isEmpty())
    req.setRawHeader("Authorization", m_authHeader);
for (auto it = m_httpHeaders.cbegin(); it != m_httpHeaders.cend(); ++it)
    req.setRawHeader(it.key().toUtf8(), it.value().toUtf8());
```

**`XYZTileLayer` additional setters:**

```cpp
void setTilePixelRatio(int ratio);   // 0=Undefined, 1=Standard, 2=HiDPI
void setAxisOrder(TileAxisOrder order);
```

`buildTileUrl()` swaps `{x}` and `{y}` when `axisOrder == ZYX`.

### AB-2.6 — Project serialisation of basemap layers

`ProjectSerializer` gains a `"basemaps"` JSON array. **Schema
version bumped to 3** when the key is present.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "inpPath": "model.inp",
  "layer": { ... },
  "canvas": { ... },
  "basemaps": [
    {
      "type": "xyz",
      "name": "CartoDB Positron",
      "urlTemplate": "https://{s}.basemaps.cartocdn.com/light_all/{z}/{x}/{y}@2x.png",
      "zMin": 0, "zMax": 19,
      "tilePixelRatio": 2,
      "axisOrder": "zxy",
      "headers": { "referer": "https://mysite.com" },
      "hasAuth": true,
      "connectionName": "CartoDB Positron"
    },
    {
      "type": "wms",
      "name": "USGS Topo",
      "url": "https://...",
      "layerName": "0",
      "style": "default",
      "imageFormat": "image/png",
      "crs": "EPSG:3857",
      "dpiMode": 7,
      "tilePixelRatio": 0,
      "ignoreAxisOrientation": false,
      "invertAxisOrientation": false,
      "ignoreGetMapURI": false,
      "smoothPixmapTransform": true,
      "headers": {},
      "hasAuth": false,
      "connectionName": ""
    },
    {
      "type": "wmts",
      "name": "USGS National Map",
      "url": "https://...",
      "layerIdentifier": "USGSTopo",
      "tileMatrixSet": "GoogleMapsCompatible",
      "style": "default",
      "imageFormat": "image/png",
      "dpiMode": 7,
      "tilePixelRatio": 0,
      "headers": {},
      "hasAuth": false,
      "connectionName": ""
    }
  ]
}
```

**Design decisions:**

1. **Passwords NOT in `.oswp`.** `hasAuth = true` + non-empty
   `connectionName` → restore looks up `BasemapConnectionStore`.
   Missing store entry → layer added without auth, layer-tree warning badge.
2. **`"headers"` object** — arbitrary key/value map, no encryption needed.
3. **`applyFromFile` ignores `"basemaps"` for `schemaVersion < 3`.**

# Gap-Coverage Slice Plan — Slices BA–CT (drafted 2026-05-13)

This block adds 44 new slice stubs covering the remaining legacy SWMM-GUI feature surface and the advanced openswmm.engine v6.0 capabilities, sequenced in four execution blocks per the approved plan in `/Users/calebbuahin/.claude/plans/soft-waddling-tarjan.md`. Each stub follows the slice-log format used for AA / AT / AU / AW so an implementing agent can expand any single stub into a 200–1000-line full design before activating that slice.

Sequencing decisions: **Block I (Vis/Reporting BA–BL) first** so existing `.inp` files become useful immediately; **Block II (Input/Edit BM–BV)** next to complete authoring; **Block III (Analytics BW–CG)** layered on shipped engine v6.0 + roadmap seams; **Block IV (XCut CI–CT)** modernization. Engine API gaps consolidated in section §G below and tracked centrally in `openswmm.engine/docs/GUI_API_REQUEST_BLOCK_BA.md`.
