## Block I — Visualization & Reporting (BA–BL)

Sequence first so existing `.inp` files become useful immediately.

### ⏳ Slice BA — Animation Controller + per-attribute theming (closes Slice AC) (Phase 8.0–8.5)

The legacy `Animator.pas` plays simulation results back across the map: a global clock drives subcatch / node / link colour fills, the time-series plot cursor (Slice AT) tracks the same instant, and a status bar shows the current simulation timestamp. Slice AC was reserved as a placeholder for this but never designed. BA delivers the full controller, wires the existing animation toolbar buttons (`actionPlay` / `actionPause` / `actionStop` / `actionStepFwd` / `actionStepRev` / `actionFirst` / `actionLast`), and per-attribute theming combos in the status bar that select which output variable drives the colour fill.

> **Concrete decision recorded 2026-05-16:** Every simulation run creates a **new** `SWMMResultsLayer` (never replaced in-place). The `AnimationController` uses a **primary + secondary layer** model rather than a single-layer bind. Per-attribute theming (combos + Legend Dock) reflects only the primary layer; each secondary layer retains its own independent `SWMMResultVariable` + colour ramp. See plan file `i-am-trying-to-atomic-chipmunk.md` for full rationale.

- **Phase 8.0 — New run = new results layer** (pre-requisite for the rest of BA): `onRunSimulation` in `src/swmmvis.cpp` calls `SWMMVis::addResultsLayer(outPath, modelLayer)` after the solver completes. Default `.out` path is `<inp-stem>_<ISO8601-compact>.out` in the same directory (overridable via SimulationOptions → Files). Layer name defaults to `"Run — HH:MM:SS"` and is editable in `LayerPropertiesDialog`. The newly added layer is auto-activated as primary (see Phase 8.3). Old layers persist; removed manually via right-click → Remove Layer. `SWMMResultsLayer` gains a `scenarioName` Q_PROPERTY (free-text, serialized in `.oswp`).
- **Phase 8.1 — `AnimationController` primary/secondary model**: `AnimationController` (`include/animation/animationcontroller.h`) is owned by `SWMMVis` (not a singleton). It holds `m_primaryLayer` (`QPointer<SWMMResultsLayer>`) and `m_secondaryLayers` (`QList<QPointer<SWMMResultsLayer>>`). The primary layer's time grid is authoritative; each secondary layer receives `setCurrentTimeStep(periodIndexForDateTime(primaryTime))` so it snaps to its nearest period. New API: `setPrimaryLayer`, `addSecondaryLayer`, `removeSecondaryLayer`, `clearSecondaryLayers`, `allLayers`. `SWMMResultsLayer` gains `int periodIndexForDateTime(const QDateTime &dt) const` — clamps `round((dt − start) / reportStep)` to `[0, totalSteps−1]`. Signals unchanged: `currentTimeChanged(QDateTime)`, `currentPeriodChanged(int)`, `playStateChanged(bool)`, `totalPeriodsChanged(int)`.
- **Phase 8.2 — Per-attribute theming UI (primary layer only)**: Status bar gets three `QComboBox`es (Nodes / Links / Subcatchments) bound to the **primary layer's** `SWMMResultVariable`. `SWMMVis::setActiveResultsLayer(layer)` (new slot) re-populates the combos and calls `primaryLayer->autoStretchColorRamp()`. Secondary layers retain their own variable/ramp independently — changing a combo does not repaint them. No separate `MapResultThemer` class is needed; theming is handled directly by `SWMMResultsLayer::setVariable` + `fetchResultsForStep`.
- **Phase 8.3 — Toolbar wiring + auto-activation**: Hook `actionPlay` / `actionPause` / `actionStop` / `actionStepFwd` / `actionStepRev` / `actionFirst` / `actionLast` to controller slots. `addResultsLayer` auto-promotes the new layer to primary (prior primary silently becomes secondary). Layer Tree right-click on a results-layer row gains **"Set as Active Results Layer"** action → `SWMMVis::setActiveResultsLayer(layer)`. Primary layer is shown **bold** in the Layer Tree (see layer-tree amendments in Slice D-2/D-fix). Emit `currentTimeChanged` so Slice BC and Slice BL pick it up automatically.
- **Phase 8.3.1 — Adaptive slider tick spacing** *(amendment 2026-05-19)*: the `mSliderAnimationTime` `QSlider` in `toolBarAnimation` ([src/swmmvis.cpp:444-451](src/swmmvis.cpp#L444-L451)) is currently created with a hard-coded `setTickInterval(10)`. For runs with many report periods (10³–10⁵) this draws an unreadable smear of ticks. Replace with adaptive spacing driven off `AnimationController::totalPeriodsChanged(int total)`:
  - Target **≤ ~50 visible ticks** along the rail.
  - Step picked from the canonical 1 / 2 / 5 × 10ⁿ sequence such that `total / step ≤ 50` (e.g. total=144 → step=5, total=8 640 → step=200, total=100 000 → step=2000).
  - `total ≤ 1` → `setTickPosition(QSlider::NoTicks)`; otherwise restore `QSlider::TicksBelow`.
  - `setPageStep(step)` is updated alongside `setTickInterval(step)` so PgUp/PgDn jumps one labelled increment (currently page-step is fixed at 10).
  - Implementation: small free helper `niceTickStep(int total, int targetTicks=50) → int` inside `swmmvis.cpp`. Before adding it, grep `mapcanvas.cpp` (`roundedMetres`) and any qcustomplot ticker helpers — if an existing nice-step routine is suitable, reuse it instead of duplicating.
- **Phase 8.4 — Speed control + skip-to-event**:
  - **Speed selector on the animation toolbar** *(amendment 2026-05-19, supersedes the bare "speed slider" wording)*: add a `QLabel("Speed:")` + `QComboBox` pair to `toolBarAnimation`. Combo values `0.25× / 0.5× / 1× / 2× / 4× / 8×` (matches `AnimationController::setSpeed`'s documented range in [include/animation/animationcontroller.h:73-77](include/animation/animationcontroller.h#L73-L77)); default selection `1×`; `currentIndexChanged` → `AnimationController::setSpeed(double)`. Insert position: after `actionStop`, before `actionSkipForward`, with a separator preceding the label so the playback-transport group stays visually intact. Tooltip / status tip: "Animation playback speed multiplier".
  - **Cross-session persistence**: last-used speed stored as `PreferencesManager::Simulation/animationSpeed` (double, default 1.0) and applied to the controller + combo on construction. Per-session persistence inside `.oswp` is still owned by Phase 8.5 below — this adds only the user-default fallback when no session value exists.
  - **Skip-to-event** (unchanged): "Jump to peak flow / peak flooding" quick action via `swmm_stat_*_time_of_occurrence` on the **primary layer's** `.out` handle (engine gap BA-01 — verify in `openswmm_statistics.h` at slice-start).
  - **No `AnimationController` API change** — the controller already exposes `setSpeed(double)` and `speed()`; the combo + label are pure view widgets.
- **Phase 8.5 — Persistence**: Each `SWMMResultsLayer` entry in `.oswp` gains `"scenarioName"`, `"variable"`, `"colorRamp"` (min/max/stops), `"profileLineColor"` (`#RRGGBB`, used by Slice BC's Sources-panel color chip), and `"isPrimary": true` (at most one per session). `applySession()` calls `setActiveResultsLayer()` for the marked entry. Animation speed persisted in the session record.
- **Files**: `include/animation/animationcontroller.h` (amended — `setPrimaryLayer` / `addSecondaryLayer` / `removeSecondaryLayer` / `clearSecondaryLayers` / `allLayers`), `src/animation/animationcontroller.cpp` (multi-layer tick dispatch); `include/layers/swmmresultslayer.h` (amended — `scenarioName` property + `periodIndexForDateTime`), `src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp`; touches `src/swmmvis.cpp` (Phase 8.0 + 8.3 + 8.3.1 adaptive ticks + 8.4 speed combo wiring), `include/swmmvis.h` (new private members `mLabelAnimationSpeed`, `mComboAnimationSpeed`), `src/ui/widgets/animationtoolbar.cpp`, `include/ui/panels/layertreepanel.h` + `.cpp` (bold primary + "Set as Active" action), `include/preferencesmanager.h` + `src/preferencesmanager.cpp` (`animationSpeed` accessor, default 1.0).
- **Engine APIs**: `swmm_output_open/close`, `_get_period_count`, `_get_report_step`, `_get_start_date`, `_get_node_result`, `_get_link_result`, `_get_subcatch_result`, `_get_period_time`.
- **Engine gap**: BA-01 — `swmm_stat_*_time_of_occurrence`.
- **Tests**: `tests/gui/test_animationcontroller.cpp` — 12 cases: open/close, period bounds, play→tick→stop, speed change, jump-to-peak (primary only), attribute change re-themes primary not secondary, secondary snaps to nearest period when primary advances, `setPrimaryLayer` demotes old primary to secondary, single-fire per tick, `setActiveResultsLayer` repopulates combos, auto-activation on `addResultsLayer`, `.oswp` round-trip with `isPrimary` + `scenarioName`. Plus a small toolbar test (`tests/gui/test_swmmvis_animation_toolbar.cpp`, ~3 cases) for the 8.3.1/8.4 amendments: `niceTickStep` table-driven check for `{0, 12, 144, 8640, 100000}` → `{0, 1, 5, 200, 2000}`; combo `currentIndexChanged` round-trips to `controller.speed()`; `PreferencesManager::animationSpeed` is restored to the combo on fresh `SWMMVis` construction.
- **Manual**: `docs/manual/13_animation.md`.
- **Dependencies**: AT, T, V.
- **Deferred**: timeline scrubber widget (ship in CS); event detection from rule firings (BR.5).

### ⏳ Slice BB — Color-ramp legend editor + 5-interval framed intervals (Phase 8.6)

Legacy `Dlegend.pas` + `Dcolramp.pas` lets users define 5-interval colour ramps (with framed-interval emphasis bands), reverse the ramp, pick from a preset library, and re-bin by quantile / equal-interval / standard-deviation / manual. BB delivers the full editor as a reusable dock so it serves both Slice BA (animation theming) and Slice BI (map symbology).

- **Phase 8.6.1 — `ColorRamp` data type**: New `include/render/colorramp.h` — `struct ColorRamp { QString name; QVector<QColor> stops; QVector<qreal> positions; bool framed; }`. Built-in catalogue: Viridis, Plasma, Magma, Inferno, Cividis, RdBu, RdYlGn, Spectral, BrBG, legacy-SWMM-5interval, legacy-SWMM-pollutant. JSON serializer.
- **Phase 8.6.2 — Interval binning**: `IntervalBinner` (`include/render/intervalbinner.h`) — `EqualInterval`, `Quantile`, `StdDev`, `Manual`, `Jenks` (Fisher–Jenks natural-breaks). Operates over a `QVector<double>` sampled from the active output attribute via Slice BA.
- **Phase 8.6.3 — Editor dialog**: `LegendEditorDialog` — left: ramp preset picker + interval count spinner + binning combo + reverse + framed-interval check; right: live preview (gradient bar + tick marks at breaks + frame highlight); bottom: per-interval colour pickers.
- **Phase 8.6.4 — Legend dock**: `LegendDock` — read-only display of the **primary layer's** legend (colour ramp + variable label); double-click opens `LegendEditorDialog` which mutates the primary layer's ramp only. Secondary layers' ramps are not shown in the dock (visible as a tooltip on the layer-tree row). Per-layer + per-attribute keyed.
- **Phase 8.6.5 — Persistence**: `ColorRamp` per (layer-id, attribute) into `.oswp`; custom ramps in `PreferencesManager → Rendering/CustomRamps`.
- **Files**: new `include/render/colorramp.h`, `intervalbinner.h`, `include/ui/dialogs/legendeditordialog.h`, `include/ui/panels/legenddock.h` + .cpps.
- **Engine APIs**: none — client-side rendering.
- **Tests**: `test_colorramp.cpp` (12 cases).
- **Manual**: `docs/manual/14_legend.md`.
- **Dependencies**: BA.
- **Deferred**: continuous (non-binned) ramps with log axis (CB.4).

### ⏳ Slice BC — Profile plot (HGL / EGL / envelope along node path) (Phase 8.7)

Legacy `Dprofile.pas` + `Dproplot.pas` + `Dproselect.pas` is the most loved hydraulic-debugging view: user picks a chain of nodes (or right-clicks a starting node and "Trace Profile…") and gets a longitudinal cross-section showing pipe inverts, ground / rim elevation, **current HGL and current EGL** driven by the animation cursor, **toggleable max-HGL and max-EGL filled-range layers** (envelope band **or** invert-to-peak fill), and live overlay of HGL / EGL from **other result layers in the same project** for run-vs-run comparison. BC delivers this plot as a primary consumer of the `AnimationController::currentTimeChanged` cursor signal.

> **Scope decision recorded 2026-05-17:** v1 supports **intra-project** multi-results comparison (primary + secondary `SWMMResultsLayer`s in the active project's `AnimationController`). **Cross-tab / cross-project comparison** — surfacing result layers from other MDI sub-windows on the same plot — is **deferred to Slice BC-2** to keep v1 scope tight.

- **Phase 8.7.1 — Endpoint-pair selection + auto-route**: `MapToolSelectProfile` builds the profile path by routing between two user-picked endpoints. Two equivalent input idioms — both accept either a **node** or a **link** at each pick (a link-click snaps to the link endpoint nearest the cursor):
  - **Click + modifier**: first map-click sets the **start**; `Ctrl`+click (`⌘`+click on macOS) sets the **end**.
  - **Modifier + modifier**: hold `Ctrl`/`⌘` for **both** clicks — same outcome, mirrors the QGIS routing-tool idiom for power users.
  
  A pulsing halo marks the captured start so the tool's "armed" state is visible. `Esc`, right-click, or re-clicking the start clears it. Selecting the same object as both start and end shows an inline error and resets.
  
  Once both endpoints are captured, `ProfileRouter` (`include/plot/profilerouter.h`) runs **Yen's k-shortest-simple-paths** (k = 5 default, `PreferencesManager → Profile/MaxPaths`) over the link graph on top of Dijkstra. Edge weight = `swmm_link_length`; non-conduit links (pumps / weirs / orifices) get a small fixed weight so they're traversable but conduit length dominates. Directed traversal is the default (respects link from→to); a toggle in the picker re-runs as undirected on demand. Traversal is bounded by node-count and a ~200 ms soft cap; if exceeded, the picker surfaces a "Search truncated" notice with a "Continue search…" button.
  
  - **No path** → status-bar message "No connected path from `<start>` to `<end>`"; tool resets.
  - **One path** → tool auto-confirms and pops `ProfilePlotDialog`.
  - **Multiple paths** → `ProfilePathPickerDialog` (`include/ui/dialogs/profilepathpickerdialog.h`) opens; **all candidate paths are highlighted on the map simultaneously** in distinct categorical colors (reuses Slice BB's "categorical" palette), start/end glyphs pulse, and each candidate is listed in a side table showing **total length, conduit count, non-conduit count, total invert drop**. Hovering a row promotes that path to full-opacity and dims the others; clicking selects; **OK** confirms and hands the path to `ProfilePlotDialog`. A `[ ] Treat graph as undirected` checkbox re-routes on demand. A **"Pick on map"** mode lets the user click an intermediate node to filter the candidate list to only paths passing through it.
  
  **Waypoint chaining**: `Shift+Ctrl/⌘`-click between the start and end captures an intermediate **waypoint**; multiple waypoints chain (`start → wpt₁ → … → end`) and the router concatenates per-segment k-shortest results. Waypoints render as numbered glyphs and are reorderable in a small chip-strip on the map toolbar.
  
  Path highlighting (the multi-color overlay while the picker is open) is rendered by `ProfilePathOverlay` (`include/map/profilepathoverlay.h`) — a transient `QGraphicsItemGroup` on the map canvas that destroys itself on picker close. The legacy right-click → "Trace Profile…" menu entry on any node remains and simply pre-seeds the tool with that node as the start, then awaits the second click.
- **Phase 8.7.2 — Profile data assembly (multi-source + envelope precompute)**: `ProfileBuilder` (`include/plot/profilebuilder.h`) walks the path accumulating chainage; queries `swmm_node_invert_elev`, `swmm_node_max_depth`, `swmm_link_offset1/2`, `swmm_link_length` for the static layer. **For each result source bound to the builder** it pulls **full time-series**: `swmm_output_get_node_series(NodeHead, NodeDepth)` per path node and `swmm_output_get_link_series(LinkVelocity)` per path link. From these it computes, per node:

  > **Engine offset-normalisation contract (added 2026-05-22):** the engine's `swmm_link_get_offset_up/dn` always returns the conduit-end offset as **depth above the connecting node invert**, regardless of the source `.inp`'s `LINK_OFFSETS` setting. `PostParseResolver` (openswmm.engine `src/engine/input/PostParseResolver.cpp` lines 1013–1022 for conduits, 463–470 for orifices) converts `ELEVATION`-mode input to depth at parse time. **The GUI must not re-convert.** A previous Phase 8.7.2 cut applied an extra `rawOffset − nodeInvert` subtraction in `profilenetworkadapter_model.cpp` whenever `swmm_options_get(eng, "LINK_OFFSETS")` reported `ELEVATION`; this double-subtraction silently shipped because the engine ABI did not expose `LINK_OFFSETS` until Slice CX.4 (2026-05-22) and the helper had always defaulted to `false`. Once CX.4 made the helper truthful, ELEVATION-mode models began rendering with wildly-wrong (typically large-negative) conduit inverts. The fix removes the helper and trusts the engine contract end-to-end; the regression guard lives in `tests/gui/test_profilenetworkadapter_model.cpp`.

  - `hgl_t[]` (direct from `NodeHead`),
  - `egl_t[] = hgl_t + v² / (2·g)` where `v` = mean of incident-link velocities — upstream-only at the path head, downstream-only at the tail, `(upstream + downstream) / 2` interior (EGL is **not** a first-class engine output and is derived in the GUI),
  - `min_hgl`, `max_hgl`, `min_egl`, `max_egl` per node, single pass over periods (engine has no `max_head` or `time_of_occurrence` for HGL/EGL — see Engine gap below).
  
  Per-source data is cached on the builder keyed by `(layer, pathHash)` and invalidated when the layer's `.out` mtime changes.
- **Phase 8.7.3 — Plot widget and layer toggle panel**: `ProfilePlotWidget` renders the path as a real network cross-section — **per-link conduit segments** and **per-node connecting-node glyphs** — not as smooth aggregate lines.
  - **Ground / rim elevation** is **derived per node** as `invertElev + maxDepth` (each node's rim = its ground elevation; no separate DEM lookup in v1). The ground line is a poly-line interpolating these rim elevations along chainage.
  - **Soil fill**: the area between the ground line and the conduit crown (and the manhole-shaft regions at each node) is rendered as a translucent earth-toned fill, giving the standard buried-pipe profile look. The fill is drawn behind the conduit and node skeleton so the pipe and any animated HGL/EGL lines remain readable.
  - **Connecting nodes** (every node on the path): vertical bar from `invertElev` up to the rim (= `invertElev + maxDepth`), with the node's ID labeled at the top. Junctions, outfalls, storage, and dividers each get a distinct glyph (filled rectangle, triangle, trapezoid, diamond — matches map-symbology defaults from Slice BI).
  - **Conduits** (every link between consecutive path nodes): an upstream invert at `nodes[i].invertElev + links[i].offset1`, a downstream invert at `nodes[i+1].invertElev + links[i].offset2`, and a parallel crown line offset above each by the link's cross-section max-depth. The conduit body between them is rendered as a translucent envelope; non-conduit links (pumps / weirs / orifices) render as a labelled glyph spanning the gap instead of a pipe outline.
  - **Animated layers** drawn over the conduit/node skeleton, in z-order: **max-HGL fill** (per source), **max-EGL fill** (per source), **current HGL** (per source, animated, solid), **current EGL** (per source, animated, dashed).
  
  `QGraphicsScene` is used for crisp pen lines; `QGraphicsPathItem` with `QBrush` for filled areas. A right-side **Layers panel** offers per-source toggles:
  - `[ ] Current HGL`   `[ ] Current EGL`
  - `[ ] Max HGL`  mode `(•) Min↔max band  ( ) Invert→max fill`
  - `[ ] Max EGL`  mode `(•) Min↔max band  ( ) Invert→max fill`
  
  Two render modes for the max layers (per-source, per-variable):
    1. **Min↔max envelope band** — translucent fill between per-node `min_hgl` and `max_hgl` (resp. EGL). Standard hydraulic envelope.
    2. **Invert→max fill** — translucent fill from `invert` up to `max_hgl` (resp. `max_egl`). Emphasizes peak wetted-surface profile.
  
  Defaults to **Min↔max band**. Source-color alpha is 35 % for fills, 100 % for line layers.
- **Phase 8.7.4 — Multi-results comparison (intra-project)**: `ProfilePlotDialog` exposes a **Sources panel** listing every `SWMMResultsLayer` currently in the active project's `AnimationController` (primary + secondaries), with checkbox, color chip (auto-assigned, editable, persisted via `SWMMResultsLayer::profileLineColor` — see BA Phase 8.5 amendment), scenario-name label, and a tooltip showing the `.out` path. Enabling a source binds it to the `ProfileBuilder` (one builder, many sources). Each source resolves the path by **node ID name**; if a node is missing in that source the source is greyed with an inline warning and skipped from render (no crash). The dialog's animation cursor follows the **active project's primary** controller; each source's HGL(t)/EGL(t) is sampled at `source.periodIndexForDateTime(primaryTime)` so different report steps are handled by per-source nearest-period snap (same convention as Slice BA's secondary-layer time-snap). The legacy "Add Snapshot" model is **dropped** — comparison is now live and continuously animated, not captured per-click.
- **Phase 8.7.5 — Save / recall named profiles + Library Dock**: `ProfileLibrary` is the in-memory model; `ProfileLibraryDock` (`include/ui/panels/profilelibrarydock.h`) is the persistent UI panel docked alongside the Object Browser. The dock shows a project-scoped tree of saved profiles (name + node-count + last-edit timestamp), with a toolbar offering **`[ + New Profile ]`** (launches `MapToolSelectProfile`) and **`[ ⋯ ]`** import/export-JSON. Per-row interactions:
  - **Double-click** → loads into the active `ProfilePlotDialog`, or opens a new dialog if none is active.
  - **Right-click → Rename / Duplicate / Delete / Show on map** (Show-on-map flashes the path via `ProfilePathOverlay` for ~2 s without opening the dialog).
  - **Drag** a profile name into an open `ProfilePlotDialog` to add it as a comparison overlay — *planned-but-deferred to Slice BC-3* (drag handler is stubbed in v1; behind a `Preview` flag).
  
  Persisted to `.oswp`:
  ```json
  "profiles":[{
    "name":"Trunk-A",
    "nodes":[…],
    "layers":{
      "currentHGL":true, "currentEGL":false,
      "maxHGL":{"on":true,"mode":"envelope"},
      "maxEGL":{"on":false,"mode":"envelope"}
    },
    "modified":"2026-05-17T14:32:10Z"
  }]
  ```
  Name uniqueness is enforced per-project; rename / duplicate collisions append `" (n)"`. Source-color assignments persist per `SWMMResultsLayer` via the BA Phase 8.5 `profileLineColor` field.
- **Phase 8.7.6 — Edit-in-place (path mutation from the plot)**: While a profile is loaded in `ProfilePlotDialog`, right-clicking exposes path-editing actions that re-invoke `ProfileRouter` and refresh the plot live (the per-source envelope cache is invalidated only for affected segments to keep edits snappy).
  - **Right-click a node *on* the path** → `Insert waypoint before` / `Insert waypoint after` / `Remove from path` / `Set as new start` / `Set as new end`.
  - **Right-click a node *off* the path** → `Insert waypoint here` (auto-chooses the nearest segment by chainage distance and re-routes start→…→here→…→end).
  - **Right-click a link on the path** → `Remove this link` (forces a detour) / `Lock this link in path` (treated as a required edge in subsequent re-routes).
  
  Each edit pushes onto a per-dialog `QUndoStack` so `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` step through path history. Edits to a profile loaded from the Library Dock are **draft-only** until the user picks `Save` (writes back to the same name) or `Save As…` (writes a new entry); the dock row gets a small "●" dirty-marker. Closing the dialog with unsaved edits prompts.
- **Phase 8.7.7 — Export**: PNG / PDF / SVG via `QPainter` capturing the current Layers-panel toggle state. CSV columns: `chainage, ground, invert, crown,` then **per enabled source**: `<src>_HGL_t, <src>_EGL_t, <src>_minHGL, <src>_maxHGL, <src>_minEGL, <src>_maxEGL`.
- **Files**: new `include/plot/profilebuilder.h` (multi-source + envelope cache), `include/plot/profilerouter.h` (Yen's k-shortest + waypoint chaining), `profileplotwidget.h` (layer panel + render modes), `profilelibrary.h`, `include/ui/dialogs/profileplotdialog.h` (Sources panel + right-click edit-in-place menu + `QUndoStack`), `include/ui/dialogs/profilepathpickerdialog.h` (multi-path picker), `include/ui/panels/profilelibrarydock.h` (saved-profile dock — recall, rename, duplicate, delete, show-on-map, import/export JSON), `include/ui/widgets/profilelayerpanel.h`, `include/map/maptoolselectprofile.h`, `include/map/profilepathoverlay.h` (transient highlight layer) + `.cpp`s; touches `src/swmmvis.cpp` (register Library Dock), `src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp`, `src/project/projectserializer.cpp`, `include/layers/swmmresultslayer.h` (add `profileLineColor` Q_PROPERTY — small BA amendment), `include/preferences/preferencesmanager.h` (add `Profile/MaxPaths` default = 5).
- **Engine APIs**: `openswmm_nodes.h` invert / max-depth getters; `openswmm_links.h::swmm_link_get_endpoints`, offsets, length; `openswmm_output.h::swmm_output_get_node_series` (`NodeHead`, `NodeDepth`) and `swmm_output_get_link_series` (`LinkVelocity`). No new engine surface required.
- **Engine gap**: BC-01 (deferred, **non-blocking**) — engine exposes no max-head, no max-EGL, and no `swmm_stat_*_time_of_occurrence` for HGL/EGL, so envelopes are computed by a full-series scan in the GUI and "Jump animation to peak HGL on path" is deferred. A future `swmm_output_get_event_window_series` would skip the full scan; tracked alongside BA-01.
- **Tests**:
  - `test_profilenetworkadapter_model.cpp` (2 cases — added 2026-05-22 as the regression guard for the Phase 8.7.2 offset-normalisation contract above): two minimal `.inp` fixtures describing the same physical conduit (J1 invert 100, J2 invert 95, offsets up=0.5 / dn=1.5) in `LINK_OFFSETS DEPTH` and `LINK_OFFSETS ELEVATION` mode are loaded into the engine; `swmm_link_get_offset_up/dn` must return identical depth values (0.5 / 1.5) in both cases. Second case is a fixture sanity check — fixtures must exercise non-zero, non-equal offsets so the contract assertion is actually meaningful. Fixtures are written to `SWMMVIS_GUI_TEST_DATA/profile_offset/` so they remain inspectable after the run.
  - `test_profilebuilder.cpp` (16 cases): single-pipe HGL@t; multi-pipe with offsets; missing-link error; `EGL = HGL + v²/(2g)` matches hand-calc within 1e-3 ft; EGL boundary node uses single-side velocity; envelope min/max match brute-force scan; invert→max fill ≥ min↔max band at every node; source-resolution-by-name when secondary layer has matching ids; source-resolution-fail when name missing (greyed not crashed); per-source time-snap to nearest period for mismatched report steps; layer-toggle persistence round-trip; CSV column ordering; color-chip persistence in `.oswp`; render-mode toggle preserves data; 3-source render does not regress 1-source perf; cache-invalidation on `.out` mtime change.
  - `test_profilerouter.cpp` (15 cases): straight-line single path; branched 2-path enumeration; parallel-pipe k=5 ordering by length; disconnected-component returns empty; directed-vs-undirected behaviour swap; link-click endpoint snap (4 endpoint-pair combinations for `link→link` query); same-node start/end rejected; non-conduit weight does not dominate over conduit-length; single-waypoint chaining concatenates correctly; soft cap fires "Search truncated"; **edit-in-place**: insert-waypoint-mid-path matches direct `start→wpt→end` query, remove-interior-node re-routes around it, set-as-new-start truncates the prior prefix, set-as-new-end truncates the prior suffix, "Insert waypoint here" off-path snaps to nearest segment by chainage distance, lock-this-link forces traversal through the locked edge.
  - `test_profilelibrary.cpp` (8 cases): save/load round-trip, name-uniqueness collision appends ` (n)`, rename round-trip, duplicate clones layer toggles, delete removes entry, `modified` timestamp updates on edit, project close → reopen preserves all entries, import/export JSON round-trip across projects.
- **Manual**: `docs/manual/15_profile.md` — auto-route endpoint-pair selection (incl. waypoints), the multi-path picker, layer toggles, both envelope modes, the Sources panel, **Library Dock** (recall / rename / duplicate / delete / import-export), **edit-in-place** context menus + undo, and a note on the deferred cross-tab and drag-to-overlay features.
- **Dependencies**: BA (primary/secondary layer model + `currentTimeChanged` + `periodIndexForDateTime` + `profileLineColor` persistence), BB (categorical color palette for path-picker highlights), AT (comparison-pattern reuse for color/style chips).
- **Deferred**:
  - **Slice BC-2 — Cross-tab / cross-project profile comparison**: surface result layers from other MDI sub-windows in the Sources panel; needs a global `SWMMVisHost::allResultLayers()` walker and a "Sync animation to:" picker for choosing which `AnimationController` drives the cursor when sources span projects with different time grids.
  - **Slice BC-3 — Drag-from-library-to-plot overlay**: dropping a saved profile name onto an open `ProfilePlotDialog` adds it as a secondary path overlay (multiple paths on one plot). v1 ships the drag handler stubbed behind a `Preview` flag only.
  - Pump / weir / orifice elevation markers as inline glyphs (already deferred to CT.3 alongside print).
  - "Jump animation to peak HGL on path" — pending BA-01 / BC-01 engine work.

### ⏳ Slice BD — Statistics / frequency analysis report (Phase 8.8)

Legacy `Fstats.pas` + `Dstats.pas` + `Ustats.pas` computes event-based statistics over user-selected windows (Annual / Seasonal / Monthly / Daily / Complete), supports threshold-based event detection, and produces ranked event tables, return-period plots, and exceedance-frequency plots. BD wraps these and exposes them as a dockable report.

- **Phase 8.8.1 — Event detector**: `EventDetector` (input: time series + threshold + min-event-duration + min-inter-event-gap → `QVector<Event>` with start, end, peak, peak-time, volume). Reuses `openswmm_statistics.h` bulk getters; supports external time series for observed-data analysis.
- **Phase 8.8.2 — Window aggregator**: Partitions events into Annual / Seasonal (winter/spring/summer/fall) / Monthly / Daily / Complete buckets; computes count, total volume, max peak, avg peak, max duration per bucket.
- **Phase 8.8.3 — Return-period analysis**: Weibull plotting-position + log-Pearson Type III fit on annual maxima series; optional rank-based exceedance-probability plot.
- **Phase 8.8.4 — Report dialog**: `StatisticsReportDialog` — tabs `Events` (rank table), `Histogram`, `Exceedance`, `Return Period`. Each is `QChart` + `QTableView`. CSV export.
- **Phase 8.8.5 — Cross-link to map**: Click a row in rank table → map zoom + animation jump to event peak time via `SelectionManager`.
- **Files**: new `include/stats/eventdetector.h`, `windowaggregator.h`, `returnperiod.h`, `include/ui/dialogs/statisticsreportdialog.h` + .cpps.
- **Engine APIs**: `openswmm_statistics.h::swmm_stat_node_max_depth_bulk`, `swmm_stat_link_max_flow_bulk`, `swmm_stat_subcatch_runoff_vol_bulk`; `openswmm_output.h::swmm_output_get_*_series`.
- **Tests**: `test_eventdetector.cpp` (12 cases — single, multi-event with min-gap, threshold edge, window partitioning across year boundary, return-period fit on synthetic series).
- **Manual**: `docs/manual/16_statistics.md`.
- **Dependencies**: BA, AT.
- **Deferred**: peaks-over-threshold (POT) frequency analysis with Generalized Pareto fit (CB.3).

### ⏳ Slice BE — Status report viewer (16 sections + continuity errors) (Phase 8.9)

Legacy `Fstatus.pas` paginates the engine's `.rpt` into 16 navigable sections plus a header pane showing runoff / routing / quality continuity errors. BE delivers a modern viewer with sticky section navigation, search, and click-to-zoom from any object reference.

- **Phase 8.9.1 — `.rpt` parser**: `RptParser` (`include/report/rptparser.h`) tokenises section headers `*** <SECTION> ***` and parses each known column schema. Emits a `RptDocument` tree (`Section` → `Row`). Sections covered: Subcatchment Runoff, LID Performance, Groundwater, Subcatchment Washoff, Node Depth, Node Inflow, Node Surcharge, Node Flooding, Storage Volume, Outfall Loading, Street Flow, Link Flow, Flow Classification, Conduit Surcharge, Pumping, Link Pollutant Load.
- **Phase 8.9.2 — Continuity error pane**: Top banner calls `swmm_get_{runoff,routing,quality}_continuity_error`; colour-coded green/yellow/red against engine-default thresholds (10% / 15%).
- **Phase 8.9.3 — Status viewer dialog**: `StatusReportDialog` — left dock = `QTreeView` of sections; centre = `QTableView` of the active section; top toolbar = search + Next-match + Zoom-to-object (when first column is an object id).
- **Phase 8.9.4 — Continuity drilldown**: Each continuity number clickable → opens Mass Balance Dashboard (Slice CA) zoomed to relevant component.
- **Phase 8.9.5 — Export**: Plain text / HTML / PDF.
- **Files**: new `include/report/rptparser.h`, `rptdocument.h`, `include/ui/dialogs/statusreportdialog.h` + .cpps.
- **Engine APIs**: `openswmm_massbalance.h::swmm_get_runoff_continuity_error`, `_routing_continuity_error`, `_quality_continuity_error`.
- **Tests**: `test_rptparser.cpp` (16 cases — one per section schema + malformed-input recovery).
- **Manual**: `docs/manual/17_status_report.md`.
- **Dependencies**: M (writes the .rpt).
- **Deferred**: real-time .rpt tail-during-simulation (CG.x — only relevant if engine adds incremental .rpt flushing).

## Block II — Input & Editing parity (BM.0, BM–BV)

### ⏳ Slice DA — Attribute editing parity + Add-Object UX + Object naming fixes (Phase 6.2.6 / 6.3 first cut)

User-reported gaps that this slice closes ahead of the deep BN–BS editor cascade:

1. **AttributePanel is read-only for most object kinds.** Only Node / Link / Subcatchment route through typed property adapters; the 13 non-spatial Data Object categories (Curves, Time Series, Patterns, LID Controls, Pollutants, Land Uses, Aquifers, Snowpacks, Control Rules, Transects, Unit Hydrographs, Streets, Inlets) plus Rain Gages fall through to a read-only `QVariantMap` display ([attributepanel.cpp:343](../src/ui/panels/attributepanel.cpp)).
2. **Add-New UX is bare.** `addNewDataObject` ([objectbrowserpanel.cpp:546](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp)) is a single `QInputDialog::getText` that hardcodes one subtype per category (curves → Storage; patterns → Monthly; LIDs → BioCell; pollutants → mg/L; inlets → GRATE). Control Rules and Unit Hydrographs are explicitly deferred and not in the Data menu at all ([swmmvis.cpp:1710-1722](../src/swmmvis.cpp)).
3. **Control rules display as "Rule 1, Rule 2, …"** via the hardcoded fallback in `dataObjectNameAt` ([swmmmodellayer.cpp:747-755](../src/layers/swmmmodellayer.cpp)) — the engine stores rules only as full text blocks (`RULE MyName\nIF …`) with no name-by-index accessor.
4. **Unit hydrograph rows appear blank.** The `[HYDROGRAPHS]` engine API stores one entry per `(group, month, response)`. `dataObjectCount(DataHydrographs)` returns the raw entry count (12 or 36 per group); `dataObjectNameAt` then de-duplicates, leaving most rows empty.

DA is positioned as the **horizontal first cut** that lands editing capability for *every* object kind via lightweight adapters and small per-type create dialogs. BM.0 (full CRUD plumbing), BM (`PropertyEditorRegistry` + form helpers + undo), and BN–BS (structured per-class editors with linters / live previews / multi-tab forms) deepen each surface afterwards.

#### DA.1 — Object naming fixes (lands first; low-risk, high-impact)

**Engine prerequisites (must ship before any DA.1 GUI work):**

| Gap ID | Header | New C API |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| DA-ENG-01 | `openswmm_inflows.h` | `SWMM_ENGINE_API int swmm_hydrograph_group_count(SWMM_Engine);`<br>`SWMM_ENGINE_API int swmm_hydrograph_group_id(SWMM_Engine, int idx, char* buf, int buflen);` |
| DA-ENG-02 | `openswmm_controls.h` | `SWMM_ENGINE_API int swmm_control_get_id(SWMM_Engine, int idx, char* buf, int buflen);` |

`swmm_hydrograph_group_*` walks the existing per-entry list and emits the de-duplicated group-name sequence in first-occurrence order (matches `[HYDROGRAPHS]` section invariant). `swmm_control_get_id` parses the stored rule text and returns the first whitespace-delimited token after `RULE`; on parse failure (malformed rule with no RULE keyword) returns `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM` so the GUI can fall back to a sentinel display name. Adds 3 + 4 engine unit-test cases respectively (happy path, lowercase `rule` keyword, leading whitespace, missing keyword).

BN–BS later replace these placeholders with the richer editors.

Reads the `DataCategory` int role, switches across the 14 cases, and instantiates the right adapter. Adapter cached on the panel via a single `m_dataAdapter` `QPointer` so the previous one is `deleteLater()`d on swap (mirrors the node/link/subcatch pattern).

#### DA.3 — Add-Object UX: type-aware mini-dialogs

Replace `addNewDataObject` ([objectbrowserpanel.cpp:546-628](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp)) and the Data-menu wiring ([swmmvis.cpp:1689-1738](../src/swmmvis.cpp)) with per-type creation flows.

New `include/ui/dialogs/newdataobjectdialog.{h,cpp}` — a single dialog class with a static factory:

```cpp
std::optional<NewObjectSpec> NewDataObjectDialog::getNew(
    SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory dc,
    SWMMModelLayer *layer,
    QWidget *parent);
```

Internally hosts a `QStackedWidget` with one page per category. Each page is laid out with `QPropertyModel`-backed editors over a per-page `QObject` config wrapper exposing `Q_PROPERTY`s for the creation parameters drawn from the legacy SWMM-GUI's corresponding `D<type>.pas` form, modernised:

| Category | Legacy form | DA.3 page contents |
|----------|-------------|--------------------|
| Curves | `Dcurve.pas` | Name + Curve Type combo (Pump1 / Pump2 / Pump3 / Pump4 / Storage / Rating / Shape / Control / Diversion / Tidal / Weir — 11 variants) |
| Time Series | `Dtseries.pas` | Name + Source radio (Table / External file) + (if file) file picker |
| Patterns | `Dpattern.pas` | Name + Pattern Type combo (Monthly / Daily / Hourly / Weekend) |
| LID Controls | `Dlid.pas` | Name + LID Type combo (BioCell / RainGarden / GreenRoof / InfilTrench / PermPavement / RainBarrel / RoofDrain / VegSwale) |
| Pollutants | `Dpollut.pas` | Name + Units combo (mg/L / µg/L / Count/L) |
| Land Uses | `Dlanduse.pas` | Name only |
| Aquifers | `Daquifer.pas` | Name only |
| Snowpacks | `Dsnow.pas` | Name only |
| Transects | `Dtsect.pas` | Name only (station-elevation rows added via adapter "Edit…") |
| Streets | `Dstreet.pas` | Name only |
| Inlets | `Dinlet.pas` | Name + Inlet Type combo (GRATE / CURB / SLOTTED / CUSTOM) |
| Rain Gages | (map tool) | Name + Source combo (Time Series / External file) + Rainfall Type (Intensity / Volume / Cumulative) + Recording Interval |
| Control Rules | `Dcontrol.pas` | Name + skeleton template radio (Empty / Pump on/off / Orifice setting / Weir bypass — pre-canned `RULE` skeletons); creates via `swmm_control_add_rule(skeleton_with_user_name)` |
| Unit Hydrographs | `Dunithyd.pas` | Name + Rain Gage picker (combo of existing gages) + Response combo (Short / Medium / Long for the initial row); creates via `swmm_hydrograph_add_gage(name, gage)` + `swmm_hydrograph_add(name, -1, response, …)` with placeholder R/T/K values the user edits afterwards |

Each page pre-fills a unique auto-suggested default name via a new helper:

```cpp
// include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h
[[nodiscard]] QString suggestUniqueDataObjectName(DataCategory dc) const;
```

Implementation iterates `dataObjectCount(dc)` + `dataObjectNameAt(dc, i)` to find the smallest positive integer `n` such that `<Prefix><n>` is unused (case-insensitive). `<Prefix>` per category: `Curve` / `TS` / `Pattern` / `LID` / `Pollut` / `LandUse` / `Aquifer` / `Snowpack` / `Rule` / `Transect` / `UH` / `Street` / `Inlet` / `Gage`. User can overwrite in the dialog. **This is a modernisation over legacy SWMM-GUI**, which requires manual naming.

**On OK:**
1. Dialog returns a `NewObjectSpec { dc, name, options }` struct.
2. `addNewDataObject` switches on `dc` and dispatches the right `swmm_<type>_add(name, type_or_options…)` call (`swmm_curve_add(name, curveType)`, `swmm_pattern_add(name, patternType)`, etc.).
3. After success, emits the new `ObjectRef::DataObject(dc, name)` selection so the Attribute Panel hydrates with the DA.2 adapter, ready to edit the remaining fields.

**Data menu updates** ([src/swmmvis.cpp:1710-1722](../src/swmmvis.cpp)):
- Append `New Control &Rule…` → routes through the new dialog's Controls page.
- Append `New Unit &Hydrograph…` → routes through the new dialog's Hydrographs page.
- Append `New Rain &Gage…` (data-object path — the existing `actionAddRainGage` map tool stays for clicking on the map; menu path covers time-series-driven gages without map coordinates).
- Reorder to match BM.0.3: Time Series, Curves, Patterns, sep, LID Controls, Pollutants, Land Uses, sep, Aquifers, Snowpacks, sep, Control Rules, Transects, Unit Hydrographs, sep, Streets, Inlets, Rain Gages.

   - Data menu → New Unit Hydrograph… → fill dialog → verify group appears.

### ⏳ Slice DA.4 — Outfall stage-data editor + rich data-object editors + picker retrofit (Phase 6.2.7)

> **Status update (2026-05-25)**: closed for the outfall feature. DA.4.0 (engine getters) and DA.4.3 (outfall property surface + picker dispatch) shipped here. DA.4.1 / DA.4.2 (the four rich editor dialogs: Curve, TimeSeries, Pattern, UnitHydrograph) shipped independently via the Slice BR-PAT / Slice BQ Phase 6.7 work plus the `ComprehensiveEditorRegistry` (Slice BM.0-Browse-Edit) singleton. DA.4.4 (retrofit of `NodeCompoundEditDialog`'s 7 pickers through the same dispatch) is **deferred** — separate slice, not outfall-related.
>
> Net behaviour today on outfalls:
> 1. Property panel exposes Stage Elev. / Tidal Curve / Stage Time Series rows, with exactly one editable at a time based on the live Outfall Type.
> 2. "…" on Tidal Curve → `CurveEditorDialog::pickCurve` (modal, auto-selects on accept).
> 3. "…" on Stage Time Series → `TimeseriesEditorDialog::pickTimeseries` (modal, auto-flushes to engine + auto-selects).
> 4. All edits route through engine setters (`swmm_node_set_outfall_*`); the adapter's `changed()` signal drives QPropertyModel re-reads — single source of truth.

User-reported gap (2026-05-24): selecting Outfall Type = FIXED / TIDAL / TIMESERIES has no follow-on row in the Property Panel for the stage value or the curve/time-series reference. The boundary condition silently defaults to 0 / unassigned. The adapter header has been flagging this as forward work (`(StageData when FIXED). … Storage curve picker … land in AG.4` at [swmmnodepropertyadapter.h:239-240, 280](../include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h)).

User also asked that the "…" buttons on every data-object picker open a **rich interactive editor** (table + chart + source-mode toggle + Undo/Redo) — not the lightweight `NewDataObjectDialog` name+type form. This carves the core editor dialogs out of [Slice BQ Phase 6.7.3](#-slice-bq--concrete-editors-curves--transect--xsection--culvert--patterns--timeseries--unit-hydrograph-phase-67) and lands them now so both the new outfall pickers and the seven existing pickers in `NodeCompoundEditDialog` can use them.

DA.4 has four sub-phases. **DA.4.0** is the engine prerequisite bundle and must ship before any GUI work in this slice (mirrors the DA.1 engine-first pattern). **DA.4.1–.4** are the GUI layers, landing roughly in dependency order.

#### DA.4.0 — Engine prerequisites (must ship before any DA.4 GUI work)

| Gap ID | Header | New C API |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| DA.4-ENG-01 | `openswmm_nodes.h` | `SWMM_ENGINE_API int swmm_node_get_outfall_tidal(SWMM_Engine, int idx, int* curve_idx);`<br>`SWMM_ENGINE_API int swmm_node_get_outfall_timeseries(SWMM_Engine, int idx, int* ts_idx);` |
| DA.4-ENG-02 | `openswmm_tables.h` | `SWMM_ENGINE_API int swmm_pattern_get_type(SWMM_Engine, int idx, int* type);`<br>`SWMM_ENGINE_API int swmm_pattern_get_factor_count(SWMM_Engine, int idx, int* count);`<br>`SWMM_ENGINE_API int swmm_pattern_get_factor(SWMM_Engine, int idx, int i, double* v);` |

Both `swmm_node_get_outfall_tidal` and `_get_outfall_timeseries` are trivial reads of the existing `ctx.nodes.outfall_param` SoA slot with a type guard — return `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM` when the outfall is not currently of the matching type (since the param slot is union-typed in the SoA; see [openswmm_nodes_impl.cpp:516-535](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_nodes_impl.cpp)).

Pattern getters complement the existing setters. `swmm_pattern_get_factor_count` returns 12 (MONTHLY), 7 (DAILY), or 24 (HOURLY/WEEKEND) per type. The plural `swmm_pattern_get_factors(idx, out, max, *actual)` is an acceptable single-call alternative.

- `openswmm/engine/_tables.pyi` + `_tables.pyx`: expose `get_pattern_type`, `get_pattern_factor_count`, `get_pattern_factor`.
- New pytest cases in `python/tests/test_nodes.py` + `test_tables.py`.

**MCP follow-ups** (`openswmm.mcp`):
- Extend `get_outfall_info` to include the resolved curve/TS name when applicable.

#### DA.4.1 — Two rich editor dialogs: `CurveEditorDialog` + `TimeseriesEditorDialog`

Both follow the same architecture as the BQ Phase 6.7.3 design — MVC, table + interactive chart, source-mode toggle, Undo/Redo. They ship together so both pickers (curve, TS) have something to call.

**Shared infrastructure (new):**
```
include/ui/models/datapointtablemodel.{h,cpp}      QAbstractTableModel over QVector<QPair<double,double>>
include/ui/widgets/interactivexychartview.{h,cpp}  QChartView subclass: rubber-band select, Y-drag, R-click insert/delete
include/ui/widgets/datasourcemodepanel.{h,cpp}     Inline / ExternalFile radio + file picker (ExternalFile greyed in MVP per DA.4-ENG-05)
include/ui/undo/dataobjectundocommands.{h,cpp}     AddRow / RemoveRow / EditCell / RenameDataObject
```

`DataPointTableModel` supports CSV/TSV clipboard paste (newline = row, tab/comma = column), Insert/Delete keys, monotonicity validation (warning only — engine tolerates). Time-series mode renders column 0 as `QDateTime`; curves render as plain `double`.

`InteractiveXYChartView` is implemented standalone (does not inherit from BL/AT's planned `InteractiveChartView`; merge in a small refactor when AT lands).

**`CurveEditorDialog`** ([include/ui/dialogs/curveeditordialog.h](../include/ui/dialogs/curveeditordialog.h)):
```cpp
class CurveEditorDialog : public QDialog {
    Q_OBJECT
public:
    enum Mode { CreateNew, EditExisting };
    explicit CurveEditorDialog(SWMMModelLayer *layer, QWidget *parent = nullptr);
    void openForCurve(const QString &name);
    void openForCreate(int typeLock = -1, const QString &suggestedName = {});
    [[nodiscard]] QString finalName() const;
    [[nodiscard]] int     finalCurveType() const;
};
```

Layout: name `QLineEdit` (uniqueness validator) + Curve Type combo (12 entries, disabled when `typeLock>=0`) + `DataSourceModePanel` on top; `QTableView`(left) + `InteractiveXYChartView`(right) horizontally split; status bar + `QDialogButtonBox(Ok|Cancel|Apply)` on bottom. Apply commits without closing.

Persistence on Accept/Apply:
- Create: `swmm_curve_add(name, type)` + loop `swmm_table_add_point(idx, x, y)`. Rollback via `swmm_table_clear` on partial failure (engine has no `swmm_table_remove`; cleared empty curve is acceptable).
- Edit: row changes → `swmm_table_clear(idx)` + re-add. Type change → blocked in MVP (would require remove-and-readd of the table, which loses references; deferred). Rename → disabled in MVP per DA.4-ENG-03; user renames via Object Browser.

Modal from picker (`exec()` returns chosen name); non-modal from Object Browser double-click (`show()`).

**`TimeseriesEditorDialog`** ([include/ui/dialogs/timeserieseditordialog.h](../include/ui/dialogs/timeserieseditordialog.h)): same shape, no type combo, column 0 is `QDateTime`, persistence uses `swmm_timeseries_add` + `swmm_table_add_point` (time-as-decimal-days encoding handled in the dialog).

**Coordination with Slice BQ**: an amendment in Slice BQ (§L.BQ — to be added) marks Phase 6.7.3's curve + TS editors as **delivered by DA.4.1**; BQ retains responsibility for `TimeseriesProvider` / `TimeseriesRegistry` MVC abstraction, `GeopackageObserved` source mode, and advanced chart-edit modes (rotate/scale).

#### DA.4.2 — Two lighter editor dialogs: `PatternEditorDialog` + `UnitHydrographEditorDialog`

Required only because the picker retrofit (DA.4.4) needs them. Lighter UI (table + bar-chart preview, no source-mode panel).

**`PatternEditorDialog`** ([include/ui/dialogs/patterneditordialog.h](../include/ui/dialogs/patterneditordialog.h)):
- Pattern Type combo: Monthly (12) / Daily (7) / Hourly (24) / Weekend (24), disabled when launched with `typeLock>=0` (DWF pickers pass their specific type).
- Single column of multipliers; row count fixed by type; X-axis labelled month/weekday/hour.
- Preview: `QBarSeries` in `InteractiveXYChartView`.
- Persistence: `swmm_pattern_add(name, type)` + `swmm_pattern_set_factors(idx, factors, count)`.

**`UnitHydrographEditorDialog`** ([include/ui/dialogs/unithydrographeditordialog.h](../include/ui/dialogs/unithydrographeditordialog.h)):
- Header: name + Rain-Gage `LabeledPickerCombo` (gage names from existing data).
- Body: response (Short/Medium/Long) × month grid; three numeric sub-columns (R, T, K) per cell. Uses a custom `QTableWidget` — too nested for `DataPointTableModel` reuse.
- Persistence: `swmm_hydrograph_add_gage(name, gage)` + `swmm_hydrograph_set_rtk(name, month, response, R, T, K)` per cell.

#### DA.4.3 — Outfall property surface (the user-facing payload)

**Three new Q_PROPERTYs on `SWMMOutfallPropertyAdapter`** ([include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h:241-274](../include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h)):

```cpp
Q_PROPERTY(double         outfallStage
           READ outfallStage WRITE setOutfallStage NOTIFY changed)
Q_PROPERTY(DataObjectRef  outfallTidalCurve
           READ outfallTidalCurveRef WRITE setOutfallTidalCurveRef NOTIFY changed)
Q_PROPERTY(DataObjectRef  outfallTimeseries
           READ outfallTimeseriesRef WRITE setOutfallTimeseriesRef NOTIFY changed)
```

Getter strategy:
- `outfallStage()`: returns `swmm_node_get_outfall_param` only when type==FIXED; else 0.
- `outfallTidalCurveRef()`: when type==TIDAL, `swmm_node_get_outfall_tidal` → table id via `swmm_table_id`; else empty `currentName`.
- `outfallTimeseriesRef()`: parallel via `swmm_node_get_outfall_timeseries`.

Setter strategy: each calls the matching `swmm_node_set_outfall_*` and emits `changed()`. The ref setters resolve `currentName` → engine index via `swmm_table_index`.

Extends `displayLabelFor()` with three new branches:
- `outfallStage` → `Stage Elev. (ft|m)` (uses `lengthLabel()`)
- `outfallTidalCurve` → `Tidal Curve`
- `outfallTimeseries` → `Stage Time Series`

**`DataObjectRef` value type** (new, broader than `NodeCompoundEditRef`):
```
include/ui/properties/dataobjectref.{h,cpp}        Q_DECLARE_METATYPE, QString converter returning currentName
```
```cpp
struct DataObjectRef {
    enum Kind { TidalCurve, AnyCurve, TimeSeries, Pattern, UnitHydrograph };
    SWMM_Engine     engine = nullptr;
    SWMMModelLayer *layer  = nullptr;
    Kind            kind   = TimeSeries;
    int             typeLock = -1;        // for Pattern: pre-locked pattern type
    QString         currentName;          // empty when unassigned
};
```

**`DataObjectPickerEditor`** widget ([include/ui/properties/dataobjectpickereditor.h](../include/ui/properties/dataobjectpickereditor.h)) wraps a `LabeledPickerCombo` with `labelText=""`. Exposes `Q_PROPERTY(DataObjectRef value READ value WRITE setValue USER true)` so `QPropertyItemDelegate` round-trips transparently.

`setValue(ref)`:
1. Populate combo via the new `SWMMModelLayer::tableIdsOfType(int type)` helper (extracted from existing `NodeCompoundEditDialog::populateTimeSeriesCombo`); for `Pattern`/`UnitHydrograph`, use their dedicated count/id functions.
2. Pre-select `ref.currentName`.
3. Wire `pickerClicked` → context-aware `launchEditor()` (see DA.4.4 — `DataObjectLauncher::launch`).
4. Wire `currentTextChanged` → mutate `m_ref.currentName`, emit `valueChanged()` so the delegate writes back via the adapter setter.

**Conditional editability** in [src/ui/panels/attributepanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/attributepanel.cpp), where the node adapter is bound. New helper `setRowEditable(QPropertyModel*, const QString &propName, bool)` toggles a property item's `setFlags(...)` (the framework's existing mechanism — see [QPropertyModel/include/qpropertyitem.h:65-69, 199-209](../../QPropertyModel/include/qpropertyitem.h) and [QPropertyModel/src/qfontpropertyitem.cpp:255-274](../../QPropertyModel/src/qfontpropertyitem.cpp)).

```cpp
auto updateOutfallRowFlags = [pm, adapter]() {
    const auto t = adapter->outfallType();
    setRowEditable(pm, "outfallStage",      t == SWMMNodePropertyAdapter::FIXED);
    setRowEditable(pm, "outfallTidalCurve", t == SWMMNodePropertyAdapter::TIDAL);
    setRowEditable(pm, "outfallTimeseries", t == SWMMNodePropertyAdapter::TIMESERIES);
};
connect(adapter, &SWMMNodePropertyAdapter::changed, pm, updateOutfallRowFlags);
updateOutfallRowFlags();  // initial pass
```

Reuses `changed()` (already emitted by every adapter setter) — no new signal. Inapplicable rows show as greyed but still visible (so the user sees what *would* apply). Because the engine uses one shared `outfall_param` slot, the disabled rows' getters return 0/empty, and the picker correctly shows no current assignment after a type switch — which matches reality.

#### DA.4.4 — Retrofit existing pickers + `DataObjectLauncher` dispatcher

New centralised dispatch helper `include/ui/properties/dataobjectlauncher.{h,cpp}`:
```cpp
struct DataObjectLauncher {
    // Returns the final selected name on Accept; empty on Cancel.
    static QString launch(SWMMModelLayer *layer,
                          DataObjectRef::Kind kind,
                          int typeLock,
                          const QString &currentName,
                          QWidget *parent);
};
```
Switches on `kind` → constructs and `exec()`s the right editor dialog (DA.4.1/.2) in CreateNew or EditExisting mode based on whether `currentName` is empty.

Both surfaces call it:
- **DataObjectPickerEditor** (DA.4.3) — outfall pickers.
- **NodeCompoundEditDialog** — all 7 existing pickers retrofitted by extending `wirePicker` ([src/ui/dialogs/nodecompoundeditdialog.cpp:161-173](../src/ui/dialogs/nodecompoundeditdialog.cpp)) with a `typeLock` parameter and a `DataObjectRef::Kind` field. Callsite mapping:

| Picker | Kind | typeLock |
|--------|------|----------|
| `m_inflowsTsPicker` | TimeSeries | -1 |
| `m_inflowsPatPicker` | Pattern | -1 (any) |
| `m_dwfPat1Picker` | Pattern | MONTHLY |
| `m_dwfPat2Picker` | Pattern | DAILY |
| `m_dwfPat3Picker` | Pattern | HOURLY |
| `m_dwfPat4Picker` | Pattern | WEEKEND |
| `m_rdiiUhPicker` | UnitHydrograph | -1 |

`NewDataObjectDialog` is retained for the Data menu "New …" entries (lightweight name+type form for users who only want to create-and-walk-away).

**Engine:** `ctest -R outfall -R pattern --output-on-failure` — all new cases green; full engine suite green. `pytest python/tests/test_nodes.py python/tests/test_tables.py -v`.

**GUI manual verification (load-bearing):**
1. Open an outfall in the property panel — three new grey rows (Stage Elev., Tidal Curve, Stage Time Series) appear below Outfall Type. Switching type enables exactly one row at a time.
2. FIXED + enter 12.5 → Python REPL confirms `engine.get_outfall_param(idx) == 12.5`.
3. TIDAL + pick a curve from combo (combo lists only type==6/TIDAL curves) → `engine.get_outfall_tidal(idx)` returns that curve's idx.

10. Switch outfall type TIDAL → FIXED → TIDAL: combo reads empty after switch (matches current engine behaviour — `outfall_param` is a union slot). Tooltip on the row notes that prior assignments are not preserved across type changes (DA.4-ENG-04 follow-up planned).

### ⏳ Slice BM.0 — Non-Spatial Data Objects: Object Browser section + Data menu + CRUD entry points (Phase 6.2.5)

The current Object Browser only surfaces spatial objects (nodes, links, subcatchments, rain gages). Every non-spatial SWMM data type — Curves, Time Series, Time Patterns, LID Controls, Pollutants, Land Uses, Aquifer definitions, Snowpack definitions, Control Rules, Transects, and Unit Hydrographs — has no navigation entry point in the GUI. Editors planned in BM–BQ presuppose this layer. BM.0 delivers it and is a **hard prerequisite** for all BN–BQ concrete editor slices.

**Design principle:** the modernised OpenSWMM GUI does not replicate the legacy per-modal-dialog approach. Non-spatial data objects are first-class citizens in the Object Browser; they are listed, created, renamed and deleted from the same tree-and-context-menu infrastructure used for spatial objects. A top-level **Data** menu provides keyboard-accelerated shortcuts; a compact toolbar strip covers the 5 most-used types. No standalone modal table-of-all-curves-type dialogs.

#### BM.0.1 — Object Browser: "Data Objects" section

Extend the Object Browser tree with a second root section rendered below the network-objects section, headed **"Data Objects"**, collapsed by default. It contains one collapsible group per non-spatial type:

| Group | Engine count accessor | Engine name accessor | Backing header |
|-------|-----------------------|----------------------|----------------|
| Curves | `swmm_curve_count` | `swmm_curve_id(i)` | `openswmm_tables.h` |
| Time Series | `swmm_timeseries_count` | `swmm_timeseries_id(i)` | `openswmm_tables.h` |
| Time Patterns | `swmm_pattern_count` | `swmm_pattern_id(i)` | `openswmm_tables.h` |
| LID Controls | `swmm_lid_count` | `swmm_lid_id(i)` | `openswmm_infrastructure.h` |
| Pollutants | `swmm_pollutant_count` | `swmm_pollutant_id(i)` | `openswmm_pollutants.h` |
| Land Uses | `swmm_landuse_count` | `swmm_landuse_id(i)` | `openswmm_quality.h` |
| Aquifers | `swmm_aquifer_count` | `swmm_aquifer_id(i)` | `openswmm_subcatchments.h` |
| Snowpack | `swmm_snowpack_count` | `swmm_snowpack_id(i)` | `openswmm_subcatchments.h` |
| Control Rules | `swmm_control_count` | `swmm_control_id(i)` | `openswmm_controls.h` |
| Transects | `swmm_transect_count` | `swmm_transect_id(i)` | `openswmm_tables.h` |
| Unit Hydrographs | `swmm_rdii_uh_group_count` | `swmm_rdii_uh_group_id(i)` | `openswmm_inflows.h` |
| Streets | `swmm_street_count` | `swmm_street_id(i)` | `openswmm_streets.h` (verify; engine gap BO-STREET-01 if absent) |
| Inlets | `swmm_inlet_count` | `swmm_inlet_id(i)` | `openswmm_inlets.h` (verify; engine gap BO-INLET-01 if absent) |

Each group header shows a live count "(n)". Leaves show the object name only. Clicking a leaf selects it in the shared `SelectionManager` under a new `ObjectRef::DataObject` subtype; double-clicking opens the appropriate editor (delegated to BM–BQ via `PropertyEditorRegistry`).

`SWMMObjectTreeModel` gains a second "section" root alongside the existing network section. A non-selectable visual-divider row separates the two sections. The virtualised model strategy from Slice S applies unchanged — leaves materialise only for visible rows.

`SWMMModelLayer` gains a parallel `DataCategory` enum (mirrors the table above) and the same `dataObjectCount(DataCategory)` / `dataObjectNameAt(DataCategory, int)` accessors as the existing spatial `categoryCount` / `objectNameAt` pair.

#### BM.0.2 — Context menus on Data Object groups and leaves

**Right-click a group header (e.g., "Time Series"):**

| Action | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Add New [Type]… | **Per Slice BM.0-Add-New (2026-05-24):** disabled with a tooltip naming the future editor slice for categories without a complex editor. For Time Series: opens `TimeseriesEditorDialog::createNew` (name + source-mode card; transitions to edit mode on Create). For Unit Hydrographs: opens `HydrographGroupEditor::beginNewGroup()` (wraps the left-pane "New" button). `NewDataObjectDialog` removed. |
| Import from File… | File picker + format-mapping wizard (CSV / DAT / xlsx depending on type) |
| Select All | Selects all leaves in the group |
| Sort A→Z | One-shot alphabetical reorder (same contract as AY.2 category sort) |
| Expand / Collapse | Standard tree ops |

**Right-click a leaf (e.g., a named curve):**

| Action | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Edit [Name]… | Opens the type-specific editor (BM–BQ) |
| Rename | Inline rename in the tree; persisted via `swmm_{type}_set_name` |
| Duplicate | Creates a copy with a generated name (`{name}_copy`) via `swmm_{type}_duplicate` or add + field-copy loop if no duplicate API exists |
| Delete | Confirmation → `swmm_{type}_remove` + tree refresh |
| Properties | Opens editor same as "Edit [Name]…" |

**Multi-select (same-type only):**

| Action | Available when |
|--------|----------------|
| Delete Selected | All selected leaves are the same group type |
| Duplicate Selected | Same restriction |

Cross-type multi-select disables destructive actions with a tooltip ("Select objects of the same type to delete/duplicate").

#### BM.0.5 — Engine API gap audit

The following symbols are required. Verify each against `openswmm_tables.h`, `openswmm_infrastructure.h`, `openswmm_pollutants.h`, `openswmm_quality.h`, `openswmm_controls.h`, `openswmm_inflows.h`; file a gap request (`BM.0-API.md`) for any that are absent:

| Operation | Expected symbol form |
|-----------|---------------------|
| Count of each type | `swmm_{type}_count(engine, int* out)` |
| Name by index | `swmm_{type}_id(engine, int idx)` |
| Add by name | `swmm_{type}_add(engine, const char* name)` |
| Remove by index | `swmm_{type}_remove(engine, int idx)` |
| Rename | `swmm_{type}_set_name(engine, int idx, const char* name)` |
| Duplicate | `swmm_{type}_duplicate(engine, int idx, const char* new_name)` — file gap if absent; fallback is add + field-copy loop |

Where `{type}` is: `curve`, `timeseries`, `pattern`, `lid`, `pollutant`, `landuse`, `aquifer`, `snowpack`, `control`, `transect`, `rdii_uh_group`, `street`, `inlet`.

#### BM.0.6 — Non-spatial property adapters

Slice AG.3 defines twelve typed property adapters for spatial objects (Junction, Outfall, Storage, Divider, Conduit, Pump, Orifice, Weir, Outlet, Subcatchment, Raingage, plus the base node/link). The non-spatial Data Objects added in BM.0.1 also need adapters so they hydrate `AttributePanel` when selected from the Data Objects tree (closes gap analysis item G15). New adapter files (one Q_OBJECT per class, mirrors AG.3 shape) under `include/ui/properties/`:

```
swmmcurvepropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmtimeseriespropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmpatternpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmlidcontrolpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmpollutantpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmlandusepropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmaquiferpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmsnowpackpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmcontrolrulepropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmtransectpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmhydrographpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmmstreetpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmminletpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
swmminletusagepropertyadapter.{h,cpp}
```

Each adapter exposes the same Q_PROPERTY set its dedicated editor edits (BN–BS) so that single-line edits work in `AttributePanel` even before the full editor is opened. For sub-object grids (e.g. a curve's X-Y rows, a pattern's 24 hourly values, a transect's station-elevation table) the adapter exposes a single Q_PROPERTY of type `QVariant` (row count + summary string) with an "Edit…" `ButtonCellDelegate` that opens the full editor.

**Note 2026-05-22:** the 14 non-spatial adapters and the `AttributePanel::routeNonSpatialFeature` dispatch land in Slice DA.2 (horizontal first cut). BM.0.6 retains only the residual `PropertyEditorRegistry` factory registration step once DA.2 ships.

### ⏳ Slice BM — Property editor framework (`PropertyEditorRegistry`) (Phase 6.3)

Today the GUI has skeletal `swmm{node,link,subcatch}propertyadapter.cpp` (Property Browser) and the Slice AG draft for compound editors. BM formalises the pattern into a registry so every legacy object class can be plugged in without bespoke wiring.

**Note 2026-05-22:** `AttributePanel` non-spatial dispatch + the 14 non-spatial adapters + the `SWMMObjectRef::DataObject(category, name)` payload ship in Slice DA.2 as a horizontal first cut. BM now reduces to: (a) formalising `IPropertyEditor` as the polymorphic contract DA.2's adapters already conform to; (b) `PropertyEditorRegistry::register(kind, factory)` factory pattern; (c) the shared `LabeledControls` form-helper widgets used by BN–BS structured editors; (d) per-project `QUndoStack` integration. Phase 6.3.2 dispatch + Phase 6.3.4 sidebar mode considered shipped via DA.2.

- **Phase 6.3.1 — `IPropertyEditor` interface**: New `include/ui/properties/ipropertyeditor.h` — `virtual QWidget* editorForObject(const ObjectRef&)`, `virtual void apply(const ObjectRef&) = 0`, `virtual QString objectKind() const = 0`. Owned by `PropertyEditorRegistry`.
- **Phase 6.3.2 — Registry + dispatch**: `PropertyEditorRegistry::register(kind, factory)`. `AttributePanel` calls `registry.editorFor(ref)` on selection change.
- **Phase 6.3.3 — Common form helpers**: `LabeledLineEdit`, `LabeledDoubleSpin`, `LabeledCombo`, `LabeledFilePicker`, `SubsectionGroupBox`, `ConditionalSubEditor` (shown only when a parent enum is set).
- **Phase 6.3.4 — Property-Browser sidebar mode**: Each editor declares which fields show in the in-panel sidebar vs. need an "Edit…" dialog (long fields like rule text, transect tables).
- **Phase 6.3.5 — Undo integration**: Edits route through per-project `QUndoStack` (exists for Slice AW).
- **Files**: new `include/ui/properties/ipropertyeditor.h`, `propertyeditorregistry.h`, `include/ui/widgets/labeledcontrols.h` + .cpps; touches `src/ui/panels/attributepanel.cpp`.
- **Engine APIs**: none directly — each downstream editor calls its own engine surface.
- **Tests**: `test_propertyeditorregistry.cpp` (6 cases — register/lookup, missing-kind fallback, undo apply/revert).
- **Manual**: `docs/manual/25_properties.md` (overview chapter).
- **Dependencies**: BM.0, AG, Z, L.
- **Deferred**: schema-driven YAML editor generation (future slice CU).

### ⏳ Slice BN — Concrete editors: hydraulic nodes + links (10 editors) (Phase 6.4)

One editor each for: Junction, Outfall, Storage, Divider, Conduit, Pump, Orifice, Weir, Outlet + the XSection sub-editor (26 shapes + dummy, see Phase 6.4.4 below) + the Street sub-editor (Phase 6.4.6). Drives every `swmm_node_*` / `swmm_link_*` setter/getter.

- **Phase 6.4.1 — `JunctionEditor`, `OutfallEditor`, `StorageEditor`, `DividerEditor`**: 4 node kinds + right-click "Change Type…" (engine gap AG.1 — `swmm_node_change_type` from AG_GUI_API_REQUEST §1).
- **Phase 6.4.2 — `ConduitEditor`**: invert offsets, length, roughness, init flow, max flow, entrance / exit / average loss coeffs, seepage, check valve, culvert code (BQ.6.7.5), inlet usage (BO.6.5.8), barrels, geometry → `XSectionEditor` sub-editor (Phase 6.4.4).
- **Phase 6.4.3 — `PumpEditor`, `OrificeEditor`, `WeirEditor`, `OutletEditor`**: compound conditional fields. `OrificeEditor` exposes Type (SIDE / BOTTOM) and Shape (CIRCULAR / RECTANGULAR) with Height / Width gated by Shape. `WeirEditor` exposes Weir Type (TRANSVERSE / SIDEFLOW / V-NOTCH / TRAPEZOIDAL / RECT / ROADWAY) with Roadway-only sub-group `{Roadway Width, Road Surface enum, Weir Shape enum}` and end-contractions only when TRANSVERSE. `OutletEditor` toggles between functional (Discharge Coeff + Exponent) and tabular (Outlet Curve name picker). `PumpEditor` shows Pump Curve picker + Startup / Shutoff depth + initial Status combo.
- **Phase 6.4.4 — `XSectionEditor` (sub-dialog launched from `ConduitEditor`'s "Geometry…" row)**: closes legacy `Dxsect.pas`. Two-pane modal:
  - **Left pane — Shape picker.** `QListView` in `IconMode` with grid size ~96×112, scrollable, search box, **26 shape entries** matching the legacy enum: CIRCULAR, FORCE_MAIN, FILLED_CIRCULAR, RECT_CLOSED, RECT_OPEN, TRAPEZOIDAL, TRIANGULAR, PARABOLIC, POWER, RECT_TRIANGULAR, RECT_ROUND, MOD_BASKETHANDLE, HORIZ_ELLIPSE, VERT_ELLIPSE, ARCH, EGG, HORSESHOE, GOTHIC, CATENARY, SEMIELLIPTICAL, BASKETHANDLE, SEMICIRCULAR, IRREGULAR, CUSTOM, STREET, DUMMY (plus shape code `DUMMY` as terminator). Icons sourced from new `resources/xsects/<shape>.svg` — extracted once (offline tooling) from legacy `SWMM-GUI/Epaswmm5/Xsects.res` then restyled to match app theme (Slice CJ); fallback recolour for light / dark.
  - **Right pane — Parameters + live parametric figure.** Top half is a procedurally-drawn live preview (QGraphicsScene or QSvgGenerator) that redraws on every Geom1–4 change (`valueChanged` debounced 50 ms). For parametric shapes (circular, rect-open, rect-closed, trapezoidal, triangular, parabolic, power, filled-circular, rect-triangular, rect-round, mod-baskethandle) the figure is closed-form; for fixed-geometry standard shapes (egg, horseshoe, gothic, catenary, semielliptical, basket-handle, semicircular) it reuses the same SVG asset rendered full-size in app-theme colours; for IRREGULAR it embeds a read-only copy of the assigned transect's profile widget (from BQ.6.7.4) plus "[Edit transect…]" launching `TransectEditor`; for CUSTOM it shows a placeholder + "[Edit shape curve…]" launching the BQ `CurveEditor` filtered to type SHAPE; for STREET it shows a stylised street section + "[Edit street section…]" launching `StreetEditor` (Phase 6.4.6); for DUMMY a greyed placeholder with text "DUMMY conduit — no hydraulic effect". The figure annotates each visible Geom parameter with a dimension arrow and current value; hovering a parameter spinbox highlights its arrow. Below the figure: a checkbox "Show design-flow water surface" overlays a horizontal water line at the depth corresponding to full-flow capacity (or user value).
  - **Per-shape parameter labels** (matches legacy `XsectShapes` table): CIRCULAR → Diameter (Geom1); FORCE_MAIN → Diameter + Roughness; FILLED_CIRCULAR → Diameter + Filled Depth; RECT_CLOSED / RECT_OPEN → Max Depth + Bottom Width; TRAPEZOIDAL → Max Depth + Bottom Width + Left Slope + Right Slope; TRIANGULAR → Max Depth + Top Width; PARABOLIC → Max Depth + Top Width; POWER → Max Depth + Top Width + Exponent; RECT_TRIANGULAR → Max Depth + Top Width + Triangle Height; RECT_ROUND → Max Depth + Top Width + Bottom Radius; MOD_BASKETHANDLE → Max Depth + Bottom Width + Top Radius; HORIZ_ELLIPSE / VERT_ELLIPSE / ARCH → Max Width + Max Height + [Standard size] (button-launched `StandardSizeDialog` — replaces legacy `Darchpipe.pas` — single-page table of standard size codes → dimensions, filterable, double-click fills Geom1/Geom2); EGG / HORSESHOE / GOTHIC / CATENARY / SEMIELLIPTICAL / BASKETHANDLE / SEMICIRCULAR → Max Depth (single param); IRREGULAR → Transect name picker; CUSTOM → Shape Curve name picker + Max Depth; STREET → Street name picker; DUMMY → no params.
  - **Conduit-wide extras** also exposed on this dialog so users don't bounce: **Barrels** (number of parallel conduits, integer ≥ 1, default 1) and the **Sidewalls** combo for RECT_OPEN (`BOTH` / `LEFT_ONLY` / `RIGHT_ONLY` / `NONE` — legacy `SidewallsCombo`, used by 2D-coupling). These are conduit-level fields but live in `XSectionEditor` to match the legacy UX.
  - **Derived read-out** (read-only group below parameters): full-flow capacity (computed via Manning's with current roughness + conduit slope), cross-section area at full depth, hydraulic radius. Helps user sanity-check.
  - **Engine wiring**: `openswmm_links.h::swmm_link_set_xsection_*` (verify exact symbol set covers all shape parameters; if Geom5+ is needed for any shape, file engine gap BN-XS-01). For IRREGULAR a transect lookup is needed (`swmm_transect_*`); for CUSTOM a shape-curve lookup (`swmm_curve_*`).
  - **Tests**: `test_xsection_editor.cpp` — 26 round-trip cases (one per shape, asserts `XSectionEditor` ↔ engine setter round-trip), parameter-change → figure-redraw signal asserted via `QSignalSpy`, `StandardSizeDialog` application sets Geom1/Geom2 correctly for HORIZ_ELLIPSE / VERT_ELLIPSE / ARCH, IRREGULAR with unset transect shows the placeholder, CUSTOM with missing shape-curve shows the placeholder.
- **Phase 6.4.5 — Variable-speed pump support**: `PumpEditor` exposes new engine fields (verify exact symbol names in `openswmm_links.h`).
- **Phase 6.4.6 — `StreetEditor` (sub-dialog launched from `XSectionEditor` when shape = STREET; also reachable as standalone editor for the STREET object class, legacy class 33)**: closes legacy `Dstreet.pas`. Single modal with three column-groups: **Street main** (Crown Width, Curb Height, Cross Slope %, Manning's Roughness, Sides combo `ONE_SIDE` / `TWO_SIDES`), **Gutter** (Depression / Gutter Depth, Gutter Width), **Backing** (Back Width, Back Slope %, Back Surface Manning's N). Right-side live parametric figure drawn the same way as `XSectionEditor`: full-width street cross-section with curb / gutter / crown / back panels annotated with dimension arrows. Engine wiring: `openswmm_streets.h` (verify accessor set; if missing, file engine gap BN-STREET-01).
- **Files**: ~22 new files under `include/ui/properties/editors/` + `src/ui/properties/editors/` (the original ~20 estimate + `xsectioneditor.{h,cpp}`, `streeteditor.{h,cpp}`, `standardsizedialog.{h,cpp}`, `xsectionfigurewidget.{h,cpp}`). New asset folder `resources/xsects/` with 26 SVG icons.
- **Engine APIs**: `openswmm_nodes.h::swmm_node_set_*`, `openswmm_links.h::swmm_link_set_*`, `openswmm_links.h::swmm_link_set_xsection_*`, `openswmm_streets.h::swmm_street_*`, `openswmm_edit.h::swmm_*_add/_remove`.
- **Engine gap**: AG.1 (`swmm_node_change_type`, `swmm_link_change_type`); possibly BN-XS-01 / BN-STREET-01 (verify at slice-start).
- **Tests**: `test_node_editors.cpp` (24 cases — per-type roundtrip + change-type), `test_link_editors.cpp` (28 cases incl. Roadway weir extras), `test_xsection_editor.cpp` (≥ 30 cases — 26 shape round-trips + figure-redraw + standard-size + transect/custom/street/dummy branches), `test_street_editor.cpp` (8 cases — per-field round-trip + sides toggle hides Back panel).
- **Manual**: `docs/manual/26_node_link_editors.md` (+ section on XSection + Street).
- **Dependencies**: BM, AG. `StandardSizeDialog`'s size-table data lives next to the editor as a static `QVector<StdSizeRow>` (extracted once from `Darchpipe.pas`).

### ⏳ Slice BQ — Concrete editors: curves / transect / xsection / culvert / patterns / timeseries / unit hydrograph (Phase 6.7)

> **Note (Slice BM.0-Add-New, 2026-05-24):** Add-New for **Transects** is currently disabled in the Object Browser with a tooltip naming this slice; landing the corresponding editor below re-enables it (one-line edit to `ObjectBrowserPanel::hasComplexEditor` + `gapTooltipFor`).
