The "tables" family — every named curve, pattern, time-series, transect, custom-xsection, culvert-code, and RDII unit-hydrograph response set. Closes Slice AH placeholder.

- **Phase 6.7.1 — `CurveEditor`** *(MVC, 3-panel, ✅ shipped 2026-05-24)*: non-modal three-pane editor for SWMM curves — left pane is a `QListView` of every curve in the project, centre pane is a 2-column `QTableView` (X / Y) with type combo at top, type-driven column headers (`CurveProvider::xLabel(type)` / `yLabel(type)` — e.g. "Depth | Surface Area" for Storage, "Volume | Flow" for Pump1, "Head | Flow" for Rating), Add Row / Delete Row(s) buttons; right pane is a Qt-Charts line + scatter chart with axis titles bound to type. **11 curve types** supported (the engine type-code space): Storage (1), Diversion (2), Rating (3), Shape (4), Control (5), Tidal (6), Pump1 (7), Pump2 (8), Pump3 (9), Pump4 (10), Pump5 (11) — note the original phase-doc list said "8 types incl. Weir" but the engine has no separate Weir curve type (weir coefficient curves are handled via the standard Rating shape). MVC layer: `CurveProvider` (one `QObject` per curve; `(x,y)` point array with strictly-monotone-X invariant validated by `setAllPoints` / `setPointAt` / `insertPoint`; emits `pointsChanged(first,count)`, `pointsInserted`, `pointsRemoved`, `typeChanged`, `nameChanged`, `mutationRejected`) + `CurveRegistry` (case-insensitive name uniqueness + `loadFromEngine` filtering `swmm_table_get_type != 0` + `saveToEngine` via `swmm_curve_add` + `swmm_table_clear` + `swmm_table_add_point` loop). Per Slice BM.0-Add-New, exposes `CurveEditorDialog::createNew(registry, undoStack, parent)` wired into the Object Browser Add-New dispatch; double-click on a `CURVE` leaf routes here too. **Files**: `include/curve/curveprovider.{h,cpp}`, `include/curve/curveregistry.{h,cpp}`, `include/ui/panels/curvepointtablemodel.{h,cpp}`, `include/ui/dialogs/curveeditordialog.{h,cpp}`. **Tests**: `tests/gui/test_curve_editor_dialog.cpp`. **Deferred**: CSV-paste into the grid (mirrors the Phase 6.7.3.4 parser extraction — wait until `TimeseriesParse::parseRow` generalises to numeric X/Y); per-point drag-edit on the chart (Phase 6.7.1-followup); a separate per-pump-type field hint panel (the type combo's tooltip currently shows the full label, e.g. "Pump 1 (Volume → Flow)"); undo-commands integration with the project `QUndoStack`.
- **Phase 6.7.2 — `PatternEditor`** *(MVC, 3-panel, ✅ shipped 2026-05-24)*: non-modal three-pane editor (`QSplitter`) for SWMM time patterns — left pane is a `QListView` of every pattern in the project (Monthly / Daily / Hourly / Weekend), centre pane is a single-column `QTableView` whose row schema is type-driven (Jan…Dec / Sun…Sat / 00:00…23:00) with a **Normalize** button + spinbox that rescales every factor so they sum to the target value (default 1.0; user-facing UX confirmed in the slice plan), right pane is a Qt-Charts bar-chart preview that refreshes live on every factor change. MVC layer: `PatternProvider` (one `QObject` per pattern; fixed-size factor array; emits `factorChanged(i)`, `factorsChanged()`, `typeChanged(prev,now)`, `mutationRejected(reason)`) + `PatternRegistry` (project-scoped factory + case-insensitive name uniqueness + `loadFromEngine` walking `swmm_pattern_*` + `saveToEngine` via `swmm_pattern_add` / `swmm_pattern_set_factors`). Per Slice BM.0-Add-New, the dialog exposes a static `PatternEditorDialog::createNew(registry, undoStack, parent)` factory wired into the Object Browser Add-New dispatch; double-click on a `TIMEPATTERN` leaf also routes here (single instance kept alive across clicks). Engine APIs needed (all already shipped per `openswmm_tables.h`): `swmm_pattern_add` / `_count` / `_index` / `_id` / `_get_type` / `_get_factor_count` / `_get_factor` / `_set_factors`. **Files**: `include/pattern/patternprovider.{h,cpp}`, `include/pattern/patternregistry.{h,cpp}`, `include/ui/panels/patternfactortablemodel.{h,cpp}`, `include/ui/dialogs/patterneditordialog.{h,cpp}`. **Test**: `tests/gui/test_pattern_editor_dialog.cpp` (12 cases — factor count per type, setFactor / setAllFactors validation, normalize semantics + zero-sum refusal, type-change reset, registry CRUD + case-insensitive lookup, table model bind + edit, dialog open + first-bind, list selection rebinds, normalize button rescales, createNew → submit transitions, providerAdded syncs the list). **Deferred**: per-factor drag-edit on the chart bars (Phase 6.7.2-followup); CSV paste into the grid (mirrors Phase 6.7.3.4 — wait until the parser is extracted); undo-commands integration with the project `QUndoStack` (set up the stack handle now, push commands in a follow-up).
- **Phase 6.7.3 — `TimeseriesEditorDialog` + `TimeseriesProvider` MVC** *(replaces the one-line stub 2026-05-24)*: a two-pane modeless dialog that edits one or more sibling `Tseries` objects through a single shared per-Tseries model object, satisfying the user's "same data, multiple UIs, always in sync" contract. A timeseries may be **inline** (stored in `.inp` or geopackage tables) or linked to an **external CSV / TSV / native .dat** file; external mode is read-only preview + plot with a one-way **Convert-to-Inline** path that supersedes the legacy mutual-exclusion checkbox. Multi-column external files use the engine's planned `FILE "path.csv:COL"` syntax (each column = one independent named Tseries); column headers in the grid ARE the Tseries names and renaming cascades through every model reference (inflows, rain gages, controls, climatology). Legacy floor only: `Dtseries.pas` supplies the capabilities checklist (3-col `(date,time,value)` parity, duplicate-name + non-monotone-time validation, `.dat` round-trip); its layout is not normative.
  - **Phase 6.7.3.1 — `TimeseriesProvider` (model + single source of truth)**. New `QObject` per Tseries, owned by a project-scoped `TimeseriesRegistry`. Carries `enum SourceMode { Inline, ExternalFile, GeopackageObserved }` (Inline = `[TIMESERIES]` inline rows; ExternalFile = `FILE "path[:COL]"`; GeopackageObserved = rows in the gpkg `observed_series` table per `openswmm_geopackage.h::swmm_gpkg_create_observed_series` / `_write_observed_values`), `QString name` (Tseries ID; uniqueness owned by the registry), `QString unitsLabel` inferred from column suffixes (`_m`, `_ft3s`) per the convention already in `ObservedCsvRunLayer`, `QVector<QPair<QDateTime,double>> points` strictly ascending in time for Inline / GpkgObserved modes, and `(filePath, columnSelector, fileMTime)` plus a lazy read-through cache for ExternalFile mode. Signals: `pointsChanged(int firstIndex, int count)`, `pointsInserted(int at, int count)`, `pointsRemoved(int at, int count)`, `metadataChanged()`, `sourceModeChanged(SourceMode prev, SourceMode now)`, `nameChanged(QString prev, QString now)`, `mutationRejected(QString reason)`. **Invariant**: strict-monotone-ascending time; the provider refuses any mutation that would violate it (drag-edit must surface the rejection in the status bar — never silently reorder, which would lose user intent). All mutations route through `QUndoCommand` subclasses (`SetPointValueCommand`, `MovePointCommand`, `InsertPointCommand`, `DeletePointsCommand`, `BulkTransformCommand`, `RenameCommand`, `ChangeSourceModeCommand`) pushed onto the project's main `QUndoStack` so a single Cmd-Z unwinds across grid, plot, and property dialog uniformly. *Per [[feedback_mvc_synchronized_uis]].*
  - **Phase 6.7.3.2 — `TimeseriesRegistry` (project-scoped factory + lookup)**. One per open project, owned by the project model next to Curves / Patterns. Loads all `[TIMESERIES]` entries from the engine via `swmm_timeseries_*` on project open into `TimeseriesProvider` instances; creates new providers; **enforces name uniqueness** with the case-insensitive check that matches the legacy validator; emits `providerAdded` / `providerRemoved` / `providerRenamed` for the Object Browser (Slice BM.0) and the editor dialog's column-tab strip to listen to. Renaming a provider also rewrites every reference in dependent objects via a `RenameTseriesReferenceCommand` composite — same pattern as Slice BU group-edit composites.
  - **Phase 6.7.3.3 — `TimeseriesEditorDialog` (two-pane shell, modeless)**. `QSplitter`-based, `Qt::Tool | Qt::WindowStaysOnTopHint` per the `ChartPropertiesDialog` convention so the user can edit while keeping other windows visible. Top toolbar: source-mode card (radio set Inline / ExternalFile / GeopackageObserved), edit-mode toolbar mirrored from `InteractiveChartView::Mode` (Select / Pan / ZoomIn / ZoomOut **plus new** EditPoints / RotatePoints / ScalePoints), Undo / Redo buttons bound to the project's stack, Convert-to-Inline button (enabled only in ExternalFile mode), Import / Export menu (CSV / TSV / .dat — file-format selector controls header writing). Closing the dialog does **not** discard edits (they live on the provider + undo stack); Cancel-only behaviour is intentionally absent. Provider data already shows up in any other open view (Object Browser property pane, calibration dock) via signal subscription with no manual refresh path. **Per Slice BM.0-Add-New (2026-05-24):** the dialog gains a `static TimeseriesEditorDialog *createNew(TimeseriesRegistry *registry, QUndoStack *stack, QWidget *parent = nullptr)` factory that opens the dialog in `Mode::CreateNew` (name field + source-mode card up front, edit toolbar hidden). On Create the dialog calls `registry->create(name)`, captures the returned provider via `providerAdded`, transitions to `Mode::Edit`, and hides the create-card. The existing edit-mode constructor `TimeseriesEditorDialog(TimeseriesProvider *, QUndoStack *, QWidget *)` is unchanged.
  - **Phase 6.7.3.4 — `TimeseriesTableModel` + grid pane (left)**. `QAbstractTableModel` subclass over `QVector<TimeseriesProvider *>` (one provider per column). Schema: column 0 = `QDateTime` (date+time merged), followed by one numeric value column per active sibling provider. The grid auto-pivots multiple providers that share a common time grid into one wide view, and falls back to one timestamp column per provider when grids diverge. The model's `setData` builds an undo command and calls `TimeseriesProvider::requestSetPoint`; subscribers to `pointsChanged` (the plot, other open dialogs) refresh automatically. Per-cell editors use `QCustomDateTimeEdit` and `QCustomDoubleSpinBox` from QPropertyModel — no hand-rolled date or number cells (per [[feedback_property_model_editors]]). **Column header is editable in place** → renames the underlying provider via `RenameCommand`; right-click on header offers **Set units**, **Set description**, **Remove series from grid** (UI-only — does not delete the provider), **Delete series…** (deletes the provider with a reference-count warning if model objects still reference it). CSV / TSV paste from clipboard into the grid via the reused `TimeseriesParse::parseRow` helper extracted from `ObservedCsvRunLayer::parseRow_()` (so file-import, clipboard-paste, and `ObservedCsvRunLayer` all share one parser covering ISO 8601, SWMM `M/D/Y H:M`, hours-since-start fallback, comma / tab / space delimiters, UTF-8 BOM, blank-row skip). New row insertion via Insert key or `Add row` button; deletion via Delete key on a row-selection. **Read-only when source mode is ExternalFile** — the grid greys out and the user is prompted to click Convert-to-Inline if they begin typing.
  - **Phase 6.7.3.5 — `TimeseriesEditChartView` (right pane, interactive)**. Built on the existing `InteractiveChartView` (Qt Charts) — extend the `Mode` enum with `EditPoints`, `RotatePoints`, `ScalePoints` and add subclass `TimeseriesEditChartView : public InteractiveChartView` overriding `mousePressEvent` / `mouseMoveEvent` / `mouseReleaseEvent` to dispatch on mode. Operations (all gated by source-mode ∈ { Inline, GpkgObserved }; disabled in ExternalFile mode):
    - **Y-drag (single + multi)** in `EditPoints` mode: hit-test the cursor against `QScatterSeries` points (~6 px radius). Press → start a `MovePointCommand` (or batch if the rubber-band selection is non-empty). Drag → `provider->setPointValueLive(idx, newY)` for each selected point — `Live` variant emits `pointsChanged` so the grid + plot refresh but does **not** push a separate undo command per frame. Release → finalise the batch as one undo entry. **X is locked** during Y-drag — monotonicity preserved by construction.
    - **Rubber-band multi-select** (Shift-drag-rect in `Select` mode): selects all `(t,v)` points whose mapped viewport position falls inside the rect; selected scatter overlay redraws with a halo. The selection set lives on `TimeseriesEditChartView` and is mirrored to the grid (and vice-versa) via a shared selection-bridge object, so the grid highlights the same rows.
    - **Rotate** (`RotatePoints` mode): rotate selection around its centroid in (t,v) space. On-canvas: a small pivot crosshair + a rotation handle the user can drag in an arc; live preview redraws transformed points. A side-panel `QPropertyModel` view (visible only when this mode is active) exposes `QDateTime pivotTime`, `double pivotValue`, `double angleDegrees`, `bool useCentroid` (default true) for numeric entry. Transform is applied via `BulkTransformCommand`, which validates **time monotonicity post-transform** — if any rotated point would equal or precede its neighbour the command is **refused** atomically and the status bar shows the offending index (no partial application).
    - **Scale** (`ScalePoints` mode): independent `scaleX` / `scaleY` around centroid or chosen anchor. Same on-canvas handles + numeric panel (`anchorTime`, `anchorValue`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`). Same monotonicity gate as rotate.
    - **Insert / delete points**: right-click on empty plot area opens a context menu with `Insert point at (t, v)…` (pre-fills numeric inputs from the click location); right-click on an existing point offers `Delete`, `Set value…`, `Set time…`. Both go through `InsertPointCommand` / `DeletePointsCommand`.
    - **Snap-to-time-step**: toggleable in the toolbar; when on, drag-released times round to the nearest project reporting step (read from `SimulationOptions`); when off, free-floating.
    - **Read-back of external changes**: the plot subscribes to `pointsChanged` and `metadataChanged`, so a grid-cell edit or a property-dialog edit elsewhere updates the plot in real time with no manual refresh path — the MVC contract is enforced by the signal wiring, not by polling.
  - **Phase 6.7.3.6 — Source-mode card (Inline / ExternalFile / GeopackageObserved)**. `QPropertyModel`-backed group at top of dialog. Inline: shows row count + first / last datetime; offers `Move to geopackage…` (mutate `SourceMode → GeopackageObserved`, persists via `swmm_gpkg_write_observed_values`). ExternalFile: shows file path, column selector (combo populated from header row), mtime + staleness indicator; offers `Detach to inline` (one-way), `Reload from file`. GeopackageObserved: shows observed_series id + quality-flag toggle column; offers `Export to inline`. Format selector under file-mode lets the user pick `Auto-detect` (default) / `CSV` / `TSV` / `Native .dat (3-col)` / `Native .dat (2-col)` — controls both parse and the Export writer.
  - **Phase 6.7.3.7 — Validation + commit**. The dialog has no OK/Cancel; edits commit live through the provider → undo stack. A status bar shows: (a) row count, (b) min/max value, (c) first/last datetime, (d) any pending validation issue (duplicate name, missing time on a value row, file-stale warning, monotonicity rejection from the most recent transform). On project save the registry serialises Inline providers back to the `.inp` `[TIMESERIES]` block via `swmm_timeseries_*`, ExternalFile providers as `FILE "path[:COL]"` rows, GpkgObserved providers into `observed_series` + `observed_values` via `swmm_gpkg_write_observed_values`.
  - **Phase 6.7.3.8 — Object Browser + property-adapter integration**. From Slice BM.0, the "TIMESERIES" leaves under Data Objects double-click open this dialog. The existing `SWMMTimeSeriesPropertyAdapter` is rewired to read from the `TimeseriesProvider` (not directly from `swmm_table_*`), and the "Data Grid" placeholder Q_PROPERTY becomes an `Edit…` button-property that opens the dialog focused on this provider. The adapter remains a thin Q_PROPERTY surface — the provider stays the source of truth. **This satisfies the MVC contract**: the Object Browser, the inline property dialog, and the `TimeseriesEditorDialog` are three views of the same `TimeseriesProvider`, all wired by Qt signals.
  - **Reuse points** (so we don't duplicate): `InteractiveChartView` shell + Pan/Zoom modes (subclass + extend the `Mode` enum; do not fork); `ObservedCsvRunLayer::parseRow_()` extracted as `TimeseriesParse::parseRow` in a new `include/io/timeseriesparse.h` so file-import, clipboard-paste, and `ObservedCsvRunLayer` share one implementation; QPropertyModel `QCustomDateTimeEdit` / `QCustomDoubleSpinBox` / `QCustomTimespanEdit` for in-grid editing; `QColorPropertyItemEditor` / `QFontPropertyItemEditor` / `QSelectFromListPropertyItemEditor` for the plot-styling side panel; engine `swmm_gpkg_*` observed-data API for GpkgObserved mode (no new engine surface needed for this path); engine inline-Tseries parser in `table.c` confirms the `[TIMESERIES]` grammar the writer must emit; engine file-Tseries parser confirms the legacy 2-col + 3-col .dat parse rules (`TBLSEPSTR = " \t\n\r,"` in `consts.h`).
- **Phase 6.7.4 — `TransectEditor`** *(MVC, 3-panel, DRAFT 2026-05-25 — awaiting review)*: non-modal three-pane editor (`QSplitter(Qt::Horizontal)`) for SWMM transects, replacing the legacy `Dtsect.pas` two-pane modal + separate `Dprevplot.pas` preview window with a single live-bound surface. **Pane 1 (left)** is a `QListView` of every transect in the project with a flat toolbar `[+][−][Rename…][Search…]` above it (same affordance as `CurveEditorDialog` / `PatternEditorDialog`). **Pane 2 (center)** is a vertical stack of: editable Name `QLineEdit` (uniqueness validated by `TransectRegistry::hasName`); rich-text Description `QTextEdit` for cross-section comments (replaces legacy single-line `CommentEdit`); a `QPropertyModel` "Geometry" group with **Bank Stations** (Left, Right — the `x_left_bank` / `x_right_bank` engine fields; see *open question Q-TR-01 below* on whether the user's distinction between "encroachment stations" and "bank stations" maps to two SWMM concepts or one), **Modifiers** (`stationMultiplier` = `xFactor`, `elevationOffset` = `yFactor`, `meanderFactor` = `lengthFactor`), and **Roughness** (`nLeftBank`, `nRightBank`, `nChannel` — Manning's N triplet from the INP `NC` record); and a 2-column `QTableView` of station-elevation pairs with Add Row / Insert Row / Delete Row(s) buttons (same pattern as `CurveEditorDialog`'s point grid). **Pane 3 (right)** is a `TransectChartView` (subclass of `InteractiveChartView`) showing the cross-section live: a `QAreaSeries` ground fill below the channel line, a `QLineSeries` overbank/channel line (colour-split at bank stations to match legacy `Dprevplot.pas` Series1 orange-red overbank + Series2 blue channel), a `QScatterSeries` of draggable point handles, and `QValueAxis` X/Y axes labelled `Station (ft/m)` / `Elevation (ft/m)` per the project unit system. Right-click on the chart opens a `QMenu` whose first item is **Chart properties…** → reuses the existing `ChartPropertiesDialog` (per `include/ui/dialogs/chartpropertiesdialog.h`) bound to a per-series-and-chart `openswmmvis::plot::ChartProperties` object, so all line colours, fill styles, marker sizes, axis title fonts, gridline visibility, and legend placement are edited through the existing QPropertyModel surface (no bespoke property pane). Standard mouse-wheel zoom + middle-button pan come free from `InteractiveChartView`; a flat `QToolBar` above the chart adds **Zoom to extent** (`:/icons/chart-fit.svg`), **Zoom in** / **Zoom out** (`chart-zoom-in.svg` / `chart-zoom-out.svg`), **Pan toggle** (`chart-pan.svg`), **Edit points toggle** (`chart-edit-points.svg`), and **Copy chart** (`copy.svg`) — icons reused from the Slice AT.2 / BL toolbar set. MVC layer: `TransectProvider` (one `QObject` per transect; holds `name`, `comments`, `nLeftBank`, `nRightBank`, `nChannel`, `xLeftBank`, `xRightBank`, `xFactor`, `yFactor`, `lengthFactor`, and a `QVector<QPair<double,double>>` of station-elevation pairs strictly ascending in station; emits `pointsChanged(first,count)`, `pointsInserted`, `pointsRemoved`, `roughnessChanged`, `bankStationsChanged`, `modifiersChanged`, `nameChanged`, `commentsChanged`, `mutationRejected(reason)`) + `TransectRegistry` (project-scoped factory + case-insensitive name uniqueness + `loadFromEngine` walking `swmm_transect_count` / `_id` / per-field getters + `saveToEngine` via `swmm_transect_add` / `_set_roughness` / `_add_station` loop). All mutations route through `QUndoCommand` subclasses pushed onto the project `QUndoStack` so a single Cmd-Z unwinds across grid, properties, and chart drag uniformly. Per Slice BM.0-Add-New, exposes `TransectEditorDialog::createNew(registry, undoStack, parent)` wired into the Object Browser Add-New dispatch; double-click on a `TRANSECT` leaf routes to `openForTransect(name)`. See *Phase 6.7.4 detail* below for the legacy field-map, MVC class shapes, chart interaction state machine, engine-gap accounting, and test plan.

#### 🔧 Phase 6.7.4 detail — `TransectEditor` (DRAFT 2026-05-25)

**Status:** drafted 2026-05-25 in response to user direction (three-pane resizable MVC editor, live cross-section chart with ground fill, right-click chart-properties via QPropertyModel, interactive point-drag, zoom-to-extent / pan / zoom toolbar). Awaiting review. Implementation does not start until this sub-section is reviewed.

**Legacy floor (per CLAUDE.md §4.01).** The legacy Delphi editor at `SWMM-GUI/Epaswmm5/Dtsect.pas` + `Dtsect.dfm` is a single modal `TTransectForm` (456×425 px) with three regions: top header (Name `TEdit` + Description `TEdit` + extended-comment dialog button), bottom button strip (View / OK / Cancel / Help), and a horizontal split body containing a `TGridEditFrame` left (3-col station-elevation `TStringGrid` — row 0 = headers `Station (ft/m)` / `Elevation (ft/m)`, ColCount = 3, RowCount = 101 default, up to 1500 max) and a `TPropEdit` right (categorised property grid: **Roughness** → Left Bank / Right Bank / Channel; **Bank Stations** → Left / Right; **Modifiers** → Stations multiplier / Elevations offset / Meander). `BtnView` launches `TPreviewPlotForm` (`Dprevplot.pas`) in a separate modal window — Series4 `TAreaSeries` ground fill (diagonal hatch), Series1 `TLineSeries` overbank (clr 16512 = orange-red), Series2 `TLineSeries` channel (`clBlue`) between the L/R bank station rows. **No interactive point drag, no right-click chart menu, no live preview** — the preview is read-only and refreshes only on each View click. Modernisations introduced here over legacy: (1) live in-pane chart, (2) point-drag with monotonicity enforcement, (3) QPropertyModel chart styling via right-click, (4) zoom-to-extent / pan / zoom toolbar with icons, (5) rich-text comments. The legacy field set is replicated 1:1; the legacy layout is **not** normative.

**Legacy → modern field map** (drives both the property panel rows and the engine round-trip):

| Legacy widget (Dtsect.dfm)         | Modern surface                                                                                              | Engine field (TTransect / Transect.hpp) | Engine API                                                                  |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NameEdit` (TEdit, 145 px)         | Pane 2 top `QLineEdit` (uniqueness + non-empty validator)                                                   | `name` / `ID`                            | `swmm_transect_add(id)` on create; rename via snapshot+rewrite              |
| `CommentEdit` (TEdit, 233 px) + extended-comment dialog | Pane 2 `QTextEdit` (rich text)                                                                              | `comments` (string)                     | Engine gap **DA-ENG-09** (see below) — no current getter/setter             |
| Roughness → Left Bank (TEdit)      | Pane 2 `QPropertyModel` row `nLeftBank` (`QCustomDoubleSpinBox`, 4 dp, ≥ 0)                                 | `n_left`                                | `swmm_transect_set_roughness(idx, n_left, n_right, n_channel)`              |
| Roughness → Right Bank (TEdit)     | Pane 2 `QPropertyModel` row `nRightBank`                                                                    | `n_right`                               | same                                                                        |
| Roughness → Channel (TEdit)        | Pane 2 `QPropertyModel` row `nChannel`                                                                      | `n_channel`                             | same                                                                        |
| Bank Stations → Left (TEdit)       | Pane 2 `QPropertyModel` row `xLeftBank` (`QCustomDoubleSpinBox`)                                            | `x_left_bank`                           | Engine gap **DA-ENG-09** for setter; getter exists via `Transect.hpp`        |
| Bank Stations → Right (TEdit)      | Pane 2 `QPropertyModel` row `xRightBank`                                                                    | `x_right_bank`                          | same                                                                        |
| Modifiers → Stations (TEdit)       | Pane 2 `QPropertyModel` row `stationMultiplier`                                                             | `xFactor` (X1 record column 8)           | Engine gap **DA-ENG-09** for setter                                          |
| Modifiers → Elevations (TEdit)     | Pane 2 `QPropertyModel` row `elevationOffset`                                                               | `yFactor` (X1 record column 9)           | Engine gap **DA-ENG-09** for setter                                          |
| Modifiers → Meander (TEdit)        | Pane 2 `QPropertyModel` row `meanderFactor`                                                                 | `lengthFactor`                          | Engine gap **DA-ENG-09** for setter                                          |
| `Grid: TStringGrid` (3 cols, 101 rows) | Pane 2 bottom `QTableView` (2 cols: Station, Elevation; row count from provider; `QCustomDoubleSpinBox` cell editors) | `stations[]` + `elevations[]`            | `swmm_transect_add_station(idx, station, elevation)` after clear            |

**Resolved Q-TR-01 (2026-05-25):** user chose **Reading B** — separate Encroachment (L/R) and Bank Stations (L/R) field sets. Both are surfaced as distinct `QPropertyModel` groups in pane 2. This pulls **engine gap BQ-TR-02** into scope for this slice (see *Engine APIs + engine gaps* below).

##### MVC layer — `TransectProvider` + `TransectRegistry` + apply helpers

Mirrors `CurveProvider` / `PatternProvider` / `TimeseriesProvider`:

```cpp
class TransectProvider : public QObject {
    Q_OBJECT
public:
    // identity
    QString name() const;
    QString comments() const;
    // Manning's N
    double nLeftBank() const;
    double nRightBank() const;
    double nChannel() const;
    // bank stations
    double xLeftBank() const;
    double xRightBank() const;
    // modifiers (X1 record cols 8-9 + lengthFactor)
    double stationMultiplier() const;   // xFactor
    double elevationOffset() const;     // yFactor
    double meanderFactor() const;       // lengthFactor
    // station-elevation pairs (strictly ascending in station)
    int                       pointCount() const;
    QPair<double,double>      pointAt(int i) const;
    QVector<QPair<double,double>> allPoints() const;
    // read-only — all mutations go through the registry / SWMMModelLayer apply helpers
signals:
    void nameChanged(QString prev, QString now);
    void commentsChanged();
    void roughnessChanged();
    void bankStationsChanged();
    void modifiersChanged();
    void pointsChanged(int firstIndex, int count);
    void pointsInserted(int at, int count);
    void pointsRemoved(int at, int count);
    void mutationRejected(QString reason);
};

class TransectRegistry : public QObject {
    Q_OBJECT
public:
    QVector<TransectProvider *> providers() const;
    TransectProvider *findByName(const QString &name) const;
    bool hasName(const QString &name) const;          // case-insensitive
    TransectProvider *create(const QString &name);    // create-new flow
    void              remove(TransectProvider *p);
    bool              rename(TransectProvider *p, const QString &newName);
    int               loadFromEngine(void *engineHandle);
    int               saveToEngine(void *engineHandle);
signals:
    void providerAdded(TransectProvider *);
    void providerAboutToBeRemoved(TransectProvider *);
    void providerRenamed(TransectProvider *, QString prev, QString now);
    void providerPointsChanged(TransectProvider *);
    void providerMetadataChanged(TransectProvider *);
};
```

**`SWMMModelLayer` apply helpers** (the only place `swmm_transect_*` mutation calls live, mirrors `applyHydrograph*` / `applyControlRule*`):

- `bool applyTransectAdd(const QString &name, QString *outError)`
- `bool applyTransectRename(const QString &oldName, const QString &newName, QString *outError)`
- `bool applyTransectRemove(const QString &name)`
- `bool applyTransectSetComments(const QString &name, const QString &comments)` *(routes through DA-ENG-09)*
- `bool applyTransectSetRoughness(const QString &name, double nLeft, double nRight, double nChannel)`
- `bool applyTransectSetBankStations(const QString &name, double xLeft, double xRight)` *(routes through DA-ENG-09)*
- `bool applyTransectSetModifiers(const QString &name, double stationMul, double elevOffset, double meander)` *(routes through DA-ENG-09)*
- `bool applyTransectSetStations(const QString &name, const QVector<QPair<double,double>> &points)` *(snapshot+clear+re-add via `swmm_transect_add_station`)*

Each emits a fine-grained `transectChanged(QString name)` signal on the layer; the registry subscribes and refreshes the matching provider. Same snapshot-and-rewrite primitive pattern as control rules — no per-field engine mutation gymnastics needed beyond what the engine already exposes for stations + roughness.

##### Qt models — `TransectListModel` + `TransectStationTableModel`

`class TransectListModel : public QAbstractListModel`. N rows × 1 column. Listens to `providerAdded` / `providerAboutToBeRemoved` / `providerRenamed` and emits the matching begin/end signals.

| Role                  | Returns                                                                                  |
|---|---|
| `Qt::DisplayRole`     | Provider name                                                                            |
| `Qt::EditRole`        | Provider name (inline rename via `QListView::edit`)                                       |
| `Qt::DecorationRole`  | `:/icons/data-object-transect.svg` (new asset, 16×16, line-art cross-section glyph)       |
| `Qt::ToolTipRole`     | `"<n> stations, banks at <xL>..<xR>"`                                                    |

`setData(EditRole)` calls `layer->applyTransectRename`; `removeRows` calls `applyTransectRemove`; `insertRows` is **not** implemented (creation goes through the dialog's create-card → `applyTransectAdd`).

`class TransectStationTableModel : public QAbstractTableModel`. N rows × 2 cols. Columns: 0 = Station (`xFactor`-adjusted display, raw on edit), 1 = Elevation (`yFactor`-adjusted display, raw on edit). Header label respects project unit system (`(ft)` / `(m)`). `setData` builds a `SetStationPointCommand` (undoable) and routes through `applyTransectSetStations` with the single-point mutation applied to the local snapshot. `insertRows` / `removeRows` mutate the local snapshot and round-trip the full vector. **Monotonicity invariant**: station values must be strictly ascending; any edit that would violate this is refused by `TransectProvider` (emits `mutationRejected` → dialog status bar shows the reason; the offending cell reverts).

##### `TransectChartView` — interactive cross-section preview

`class TransectChartView : public InteractiveChartView`. Owns three `QtCharts` series bound to the active `TransectProvider`:

- `m_groundFill` (`QAreaSeries`): semi-transparent fill below `m_overbankLine`, snapped to a Y-baseline = `min(elevations) − margin`. Replaces legacy `Dprevplot.pas::Series4`.
- `m_overbankLine` (`QLineSeries`): full extent left→right of the cross-section, colour from `ChartProperties::overbankColour` (default orange-red `#FF4040` matching legacy `clr 16512`). Replaces legacy Series1.
- `m_channelLine` (`QLineSeries`): the slice between `xLeftBank` and `xRightBank`, colour from `ChartProperties::channelColour` (default `clBlue` matching legacy Series2).
- `m_pointHandles` (`QScatterSeries`): one marker per station-elevation pair; this is the drag-handle layer. Marker shape / size from `ChartProperties::handleMarker` + `handleSize`. Hidden when **Edit points** toggle is off.
- Two `QValueAxis` axes (`stationAxis`, `elevationAxis`) with titles bound to the project unit system.
- A vertical `QLineSeries` overlay at each bank station (`xLeftBank` / `xRightBank`) drawn dotted in the channel colour — replaces legacy's row-index lookup with visual markers (improvement over legacy which had no on-chart bank markers).

**Mode extension.** Extends the `InteractiveChartView::Mode` enum with `EditPoints` (same approach Phase 6.7.3.5 takes for the timeseries chart — extend, do not fork):

- **Idle (default)** — mouse wheel zooms; middle-button drag pans; left-button drag rubber-band-zooms (existing `InteractiveChartView` behaviour).
- **Pan toggle** — left-button drag pans instead of rubber-band-zoom.
- **EditPoints toggle** — hit-test the cursor against `m_pointHandles` (~6 px radius). On press, capture the index, push a `MoveStationPointCommand::beginInteractive`; on drag, call `provider->setPointLive(idx, x, y)` (live signal variant — emits `pointsChanged` so the grid + chart refresh per frame but does not push a separate undo command per mouse move); on release, finalise as one undo entry. **Monotonicity gate**: if the dragged X would equal or cross a neighbour, the live move clamps X to `prev + ε` / `next − ε` and the status bar shows `"Station clamped to maintain ascending order"`. Y is unconstrained. Holding `Shift` constrains the drag to vertical only (Y-edit); holding `Ctrl` constrains to horizontal only (X-edit). Right-click on a handle offers **Set station…** / **Set elevation…** / **Delete point** via small inline dialogs.
- **Zoom to extent** (toolbar button or `F` keyboard shortcut) — fits both axes to `[min(station)−10%, max(station)+10%]` × `[min(elev)−10%, max(elev)+10%]`.

The chart subscribes to `pointsChanged`, `pointsInserted`, `pointsRemoved`, `bankStationsChanged`, and `modifiersChanged` on the bound provider and refreshes the affected series only — never a full rebuild — so grid edits reflect in the chart and chart drags reflect in the grid in real time. This is the MVC contract the user mandated.

##### Right-click chart context menu — `ChartPropertiesDialog` reuse

`m_chartView->setContextMenuPolicy(Qt::CustomContextMenu)` + a slot that builds a `QMenu` at the click position with:

| Item                          | Action                                                                                                   |
|---|---|
| **Chart properties…**         | `ChartPropertiesDialog(m_chartProps, this).exec()` — `m_chartProps` is the per-editor `ChartProperties` instance (see `include/ui/dialogs/chartpropertiesdialog.h`); QPropertyModel rows expose `channelColour`, `overbankColour`, `groundFillColour`, `groundFillOpacity`, `lineWeight`, `handleMarker`, `handleSize`, `axisTitleFont`, `axisLabelFont`, `gridlinesVisible`, `legendVisible`, `legendAnchor` — all of which the chart re-applies on `chartPropertiesChanged()`. |
| ─────────                     |                                                                                                          |
| **Zoom to extent** (`F`)      | `m_chartView->zoomToExtent()`                                                                            |
| **Reset zoom**                | `m_chartView->resetZoom()`                                                                               |
| ─────────                     |                                                                                                          |
| **Copy chart as image**       | renders the chart to a `QPixmap` and copies to clipboard                                                 |
| **Copy data to clipboard**    | writes TSV of `(station, elevation)` pairs to the clipboard                                              |
| **Export chart as PNG…**      | `QFileDialog` + `chart->grab().save(path)`                                                               |

The `ChartProperties` instance is persisted per-project via `QSettings` keyed by `transect/<name>/chartProps` (same idiom `PatternEditorDialog` uses for splitter sizes), so styling survives editor close/reopen.

##### Chart toolbar (above the chart pane)

Flat `QToolBar`, icon-only, 16×16 SVG assets. Reuse existing chart icons from the Slice AT.2 / BL set wherever possible:

| Button                 | Icon                       | Tooltip / action                                                |
|---|---|---|
| Zoom to extent         | `chart-fit.svg`            | `Fit chart to data (F)` — `m_chartView->zoomToExtent()`         |
| Zoom in                | `chart-zoom-in.svg`        | `Zoom in (Ctrl++)` — scales axes by 0.8                          |
| Zoom out               | `chart-zoom-out.svg`       | `Zoom out (Ctrl+-)` — scales axes by 1.25                        |
| Pan toggle             | `chart-pan.svg`            | checkable; toggles `Mode::Pan`                                   |
| Edit points toggle     | `chart-edit-points.svg`    | checkable; toggles `Mode::EditPoints` and shows `m_pointHandles` |
| Snap to grid toggle    | `chart-snap.svg`           | checkable; rounds station drags to nearest project-unit grid     |
| Copy chart             | `copy.svg`                 | copies chart pixmap to clipboard                                  |
| Chart properties…      | `chart-properties.svg`     | opens `ChartPropertiesDialog` (same as right-click first item)    |

Mouse wheel zoom + middle-button pan are always-on regardless of toggles (existing `InteractiveChartView` behaviour) so the toolbar is a redundant affordance, not a gate.

##### Engine APIs + engine gaps

**Already shipped** (per `openswmm_infrastructure.h`): `swmm_transect_add`, `swmm_transect_count`, `swmm_transect_index`, `swmm_transect_id`, `swmm_transect_set_roughness`, `swmm_transect_add_station`. Stations are written via clear + re-add loop (no individual station setter today — acceptable since the editor always rewrites the full station list on commit, same primitive as control rules).

**New gap — DA-ENG-09 (file at slice start, blocks Phase 6.7.4 ship):** per-field getters + setters for the read-only-today transect fields. The C++ `TransectData` struct already carries `comments`, `x_left_bank`, `x_right_bank`, `xFactor`, `yFactor`, `lengthFactor` — but `openswmm_infrastructure.h` exposes no public C API for them. Engine work needed:

```c
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_get_comments(void *eng, int idx, char *buf, int buflen);
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_set_comments(void *eng, int idx, const char *text);
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_get_bank_stations(void *eng, int idx, double *xL, double *xR);
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_set_bank_stations(void *eng, int idx, double xL, double xR);
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_get_modifiers(void *eng, int idx, double *xFactor, double *yFactor, double *lengthFactor);
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_set_modifiers(void *eng, int idx, double xFactor, double yFactor, double lengthFactor);
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_get_roughness(void *eng, int idx, double *nL, double *nR, double *nCh);     // mirror of existing setter
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_get_station_count(void *eng, int idx);
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_get_station(void *eng, int idx, int stationIdx, double *station, double *elev);
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_clear_stations(void *eng, int idx);   // for the rewrite-on-commit path
```

**Decision 2026-05-25:** DA-ENG-09 is implemented **first** with unit tests in `openswmm.engine` (per CLAUDE.md §4 goal-driven execution — tests-then-pass), then the GUI consumes it. The editor ships at full fidelity.

**In scope — BQ-TR-02 (Reading B chosen 2026-05-25):** separate encroachment stations distinct from bank stations. Engine work needed:

```c
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_get_encroachment_stations(void *eng, int idx, double *xL, double *xR);
SWMM_API int swmm_transect_set_encroachment_stations(void *eng, int idx, double xL, double xR);
```

Plus new fields `x_left_encroachment` / `x_right_encroachment` on `TransectData` (modern C++) and the legacy `TTransect` struct, with INP `[TRANSECTS]` X1 record extension (two optional trailing columns; on load, when absent default each to the corresponding bank station — preserves backward compatibility with every existing `.inp` file in the wild). Engine unit tests cover the legacy-file-defaults-to-bank-stations path explicitly.

##### Acceptance checklist (verifiable per CLAUDE.md §4)

1. Open project with ≥ 1 transect → dialog list shows it → verify: `listModel()->rowCount() == swmm_transect_count(eng)`.
2. Drag a station handle on the chart → grid row updates same frame → verify: `tableModel()->data(QModelIndex(idx,0))` equals new station value.
3. Edit a grid cell → chart point redraws → verify: `chartView()->seriesPoint(idx)` matches grid.
4. Right-click chart → Chart properties… → change overbank colour → live redraw → verify: `m_overbankLine->pen().color()` equals chosen colour.
5. Rename in list → Object Browser TRANSECT leaf relabels → verify: `objectBrowser->itemText(transectLeaf)` equals new name (cross-view sync per MVC contract).
6. Cmd-Z after a drag + grid edit + roughness change → all three revert in one undo → verify: `undoStack->index()` decremented by exactly the number of `*Command` pushes.
7. Close + reopen dialog → splitter sizes + chart-properties persist → verify: `QSettings` round-trip via test hook `saveAndReloadState()`.

### ⏳ Slice BR — Controls / rules editor (IF-THEN-ELSE with syntax help + lint) (Phase 6.8)

> **Note (Slice BM.0-Add-New, 2026-05-24):** Add-New for **Control Rules** is currently disabled in the Object Browser with a tooltip naming this slice; landing `RulesEditorDialog` below re-enables it (one-line edit to `ObjectBrowserPanel::hasComplexEditor` + `gapTooltipFor`).

Legacy `Dcontrol.pas` is a free-form text editor with rule-syntax checking and a syntax-help panel.

**Note 2026-05-22 (still in force):** rule-name extraction lands in Slice DA.1 via the new engine API `swmm_control_get_id` (parses `RULE <name>` server-side; returns `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM` on malformed text, GUI then surfaces `Rule N [unnamed]` sentinel). DA.3 ships a skeleton-template "New Control Rule…" creation flow with 4 pre-canned RULE skeletons (Empty / Pump on/off / Orifice setting / Weir bypass) which Phase 6.8.5 reuses in the dialog's create-card. DA.2 ships the interim `MultiLineCellDelegate` editing surface on the `ruleText` row of `SWMMControlRulePropertyAdapter`; Phase 6.8.4 keeps that surface working and adds the dialog as an **additive** browse path rather than replacing it.

**Note 2026-05-25 (shape decisions, supersedes earlier drafts):** the dialog is a **two-pane** layout (rule list + rich-text body editor) with no side reference tree — per user direction the body editor uses `QTextEdit` (rich text) rather than `QPlainTextEdit`, and auto-suggest via `QCompleter` + an `Insert object…` toolbutton replaces the reference tree. The earlier `RuleLinter` (GUI-side mini-parser) is renamed `RuleValidator` and runs the **full engine parser** through new engine gap **BR-02** (`swmm_control_validate_rule`). List-view rows carry per-rule valid / invalid / pending icons. The browse path from `AttributePanel` is the `…` button on the `ruleText` row plus Slice BM.0-Browse-Edit's right-click "Edit…". See *Phase 6.8.1 detail* and *Phase 6.8.2 detail* below.

- **Phase 6.8.1 — Control-rule MVC layer + `RulesEditorDialog`**: project-scoped `ControlRuleRegistry` of `ControlRuleProvider` instances, `RuleListModel` (`QAbstractListModel`) exposing each rule's name + validation state for the list pane, and a two-pane non-modal `RulesEditorDialog` (rule list + rich-text rule body). The dialog is pure view code; every mutation routes through `SWMMModelLayer::applyControlRule*` helpers that wrap the engine round-trip and emit `controlRulesChanged(QString ruleName)` so the Object Browser, the DA.2 `SWMMControlRulePropertyAdapter`, and any future picker stay synchronized. See *Phase 6.8.1 detail* below.
- **Phase 6.8.2 — `RuleSyntaxHighlighter` + `RuleCompleter` + `RuleValidator`**: `QSyntaxHighlighter` colourises keywords / operators / object refs / numbers / comments inside `QTextEdit` (rich text per user request). `RuleCompleter` is a `QCompleter` whose source model is rebuilt on each show from the live `SWMMModelLayer` object name lists + the static keyword vocabulary, so auto-suggest reflects what is actually in the model. `RuleValidator` runs the **full engine parser** against a sandbox engine handle (no GUI-side mini-parser); it returns `(ok, errorMessage, errorLine)` and the dialog uses that triple to drive the list-view status icon, the editor's bottom error strip, and the gutter marker. See *Phase 6.8.2 detail* below.
- **Phase 6.8.3 — Round-trip with engine (load + save)**: Load via `swmm_control_count` + `swmm_control_get_rule`; save via `SWMMModelLayer::applyControlRule*` which, for a per-rule edit, snapshots every rule, replaces the target slot, calls `swmm_control_clear_rules`, and re-`swmm_control_add_rule`s the snapshot — matching today's `SWMMControlRulePropertyAdapter::setRuleText` pattern. **No new engine mutation surface is required.** All four CRUD operations (add / replace / rename / remove) reduce to one snapshot-and-rewrite primitive on the layer.
- **Phase 6.8.4 — `AttributePanel` integration (Browse + inline edit)**: the existing DA.2 `MultiLineCellDelegate` text editor on the `ruleText` row keeps working — typing in the property panel still round-trips through `setRuleText`. Slice BM.0-Browse-Edit's right-click "Edit…" routing gets a new arm for `K::Control` that opens `RulesEditorDialog` pre-selected on the current rule; in addition, the `ruleText` row gains a small browse `…` button (same affordance as `DataObjectPickerEditor`) that launches the dialog. Inline edit and editor edit are two views of the same `ControlRuleProvider` — `controlRulesChanged` fires once on save and the property panel refreshes through the existing `QPropertyModel::refreshValues()` connection wired in `attributepanel.cpp`.
- **Phase 6.8.5 — Object Browser Add-New re-enable**: flip the `K::Control` arm of `ComprehensiveEditorRegistry` from disabled-with-tooltip to `RulesEditorDialog::createNew(layer, undoStack, parent)`. Right-click "Add New…" on the Control Rules group header opens the editor in `Mode::CreateNew` (name field + uniqueness validator + skeleton-template combo + Create button), mirroring `PatternEditorDialog::createNew` / `CurveEditorDialog::createNew`.
- **Phase 6.8.6 — Run-time rule firing log** *(deferred — depends on Slice BX)*: when attached to a live run, editor highlights the currently-firing rule via engine gap **BR-01** (`swmm_set_control_rule_fired_callback`). Out of scope for the CRUD editor delivery; tracked here so the firing-log UI surface lives in the same dialog.

- **Dependencies**: BM (property editor framework), BM.0 (Object Browser non-spatial section), DA.1 (`swmm_control_get_id` rule-name extraction), DA.2 (`SWMMControlRulePropertyAdapter`), **BR-02** (engine validation API — must land before Phase 6.8.2 ships).

#### 🔧 Phase 6.8.1 detail — Control-rule MVC layer + `RulesEditorDialog` (DRAFT 2026-05-25)

**Status:** drafted 2026-05-25 in response to user direction (two-pane CRUD editor, MVC, rich-text body with syntax highlighting + auto-suggest from model objects, list-view validity icons, browse-from-attributes-panel, rename support). Awaiting review. Implementation does not start until this sub-section is reviewed.

**User-mandated requirements driving the shape below** (verbatim mapping so review can verify each one lands):

| Requirement | Where it is solved |
|---|---|
| Two-panel view: list + code editor | `RulesEditorDialog` top-level `QSplitter(Qt::Horizontal)` — only two children, no third reference-tree pane |
| Add + Delete buttons next to the list | `QToolBar` above `QListView` in pane 1; flat `QToolButton`s — same affordance as the curve / pattern editors |
| Rich-text editor with syntax highlighting | `RuleCodeEditor` subclasses `QTextEdit` (rich text, **not** `QPlainTextEdit`) + `RuleSyntaxHighlighter` attached to its `QTextDocument` |
| Auto-suggestions from model objects | `RuleCompleter` `QCompleter` whose `QStringListModel` is rebuilt from `SWMMModelLayer::objectNamesByCategory` (Nodes / Links / Subcatchments) + static SWMM keyword list at popup time |
| Syntax validation | `RuleValidator` round-trips current document text through engine gap BR-02 (`swmm_control_validate_rule`); debounced 250 ms |
| Invalid rules show icon in list view; valid rules another icon | `RuleListModel::data(Qt::DecorationRole)` returns `:/icons/rule-valid.svg` / `rule-invalid.svg` / `rule-pending.svg` based on the provider's cached validation result |
| Attributes-panel **browse button** opens this editor on the selected rule | Slice BM.0-Browse-Edit right-click "Edit…" + new browse `…` button on the `ruleText` row → `RulesEditorDialog::openForRule(name)` |
| Direct edit in attributes panel **still works** | DA.2 `MultiLineCellDelegate` on `ruleText` is left in place; both surfaces mutate through the same `ControlRuleProvider` |
| Rename support | `RuleListModel::setData(Qt::EditRole)` + a `Rename…` button in pane 1; rewriting `RULE <newName>` on the body when needed |

**Why MVC matters here.** The same control-rule text is surfaced today by the Object Browser (Control Rules group), the `SWMMControlRulePropertyAdapter` property panel (DA.2), and — once Phase 6.8 lands — the new editor and any future scenario-comparison / firing-log views. Without an MVC layer each surface polls `swmm_control_get_rule` independently and they drift; with it, every surface binds to the **same** `ControlRuleProvider` instances and refreshes through the layer's `controlRulesChanged(QString)` signal. This applies the pattern Phase 6.9.2 prototyped for hydrographs (engine-backed `QAbstractItemModel`s owned by `SWMMModelLayer` + fine-grained name-keyed change signal) per the Phase 6.9.2 *Pattern reuse* note.

##### MVC layer — `ControlRuleProvider` + `ControlRuleRegistry` + apply helpers

**New signal on `SWMMModelLayer`** — sits alongside `hydrographChanged(QString)`:

```cpp
/*! Emitted whenever any [CONTROLS] mutation lands in the engine (add,
 *  replace, rename, remove, bulk reorder). ruleName is empty for
 *  "rebuild everything" (cleared, reordered, or imported from .inp).
 *  All control-rule models listen here and refresh; the editor UI is
 *  pure view code. */
void controlRulesChanged(const QString &ruleName);
```

**New `SWMMModelLayer` mutation helpers** — the *only* place engine `swmm_control_*` mutation calls live (mirrors `applyHydrograph*`):

- `bool applyControlRuleAdd(const QString &name, const QString &body, QString *outError)` — appends `RULE <name>\n<body>` to the rule list (`name` may be empty if `body` already starts with `RULE …`).
- `bool applyControlRuleReplace(const QString &name, const QString &newText, QString *outError)` — snapshot+clear+re-add with target slot replaced.
- `bool applyControlRuleRename(const QString &oldName, const QString &newName)` — rewrites the `RULE <name>` header on the matching slot, snapshot+clear+re-add. Refuses on duplicate.
- `bool applyControlRuleRemove(const QString &name)` — snapshot, drop the matching slot, clear, re-add.
- `bool applyControlRulesReorder(const QStringList &newOrder)` — snapshot, permute, clear, re-add. *(Out of scope for first cut — listed for completeness so the API is stable when reorder lands.)*

Each calls the corresponding engine calls, then emits `controlRulesChanged(ruleName)` (or `""` for bulk operations). Each returns `false` and populates `*outError` on rejection so the dialog can surface the reason inline (no `QMessageBox` for the routine cases).

**`ControlRuleProvider` (new) — one instance per rule, owned by the registry.** Holds:

```cpp
QString          m_name;          // mirrors RULE <name>; updated on rename.
QString          m_body;          // full rule text including the RULE header.
ValidationState  m_validation;    // Pending / Valid / Invalid; cached.
QString          m_lastError;     // Empty unless m_validation == Invalid.
int              m_lastErrorLine; // 1-based; -1 when unknown.
```

Signals: `nameChanged(prev, now)`, `bodyChanged()`, `validationChanged()`. Methods are read-only — all mutations go through the registry / layer.

**`ControlRuleRegistry` (new)** — mirrors `CurveRegistry` / `PatternRegistry` / `TimeseriesRegistry`:

```cpp
QVector<ControlRuleProvider *> providers() const;
ControlRuleProvider *findByName(const QString &name) const;
bool hasName(const QString &name) const;
ControlRuleProvider *create(const QString &name, const QString &body); // for create-new mode
void                 remove(ControlRuleProvider *p);
bool                 rename(ControlRuleProvider *p, const QString &newName);
int                  loadFromEngine(void *engineHandle);  // walks _count + _get_rule + _get_id
int                  saveToEngine(void *engineHandle);    // emitted to engine on project-save path
signals:
  void providerAdded(ControlRuleProvider *);
  void providerAboutToBeRemoved(ControlRuleProvider *);
  void providerRenamed(ControlRuleProvider *, const QString &prev, const QString &now);
  void providerBodyChanged(ControlRuleProvider *);
  void providerValidationChanged(ControlRuleProvider *);
```

The registry is owned by `SWMMModelLayer` and accessed via `layer->ensureControlRuleRegistry()` (same lazy-construct pattern as `ensureCurveRegistry` / `ensurePatternRegistry`). It subscribes to `controlRulesChanged(QString)` and refreshes providers — load-from-engine is a single function so reload after an undo or external `.inp` reload Just Works.

##### Qt model — `RuleListModel`

`class RuleListModel : public QAbstractListModel`. N rows × 1 column. Read-only-except-for-rename. Holds a pointer to the registry; listens to `providerAdded` / `providerAboutToBeRemoved` / `providerRenamed` / `providerValidationChanged` and emits `beginInsertRows` / `dataChanged(Qt::DecorationRole)` / etc. accordingly.

Roles:

| Role | Returns |
|---|---|
| `Qt::DisplayRole` | Provider name, or `tr("Rule %1 [unnamed]").arg(row + 1)` when the engine returned `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM` from `_get_id` (matches the existing DA.1 sentinel convention) |
| `Qt::EditRole` | Provider name (for inline rename via `QListView::edit`) |
| `Qt::DecorationRole` | One of three SVG icons keyed off `m_validation`: `:/icons/rule-valid.svg` (green check), `:/icons/rule-invalid.svg` (red exclamation), `:/icons/rule-pending.svg` (grey ellipsis, used while the 250 ms debounce window is open or the validator is still running) |
| `Qt::ToolTipRole` | Empty when valid; `tr("Line %1: %2").arg(lastErrorLine).arg(lastError)` when invalid |
| `Qt::TextAlignmentRole` | `Qt::AlignVCenter \| Qt::AlignLeft` |

`setData(EditRole)` calls `layer->applyControlRuleRename(oldName, newName)`. `removeRows` calls `applyControlRuleRemove` on each provider; `insertRows` is **not** implemented (creation goes through the dialog's create-card, which calls `applyControlRuleAdd` directly — list insertion happens via the `providerAdded` signal). This matches `HydrographGroupListModel` per Phase 6.9.2.

Three new icon assets land under `resources/images/`: `rule-valid.svg` (12×12 green check), `rule-invalid.svg` (12×12 red exclamation in a circle), `rule-pending.svg` (12×12 grey three-dot ellipsis). Sourced from the existing icon set (same line weight + corner radius as `data-object-edit.svg`).

##### `RulesEditorDialog` — two-pane shape (per user request)

**Class.** `class RulesEditorDialog : public QDialog`. Non-modal (`setModal(false)`). Geometry + splitter sizes persist via `QSettings` keyed by the project file path (same idiom as `PatternEditorDialog`). Mirrors `CurveEditorDialog` / `PatternEditorDialog` for the public API surface so the `ComprehensiveEditorRegistry` entry slots in mechanically:

```cpp
class RulesEditorDialog : public QDialog {
public:
    enum class Mode { Edit, CreateNew };
    RulesEditorDialog(SWMMModelLayer *layer, QUndoStack *undoStack, QWidget *parent = nullptr);
    static RulesEditorDialog *createNew(SWMMModelLayer *layer, QUndoStack *undoStack, QWidget *parent = nullptr);
    void openForRule(const QString &name);
    Mode mode() const noexcept;
    ControlRuleProvider *currentProvider() const noexcept;
    // test hooks: listView(), codeEditor(), listModel(), pendingName(), invokeNew(), invokeDelete(), renameCurrent(), submitCreateNew()
};
```

**Layout** (top-level `QSplitter(Qt::Horizontal)` with `setChildrenCollapsible(false)`, `setHandleWidth(6)`; initial stretch `(2, 5)` saved/restored via `QSplitter::saveState()`):

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [+][−][Rename…]  [Search…]       │  Name: [<read-only label> ] [Rename…]          │
│ ──────────────────               │  Status: ● Valid     (or ⚠ Line 3: missing THEN)│
│ ✓ R1                              │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────│
│ ✓ DryWeatherPump                  │                                                │
│ ⚠ Outfall1                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ … RDII_Bypass                     │  │ RULE DryWeatherPump                      │ │
│                                  │  │ IF NODE J1 DEPTH > 5                     │ │
│                                  │  │ AND CONDUIT C1 FLOW < 10                 │ │
│ N rules                          │  │ THEN PUMP P1 STATUS = ON                 │ │
│                                  │  │ ELSE PUMP P1 STATUS = OFF                │ │
│                                  │  │ PRIORITY 5                               │ │
│                                  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                  │  Gutter shows error markers; popup completer │
│                                  │  pinned under cursor on Ctrl+Space or trigger │
└──────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Modern UI conventions applied throughout** (same set as Phase 6.9.2):

- Flat `QToolButton` with icons (`:/icons/data-object-add.svg`, `data-object-remove.svg`, `data-object-rename.svg`) and tooltips — no bordered `QPushButton`.
- Styled splitter handle, 8-px content margins, 6-px form spacing.
- Header `QLabel` per pane uses `QFont::Bold` and secondary-text palette colour.
- Bottom status strip on the dialog frame: `"N rules · M invalid · last edit: <ruleName>"` — quiet inline feedback rather than `QMessageBox` for non-errors.

**Pane 1 — rule list (the "first panel" in the user's spec).**

- `QListView` bound (through a `QSortFilterProxyModel`) to `layer->controlRuleListModel()`. Selection drives pane 2. Single-selection.
- `QToolBar` above the list with three flat actions:
  - **`+ Add`** → opens a small inline create-card (Name field with uniqueness validator + skeleton-template combo with the DA.3 templates: Empty / Pump on/off / Orifice setting / Weir bypass + Create button). On Create calls `layer->applyControlRuleAdd(name, skeletonBody)`; new provider arrives via `providerAdded`, the list selects it, and the editor pane focuses on the body.
  - **`− Delete`** → confirmation dialog, then `removeRows` on the list model (which calls `applyControlRuleRemove`). Multi-rule delete is out of scope (single selection).
  - **`Rename…`** → `QListView::edit(currentIndex())` — same affordance as the curve / pattern editors. Also reachable via F2.
- `QLineEdit` search field at the top with placeholder `"Search rules…"`, drives the `QSortFilterProxyModel`'s `setFilterFixedString`. Filters on rule name only — not body text — keeping behaviour predictable.
- Right-click context menu: `Add…`, `Rename…`, `Duplicate…` *(out of scope; greyed)*, `Delete`, `Copy text`, `Validate now`.

**Pane 2 — rule body editor (the "code dialog" in the user's spec).**

A vertical layout with four stacked sections:

1. **Name strip** — `QLabel` (large, bold, read-only) showing the current rule name + a `Rename…` flat toolbutton (right-aligned). Identical to Phase 6.9.2's name strip. Rename routes through the same `applyControlRuleRename` path as the list-pane button so the two UIs stay in sync.
2. **Validation banner** — a single-line strip with the current validation badge (green check + `"Valid"`, red exclamation + `"Line N: <message>"`, or grey ellipsis + `"Validating…"`). Clicking the line number jumps the cursor in the editor. Empty when the rule body is blank.
3. **`RuleCodeEditor`** — the rich-text body editor. **`QTextEdit`** subclass (rich text per user request), not `QPlainTextEdit`. Configured with a monospace font (`QFontDatabase::systemFont(QFontDatabase::FixedFont)`), word-wrap off, tab stop = 4 chars, line-number gutter painted via `paintEvent` override on a left-side companion widget. Hosts the `RuleSyntaxHighlighter` (attached to the document) and the `RuleCompleter` (popup tied to the editor's viewport).
4. **Action strip** — flat right-aligned `Validate now` + `Insert keyword…` + `Insert object…` toolbuttons. `Insert object…` opens a small menu populated from the live model (Nodes / Links / Subcatchments / Pollutants) so the user can insert by clicking when typing-driven completion is not preferred.

Save semantics: edits commit on **focus loss** of `RuleCodeEditor` and on **list-selection change**, via a single `flushPendingEdit()` that calls `applyControlRuleReplace(currentName, currentBody)`. There is no OK/Cancel button — the dialog matches the live-commit convention used by the curve / pattern / timeseries editors. The validation badge updates per keystroke (debounced 250 ms) **without** committing.

**Create-new mode.** The same dialog launched via `RulesEditorDialog::createNew(layer, undoStack, parent)` shows a create-card above the splitter (Name + uniqueness validator + skeleton-template combo + Create button), mirroring `PatternEditorDialog::createNew`. On Create the dialog calls `layer->applyControlRuleAdd(name, skeletonBody)`, binds to the new provider, hides the card, and transitions to `Mode::Edit`. The skeleton-template combo reuses the DA.3 templates already defined for the legacy `NewDataObjectDialog` path so behaviour matches the old Add-New flow.

**Entry points into the editor:**

- Object Browser → right-click Control Rules group header → **Add New…** → `RulesEditorDialog::createNew(...)`.
- Object Browser → double-click a rule node → `RulesEditorDialog::openForRule(name)`.
- `AttributePanel` → right-click `ruleText` row → **Edit "R1" in Rules Editor…** (Slice BM.0-Browse-Edit) → same `openForRule(name)`.
- `AttributePanel` → click the new browse `…` button on the `ruleText` row → same `openForRule(name)`.

All four entry points reuse the same singleton dialog instance per project (raised + activated if already open). When already open and pointing at a different rule, `openForRule` calls `flushPendingEdit()` on the current rule before switching selection — no edits lost.

##### `AttributePanel` integration — browse button + right-click "Edit…"

Today (`src/ui/panels/attributepanel.cpp:613`) the panel constructs `SWMMControlRulePropertyAdapter` for `K::Control` and renders the `ruleText` row with the `MultiLineCellDelegate` text editor. Two surgical changes per [[feedback_mvc_synchronized_uis]]:

1. **Browse `…` button on the `ruleText` row.** A new `RuleTextRowDelegate` adds a small browse button next to the multi-line editor, matching the affordance `DataObjectPickerEditor` already adds for `DataObjectRef` rows. Clicking it calls `RulesEditorDialog::openForRule(currentRuleName)`. Inline typing keeps working — the button is additive.
2. **Right-click "Edit…" menu arm.** The existing Slice BM.0-Browse-Edit context menu in `attributepanel.cpp` gets a new `case K::Control:` that pops `"Edit "<name>" in Rules Editor…"` and routes to `RulesEditorDialog::openForRule`.

`SWMMControlRulePropertyAdapter` is rewired to listen to `SWMMModelLayer::controlRulesChanged(QString)`. On match (or empty broadcast) it calls its own `emit changed()`, which the `QPropertyModel` already routes to `refreshValues()` (the same pattern wired for the hydrograph case at `attributepanel.cpp:592-606`). Inline edit and editor edit now converge through a single signal — no polling.

1. **MVC sync smoke** (manual, the synchronization claim):
   - Open a `.inp` containing `[CONTROLS]`. Open `RulesEditorDialog` from the Object Browser. Pin `AttributePanel` on the same rule.
   - Edit the body in the editor → confirm (a) the list-view badge transitions Pending → Valid/Invalid within 250 ms, (b) the property-panel `ruleText` row updates on save without a manual refresh, (c) the Object Browser rule name updates if `RULE <name>` was rewritten in the body.
   - Edit the body in the property panel → confirm the editor's body updates (when open) and the list badge re-evaluates.
   - Rename via the list → confirm the property-panel header, the Object Browser rule node, and the `RULE <name>` header in the body all update in one round-trip.
   - Delete via the list → confirm the property panel clears, the Object Browser rule disappears, the engine round-trip drops exactly that slot.
2. **Model tests:** `cmake --build build --target test_control_rule_models && ctest -R control_rule_models`.
3. **Dialog tests:** `cmake --build build --target test_rules_editor_dialog && ctest -R rules_editor_dialog`.
4. **Round-trip:** save the `.inp` and re-open → every edited rule round-trips byte-for-byte (modulo the engine's canonical whitespace normalisation).

- Per-rule undo/redo through `QUndoStack` — Slice BU territory.

#### 🔧 Phase 6.8.2 detail — `RuleSyntaxHighlighter` + `RuleCompleter` + `RuleValidator` (DRAFT 2026-05-25)

**`RuleSyntaxHighlighter`** (`include/controls/rulesyntaxhighlighter.{h,cpp}`) — `QSyntaxHighlighter` attached to the `RuleCodeEditor`'s `QTextDocument`. Token classes + palette roles (palette pulled from `resources/styles/style.qss` so dark/light themes Just Work):

| Token class | Examples | Style |
|---|---|---|
| Block keyword | `RULE`, `IF`, `THEN`, `ELSE`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `PRIORITY` | Bold, palette `Highlight` |
| Object type | `NODE`, `LINK`, `CONDUIT`, `PUMP`, `ORIFICE`, `WEIR`, `OUTLET`, `SUBCATCH`, `SIMULATION`, `GAGE` | Bold, palette `LinkVisited` |
| Variable | `DEPTH`, `HEAD`, `FLOW`, `VOLUME`, `INFLOW`, `SETTING`, `STATUS`, `CLOCKTIME`, `DATE`, `MONTH`, `DAY`, `TIME` | Italic, palette `Link` |
| Action target | `STATUS`, `SETTING` (when in THEN / ELSE clause) | Italic, palette `Link` |
| Operator | `=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `<>`, `IS`, `NOT`, `BETWEEN` | Palette `WindowText` (no decoration) |
| Number | Integer + decimal literals + `HH:MM[:SS]` clock literals | Palette `Text`, slight tint |
| Comment | Anything after `;` to EOL (legacy SWMM comment syntax) | Italic, palette `PlaceholderText` |
| Identifier | Anything else after an object type — the actual NODE / LINK name | Palette `WindowText` |

Keyword + object-type + variable + action vocabularies are pulled from `src/engine/controls/Controls.cpp` (the existing `obj_type ==` / `attr ==` ladders at lines 650–736 of that file) and exposed as `constexpr` `QStringView` arrays in `rulesyntaxhighlighter.cpp` so the GUI and engine vocabularies cannot drift.

**`RuleCompleter`** (`include/ui/widgets/rulecodeeditor.{h,cpp}` — co-located with the editor since they're tightly coupled). `QCompleter` with `Qt::MatchStartsWith` + `Qt::CaseInsensitive`, popup mode `QCompleter::PopupCompletion`. Source model is rebuilt on each popup show by `RuleCodeEditor::buildCompletionsForContext_()`, which inspects the token immediately to the left of the cursor and picks a category-scoped completion list:

| Preceding token | Completions |
|---|---|
| Start of line (no preceding token) | `RULE`, `IF`, `THEN`, `ELSE`, `AND`, `OR`, `PRIORITY` |
| After `RULE` | (empty — user types a new name) |
| After `IF` / `AND` / `OR` | `NODE`, `LINK`, `CONDUIT`, `PUMP`, `ORIFICE`, `WEIR`, `OUTLET`, `SUBCATCH`, `SIMULATION`, `GAGE`, `NOT` |
| After `NODE` | live node names from `layer->objectNamesForCategory(CatJunctions \| CatOutfalls \| CatStorage \| CatDividers)` |
| After `LINK` / `CONDUIT` / `PUMP` / `ORIFICE` / `WEIR` / `OUTLET` | live link names from the matching category accessor |
| After `<NODE_NAME>` | `DEPTH`, `HEAD`, `VOLUME`, `INFLOW`, `OVERFLOW`, `TIMEOPEN`, `TIMECLOSED` |
| After `<LINK_NAME>` | `FLOW`, `DEPTH`, `SETTING`, `STATUS` |
| After `SIMULATION` | `TIME`, `DATE`, `CLOCKTIME`, `MONTH`, `DAY` |
| After `THEN` / `ELSE` | `PUMP`, `ORIFICE`, `WEIR`, `OUTLET`, `CONDUIT` |
| Comparator position | `=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `<>`, `IS` |

`Ctrl+Space` force-triggers the popup at any cursor position. Otherwise the popup is automatic after 2 characters typed at a context where completions exist. Tab / Enter accept the current selection; Esc dismisses without insertion.

**`RuleValidator`** (`include/controls/rulevalidator.{h,cpp}`) — full engine parser round-trip via new engine gap **BR-02**. One sandbox engine handle is constructed lazily on the layer (`layer->ensureValidationSandbox()`) by opening the same `.inp` in `SWMM_ENGINE_STATE_LOADED` and **not** running it. The validator's `validate(const QString &text)` calls:

```cpp
char errbuf[512] = {};
int  errline = -1;
int  rc = swmm_control_validate_rule(sandbox, text.toUtf8().constData(),
                                      errbuf, sizeof(errbuf), &errline);
return (rc == SWMM_OK)
       ? Result{Valid, {}, -1}
       : Result{Invalid, QString::fromUtf8(errbuf), errline};
```

The sandbox engine is **shared** across all open `RulesEditorDialog` instances on the same project — one per `SWMMModelLayer`. It is reloaded when the project's network changes (node/link add/rename/remove via the existing layer signals) so name resolution catches up; reload itself is debounced 500 ms via a single-shot `QTimer` so a bulk import or rename storm coalesces into one reload rather than N. Validator calls are debounced 250 ms per editor and run on the GUI thread (the sandbox call is microseconds for a typical 2-KB rule body — synchronous is fine).

When BR-02 is not yet shipped, `RuleValidator` falls back to a **lexical-only** check (balanced `IF/THEN`, presence of `RULE <name>`, no other GUI-side mini-parser) and surfaces a yellow "Lint deferred — engine BR-02 not yet shipped" banner. This keeps the dialog usable during the engine lead-in but the user-requested "full engine validator" lands the moment BR-02 ships.

##### Engine gap BR-02 — `swmm_control_validate_rule` (mandatory for Phase 6.8.2)

| New symbol | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `swmm_control_validate_rule(eng, text, errbuf, buflen, *line_out)` | Parse a rule **without** storing it. Returns `SWMM_OK` on accept; on reject returns `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM` (or a more specific code) and writes a human-readable message to `errbuf` plus the 1-based offending line index to `*line_out`. Implementation factors the existing tokeniser/grammar in `src/engine/controls/Controls.cpp` into a `parseRuleTokens(text, errbuf, buflen, *line_out, store=false)` helper shared with `swmm_control_add_rule`. |

Test in `tests/unit/engine/test_control_rule_validate_api.cpp` (~12 cases — listed in the BR Tests bullet above). All cases assert the validator does **not** mutate engine state (rule count + per-rule text unchanged across the call).

##### Pattern reuse

This sub-slice closes the controls leg of the Phase 6.9.2 *Pattern reuse* note. The pattern in play is now applied to four categories: hydrographs (BS), curves / patterns / timeseries (BQ), and control rules (BR). Future categories (LID controls — BO; pollutant / land-use / treatment — BP) should follow the same shape: engine-backed `QAbstractItemModel`s owned by `SWMMModelLayer` + a fine-grained `xxxChanged(QString)` signal + a project-scoped `XRegistry` of `XProvider`s.

### ⏳ Slice BS — Climatology editor + hydrograph (RDII) group editor (Phase 6.9)

Legacy `Dclimat.pas` exposes 5 climate panels.

**Note 2026-05-22:** hydrograph group-count + name accessors land in Slice DA.1 via the new engine API `swmm_hydrograph_group_count` / `swmm_hydrograph_group_id` (de-duplicates the per-`(group, month, response)` entry list in first-occurrence order). DA.3 ships the "New Unit Hydrograph…" creation flow with rain-gage picker + response combo, creating via `swmm_hydrograph_add_gage` + `swmm_hydrograph_add(-1, response, …)`. DA.2 ships the `SWMMHydrographPropertyAdapter` exposing the monthly grid via a `ButtonCellDelegate` placeholder. BS now reduces to: (a) `HydrographGroupEditor` — the structured per-month R/T/K + Dmax/Drecov/Dinit grid replacing the DA.2 placeholder; (b) `ClimatologyDialog` (Temperature / Evaporation / Wind / Snowmelt / Areal-Depletion-Curve tabs); (c) forcing-override seam per panel.
