#### 🔧 Phase 6.9.2 detail — `HydrographGroupEditor` + hydrograph MVC layer (DRAFT 2026-05-24)

**Status:** drafted 2026-05-24, awaiting review. Replaces the one-line stub above. User-approved decisions: three-pane resizable layout (groups list / details + RTK + IA tabs / live UH preview plot); MVC architecture so the same data edited via multiple UIs stays synchronized; modern UI conventions (flat toolbuttons, styled splitter, inline status strip, narrow-width collapse). Implementation does not start until this sub-section is reviewed.

**Why MVC matters here.** The same `(group, month, response)` parameters are surfaced today by the Object Browser, the `SWMMHydrographPropertyAdapter` (DA.2), `NodeCompoundEditDialog`'s UH picker (DB.4f), and the `NewDataObjectDialog` "New Hydrograph" flow (DA.3). Without an MVC layer each surface polls the engine independently and they drift; with it, every surface binds to the **same** Qt model instances and refreshes through a single `hydrographChanged(QString)` signal. This pattern (engine-backed `QAbstractItemModel`s owned by `SWMMModelLayer` + a fine-grained `xxxChanged(QString)` signal) is the prototype for future multi-UI data categories (curves, time series, patterns, controls).

##### MVC layer — engine-backed Qt models owned by `SWMMModelLayer`

**New signal on `SWMMModelLayer`** — sits alongside `attributeChanged(QString)` / `geometryChanged()` / `optionsChanged(QStringList)` at `swmmmodellayer.h:967–1012`:

```cpp
/*! Emitted whenever any [HYDROGRAPHS] / [RDII_DECAY] mutation lands in
 *  the engine (add, set, remove, rename, gage assignment). uhName is
 *  empty for "rebuild everything" (group rename or bulk clear). All
 *  hydrograph models listen here and refresh; the editor's UI is purely
 *  view code. */
void hydrographChanged(const QString &uhName);
```

**New `SWMMModelLayer` mutation helpers** (the *only* place engine `swmm_hydrograph_*` / `swmm_rdii_decay_*` mutation calls live — mirrors the `applyRename` / `applyNodeDelete` pattern at `swmmmodellayer.h:946–965`):

- `bool applyHydrographAddGroup(name, gageName, initialResponse)`
- `bool applyHydrographRemoveGroup(name)`
- `bool applyHydrographRenameGroup(oldName, newName)`
- `bool applyHydrographSetGage(name, gageName_or_empty)`
- `bool applyHydrographSetRtk(name, month, response, r, t, k)`
- `bool applyHydrographSetIa(name, month, response, dmax, drecov, dinit)`
- `bool applyHydrographRemoveEntry(name, month, response)`
- `bool applyHydrographClearMonths(name)` *(seasonal → ALL)*
- `bool applyRdiiDecaySet(name, response, k_dep, k_0, k_T, T_ref, theta_rec, T_freeze)`
- `bool applyRdiiDecayRemove(name, response)`

Each calls the corresponding engine API (added by BS-02), then emits `hydrographChanged(name)`.

**Four Qt models in `include/data/hydrographmodels.h`** (pattern follows `HotstartSavesModel` at `include/ui/dialogs/hotstartsavesmodel.h` and the engine-backed `SWMMAttributeTableModel`). Each holds a pointer to its `SWMMModelLayer`, listens to `hydrographChanged()`, and refreshes lazily.

| Model class | Subclass of | Shape | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HydrographGroupListModel` | `QAbstractListModel` | N rows × 1 col | Pane 1 list of UH group names. Editable in place (rename). `insertRows` opens NewDataObjectDialog flow; `removeRows` calls `applyHydrographRemoveGroup`. |
| `HydrographRtkTableModel` | `QAbstractTableModel` | 3 rows × 4 cols (Response, R, T, K) | Parameterized by `(groupName, month)`. Setters → `applyHydrographSetRtk`. Column 0 non-editable via `flags()` override. Blank cells (no entry yet for that response) render as empty `QVariant`, distinct from explicit 0. |
| `HydrographIaTableModel` | `QAbstractTableModel` | 3 rows × 4 cols (Response, Dmax, Drec, Do) | Parameterized by `(groupName, month)`. Setters → `applyHydrographSetIa`. Same blank/zero distinction. |
| `HydrographDecayTableModel` | `QAbstractTableModel` | 3 rows × 8 cols (Response, Active, k_dep, k_0, k_T, T_ref, theta_rec, T_freeze) | Parameterized by `groupName` only — no month dimension (engine has none — see `InflowData.hpp:174`). Active is `Qt::CheckStateRole` on col 1; existence of a decay row IS active (struct has no `active` field). Setters → `applyRdiiDecaySet`; unchecking Active → `applyRdiiDecayRemove`. |

Accessors on `SWMMModelLayer`:

```cpp
HydrographGroupListModel  *hydrographGroupListModel();
HydrographRtkTableModel   *hydrographRtkModel(const QString &name, int month);
HydrographIaTableModel    *hydrographIaModel(const QString &name, int month);
HydrographDecayTableModel *hydrographDecayModel(const QString &name);
```

The list model is a singleton on the layer. Per-group models are cached in a `QHash<key, model*>` so re-opening the editor reuses the same instance — and the Object Browser / property panel subscribe to the *same* model the editor mutates.

`SWMMHydrographPropertyAdapter` is refactored to listen to `hydrographChanged(name)` and emit its `changed()` so the QPropertyModel-backed property panel auto-refreshes. The DA.2 `ButtonCellDelegate` "Edit…" placeholder opens the new editor pre-selected on its group.

**Synchronization path in practice.** User edits R in the editor's RTK table → `HydrographRtkTableModel::setData` → `layer->applyHydrographSetRtk(...)` → engine call → `emit hydrographChanged(uhName)` → all four models call `refresh()` + emit `dataChanged()` → editor's `QTableView`s, the Object Browser UH branch, the property-panel `SWMMHydrographPropertyAdapter`, and `NodeCompoundEditDialog`'s UH picker all redraw. No polling. No `refreshActivePage()` calls. No diverging caches.

##### `HydrographGroupEditor` — dialog shape

**Class.** `class HydrographGroupEditor : public QDialog`. **Non-modal** (`setModal(false)`) — matches the `ProfileOptionsDialog` convention so the user can keep it open while clicking around the network for calibration context. Geometry + splitter sizes persist via `QSettings` using `ProfileOptionsDialog`'s `persistenceKey()` idiom. The dialog is pure view code — it owns no engine state, only `QTableView` / `QComboBox` widgets bound to layer-owned models.

**Layout.** Top-level `QSplitter(Qt::Horizontal)` with `setChildrenCollapsible(false)`, `setHandleWidth(6)`, three resizable panes. Initial stretch factors `(2, 4, 3)` saved/restored via `QSplitter::saveState()`.

**Modern UI conventions applied throughout:**
- Flat `QToolButton` with icons (from `resources/images`) instead of bordered `QPushButton` for `+`, `−`, `Rename`, `Edit gage`. Tooltips on every button.
- Styled `QSplitter` handle (matches `resources/styles/style.qss`).
- 8-px content margins, 6-px form spacing.
- Header `QLabel` per pane uses `QFont::Bold` and secondary-text palette colour (no raw `<b>…</b>` HTML).
- Bottom status strip: "N groups · group X has Y entries · Active decay rows: Z" — quiet inline feedback rather than `QMessageBox` for non-errors.
- Narrow-width mode: when dialog width drops below 1100 px, the right (preview) pane collapses into a tab on the middle pane via `QSplitter::setSizes(..., 0)` so the editor stays usable on small screens.

**Pane 1 — UH group list.**
- `QListView` bound to `layer->hydrographGroupListModel()`. Selection drives the rest of the dialog.
- Compact `QToolBar` above the list with three flat actions: `New…` (opens `NewDataObjectDialog(Hydrographs)`), `Delete` (confirmation → `removeRows`), `Rename…` (inline rename via `QListView::edit`).
- Filter `QLineEdit` at the top with placeholder "Search groups…" — uses a `QSortFilterProxyModel` over the list model.

**Pane 2 — Group details** (vertically stacked, each section in a flat `QGroupBox`):
1. **Name** — read-only label, large font; right-aligned `Rename…` toolbutton.
2. **Rain gage** — `QComboBox` listing rain gages from `swmm_gage_count`/`_id`, leading "(none)" entry. `currentTextChanged` → `applyHydrographSetGage`.
3. **Season** — `QComboBox` with 13 entries ("All", "January" … "December"). "All" → month `-1`; rest → `0..11`. On `currentIndexChanged`, dialog calls `view->commitData(...)` to flush any in-flight cell editor before rebinding the RTK / Linear-IA views to the new `(name, month)`-keyed model.
4. `QTabWidget` below with two tabs:
   - **Tab 1 — "RTK"**: `QTableView` bound to `layer->hydrographRtkModel(currentName, currentMonth)`. 3 fixed rows (Short-Term / Medium-Term / Long-Term) × 4 columns (Response, R, T, K). Column header tooltips: R = fraction of rainfall volume → RDII; T = time-to-peak (h); K = ratio of base time to peak time (≥ 1, so the falling limb spans `(K−1)·T` hours past the peak). When season = "All" but per-month entries exist, `setData` prompts before write — "Replace 12 monthly entries with a single ALL row?" → `applyHydrographClearMonths` before writing. Derived label beneath: "Falling limb: (K−1)·T h".
   - **Tab 2 — "Initial Abstraction"**: two `QGroupBox` sections.
     1. **Linear IA (per season)** — `QTableView` bound to `layer->hydrographIaModel(currentName, currentMonth)`. 3 × 4 (Response, Dmax, Drec, Do).
     2. **Exponential IA decay (season-agnostic)** — `QTableView` bound to `layer->hydrographDecayModel(currentName)`. 3 × 8. `QLabel` above states "These parameters are independent of season — they apply year-round; temperature drives the variation." Active is a checkbox via `Qt::CheckStateRole` on col 1. Checking → `applyRdiiDecaySet` with sane defaults (`T_ref=10`, others 0). Unchecking → `applyRdiiDecayRemove`. Numeric cols 2–7 are visually greyed when Active is unchecked.

**Pane 3 — UH preview plot.** `InteractiveChartView` (`comparisonplotdialog.cpp:1262`) hosting a `QChart`. **Qt Charts, not QCustomPlot.** `InteractiveChartView` already provides rubber-band zoom, wheel zoom, pan, and context-menu "Zoom to extent" — standard plot affordances inherited for free.

- **Y-axis**: unit flow (`QValueAxis`, label "Unit flow").
- **X-axis**: time in hours (`QValueAxis`, label "Time (h)").
- **Three filled triangles**, one per response (Short / Medium / Long), drawn with `QAreaSeries` between a `QLineSeries` outline and the x-axis. Semi-transparent fills (Slice AT.3 palette colours); opaque outlines. For `(R, T, K)`: vertices `(0, 0) → (T, peak) → (K·T, 0)` where `peak = 2·R / (K·T)` (triangle area = R, the response fraction).
- **Composite (summation) series** — `QLineSeries` overlay summing the three triangles ordinate-wise (densified to ~200 samples over `[0, max(K·T)]`). Distinct palette colour; drawn on top.
- Legend with four entries; empty/missing response rows drop out of legend and sum.
- Plot listens to `hydrographChanged(currentName)` and recomputes — same MVC seam.
- Plot toolbar: `Zoom to extent`, `Reset zoom`, `Copy to clipboard` (PNG), `Export…` (PNG/SVG).
- Math replicated GUI-side (not engine round-trip). A unit test in `test_hydrograph_models.cpp` pins the GUI ordinate against an engine reference for a fixed `(R, T, K)` so drift surfaces immediately (reference: `RDIISolver::uhOrdinate` at `RDII.hpp:157`).

**Entry points into the editor:**
- `SWMMHydrographPropertyAdapter`'s deferred "Edit…" button (DA.2 placeholder) → `HydrographGroupEditor::openForGroup(name)`.
- Object Browser → double-click a UH group node.
- `NodeCompoundEditDialog::buildRdiiPage()` gets an "Edit UH group…" button next to the UH picker that opens the editor pre-selected on the picker's current name.
- All three entry points reuse the same singleton dialog instance (raised/activated if already open).

##### Engine gap BS-02 — Hydrograph + RDII decay mutation surface

`openswmm.engine` today exposes only `_add` / `_get` / `_count` / `_group_count` / `_group_id` for hydrographs and `_add` / `_get` / `_count` for `rdii_decay` (`openswmm_inflows.h:229–408`). The MVC layer requires:

| New symbol in `openswmm_inflows.h` | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `swmm_hydrograph_set_rtk(eng, uh_name, month, response, r, t, k)` | Upsert R/T/K for one `(group, month, response)` | Update-in-place when match exists, else append |
| `swmm_hydrograph_set_ia(eng, uh_name, month, response, dmax, drecov, dinit)` | Upsert linear IA for one `(group, month, response)` | Same upsert contract |
| `swmm_hydrograph_remove_entry(eng, uh_name, month, response)` | Remove one entry — **key-based, not index-based** (indices shift on remove) | Idempotent: returns `SWMM_OK` if no match |
| `swmm_hydrograph_remove_group(eng, uh_name)` | Remove all `(uh, *, *)` entries + gage assignment + decay rows | Single transaction on the data side |
| `swmm_hydrograph_clear_group_months(eng, uh_name)` | Bulk-clear all per-month entries for a group (used when switching to "ALL") | Avoids O(n²) repeated remove |
| `swmm_hydrograph_set_gage(eng, uh_name, gage_name_or_null)` | Replace existing gage assignment, or clear (when `gage_name` is `NULL`/empty) | Touches the parallel vectors at `InflowData.hpp:148–150` |
| `swmm_hydrograph_group_rename(eng, idx, new_id)` | Rename a UH group; walks `UnitHydData::entries[].name`, `gage_assignments`, and `RDIIDecayData::entries[].uh_name` | Mirrors `swmm_gage_rename` at `openswmm_gages.h:185` |
| `swmm_rdii_decay_set(eng, uh_name, response, k_dep, k_0, k_T, T_ref, theta_rec, T_freeze)` | Upsert one decay row | Same upsert contract |
| `swmm_rdii_decay_remove(eng, uh_name, response)` | Remove one decay row | Key-based, idempotent |

Implementation lands in `src/engine/core/openswmm_inflows_impl.cpp` alongside the existing `swmm_hydrograph_*` symbols (lines 227–383). All setters share the same `(name, month, response)` upsert pattern for symmetry. Test in `tests/unit/engine/test_hydrograph_mutation_api.cpp` (new, ~14 cases — listed in the BS Tests bullet above).

##### Verification

1. **Engine round-trip:** `cmake --build build --target test_hydrograph_mutation_api && ctest -R hydrograph_mutation`.
2. **Model tests:** `cmake --build build --target test_hydrograph_models && ctest -R hydrograph_models`. Specifically validate that two `HydrographRtkTableModel` instances on the same `(group, month)` key both receive `dataChanged` on a single `applyHydrographSetRtk` call.
3. **Dialog tests:** `cmake --build build --target test_hydrograph_group_editor && ctest -R hydrograph_group_editor`.
4. **Manual MVC smoke (the synchronization claim):**
   - Open a `.inp` containing `[HYDROGRAPHS]` and `[RDII_DECAY]` sections.
   - Open the HydrographGroupEditor from the Object Browser. Pin the property panel beside it so `SWMMHydrographPropertyAdapter` is visible. Open `NodeCompoundEditDialog` on a node referencing the same UH.
   - Edit an R value in the editor's RTK table → confirm (a) the preview triangle updates instantly, (b) the property panel's `rowSummary` refreshes without clicking elsewhere, (c) the `NodeCompoundEditDialog` UH picker shows the same group with no manual refresh.
   - Rename the group via the editor's context menu → confirm the rename ripples to the property panel header, the Object Browser node, and the per-node RDII page picker.
   - Switch season mid-edit → confirm the in-flight value does not land in the wrong slot.
   - Tick Active on Long-Term decay → confirm row gains defaults and lights up; untick → row disappears, numeric cells grey out.
   - Save the `.inp` and re-open → confirm all changes round-trip.
   - Run a short simulation → confirm RDII flows match engine reference for the edited group.
5. **End-to-end plot:** render a multi-response group and visually verify the composite series envelopes the three component triangles; zoom / pan / zoom-to-extent all work.

##### Out of scope (deferred)

- Undo/redo through `QUndoStack` for per-cell edits — Slice BU territory.
- Per-month tab visualisation (12 sub-tabs instead of a season combo).
- Drag-resize triangles directly on the preview plot.
- Cross-group plot overlay (compare two UH groups side by side) — belongs in `ComparisonPlotDialog`.

##### Pattern reuse

This sub-slice establishes a pattern — engine-backed `QAbstractItemModel`s owned by `SWMMModelLayer` + a fine-grained `xxxChanged(QString)` signal — that should be applied to other multi-UI data categories (curves, time series, patterns, controls) as those editors are built out. The existing `[[feedback_property_model_editors]]` rule (prefer QPropertyModel-backed editors for property dialogs) still applies to `SWMMHydrographPropertyAdapter`, but does **not** apply to the three fixed-row tables here — those need first-class `QAbstractTableModel`s so multiple views can share state.

### 🔧 Slice BM.0-Add-New — Object Browser "Add New…" launches complex MVC editors; `NewDataObjectDialog` removed (drafted 2026-05-24)

**Context.** Slice BM.0 wires "Add New…" on each non-spatial data-category group header to `NewDataObjectDialog` — a per-category simplistic name+subtype mini-dialog that creates the object via `swmm_{type}_add` and drops the user back into the tree with no editor wired up (except for Time Series and Unit Hydrographs, which can be reached by double-click). User-mandated UX: Add-New should launch the **complex MVC editor** directly — name capture happens inside that editor's create-mode. For data categories without a complex editor today, Add-New is **disabled** with a tooltip naming the future editor slice (no fallback to the simplistic dialog; no "coming soon" stub). `NewDataObjectDialog` is deleted entirely (no backwards-compat shim — aligns with the project's no-backwards-compat convention per [[feedback_dont_blindly_follow_plan_docs]]). Each future editor slice (BO/BP/BQ/BR) re-enables exactly one category by adding one switch arm to `ObjectBrowserPanel::launchAddNewEditor` + flipping one entry in `hasComplexEditor` / `gapTooltipFor`.

**Scope.**

| Category | After this slice | Editor |
|---|---|---|
| Time Series | `TimeseriesEditorDialog::createNew(registry, undoStack, parent)` (new factory; Mode::CreateNew → Mode::Edit transition on Create) | `include/ui/dialogs/timeserieseditordialog.h` |
| Unit Hydrographs | `HydrographGroupEditor::beginNewGroup()` (new public slot wraps the existing left-pane "New" button) | `include/ui/dialogs/hydrographgroupeditor.h` |
| Curves | **Disabled** (tooltip: *"Editor coming in Slice BQ Phase 6.7.1 (CurveEditor)"*) | future |
| Patterns | **Disabled** (Slice BQ Phase 6.7.2 `PatternEditor`) | future |
| Transects | **Disabled** (Slice BQ Phase 6.7.4 `TransectEditor`) | future |
| LID Controls | **Disabled** (Slice BO Phase 6.5.x `LIDControlEditor`) | future |
| Pollutants | **Disabled** (Slice BP Phase 6.6.1 `PollutantEditor`) | future |
| Land Uses | **Disabled** (Slice BP Phase 6.6.2 `LandUseEditor`) | future |
| Aquifers | **Disabled** (Slice BP Phase 6.6.x `AquiferEditor`) | future |
| Snowpacks | **Disabled** (Slice BP Phase 6.6.x `SnowpackEditor`) | future |
| Control Rules | **Disabled** (Slice BR Phase 6.8.1 `RulesEditorDialog`) | future |
| Streets | **Disabled** (Slice BO Phase 6.5.x `StreetEditor`; engine gap **BO-STREET-01**) | future |
| Inlets | **Disabled** (Slice BO Phase 6.5.x `InletEditor`; engine gap **BO-INLET-01**) | future |

**Implementation.**

1. **`TimeseriesEditorDialog::createNew`** — add `enum class Mode { Edit, CreateNew }` private state. Static factory builds the dialog without a bound provider, renders a create-card (QLineEdit Name + uniqueness validator that pings `registry->findByName(text)` and shows a red border on collision, source-mode radio set Inline / ExternalFile / GeopackageObserved). Create button calls `registry->create(name)`, captures the provider via `providerAdded`, transitions to Mode::Edit, hides the card, hands off to existing edit-mode init.
2. **`HydrographGroupEditor::beginNewGroup()`** — `public slots` adding a one-liner that calls `show() + raise() + activateWindow()` and invokes the existing private slot the left-pane "New" button is wired to.
3. **`ObjectBrowserPanel` rewire** — three private members: `static bool hasComplexEditor(SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory)`; `static QString gapTooltipFor(SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory)` (hardcoded per-category strings); `void launchAddNewEditor(SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory)` (switch on the 2 wired categories; `Q_ASSERT_X(false, ...)` on the 11 gap categories — they're meant to be unreachable since the menu disables them). Extract `TimeseriesRegistry *ensureTimeseriesRegistry()` private helper from the inlined lazy-init in `onItemDoubleClicked` so Add-New and double-click share one source of truth. ### 🔧 Slice BM.0-Browse-Edit — Unified comprehensive-editor access surface: browse buttons + right-click on attribute-panel rows + category-header context menu (drafted 2026-05-25)

**Context.** Slice BM.0-Add-New routes Object-Browser "Add New…" through the comprehensive MVC editors (TimeseriesEditorDialog, HydrographGroupEditor, etc.) — that's surface #1 of three the user wants for **every** complex-typed data object. Surface #2 is the **attribute panel row**: today only `DataObjectRef` (outfall stage data) and `NodeCompoundEditRef` (inflows/DWF/RDII/treatment) grow a "…" or "Edit…" button via `registerCustomTypeEditorCreator` at [attributepanel.cpp:178-192](../src/ui/panels/attributepanel.cpp#L178); other complex-typed properties (curve reference on a storage unit, pattern reference on an inflow, transect reference on a conduit, etc.) display as plain text. Surface #3 is **right-click on a complex row** in the attribute panel — currently no `customContextMenuRequested` handler exists on the panel's `QTreeView`.

User-mandated UX (verbatim): *"Generally I want the attribute panel to have a browse button to access editors for complex object types. I also want an edit menu for the complex object types via right click. I also want right click menu on object type header to add new using the comprehensive editor GUIs."* The first two are net-new wiring; the third is the BM.0-Add-New work plus consolidation around a shared dispatch table so the three surfaces never drift.

The shared seam is a single **`ComprehensiveEditorRegistry`** keyed by `SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory`. Today `ObjectBrowserPanel::launchAddNewEditor` is a switch on 13 categories with `Q_ASSERT_X` on the 11 gaps ([objectbrowserpanel.cpp:763-820](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp#L763)); `DataObjectPickerEditor` has a duplicate hard-coded TimeSeries/Hydrographs branch when the user clicks "…"; the attribute-panel right-click handler doesn't exist yet. Replacing all three with one registry means each future editor slice (BO/BP/BQ/BR) lights up all three surfaces at once via one registration call.

**Scope.**

| Surface | Today | After this slice |
|---|---|---|
| Object Browser category header → "Add New…" | Hard-coded switch on TimeSeries / UH; assert on 11 gaps | Registry lookup; same disabled-with-tooltip behaviour for gap categories — but pattern is now uniform |
| Attribute panel row → "…" browse button | Only `DataObjectRef` (outfalls) + `NodeCompoundEditRef` rows | Every `DataObjectRef` row, regardless of category; gap categories show button greyed with the same gap tooltip |
| Attribute panel row → right-click "Edit in …" | Not implemented | Menu on any row whose metatype the registry recognises; first item "Edit `<name>` in `<Editor>`…", second item "Open `<Editor>` (no selection)…", third "Pick another…" (replace ref) |
| Attribute panel **category header** in the property tree (if the row represents an embedded category like `Inflow` / `Treatment` / `LID Group`) | No context menu | "Add new `<Category>`…" routed through the same registry |

**Implementation.**

1. **`include/ui/editors/comprehensiveeditorregistry.h`** (new) — singleton-ish header-only struct:
   ```cpp
   class ComprehensiveEditorRegistry {
   public:
       using OpenFn = std::function<void(SWMMModelLayer*, const QString &initialName, QWidget *parent)>;
       struct Entry {
           QString editorTitle;     // user-visible: "Curve Editor"
           QString gapSliceLabel;   // for disabled tooltip: "Slice BQ Phase 6.7.1"
           OpenFn  open;            // null if editor not yet shipped
       };
       static ComprehensiveEditorRegistry &instance();
       void registerEditor(SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory cat, Entry entry);
       const Entry *find(SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory cat) const;
       bool hasEditor(SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory cat) const;          // true iff Entry::open is non-null
       QString gapTooltip(SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory cat) const;      // "Editor coming in {gapSliceLabel}"
   private:
       QHash<SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory, Entry> m_entries;
   };
   ```
   Populated at app start in `MainWindow` (or a dedicated `registerComprehensiveEditors()` free function in `src/ui/editors/comprehensiveeditorregistry.cpp`) with the four currently-shipped editors:
   ```cpp
   reg.registerEditor(DataCategory::TimeSeries, {"Time Series Editor", "shipped",
       [](SWMMModelLayer *layer, const QString &name, QWidget *parent) {
           TimeseriesEditorDialog::openForName(layer->timeseriesRegistry(), layer->undoStack(), name, parent);
       }});
   reg.registerEditor(DataCategory::Hydrographs, {"Hydrograph Group Editor", "shipped",
       [](SWMMModelLayer *layer, const QString &name, QWidget *parent) {
           HydrographGroupEditor::openForGroup(layer, name, parent);
       }});
   reg.registerEditor(DataCategory::Curves,   {"Curve Editor",   "Slice BQ Phase 6.7.1", /*open=*/nullptr});
   reg.registerEditor(DataCategory::Patterns, {"Pattern Editor", "Slice BQ Phase 6.7.2", /*open=*/nullptr});
   // ...remaining 8 gap categories with null open and per-category gapSliceLabel
   ```
   Each `Entry` with `open == nullptr` represents a gap; UI surfaces grey out and show `gapTooltip()`.

2. **`TimeseriesEditorDialog::openForName` / `HydrographGroupEditor::openForGroup`** — add static factories that mirror the existing `createNew` / `beginNewGroup` entry points but accept an `initialName` so the registry's `OpenFn` signature is uniform. Both should reuse a singleton dialog instance per editor class (raise + activate if already open) to match the MVC sync expectation that `feedback_mvc_synchronized_uis` codifies — opening the same editor from two surfaces must not produce two diverging windows.

3. **`ObjectBrowserPanel` consolidation** ([objectbrowserpanel.cpp:763-820](../src/ui/panels/objectbrowserpanel.cpp#L763)) — delete `hasComplexEditor` / `gapTooltipFor` / the switch in `launchAddNewEditor`. Replace with:
   ```cpp
   void ObjectBrowserPanel::launchAddNewEditor(SWMMModelLayer::DataCategory dc) {
       const auto *entry = ComprehensiveEditorRegistry::instance().find(dc);
       if (!entry || !entry->open) return;     // caller already greyed the action
       entry->open(m_layer, /*initialName=*/QString(), window());
   }
   ```
   Context-menu construction in `onContextMenuRequested` uses `hasEditor` / `gapTooltip` from the registry. Net deletion of ~60 lines of duplicated switch logic.

4. **`DataObjectPickerEditor` consolidation** ([dataobjectpickereditor.h](../include/ui/properties/dataobjectpickereditor.h)) — the "…" button handler today branches on category for the two wired editors. Replace with a single `registry.find(cat); if (!entry->open) showGapTooltip(); else entry->open(layer, currentName, this);`. Picker becomes ~30 lines lighter and supports all 14 categories the day each editor lands.

5. **Attribute panel right-click handler** ([attributepanel.cpp](../src/ui/panels/attributepanel.cpp)) — add `m_treeView->setContextMenuPolicy(Qt::CustomContextMenu)` in `setupUi()`. New private slot `onTreeContextMenu(const QPoint &)`:
   - Resolve the index → `QPropertyModel` row → read the property's Qt metatype.
   - If metatype is `DataObjectRef`: derive `(category, currentName)` from the value, look up the registry entry, build a menu with `Edit "<currentName>" in <editorTitle>…`, `Open <editorTitle>…` (no initial selection), `Pick another…` (delegates to the existing combo of the `DataObjectPickerEditor` — index becomes editable for the duration of the menu invocation).
   - If metatype is `NodeCompoundEditRef`: single item `Edit…` opens `NodeCompoundEditDialog` (already wired; just exposes it via context menu instead of requiring a click on the inline button).
   - If metatype is neither: do not show a menu (don't pop an empty one).
   - For rows the QPropertyModel introduces as **embedded category headers** (e.g. a `Node Inflows ▸` collapsible group), show `Add new…` routed to the same registry via the embedded category's `DataCategory`.

6. **Adapter property-type retype** — the audit (2026-05-25) confirms the retype surface is small. `DataObjectRef` already exists at [include/ui/properties/dataobjectref.h:33-58](../include/ui/properties/dataobjectref.h#L33) and ships today with `Kind ∈ {TidalCurve, AnyCurve, TimeSeries, Pattern, UnitHydrograph}`. Two new kinds + three property retypes complete the slice:

   **Extend `DataObjectRef::Kind`** with `Pollutant` and `RainGage`. Both behave identically to existing kinds (engine + layer + currentName + typeLock semantics); they only differ in which `swmm_*_count` / `_id` family the `DataObjectPickerEditor` enumerates.

   **Retype three Q_PROPERTYs from `QString` to `DataObjectRef`:**

   | Adapter | Property | Line | New kind |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `SWMMLinkPropertyAdapter` (pumps) | `pumpCurve` | [swmmlinkpropertyadapter.h:127](../include/ui/properties/swmmlinkpropertyadapter.h#L127) | `AnyCurve` |
   | `SWMMHydrographPropertyAdapter` | `gageName` | [swmmhydrographpropertyadapter.h:22](../include/ui/properties/swmmhydrographpropertyadapter.h#L22) | `RainGage` |
   | `SWMMPollutantPropertyAdapter` | `coPollutant` | [swmmpollutantpropertyadapter.h:33](../include/ui/properties/swmmpollutantpropertyadapter.h#L33) | `Pollutant` |

   For each: change the property's declared type, add a value-getter that constructs the `DataObjectRef` with the engine handle + layer + current name, and adapt the setter to accept either the typed ref (writes `ref.currentName`) or a plain string (for `.inp` round-trip / legacy callers). `displayLabelFor` is unchanged. Cell rendering changes from "plain text" to "picker combo + browse button" for these three rows; right-click on the row gets the registry-driven menu.

   **Outfall stage-data fields** (`outfallTidalCurve` at [swmmnodepropertyadapter.h:282](../include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h#L282), `outfallTimeseries` at [swmmnodepropertyadapter.h:284](../include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h#L284)) are **already** `DataObjectRef` (shipped by Slice DA.4). They light up automatically once the registry is wired — no adapter edit needed.

   **Deferred to Slice AG.4 (out of scope here):**
   - Storage-curve picker on `SWMMNodePropertyAdapter` (STORAGE-shape branch) — Q_PROPERTY missing entirely per the in-code comment at [swmmnodepropertyadapter.h:315](../include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h#L315).
   - Outlet-curve picker on `SWMMLinkPropertyAdapter` (OUTLETS branch) — Q_PROPERTY missing per [swmmlinkpropertyadapter.h:168](../include/ui/properties/swmmlinkpropertyadapter.h#L168).
   - Transect picker on `SWMMConduitPropertyAdapter` for `crossSection == IRREGULAR` — Q_PROPERTY missing.
   - These three additions (which will need `Transect` added to `DataObjectRef::Kind`) belong in AG.4 because they require new adapter surface, not just retyping existing surface. Once AG.4 ships, the registry already in place from this slice handles them with zero further wiring beyond declaring the kind.

   **Inflows / DWF / RDII / Treatment** stay routed through `NodeCompoundEditRef` (the compound editor button), not through scalar `DataObjectRef` picker rows. Their internal pattern / time-series / hydrograph pickers will eventually consume the same registry in a follow-up — tracked under [[project_swmm_profile_followups]] — but it's not load-bearing for the three surfaces this slice ships.

7. **`AttributeTablePanel` parity** — the table panel reuses `CompoundEditDelegate` for compound cells; this slice adds a parallel `DataObjectPickerDelegate` (table-cell flavor of `DataObjectPickerEditor`) so cells in the Attribute Table also grow browse buttons and right-click menus. Right-click on a table cell whose `EditorKind` is `Compound` or `DataObjectRef` invokes the same registry path.

**Tests.**

`tests/ui/test_comprehensive_editor_registry.cpp` (~8 cases):
1. `registerEditor` + `find` round-trip for one shipped + one gap category.
2. `hasEditor` returns true for shipped TimeSeries, false for gap Curves; `gapTooltip` text matches the documented slice label.
3. Registering the same category twice replaces the entry (last-write-wins; no duplicates accumulate).
4. `OpenFn` invocation with an `initialName` calls the matching editor factory — verified via a mock factory recording invocation.
5. Singleton-raise: opening the same editor twice from two surfaces yields one dialog instance (verified by counting `QApplication::topLevelWidgets`).
6. Registry survives `SWMMModelLayer` swap (loading a new project) without re-registration — entries are layer-agnostic; `OpenFn` receives layer pointer per call.
7. Unregistered category → `find` returns nullptr; surfaces interpret this as "do not show menu / show greyed control".
8. Engine-side handle invalidation between registration and `open()` invocation surfaces a clean error (the editor opens against the *current* layer, not a captured one) — guarded by the slice's "OpenFn signature receives `SWMMModelLayer*` per call, never a captured layer pointer" contract.

`tests/ui/test_attributepanel_context_menu.cpp` (~6 cases):
1. Right-click on a `DataObjectRef` row for TimeSeries shows menu with `Edit "<name>" in Time Series Editor…` + `Open Time Series Editor…` + `Pick another…`.
2. Right-click on a `DataObjectRef` row for a gap category (Curves) shows the same items but disabled with the gap tooltip.
3. Right-click on a plain numeric row shows no menu (does not pop empty).
4. `Edit "<name>"…` invocation opens the editor pre-selected on `<name>` (verified by inspecting the editor's `currentName()` after the action).
5. `Pick another…` triggers `QTreeView::edit` on the current cell so the picker combo becomes editable.
6. Right-click on a `NodeCompoundEditRef` row shows single `Edit…` item that opens `NodeCompoundEditDialog`.

`tests/ui/test_objectbrowser_add_new_dispatch.cpp` (extended; currently lives under BM.0-Add-New): replace the hard-coded switch assertions with registry-mediated assertions (case count unchanged; semantics unchanged).

**Engine APIs.** None new — every wiring change is GUI-side. Reuses the engine surface already required by BM.0-Add-New and each individual editor slice.

**Dependencies.** **BM.0** (Object Browser Data section), **BM.0-Add-New** (must land first so the four shipped editors expose `createNew` / `beginNewGroup` factories), **BS Phase 6.9.2** (HydrographGroupEditor + the singleton-raise pattern). Each future editor slice (BO/BP/BQ/BR) gains one `registry.registerEditor(...)` line in its implementation; no other change to those slices is required.

**Manual.** Extend `docs/manual/06_attribute_panel.md` (or create if absent) with "Editing complex references" describing the browse button + right-click menu. Extend `docs/manual/05_object_browser.md` with the parity statement that Add-New on a category header opens the same editor as the row-level browse button.

**MVC interaction.** All three surfaces share the same `SWMMModelLayer`-owned models (curves model, patterns model, hydrograph models per [[feedback_mvc_synchronized_uis]]). Editing a curve via a browse-button-launched `CurveEditorDialog` emits `curvesChanged(name)` from the layer, which the attribute-panel adapter listens to and re-renders the row label without manual refresh — same seam as the [[project_swmm_profile_followups]] cross-tab subscription. The slice does not introduce any new synchronization mechanism; it only adds new *entry points* into the existing one.

### ⏳ Slice BV — Tab 7 Simulation Options (Files / Output / Plugins) — closes G-4 (Phase 3.10)

Slice G-4 was reserved but unbuilt. BV implements it.

- **Phase 3.10.1 — Files sub-tab**: per-instance `.rpt` / `.out` path overrides plus the `[FILES]` hot-start surface. **USE HOTSTART** stays as a single path field with a Browse button (engine stores one `hotstart_use_path`). **SAVE HOTSTART** replaces the single field with a multi-row uncapped table — one row per `HotstartSaveEntry`, columns *Path* (with Browse-to-save-as button) and *Datetime (optional)*; an empty datetime stores `0`, which the engine writes as a no-timestamp `SAVE HOTSTART` row meaning "save at end of run". Add / Remove / Reorder buttons. Reads via the new dedicated hot-start C API (BV-01 below), writes back via the same. Existing `ProjectSerializer::toRelativePath` conversion still applies on write-back.
- **Phase 3.10.2 — Output sub-tab**: reporting frequency, ignore-rainfall / -runoff / -groundwater / -snow / -routing / -quality switches (single source of truth — relocated from Tab 1 / Tab 2 if duplicated), and `[REPORT]` section variable selectors backed by the new `swmm_report_*` engine API (BV-02 below).
- **Phase 3.10.3 — Plugins sub-tab**: **relocate** the existing `[PLUGINS]` table + Add/Remove buttons out of the Files-tab "Secondary file references" area and into a dedicated Plugins sub-tab inside Tab 7. No engine change — reuses the AA-3.5 `readPluginsFromEngine` / `writePluginsToEngine` wiring intact.
- **Phase 3.10.4 — Validation**: warn when `.out` / `.rpt` paths are unwritable; warn when reporting frequency exceeds the routing step. Runs in `validate()` invoked from `onApply()`.
- **Files**: touches `src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp` (+ `.h`), `include/simulation/simulationoptions.h`; new `include/simulation/filesoptions.h` if not present; new `include/ui/widgets/hotstartsavestable.h` (+ `.cpp`).
- **Engine APIs**: `openswmm_engine.h::swmm_plugins_*` (shipped via AA-3.1); new `openswmm_hotstart.h::swmm_hotstart_saves_*` (BV-01); new `openswmm_engine.h::swmm_report_*` (BV-02).
- **Engine gap BV-01** — *engine work landed 2026-05-21*. New surface in `openswmm_hotstart.h`: `swmm_hotstart_saves_count`, `_get_path`, `_get_datetime`, `_set_path`, `_set_datetime`, `_add`, `_remove`, `_clear`. Implementation lives in `src/engine/core/openswmm_model_impl.cpp` next to `swmm_files_*` so they share `to_engine()` / `fill_buf()` helpers. Wires to `SimulationContext::hotstart_saves` vector. The legacy singular `swmm_files_set("HOTSTART_SAVE_PATH", …)` / `_DATETIME` keys remain as slot-0 sugar (back-compat). Tests appended to `tests/unit/engine/test_files_section.cpp` (9 new cases — count, add/get round-trip, in-place set, remove shift-down, clear, out-of-range bounds, slot-0 sugar coexistence, writer round-trip, null args). Syntax-checked under g++ 11 / C++20; awaiting full build verification on host.
- **Engine gap BV-02** — **resolved 2026-05-22, approach pivoted from `swmm_report_*` to `swmm_options_*` extension** after the engine audit (see Phase 3.10.2 detail below). The `[REPORT]` keywords are exposed via the existing `swmm_options_get/set` surface using new `RPT_*` keys (`RPT_DISABLED`, `RPT_INPUT`, `RPT_CONTINUITY`, `RPT_FLOWSTATS`, `RPT_CONTROLS`, `RPT_AVERAGES`, `RPT_SUBCATCHMENTS`, `RPT_NODES`, `RPT_LINKS`). Boolean keys round-trip as `YES`/`NO`; selector keys round-trip as `ALL`, `NONE`, or comma-separated name lists. Smaller engine surface, reuses the GUI's existing `getOption`/`setOption` plumbing.
- **Phase 3.10.1 GUI work** — *landed 2026-05-21*. `m_hotstartSaveEdit` removed; new `m_hotstartSavesTable` group ships below the "Secondary file references" group, with Add / Browse / Remove / Move-up / Move-down buttons. Path column is an editable text item; Datetime column is a `QDateTimeEdit` cell widget whose `minimumDateTime` is the OA-epoch (1899-12-30) and whose `setSpecialValueText("(end of run)")` renders the 0.0 sentinel readably. Add-button creates an empty row and immediately opens the save-as dialog. Reorder is swap-in-place to keep cell widgets stable. `readFilesSectionFromEngine` loops `swmm_hotstart_saves_count` and populates the table; `writeFilesSectionToEngine` snapshots vs. the engine, and on diff calls `swmm_hotstart_saves_clear` + `_add` for each row (paths run through the existing `toRelative` helper). Empty rows (no path, no datetime) are silently dropped on write. Awaiting host build (Linux sandbox has no Qt6 headers).

#### 🔧 Phase 3.10.2 detail — Report contents (`[REPORT]`) sub-slice (APPROVED 2026-05-22)

**Status:** drafted + reviewed 2026-05-22 after a Tab 7 audit confirmed that everything except the `[REPORT]` selectors was already shipped (Writers/Plugins/[FILES]/Report-path/Output-path via AA-3.5 / AA-4 / BV-01). The reporting-frequency and ignore-* flags called out in the BV stub already live in Tab 2 (Dates) and Tab 1 (Models); duplicating them in Tab 7 would violate the §M.1 single-source-of-truth contract, so the relocation in the original 3.10.2 phrasing is dropped — this sub-slice ships **only** the `[REPORT]` selectors. User-approved decisions:

1. Engine API path = **extend `swmm_options_get/set` with `RPT_*` keys** (smaller surface; reuses GUI plumbing).
2. UI placement = **new group inside the existing Tab 7** (between `[FILES]` Secondary refs and the Report-file path block).
3. Selectors UX = **three-radio `NONE` / `ALL` / `Selected` + name list** (legacy SWMM 5 parity; works for large models without enumerating every object).
4. Engine + GUI work ship **together** as Slice BV.1.

**Engine-side (`openswmm.engine`).**
- `src/engine/input/handlers/OptionsHandler.cpp` (or the dispatch table behind `swmm_options_get/set`): add 9 new keys routed to `ctx.options.rpt_*`:
  - Bool keys (`YES`/`NO`): `RPT_DISABLED`, `RPT_INPUT`, `RPT_CONTINUITY`, `RPT_FLOWSTATS`, `RPT_CONTROLS`, `RPT_AVERAGES`.
  - Selector keys (`ALL` / `NONE` / `name1,name2,…`): `RPT_SUBCATCHMENTS`, `RPT_NODES`, `RPT_LINKS`.
- Selector serialization: int-mode `0 → "NONE"`, `1 → "ALL"`, `2 → comma-joined names`. Setter accepts `NONE`, `ALL`, or any comma/whitespace-delimited list (treat each token as a name to push into `rpt_*_names`; mode set to `2`).
- New test: `tests/unit/engine/test_report_options_api.cpp` — 8 cases: bool round-trip (each of 6 keys), selector ALL/NONE/SOME round-trip per kind (3 kinds × 3 modes = 9 sub-assertions), invalid selector value rejected with `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM`, names with spaces split correctly, name list survives `writeInpFile` → re-parse (uses the already-shipped writer in `InpWriter.cpp:829–847`).

**GUI-side (`openswmm.gui`).**
- New members on `SimulationOptionsDialog` (header):
  - `QCheckBox*` for each of the 6 bool flags.
  - For each of `Subcatchments` / `Nodes` / `Links`: a `QButtonGroup` with 3 `QRadioButton`s (`None` / `All` / `Selected`), a `QLineEdit` for the comma-separated name list, all wrapped in a small inline `QWidget` per kind.
- New `buildReportGroup(QWidget *parent)` helper called from `buildFilesTab` before the Report-file path group.
- `readFromEngine` extension: read the 9 keys; for bools call `parseEngineBool`; for selectors parse `NONE`/`ALL` → set the matching radio; anything else → set `Selected` and put the value verbatim into the line edit.
- `writeToEngine` extension: write each bool key via the existing `writeIfChanged` helper; selectors emit `NONE`, `ALL`, or the line-edit text trimmed.
- Selector line-edit is greyed out unless the `Selected` radio is checked.
- Validation: if `Selected` is chosen but the line-edit is empty, treat as `NONE` on save with a `QMessageBox::information` nudge.

## Block III — Analytics & Advanced (BW–CG)

### ⏳ Slice BW — Hot-start save/load workflow UI (Phase 9.1)

Engine ships `openswmm_hotstart.h` (UUID-robust mapping, CRS consistency, CRC32 integrity).

Hot-start has two distinct surfaces. **Scheduled saves at user-specified sim times** are configured statically via the `[FILES]` SAVE HOTSTART rows in Tab 7 (Slice BV) — the engine writes them automatically as it crosses each datetime, and rows with no datetime save at end of run. **Interactive save/load** (this slice) operates on the running engine: one ad-hoc save at the current sim time, and a single USE-slot load that supersedes any `[FILES]` USE entry for the next run.

- **Phase 9.1.1 — `File → Save Hot Start…`**: calls `swmm_hotstart_save` at the **current sim time** (only meaningful when a run is paused via BX). Dialog: file picker with **Browse-to-save-as button** + summary panel (sim time, node/link counts). On confirm, appends the resulting `{path, datetime=current_sim_time}` as a new row to the `[FILES]` SAVE HOTSTART table via `swmm_files_set` (so the saved file is recorded alongside any scheduled rows from Slice BV).
- **Phase 9.1.2 — `File → Load Hot Start…`**: opens `swmm_hotstart_open`, displays metadata (sim_time, CRS, warning_count + warnings), confirmation → `swmm_hotstart_apply`. Writes the selected path to the single `hotstart_use_path` slot via `swmm_files_set("HOTSTART_USE_PATH", …)` (overwrites any existing USE entry — only one USE file is supported).
- **Phase 9.1.3 — Hot-start library**: dockable list of recently-saved hot-starts per project.
- **Phase 9.1.4 — CRS-mismatch handling**: prompt when hot-start CRS ≠ project CRS (reuses Slice C reproject flow).
- **Files**: new `include/ui/dialogs/hotstartdialog.h`, `include/ui/panels/hotstartlibrarypanel.h` + .cpps.
- **Engine APIs**: `openswmm_hotstart.h::swmm_hotstart_save`, `_open`, `_apply`, `_get_sim_time`, `_get_crs`, `_warning_count`, `_warning`, `_close`.
- **Tests**: `test_hotstart.cpp` (8 cases — save at t, load, CRS mismatch prompt, library round-trip).
- **Manual**: `docs/manual/34_hotstart.md`.
- **Dependencies**: M, V.

Engine ships per-timestep / progress / warning callbacks in `openswmm_callbacks.h`. Today the GUI just runs to completion.

##### Implementation-status gap discovered 2026-05-20 — Step 0 added

Audit found that the engine's 2D output to disk is **dead code today**:

- `Default2DOutputPlugin.cpp` is not in any `CMakeLists.txt` (unbuilt).
- It references `snap.surface_depth` / `surface_head` fields that do not exist on the public `SimulationSnapshot` (would not compile).
- `[2D_OPTIONS]` parser recognizes `MAX_TIMESTEP`, `DRY_DEPTH`, etc., but **no `OUTPUT_FILE` key**.
- The plugin is never instantiated or registered with `PluginFactory`. The 1D analogue is auto-instantiated at [SWMMEngine.cpp:178-183](../../openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/SWMMEngine.cpp#L178); there is no 2D block.

**Therefore the engine produces no 2D output file today, even with `OPENSWMM_BUILD_2D=ON`.** Decision (2026-05-20): Path B — fix the engine gap as Step 0 of the MVP before any GUI work. Path A (live-only viz, no scrub) and Path C (GUI-side in-memory buffer with client-side HDF5 dump) were considered and rejected — Path A drops the load-bearing scrub-to-peak demo beat, Path C diverges from the documented engine format that ParaView / QGIS already consume.

**Engine-side work — Step 0 (1–1.5 days):**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `include/openswmm/plugin_sdk/SimulationSnapshot.hpp` | Append 2D state fields (`surface_tri_count`, `surface_vert_count`, `surface_depth`, `surface_head`, `surface_grad_h{x,y}`, `surface_grad_h{x,y}_lim`, `surface_rainfall`, `surface_coupling_flux`, `surface_net_source`, `surface_edge_flux`, `surface_vert_head`). Source-compatible additions; vectors empty when 2D inactive. Binary-incompatible for compiled SDK plugins (none exist yet). |
| `src/engine/2d/data/SolverOptions2D.hpp` | Add `std::string output_file;`. |
| `src/engine/2d/input/SectionHandlers2D.cpp` | Add `OUTPUT_FILE` key to `handle_2d_options`; resolve relative paths against parent `.inp` directory. |
| `src/engine/CMakeLists.txt` | Add `2d/output/Default2DOutputPlugin.cpp` to the source list inside `if(OPENSWMM_BUILD_2D)`. |
| `src/engine/core/SWMMEngine.cpp` | (a) After line 183, `#ifdef OPENSWMM_HAS_2D` block to auto-instantiate `Default2DOutputPlugin(ctx_.options_2d.output_file)` when 2D active + path set. (b) At `postOutputSnapshot()` ~line 2344, populate `snap.surface_*` from `ctx_.surface_2d` / `ctx_.mesh_2d`. |
| `src/engine/2d/output/Default2DOutputPlugin.cpp` | Reconcile field names with the new SDK; verify compiles. |
| `tests/unit/engine/test_2d_surface_routing.cpp` | New case `runs_with_hdf5_output` — sets `OUTPUT_FILE`, runs sim, opens `.h5`, asserts datasets exist with expected ranks. |

Engine-side **PR is independent and lands first** — without it, the GUI MVP's `HDF5Mesh2DSource` has no file to read. Engine CHANGELOG entry required (SDK contract change).

**Architecture decision — two interchangeable data sources, one rendering path:**

```cpp
class IMesh2DSource {
public:
    virtual ~IMesh2DSource() = default;
    virtual int  vertexCount() const = 0;
    virtual int  triangleCount() const = 0;
    virtual int  timeCount() const = 0;            // grows during live mode
    virtual void readMeshGeometry(/* vx,vy,vz, tris */) = 0;
    virtual void readDepthsAt(int timeIdx, std::vector<float>& out) = 0;
};
```

Two implementations:

- `EngineMesh2DSource(SWMM_Engine eng)` — live source. Calls `swmm_2d_vertex_get_xyz_bulk`, `swmm_2d_triangle_get_vertices`, `swmm_2d_get_depths_bulk`. Used during the run; UI hides the scrub slider while live.
- `HDF5Mesh2DSource(QString path)` — post-run source. Wraps a new `Mesh2DH5Reader` (libhdf5; already a vcpkg dep via GDAL). Reads `/Mesh2_node_x/y/z`, `/Mesh2_face_nodes`, hyperslab on `/Mesh2_face_depth[t,:]`. Same source can later be used for HDF5 tailing if live mode is ever bypassed.

`SWMM2DResultsLayer` extends `OpenSWMMVisLayer` and **copies the `SWMM2DMeshGraphicsItem` paint pattern** from [`src/layers/swmm2dmeshlayer.cpp`](../src/layers/swmm2dmeshlayer.cpp) verbatim — same `SceneTri` buffer, same `prepareGeometryChange()` / `paint()` flow. Only the color function changes:

```cpp
// alpha = 0 below dry_depth so the underlying SWMM2DMeshLayer terrain shows through dry cells.
void inundationColorRgba(double depth_m, double dry_depth, double max_depth,
                         int& r, int& g, int& b, int& a);
```

This lives at exactly the seam Slice CF Phase 9.9.1 identifies for AC.4 theming (lines 5430-5437 above) — the eventual theming slice can swap ramps without restructuring.

**Lifecycle wire — `SimulationRunner` extensions** (Slice N pattern):

The in-process new-engine step loop in [`src/simulation/simulationrunner.cpp`](../src/simulation/simulationrunner.cpp#L279) gains three signals on the existing 1 Hz tick budget:

- `twoDInitialized(int jobId, SWMM_Engine eng)` — emitted right after `swmm_engine_initialize` succeeds. GUI thread builds an `EngineMesh2DSource` and attaches a `SWMM2DResultsLayer` to the canvas before the step loop starts.
- `twoDOutputPathKnown(int jobId, QString h5Path)` — `2D_OUTPUT_FILE` from `[2D_OPTIONS]`, parsed once at job start. Used for the post-run swap.
- `twoDDepthsAvailable(int jobId, std::vector<float> depths, QDateTime simTime, double elapsedSec)` — emitted per tick, gated by `swmm_2d_is_active`. Pushed into the layer's source via queued connection; layer recolors.

On `finished` (success), the GUI swaps the layer's source from `EngineMesh2DSource` to `HDF5Mesh2DSource(h5Path)`, shows a `QSlider` + play/pause in the layer row (mirrors animation controls in [`swmmresultslayer.cpp`](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp)), and persists `h5Path` in `.oswp` `resultLayers` (Slice X infrastructure — same place `.out` paths go; matched by content sniffing on `.h5`). Mesh geometry doesn't change on swap — same triangulation, source is the only difference.

**5.x routing reminder.** 2D only runs on the new engine; the legacy worker subprocess has no 2D module. `SimulationRunner` already auto-routes to the new-engine in-process path for `engineVersion >= 6.0` ([simulationrunner.cpp:175](../src/simulation/simulationrunner.cpp#L175) — `useLegacy = engineVersion.startsWith("5.")`). No new branching needed; any project containing `[2D_*]` sections silently runs on the new engine.

#### ⏳ CF.2 — Velocity vectors, flow-direction overlay, and cell-pick path profile (Phase 9.9.4 + extension)

CF.MVP closed the depth-heatmap beat. CF.2 picks up the **deferred Phase 9.9.4 velocity-vector glyphs** and extends the layer with a **cell-pick path-profile tool** that mirrors the 1D `ProfilePlotDialog` UX but operates on the mesh. Two-mode picker (streamline along the current flow field, or hand-drawn polyline) emits a chainage-indexed sample list; a new `Profile2DPathDialog` reuses `ProfilePlotWidget` to draw ground + animated water-depth curves along the path.

Engine surface needed: there is no live API for edge flux today (`openswmm_2d.h` exposes depth/head bulk only) and the HDF5 reader doesn't expose `/Mesh2_edge_flux` either, even though `Default2DOutputPlugin` already writes that dataset. CF.2.1 closes the gap with two thin bulk accessors plus three time-invariant HDF5 datasets for edge geometry. Older engines + older `.h5` files are tolerated: every new symbol is gated via `QLibrary::resolve` on the GUI side, and the reader has a vertex-derived fallback when the geometry datasets are absent.

Velocity is reconstructed client-side from the three edge-normal fluxes using standard RT0 (lowest-order Raviart–Thomas) cell-velocity reconstruction. For three outward unit normals **n₀, n₁, n₂** and signed normal speeds `qₑ = flux[tri·3+e] / edge_length[tri·3+e]`, the cell-centre velocity is the least-squares solution of the 3×2 system `N·v ≈ q`, which has a closed-form 2×2 inverse via the normal equations `(NᵀN)v = Nᵀq` — about five lines, no SVD, no allocation. Dry cells (`depth < dry_depth`) are skipped. `|qₑ|` is clamped to 10 m/s before assembly to suppress wet/dry-front spikes.

##### Reused, not reinvented

- Polyline state machine + rubber-band paint → mirrors `MapToolAddLink` ([src/map/tools/maptooladdlink.cpp](../src/map/tools/maptooladdlink.cpp)).
- Profile-dialog activation flow → mirrors `MapToolSelectProfile → SWMMVis::openProfilePlotFor`.
- Plot rendering (axes, zoom/pan, time cursor, tooltip) → `ProfilePlotWidget` via the new `IProfilePlotDataProvider` shim — `ProfileBuilder::SourceDerived` and `Profile2DPathAdapter` both implement it.
- Canvas coord helpers → `canvas->toMapCoords()` already exists.
- Colour ramp for arrow magnitude → reuses the existing `SWMM2DResultsLayer` inundation-ramp utility with a different range and ramp choice.

##### Risks / open questions

1. **HDF5 chunk shape for flux reads** — `/Mesh2_edge_flux` chunks were sized for write throughput; single-frame reads may straddle chunks. Acceptable now; revisit if `readEdgeFluxAt` shows up in profiling.
2. **Wet/dry-front flux spikes** — `qₑ = flux / length` can blow up near drying edges. Clamp `|qₑ| ≤ 10 m/s` before the RT0 solve.
3. **CRS for streamline integration** — assumes projected CRS (Slice AU enforces this at mesh build). Refuses Streamline in geographic CRS with a status-bar message; Polyline still works.
4. **Paint cost at scale** — arrow paint walks all triangles. Viewport culling + magnitude threshold + zoom-based decimation for meshes ≫ 100k tris.
5. **Older engines / older `.h5`** — every new symbol gated via `QLibrary::resolve`; reader falls back to vertex-derived edge geometry. Velocity toggle hides itself with a tooltip when the engine lacks the API. Polyline path profile still works on depth-only data.
6. **`ProfilePlotWidget` refactor scope** — the data-provider extraction must not regress 1D rendering. Mitigation: land CF.2.6 in two steps — first adapt `ProfileBuilder::SourceDerived` to the new shim (verify 1D suite stays green), then add the 2D adapter.

#### ⏳ Slice CF.3 — Per-cell 2D mesh time-series plotting (drafted 2026-05-21)

Lands the per-cell time-series that Slice CF (Phase 9.9) lists as a roadmap seam ("future engine surface for 2D overland flow time-series") and that CF.MVP explicitly defers. The deliverable is **single-click / box-select / lasso-select on the 2D mesh → open the Slice AT/BL `ComparisonPlotDialog` with one row per attribute (Depth, HGL/WSE, |V|, Vx, Vy) and one series per selected cell**. Nothing in the existing AT/BL plot surface changes shape; CF.3 is an additive extension of the same model.

##### Goals (user-stated, 2026-05-21)

1. **Per-cell time-series** on the 2D mesh for **Depth**, **HGL/WSE**, **|V| (magnitude)**, **Vx**, **Vy**.
2. **Box / lasso selection** of multiple cells; all selected cells plot together on the same attribute row.
3. **Reuse Slice AT/BL plot infrastructure** verbatim — `ComparisonPlotDialog`, `ComparisonPlotModel`, `SeriesStyle`, calendar X axis, animation cursor, 1v1 scatter when ≥2 runs are loaded.
4. **Single canonical time-series surface** in the GUI — after CF.3, nodes / links / subcatchments / 2D mesh cells all plot through the same dialog.
5. **Lands after CF.2** so velocity attributes work from day one (depth + HGL + |V| + Vx + Vy all live on first ship). HGL is computed GUI-side as `depth + z_bed` (no engine change required for HGL).

##### Architecture — additive to AT/BL

**`PlotAttribute` extension** (`include/plot/plotattribute.h`). Five new enumerators:

```cpp
enum class PlotAttribute {
    // … existing 1D attrs …
    Mesh2DDepth,        // m  (US: ft)
    Mesh2DHGL,          // m  (US: ft)  — HGL = depth + z_bed, GUI-computed
    Mesh2DVelocityMag,  // m/s (US: ft/s)
    Mesh2DVelocityX,    // m/s — projected map CRS (Vx positive east)
    Mesh2DVelocityY,    // m/s — projected map CRS (Vy positive north)
};
```

`PlotAttribute::units(UnitSystem)` returns the correct unit per attribute so the existing per-row Y-axis logic in AT keeps working. **2D depth and 1D node depth are intentionally different `PlotAttribute` values** — they share units but live on separate rows; mixing them would conflate two physically different quantities (node free-surface depth vs cell-averaged surface water depth).

**`SeriesSpec::objectRef` extension** (`include/plot/comparisonplotmodel.h`). The opaque `ObjectRef` discriminator gains a new kind:

```cpp
struct Mesh2DCellRef {
    SWMM2DResultsLayer* layer;  // run identity = layer's parent RunSource
    int triIdx;                 // triangle index in the layer's mesh
};
```

Series resolution dispatches on the discriminator. Code paths that don't know about mesh cells (the 1D `.out` resolver, the observed-CSV resolver) are untouched.

**`RunSource` extension** (`include/plot/comparisonplotmodel.h`). BL defines `RunSource { SWMMResultsLayer*; QString; bool; SeriesStyle; }`. CF.3 makes `layer` polymorphic over `SWMMResultsLayer*` and `SWMM2DResultsLayer*` via a small `IRunLayer` interface (the only methods AT/BL call on it are `scenarioName()` / `getSeriesAt(ObjectRef, PlotAttribute, ...)`, so the surface stays tiny). The "Add Series" dialog's "From open layers" tab lists both 1D and 2D layers; picking a 2D layer surfaces a mesh-cell picker (or accepts a triIdx list passed in from the canvas tool).

##### Series-read paths (per attribute)

`SWMM2DResultsLayer::getSeriesAt(Mesh2DCellRef ref, PlotAttribute attr, std::vector<double>& t_julian, std::vector<double>& y)` dispatches to the underlying `IMesh2DSource`:

| Attribute | `HDF5Mesh2DSource` path | `EngineMesh2DSource` path (live) |
|-----------|-------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `Mesh2DDepth` | `Mesh2DH5Reader::readCellDepthSeries(triIdx)` — hyperslab `/Mesh2_face_depth[:, triIdx]`. | Accumulated `pushDepths` tick buffer at `tris[triIdx]` across all received ticks. |
| `Mesh2DHGL` | `readCellDepthSeries(triIdx) + z_bed[triIdx]`. `z_bed` cached on layer construction from `/Mesh2_node_z` + `/Mesh2_face_nodes` (mean of three vertex z's per triangle). | Same: live depth tick + cached `z_bed`. |
| `Mesh2DVelocityMag` | `readCellVelocitySeries(triIdx)` (new — see below) → `(Vx[t], Vy[t])`, magnitude via `sqrt(Vx² + Vy²)`. | Same RT0 reconstruction per tick using cached edge geometry + buffered `pushFlux` ticks. |
| `Mesh2DVelocityX` | `readCellVelocitySeries` → `Vx[t]`. | Same. |
| `Mesh2DVelocityY` | `readCellVelocitySeries` → `Vy[t]`. | Same. |

**`Mesh2DH5Reader::readCellVelocitySeries`** (new — extends CF.2.2's `readEdgeFluxAt`). Reads three edge-flux columns `/Mesh2_edge_flux[:, triIdx, 0..2]` plus the cached edge geometry from CF.2.2 (`length`, `nx`, `ny`). For each time step, runs the same closed-form RT0 inversion CF.2.3 uses for the per-tick arrow field. Cost: 3 hyperslab reads + N×(2x2 normal-equations solve) per selected cell — trivial vs. the per-tick all-cells path. Same wet/dry-front clamp `|qₑ| ≤ 10 m/s` as CF.2.3.

##### Canvas tool — `MapToolPick2DCells` (box + lasso)

New `OpenSWMMVisMapTool` subclass (`include/map/tools/maptoolpick2dcells.{h,cpp}`).

```cpp
class MapToolPick2DCells : public OpenSWMMVisMapTool {
public:
    enum class Mode { Box, Lasso };
    void setMode(Mode m);
    void mousePressEvent(QMouseEvent*) override;
    void mouseMoveEvent(QMouseEvent*) override;
    void mouseReleaseEvent(QMouseEvent*) override;
    void mouseDoubleClickEvent(QMouseEvent*) override;  // lasso close
    void keyPressEvent(QKeyEvent*) override;            // Esc cancels, B/L swap modes
    void paint(QPainter*) override;                     // rubber band
signals:
    void cellsPicked(SWMM2DResultsLayer* layer, QVector<int> triIdxList);
};
```

**Box mode** mirrors the existing rubber-band logic in `MapToolSelect` (Slice W.7). On release, calls `SWMM2DResultsLayer::pickCellsInRect(QRectF mapRect)` which walks `m_sceneTris`, tests centroid-in-rect (fast path), and returns the matching `triIdx` list. **Lasso mode** mirrors `MapToolAddSubcatchment`'s polygon state machine — left-click adds vertices, double-click closes, Escape cancels. Hit test: `SWMM2DResultsLayer::pickCellsInPolygon(QPolygonF mapPoly)` — centroid-in-polygon via the existing `QPolygonF::containsPoint(Qt::OddEvenFill)`. Single-click defaults to single-cell pick (degenerate rect of one pixel).

Toolbar gets a checkable **Pick 2D Cells** action sibling to **Pick 2D Path** from CF.2.5. Hot-keys: `B` / `L` swap modes while active.

##### Plot entry points

`src/swmmvis.cpp` gains `openComparisonPlotForCells(SWMM2DResultsLayer* layer, QVector<int> triIdxList)`. The function pops a small companion popover with checkboxes for the five attributes (Depth on by default; user can tick HGL, |V|, Vx, Vy); on OK, it constructs `triIdxList.size() × selectedAttrCount` `SeriesSpec`s, finds-or-creates the AT/BL `ComparisonPlotDialog`, calls `addSeries(spec)` for each, and shows the dialog. Existing AT/BL behavior handles row creation and styling cycle.

`MapToolPick2DCells::cellsPicked` is wired in `swmmvis.cpp` (near the existing `MapToolPick2DPath::pathPicked` wiring) to `openComparisonPlotForCells`.

Object-Browser / Layer-Tree context menu on the `SWMM2DResultsLayer` row adds **Plot Time Series at Selected Cells…** (uses the layer's persisted highlight set from a prior pick). Canvas right-click on a single mesh cell adds **Plot Time Series at This Cell…** (single-element `triIdxList`).

##### Selection persistence + plot↔canvas hover sync

`SWMM2DResultsLayer::highlightCells(QSet<int> triIdxSet)` stores the picked set and paints the selected triangles with a thin outline (re-uses the existing `SceneTri` paint loop; selection rendered as a second-pass overlay so it doesn't disturb the depth ramp). The selection persists across re-runs of the same project until cleared.

Plot↔canvas hover sync: the dialog already has a `pointHovered(rowIdx, seriesIdx, timeIdx)` signal. CF.3 maps `seriesIdx → triIdx` and emits a new `SWMM2DResultsLayer::cellHovered(triIdx)` that the layer paints with a contrasting outline — symmetric with the 1D plot's hover-highlight-on-canvas wiring already in BL.

##### Behaviour edge cases

- **Live mode, no buffered ticks yet.** Series for a newly-picked cell renders empty until the first tick fires (same as AT's `timeCount()` growing behaviour). Dialog shows a small spinner per empty series.
- **Older `.h5` without `/Mesh2_edge_flux`.** CF.3 hard-depends on CF.2 (per the slice index "Depends on" column), so older files are out of scope. If the user opens such a file with CF.3 installed, velocity attribute checkboxes in the popover are disabled with the tooltip "Edge flux not present in this `.h5` — re-run with current engine to enable velocity time-series." Depth + HGL still work.
- **Dry cells.** Depth = 0 (and HGL = z_bed) renders as a flat line. Velocity reconstruction skips the cell (returns NaN for that timestep), drawn as a gap.
- **Box-pick that lands on no cells.** Status bar message; no dialog opens.
- **Big selection (≥500 cells).** Confirmation prompt — "Plot N cell series? This may be slow." Threshold configurable via `PreferencesManager::mesh2dCellSelectionWarnThreshold` (default 500). RT0 cost is per-cell-per-tick; 500 cells × 8640 timesteps ≈ 4.3M RT0 inversions, on the order of seconds.
- **`.oswp` round-trip.** Highlight set + open plot dialogs restored — same persistence path AT/BL uses for 1D plots, plus the new 2D mesh selection (Slice X infrastructure).

##### Verification

1. **Synthetic build green** — `cmake --build build/darwin-debug --target SWMMVis`.
2. **Unit — picker** — `tests/gui/test_maptoolpick2dcells.cpp` — given a 3x3 grid of triangles, a box around 4 of them picks exactly those 4; a lasso around a diagonal picks the diagonal cells.
3. **Unit — reader** — `tests/gui/test_mesh2dh5reader_cell_series.cpp` — `readCellDepthSeries(triIdx)` returns the same column as `numpy.array(h5['/Mesh2_face_depth'][:, triIdx])`; HGL path = depth column + z_bed gives the same result whether computed in the reader fixture (numpy) or in the layer (cached `z_bed`).
4. **Unit — velocity** — `readCellVelocitySeries` on the test fixture produces `(Vx, Vy)` matching a hand-computed RT0 inversion to 1e-6.
5. **Unit — model wiring** — `tests/gui/test_comparisonplot_mesh2d.cpp` — wire `HDF5Mesh2DSource` to a fresh `ComparisonPlotDialog`, add 2 cells × 3 attributes (Depth, HGL, |V|); 3 rows × 2 series each appear; animation cursor moves through them.
6. **Manual — snoopy demo, box** — open `examples/demo_snoopy_lagoon/snoopy.inp`, run, finish; drag-box across the wet patch → dialog opens with Depth row containing N series; tick HGL + |V| → two more rows appear.
7. **Manual — snoopy demo, lasso** — `L` swaps to lasso, drag polygon around a curved wet front; same dialog opens.
8. **Manual — single cell** — right-click one wet cell → **Plot Time Series at This Cell…** → dialog opens with one series per ticked attribute.
9. **Manual — live** — run a fresh project, drag-box during the run; dialog opens, series grow tick-by-tick as `twoDDepthsAvailable` / `twoDFluxAvailable` fire.
10. **Manual — 1v1 scatter** — open a second project window with a perturbed bowl, drag-add same triIdx range from Run B → column-1 scatter appears with 45° dashed and NSE label.
11. **Manual — `.oswp` round-trip** — close project with the dialog open, re-open → highlight set + dialog restored with same series.
12. **Manual — hover sync** — hover a point in the Depth chart → corresponding cell outline brightens on the map.

##### Reused, not reinvented

- Plot rendering (axes, calendar X, animation cursor, 1v1 scatter, per-series styling) — `ComparisonPlotDialog` from AT/BL, **no fork**.
- `IMesh2DSource` switching (engine live → HDF5 post-run) — CF.MVP's existing dual-source architecture.
- Edge flux + edge geometry HDF5 datasets — written by CF.2.1, read by CF.2.2.
- RT0 client-side velocity reconstruction — CF.2.3 (the same code path, run only on the selected cells per timestep).
- Rubber-band drag rendering — `MapToolSelect` W.7.
- Polygon state machine for lasso — `MapToolAddSubcatchment`.
- `.oswp` series + selection persistence — Slice X.

- **Depends on** BL (AT delivery — must be in place for `ComparisonPlotDialog` to exist).

### ⏳ Slice CU — Terrain Toolbar: active DTM, Z readout, node/link invert estimation (Phase 6.2 companion)

When a Digital Terrain Model (DTM) raster is loaded the user needs a lightweight way to designate it as the "active terrain" for the editing session and have the application assist with invert elevations. CU delivers a dedicated **Terrain Toolbar** that: (a) exposes the active terrain picker; (b) streams terrain Z values into the status-bar coordinate display on mouse move; (c) auto-fills node `InvertElev` = terrain Z + node offset when a node is placed; (d) auto-fills link endpoint invert offsets and estimates the slope when a pipe or channel is drawn.

#### Phase CU.1 — `TerrainToolbar` widget

New `TerrainToolbar` (`include/ui/toolbars/terraintoolbar.h`) inherits `QToolBar`. Contains:

- **Active terrain `QComboBox`** (`m_terrainCombo`) — populated with the display name of every `GISRasterLayer` currently in `LayerManager`; a leading `"(none)"` entry makes it optional. Connects to `LayerManager::layerAdded` / `layerRemoved` to stay in sync. When the active window changes (`onActiveSubWindowChanged`), the combo is rebound to the per-project selection.
- **Node offset `QDoubleSpinBox`** (`m_nodeOffsetSpin`) — label `"Node offset:"`, range −100.0 to +100.0 in model vertical units (`UnitSystem::elevationUnit()`), default 0.0. Tooltip: "Invert elevation = terrain Z + offset (use a negative value to place the invert below ground)."
- **Link offset `QDoubleSpinBox`** (`m_linkOffsetSpin`) — label `"Link offset:"`, same range/default. Applied identically to both endpoints of a newly drawn link.
- Unit labels (`QLabel`) after each spinbox reflect `UnitSystem::elevationUnitLabel()` and refresh on `UnitSystem::unitsChanged`.

`TerrainToolbar` emits:
- `activeTerrainChanged(GISRasterLayer*)` — null when "(none)".
- `nodeOffsetChanged(double)`.
- `linkOffsetChanged(double)`.

**Files**: new `include/ui/toolbars/terraintoolbar.h`, `src/ui/toolbars/terraintoolbar.cpp`; touches `src/swmmvis.cpp` (add toolbar, connect signals), `src/swmmvis.ui` (toolbar slot).

#### Phase CU.2 — Terrain Z readout in coordinate display

`MapCanvas` (or its parent `SWMMVisProjectWindow`) already emits `coordinatesChanged(QPointF mapPt)` on every mouse move that drives the status-bar `X / Y` labels.

Extend the pipeline:

1. `SWMMVisProjectWindow` holds a `GISRasterLayer* m_activeTerrain` (set from `TerrainToolbar::activeTerrainChanged`).
2. In the `mouseMoveEvent` (or `coordinatesChanged` handler), if `m_activeTerrain` is non-null, call a new `TerrainSampler::sampleBilinear(GISRasterLayer*, QPointF mapCrs) -> std::optional<double>`.
3. `TerrainSampler` uses `GDALRasterBand::RasterIO` with a 1×1 window and bilinear resampling. Returns `std::nullopt` when the point is outside the raster extent or hits the NoData value.
4. Status-bar coordinate label extended: `"X: %.3f  Y: %.3f"` → `"X: %.3f  Y: %.3f  Z: %.3f <unit>"` when Z is available, or `"X: %.3f  Y: %.3f  Z: —"` when out-of-extent/NoData.

`TerrainSampler` is a pure static helper — no `Q_OBJECT`, no state — reusing the GDAL handle already held by `GISRasterLayer` (no extra file open).

**Files**: new `include/core/terrainsampler.h`, `src/core/terrainsampler.cpp`; touches `src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp` (coordinate update slot), `src/swmmvis.cpp` (wire `activeTerrainChanged` → `m_activeTerrain`).

#### Phase CU.3 — Node invert elevation from terrain

`MapToolAddNode::mouseReleaseEvent` currently creates a node at cursor position and prompts (or directly commits) with default `InvertElev = 0.0`.

Change: after the click position is finalized, if an active terrain is set:

```cpp
double z;
if (TerrainSampler::sampleBilinear(activeTerrain, clickPt, &z))
    proposedInvertElev = z + nodeOffset;   // nodeOffset is typically ≤ 0
```

`proposedInvertElev` is passed as the pre-filled default to the node-creation flow (property dialog or inline commit). If sampling fails (NoData / out of extent), fall back to the current default (0.0 or the model default invert from `PreferencesManager`).

No engine API change required — `swmm_node_set_invert_elev` (or equivalent existing setter) is called as normal.

**Files**: touches `src/map/maptooladdnode.cpp`; reads `TerrainSampler` + `TerrainToolbar` state via a thin `ITerrainContext` interface on `SWMMVisProjectWindow` (avoids circular header dependency).

#### Phase CU.4 — Link invert offset + slope estimation

`MapToolAddLink` places a link between two nodes. After the link geometry is confirmed:

1. Sample terrain Z at each endpoint node position: `Z_from`, `Z_to`.
2. Compute invert at each end: `inv_from = Z_from + linkOffset`, `inv_to = Z_to + linkOffset`.
3. Derive slope: `slope = (inv_from − inv_to) / linkLength` (positive = downhill from → to).
4. If the link type supports `offset1` / `offset2` (conduits, channels): set them relative to the node invert elevations produced in Phase CU.3 (if those nodes were also placed with terrain assistance) or from the raw terrain Z if nodes pre-existed.
5. If either endpoint sampling fails, no auto-fill for that endpoint.

For links drawn to pre-existing nodes whose `InvertElev` was not terrain-derived, the offset defaults remain 0.0 (preserving existing behavior).

**Files**: touches `src/map/maptooladdlink.cpp`; same `ITerrainContext` accessor.

#### Phase CU.5 — Persistence

Per-project terrain state stored in `.oswp` session JSON under a `"terrain"` key:

```json
"terrain": {
  "activeLayerPath": "relative/path/to/dem.tif",
  "nodeOffsetM": -1.5,
  "linkOffsetM": -1.0
}
```

`ProjectSerializer` serializes / restores on save / open. On restore: match `activeLayerPath` against currently loaded layers; if not found, set to "(none)" and emit a warning to the message log.

`PreferencesManager` gets two new app-wide default accessors: `terrain/defaultNodeOffsetM` (0.0), `terrain/defaultLinkOffsetM` (0.0). No `activeLayerPath` default — always starts as `(none)` per session.

**Files**: touches `src/project/projectserializer.cpp`, `include/core/preferencesmanager.h` + `.cpp`.

#### Phase CU.6 — Tests

`tests/gui/test_terraintoolbar.cpp` (6 cases):
- Combo starts with "(none)"; adding a `GISRasterLayer` mock appends it.
- Removing the active layer resets combo to "(none)" and emits `activeTerrainChanged(nullptr)`.
- Unit-label updates when `UnitSystem::unitsChanged`.
- `nodeOffsetChanged` fires on spinbox change.
- Per-project rebind: switching active window restores previously saved combo index.
- `.oswp` round-trip: save with offset −1.5, reload, spinbox reads −1.5.

`tests/gui/test_terrainsampler.cpp` (6 cases):
- Point at centre of synthetic 3×3 raster → correct bilinear value.
- Point outside extent → `std::nullopt`.
- NoData cell → `std::nullopt`.
- Bilinear interpolation at mid-cell.
- Unit conversion: metre raster, feet project → value scaled correctly.
- Thread-safety: two concurrent calls return consistent results (GDAL handle shared read-only).

#### Summary

- **Files**: new `include/ui/toolbars/terraintoolbar.h`, `src/ui/toolbars/terraintoolbar.cpp`, `include/core/terrainsampler.h`, `src/core/terrainsampler.cpp`; touches `src/map/maptooladdnode.cpp`, `src/map/maptooladdlink.cpp`, `src/swmmvis.cpp`, `src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp`, `src/project/projectserializer.cpp`, `include/core/preferencesmanager.h`, `src/core/preferencesmanager.cpp`.

### ⏳ Slice CV — Edit Session Toggle: explicit editing gate in the editing toolbar

The current design allows vertex editing to begin on any double-click of a selected element, with no explicit user intent required. This creates a risk of accidental geometry modifications when the user is simply trying to inspect the model. Slice CV reintroduces a dedicated **Edit Session** toggle as the first button in the editing toolbar, providing a clear intentional gate before any destructive geometry operation can occur.

#### Phase CV.1 — `actionEditSession` in the UI

Add a new **checkable** `QAction` named `actionEditSession` to `forms/swmmvis.ui`:

- **Icon**: `:/swmmvis/SelectEdit` (`resources/images/select_edit.svg` — cursor with edit pencil, already registered in `swmmvis.qrc`)
- **Text**: `"Edit"`
- **Tooltip**: `"Toggle editing session — must be active to create or modify network geometry"`
- **Checkable**: `true`

Insert as the **first action** in `toolBarEdit`, followed by a separator, ahead of all creation tools (Add Junction, Add Conduit, etc.).

#### Phase CV.2 — Edit-session state on `SWMMVisProjectWindow`

In `include/swmmvisprojectwindow.h`:
```cpp
bool m_editSessionActive = false;
bool isEditSessionActive() const { return m_editSessionActive; }
void setEditSessionActive(bool active);
signals:
    void editSessionChanged(bool active);
```

In `src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp`, `setEditSessionActive`:
- Sets `m_editSessionActive`
- Emits `editSessionChanged(active)`
- No tool-level propagation needed — gating happens at the event-handler level (Phase CV.3, CV.4)

#### Phase CV.3 — Gate double-click vertex editing in `maptoolselect.cpp`

In `OpenSWMMVisMapToolSelect::mouseDoubleClickEvent` (currently line ~1206 of `src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp`):

```cpp
// Early-out if no edit session is active on the parent project window.
if (auto *pw = qobject_cast<SWMMVisProjectWindow *>(m_canvas ? m_canvas->parent() : nullptr))
    if (!pw->isEditSessionActive()) return;
```

This single guard is sufficient — the remainder of the method is unchanged.

#### Phase CV.4 — Gate creation and geometry tools in `swmmvis.cpp`

Collect all edit-only actions into a helper list (in `src/swmmvis.cpp`):
```cpp
QList<QAction*> editSessionActions() const;
// Returns: actionAddJunction, actionAddConduit, actionMoveNode,
//          actionEditVertex, actionDeleteSelected, etc.
```

Connect `actionEditSession::toggled(bool)` to:
1. `activeProjectWindow()->setEditSessionActive(bool)` — sets the flag
2. `for (auto *a : editSessionActions()) a->setEnabled(active)` — enable/disable actions

On `onActiveSubWindowChanged`:
- Sync `actionEditSession->setChecked(pw ? pw->isEditSessionActive() : false)`
- Sync enable/disable of all edit-session actions to match the incoming window's state
- Disable `actionEditSession` itself when `pw == nullptr`

#### Phase CV.5 — Tests

- `tests/gui/test_editsession.cpp`:
  - Edit session off → double-click does not enter vertex edit mode
  - Edit session on → double-click enters vertex edit mode as before
  - Edit session off → creation tool actions are disabled
  - Edit session on → creation tool actions are enabled
  - Window switch → `actionEditSession` reflects the incoming window's state

#### Summary

- **Files**: `forms/swmmvis.ui`, `include/swmmvisprojectwindow.h`, `src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp`, `src/map/tools/maptoolselect.cpp`, `src/swmmvis.cpp`
- **Icon**: existing `:/swmmvis/SelectEdit` (no new assets)
- **Default state**: OFF — model opens in read-only/inspect mode; user must explicitly click Edit to modify geometry
- **Behaviour preserved**: within an active session, double-click vertex editing works exactly as today
