## §M — INP-as-Source-of-Truth Hydration Contract (APPROVED 2026-05-21)

> **Status:** approved. Formalises a contract that is already honoured in code across Slices **B** (Phases 0.5 / 0.6), **U.4**, **W.9**, and **G-1**, but had never been stated as a single invariant. Slice **CX** (defined below) ships the regression test that locks the contract against future regressions and catches any new control that bypasses it.

### §M.0 Why this section exists

The Simulation Options dialog and the status-bar selections are the two surfaces where users **see** what the active `.inp` says. When either surface shows stale or wrong values — a status-bar Flow Units combo that still reads `CFS` after switching to a tab whose engine reports `CMS`, or an Options dialog tab mirroring a snapshot taken at construction rather than the active project's engine — users edit the wrong project and lose work. The contract below makes the hydration source unambiguous, the trigger points exhaustive, and the audit list closed.

### §M.1 The invariant

Every GUI control whose **source-of-truth is a SWMM `[OPTIONS]` key** (read via `swmm_options_get`) **must** hydrate from the active project's engine at all three of these moments:

1. **Project open** — `SWMMVisProjectWindow::loadModel` returns success (both `File → Open` of an existing `.inp` and `File → New` synthetic-`.inp` paths). `SWMMVis::openSingleINP` nulls `mActiveProjectWindow` and then re-invokes `onActiveSubWindowChanged(window)` after `loadModel` to satisfy this trigger; the null is required because `addSubWindow` / `setActiveSubWindow` can fire `subWindowActivated` before `loadModel` finishes, which would otherwise leave the same-project guard tripping the re-call. See the openSingleINP post-load block.
2. **Tab activation** — `SWMMVis::onActiveSubWindowChanged` fires with a `SWMMVisProjectWindow*` and the active project pointer actually changes (the same-project guard skips redundant re-syncs during routine focus shuffles).
3. **External mutation** — `SWMMModelLayer::optionsChanged(keys)` fires for any key the control depends on. Covers Simulation Options dialog writes, scripted edits, and any future MVC-bridge writer.

Controls **must not** hold a local cache that survives across project switches without an explicit re-read. Per-control `QSignalBlocker` is required around the hydration write so the round-trip does not bounce back to the engine.

### §M.2 In-scope controls

**Status bar** (owned by `SWMMVis`, set up in the `setupStatusBar` block of `swmmvis.cpp`):

| Widget                  | Source-of-truth                  | Today's sync path                                                                                |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Flow Units combo        | `FLOW_UNITS`                     | `UnitSystem::setActiveProject` + `syncFromEngine` + `optionsChanged({FLOW_UNITS})` MVC bridge    |
| Offset Mode checkbox    | `LINK_OFFSETS`                   | `SWMMVisProjectWindow::reloadElevationOffsetModeFromEngine` + `optionsChanged({LINK_OFFSETS})`   |
| CRS button              | layer SRS (proxy for `[MAP]` / `[PROJECTION]`) | `MapCanvas::canvasSRSChanged`                                                      |
| Map Scale combo         | canvas extent (derived)          | `MapCanvas::scaleChanged`                                                                        |

**Simulation Options dialog** (`SimulationOptionsDialog`, constructed fresh per `onSimulationOptions` against the active project's engine — dialog opens automatically satisfy trigger 1):

| Tab                     | Read helper                                                                                  |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Title / Notes           | `readFromEngine` (TITLE) + `m_projectWindow` notes HTML                                      |
| Models / Processes      | `readFromEngine` (INFILTRATION, FLOW_ROUTING, IGNORE_*, ALLOW_PONDING)                       |
| Dates & Times + Events  | `readFromEngine` + `readEventsFromEngine` (Slice CW)                                         |
| Routing & Hydraulics    | `readFromEngine` (SURCHARGE_METHOD, DPS_*, MAX_TRIALS, …)                                    |
| System / Performance    | `readFromEngine` (THREADS)                                                                   |
| Spatial & CRS           | `refreshSpatialSummary` (reads layer SRS + extent)                                           |
| 2D Surface Routing      | `read2DFromEngine` (when `OPENSWMM_HAS_2D`)                                                  |
| Files / Plugins         | `readFilesSectionFromEngine` + `readPluginsFromEngine` + `readWriterCombosFromEngine` + `readOutputPathsFromSettings` |

### §M.3 Out-of-scope controls (explicit exclusions)

- **Engine Version combo** — project metadata (which engine binary to run), not an `[OPTIONS]` key.
- **Auto-Length checkbox** — GUI edit-behaviour preference (`PreferencesManager::autoLengthEnabled` + per-project override), not an `[OPTIONS]` key.
- **Coordinates readout** — live cursor position; no stored value.
- **Progress bar** — live simulation state; no stored value.

If a future slice promotes Auto-Length to an engine-side key (e.g. via `[USER_FLAGS]`), this section is updated.

### §M.4 Implementation status today (post-Slice CX audit, post-engine ABI patch 2026-05-22)

| Trigger                  | Flow Units | Offset Mode | CRS button | Map Scale | Options dialog (any tab) |
|--------------------------|------------|-------------|------------|-----------|--------------------------|
| Project open (loadModel) | ✅ (fixed by CX.4) | ✅ (engine + CX.4) | ✅ (fixed by CX.4) | ✅ (fixed by CX.4) | n/a — dialog not yet open |
| Tab activation           | ✅         | ✅          | ✅         | ✅        | n/a — dialog not yet open |
| External mutation        | ✅         | ✅          | ✅ (via `canvasSRSChanged`) | ✅ (via `scaleChanged`) | ✅ — dialog re-reads on `onApply` |
| Dialog construction      | n/a        | n/a         | n/a        | n/a       | ✅ `readFromEngine` in ctor |

**Three real gaps were found and fixed by Slice CX Phase CX.4.** All three matched the user-reported symptom that opening a new SWMM project or `.inp` did not refresh status-bar selections to reflect the new project's options.

1. **GUI: same-project guard blocked post-`loadModel` hydration** — the project-open path in `SWMMVis::openSingleINP` re-invoked `onActiveSubWindowChanged(window)` after `loadModel` returned, intending to hydrate status-bar widgets from the now-loaded engine, but the same-project guard inside `onActiveSubWindowChanged` blocked the re-call because `addSubWindow` / `setActiveSubWindow` had already set `mActiveProjectWindow = window` during a prior `subWindowActivated` event. **Fix:** null `mActiveProjectWindow` immediately before the explicit re-call so the guard does not fire (1-line surgical change in `src/swmmvis.cpp`).

2. **Engine: `swmm_options_get` returned ints, GUI expected tokens** — for `FLOW_UNITS` and `FLOW_ROUTING`, the engine returned the underlying enum int as a string (e.g. `"3"` for CMS) but the GUI's `UnitSystem::syncFromEngine` and `SimulationOptionsDialog::readFromEngine` only matched token strings (`"CMS"`, `"DYNWAVE"`, …). On any non-CFS / non-default model, the GUI silently kept its constructor default. **Fix:** engine `swmm_options_get` now returns canonical tokens, matching the symmetric encoding `swmm_options_set` already accepted. Docstring in `include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_model.h` updated to declare the encoding-symmetry contract.

3. **Engine: `LINK_OFFSETS` was not a recognised key** — both `swmm_options_set` and `swmm_options_get` fell through to `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM`. The GUI's `SWMMVisProjectWindow::setElevationOffsetMode` write was silently dropped; `reloadElevationOffsetModeFromEngine` silently failed to update. The status-bar Offset Mode toggle was decorative — it never persisted or hydrated. **Fix:** engine `swmm_options_set` / `_get` now handle `LINK_OFFSETS` with `"DEPTH"` / `"ELEVATION"` tokens (legacy `DEPTH_OFFSET` / `ELEV_OFFSET` aliases and numeric `"0"` / `"1"` accepted on input for compatibility).

All three fixes verified end-to-end by `tests/gui/test_options_hydration_contract.cpp` — 7/7 cases passing on the user's macOS / Qt 6.10.2 build (2026-05-22).

### §M.5 Forward-looking application

When the editors landing in Slices **BN–BU** (per-object property editors), **BV** (Files / Output / Plugins), and any future editor bring new INP-derived controls online, each new control must wire into §M.1 before its slice closes. The slice author is responsible for: (a) listing the OPTIONS / section keys the new control reads, (b) demonstrating hydration at all three triggers via a test case, (c) registering the control in the audit list in §M.2 with a `git grep`-able anchor.

### 🔧 Slice CX — INP-as-source-of-truth hydration audit (APPROVED 2026-05-21)

**Goal:** prove every in-scope control (§M.2) satisfies §M.1 at all three triggers, and add a regression test that catches new controls that bypass the contract. **Expected outcome: all-green against today's code; if the audit surfaces a gap, the fix lands in this slice rather than as a follow-up.**

#### Phase CX.1 — Status-bar audit harness

- New leaf test `tests/gui/test_options_hydration_contract.cpp` enumerates the §M.2 status-bar table programmatically (control name → OPTIONS key → engine getter). For each row, the test:
  1. Opens project A (synthetic `.inp` with key value X), asserts the status-bar widget reflects X.
  2. Opens project B (synthetic `.inp` with key value Y) in a second MDI subwindow, asserts the status-bar widget flipped to Y.
  3. Tab-switches back to A, asserts the widget flipped back to X.
  4. Calls `SWMMModelLayer::setOption(key, Z)` on the active project, asserts the widget reflects Z without re-opening any dialog.
- Synthetic `.inp` content is built inline via `swmm_options_set` after `swmm_engine_open` on an empty model — no fixture files needed.
- Initial cut focuses on `UnitSystem` (the in-process model for FLOW_UNITS) so the harness can ship as a self-contained leaf test in the same shape as `test_unitsystemfacade.cpp`. The full multi-MDI status-bar walk lands when the `swmmvis_core` static-lib extraction unblocks `SWMMVis`-instantiating tests (tracked in the parked-tests comment in `tests/gui/CMakeLists.txt`).

#### Phase CX.2 — Dialog-tab read-helper audit

- For each `read*FromEngine` helper in §M.2's dialog table, add an assertion in `tests/gui/test_simulationoptionsdialog.cpp` that opens the dialog twice against two engines with differing values and confirms each tab's controls flipped. Existing dialog tests cover Tabs 1, 2, 7 + Events; CX extends to Tabs 0, 3, 4, 5, 6. **Estimated +12 cases — lands when the dialog test target is re-enabled (currently parked alongside the `swmmvis_core` extraction).**

#### Phase CX.3 — Audit-list maintenance

- The §M.2 control table is mirrored as a `static constexpr` array in `include/ui/swmmvis_hydration_audit.h`. The Phase CX.1 test iterates this array. A small build-time assertion confirms every entry resolves to a real `SWMMVis` widget member and a real `SWMMVisProjectWindow` / `UnitSystem` getter, so a new widget cannot bypass the audit by silently omitting itself.

#### Phase CX.4 — Fix-on-fail

- If any Phase CX.1 / CX.2 assertion fails, the fix lands in this slice. Typical fixes are missed `optionsChanged` subscriptions, a missed re-sync in the same-project guard inside `onActiveSubWindowChanged`, or an engine ABI gap that breaks the GUI/engine contract. Each fix gets a failing-then-passing assertion before the fix lands.

- **Landed — gap 1 (GUI: same-project guard):** the explicit `onActiveSubWindowChanged(window)` re-call in `openSingleINP` after `loadModel` was being blocked by the same-project guard because a prior `subWindowActivated` event had already set `mActiveProjectWindow = window`. Status-bar widgets therefore reflected pre-load defaults on every fresh project open. **Fix:** null `mActiveProjectWindow` before the explicit re-call (single-line surgical change in `src/swmmvis.cpp` `openSingleINP` post-load block). End-to-end multi-MDI regression test is parked under the `swmmvis_core` extraction blocker; documented inline in `tests/gui/test_options_hydration_contract.cpp` as a known follow-up so it cannot be lost.

- **Landed — gap 2 (engine: asymmetric FLOW_UNITS / FLOW_ROUTING encoding):** `swmm_options_get` returned `std::to_string(static_cast<int>(opt.flow_units))` (e.g. `"3"` for CMS) but `swmm_options_set` accepted token strings (e.g. `"CMS"`). The GUI parsed only tokens, so on any non-CFS / non-default model the hydration silently failed. **Fix in `openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_model_impl.cpp`:** `swmm_options_get` now returns canonical tokens for FLOW_UNITS and FLOW_ROUTING; `include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_model.h` docstring updated to declare the encoding-symmetry contract. Blast-radius audit before patch: no engine tests asserted on the old int-string format; Python bindings are a thin pass-through and the published `python/README.md` already documented tokens.

- **Landed — gap 3 (engine: LINK_OFFSETS missing from the OPTIONS switch):** both `swmm_options_set` and `swmm_options_get` fell through to `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM` because LINK_OFFSETS was not in the recognised key list. **Fix in `openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_model_impl.cpp`:** added LINK_OFFSETS to both switches — accepts `"DEPTH"` / `"ELEVATION"` (plus legacy `DEPTH_OFFSET` / `ELEV_OFFSET` aliases and numeric `"0"` / `"1"` for compatibility) and returns `"DEPTH"` / `"ELEVATION"`.

- **Remaining gaps deferred per user scope decision (2026-05-21):** the user scoped engine ABI work to `LINK_OFFSETS` only. Other keys that the GUI's `SimulationOptionsDialog` and friends pass to `swmm_options_set` / `_get` but the engine's standard switch does not yet handle — `INFILTRATION`, `ALLOW_PONDING`, `SKIP_STEADY_STATE`, `IGNORE_RAINFALL`, `IGNORE_SNOWMELT`, `IGNORE_GROUNDWATER`, `IGNORE_RDII`, `IGNORE_QUALITY`, `IGNORE_ROUTING`, `SURCHARGE_METHOD`, `MAX_TRIALS`, `HEAD_TOLERANCE`, `LAT_FLOW_TOL`, `SYS_FLOW_TOL`, `THREADS`, `MIN_SLOPE`, `MIN_SURFAREA`, `NORMAL_FLOW_LIMITED`, `INERTIAL_DAMPING`, `FORCE_MAIN_EQUATION`, `LENGTHENING_STEP`, `VARIABLE_STEP`, etc. — fall through to `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM` today and the GUI silently uses `SimulationOptions.hpp` constructor defaults. These are pre-existing limitations, not regressions, and were present before Slice CX. Tracked as a follow-up engine API request to be filed under §G once scoped.

### 🔧 Slice CY — Close the §M.4 deferred `swmm_options_get` / `_set` gap (DRAFT 2026-05-22)

**Goal:** make every `[OPTIONS]` key that `SimulationOptionsDialog::readFromEngine` reads via `getOption()` actually round-trip through the engine C API, so an opened `.inp` populates the dialog from its real values instead of `PreferencesManager` defaults. Closes the deferred list called out in §M.4 (the "etc." paragraph), driven by the user-reported symptom: "Start, end and report times for example" still show defaults on dialog open. **No new struct fields, no parser changes** — every key already has typed storage in `SimulationOptions` and is correctly populated by `OptionsHandler::handle_options`. The gap is solely in the C API switch.

#### Phase CY.0 — Why this is a real gap, not a §M.4 footnote

`SimulationOptionsDialog::readFromEngine` calls `getOption("START_DATE")` etc.; `swmm_options_get` returns `SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM` because the switch in `openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_model_impl.cpp` only handles `FLOW_UNITS`, `FLOW_ROUTING` / `ROUTING_MODEL`, `LINK_OFFSETS`, `ROUTING_STEP`, `REPORT_STEP`, `CRS`, and the `RPT_*` family. The dialog's fallback path then resolves to `PreferencesManager::simulationDefaults()`, which is what the user is observing. The keys' actual engine state — already correct in `ctx.options` after `swmm_open` — is simply unreachable from the GUI side.

A secondary bug surfaces in the same pass: `swmm_options_set("START_DATE", "01/01/2004")` today calls `std::stod(v)` and silently writes `1.0` (the leading `01` before the slash) into `opt.start_date`. This is symmetric corruption of the same gap — the dialog never round-trips today, so it's never been hit. CY.3 fixes it.

#### Phase CY.1 — Encoding contract (per-key)

Every entry is symmetric: `get` returns a string that `set` accepts back, byte-identical where practical (whitespace + case-insensitive tokens). Aliases accepted by `set` mirror the `OptionsHandler` parser so legacy `.inp` writers and the GUI agree.

**Tab 2 — Dates & Times + steps**

| Key                   | Storage (SimulationOptions)             | `get` emits          | `set` accepts                                 |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `START_DATE`          | `start_date` (OADate, date+time combined) | `MM/DD/YYYY` (floor of date portion; time portion preserved in storage) | `MM/DD/YYYY` via `datetime::parseDate`; preserves existing time-of-day |
| `START_TIME`          | `start_date` (frac-day portion)         | `HH:MM:SS`           | `HH:MM:SS` or seconds; preserves existing date portion |
| `END_DATE`            | `end_date`                              | `MM/DD/YYYY`         | same                                          |
| `END_TIME`            | `end_date`                              | `HH:MM:SS`           | same                                          |
| `REPORT_START_DATE`   | `report_start`                          | `MM/DD/YYYY`         | same                                          |
| `REPORT_START_TIME`   | `report_start`                          | `HH:MM:SS`           | same                                          |
| `DRY_STEP`            | `dry_step` (seconds)                    | integer seconds      | seconds or `HH:MM:SS` via `parse_time_seconds` |
| `WET_STEP`            | `wet_step`                              | integer seconds      | same                                          |
| `RULE_STEP`           | `rule_step`                             | integer seconds      | same                                          |
| `DRY_DAYS`            | `dry_days` (double)                     | `%g` double          | `std::stod`                                   |
| `SWEEP_START`         | `sweep_start` (day-of-year int)         | `MM/DD`              | `MM/DD` → day-of-year (year 2000 reference, matches parser) |
| `SWEEP_END`           | `sweep_end`                             | `MM/DD`              | same                                          |

**Tab 1 — Models / Processes**

| Key                   | Storage                                 | `get` emits          | `set` accepts                                 |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `INFILTRATION`        | `infiltration` (enum)                   | `HORTON` / `MOD_HORTON` / `GREEN_AMPT` / `MOD_GREEN_AMPT` / `CURVE_NUMBER` | tokens above; `MODIFIED_HORTON` / `MODIFIED_GREEN_AMPT` aliases per parser |
| `ALLOW_PONDING`       | `allow_ponding` (bool)                  | `YES` / `NO`         | `YES`/`NO`/`TRUE`/`FALSE`/`1`/`0`             |
| `SKIP_STEADY_STATE`   | `skip_steady_state`                     | `YES` / `NO`         | same                                          |
| `IGNORE_RAINFALL`     | `ignore_rainfall`                       | `YES` / `NO`         | same                                          |
| `IGNORE_SNOWMELT`     | `ignore_snow_melt`                      | `YES` / `NO`         | same                                          |
| `IGNORE_GROUNDWATER`  | `ignore_groundwater`                    | `YES` / `NO`         | same                                          |
| `IGNORE_RDII`         | `ignore_rdii`                           | `YES` / `NO`         | same                                          |
| `IGNORE_QUALITY`      | `ignore_quality`                        | `YES` / `NO`         | same                                          |
| `IGNORE_ROUTING`      | `ignore_routing`                        | `YES` / `NO`         | same                                          |

**Tab 3 — Routing & Hydraulics**

| Key                   | Storage                                 | `get` emits          | `set` accepts                                 |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `SURCHARGE_METHOD`    | `surcharge_method` (int 0/1/2)          | `EXTRAN` / `SLOT` / `DYNAMIC_SLOT` | tokens above                       |
| `NODE_CONTINUITY`     | `node_continuity` (enum)                | `EXPLICIT` / `SEMI_IMPLICIT` | tokens above                          |
| `FORCE_MAIN_EQUATION` | `force_main_eqn` (int 0/1)              | `H-W` / `D-W`        | `H-W`/`HW`/`HAZEN-WILLIAMS`/`D-W`/`DW`/`DARCY-WEISBACH` |
| `NORMAL_FLOW_LIMITED` | `normal_flow_ltd` (int 0–3)             | `SLOPE` / `FROUDE` / `BOTH` / `NEITHER` | tokens above                  |
| `INERTIAL_DAMPING`    | `inertial_damping` (int 0/1/2)          | `NONE` / `PARTIAL` / `FULL` | tokens above                            |
| `ANDERSON_ACCEL`      | `anderson_accel` (bool)                 | `YES` / `NO`         | YES/NO/TRUE/FALSE/1/0                         |
| `DPS_CELERITY`        | `dps_target_celerity` (double)          | `%g` double          | `std::stod`                                   |
| `DPS_ALPHA`           | `dps_alpha`                             | `%g` double          | `std::stod`                                   |
| `DPS_DECAY_TIME`      | `dps_decay_time`                        | `%g` double          | `std::stod`                                   |
| `LENGTHENING_STEP`    | `lengthening_step` (seconds)            | `%g` double          | `std::stod`                                   |
| `VARIABLE_STEP`       | `variable_step` (Courant fraction)      | `%g` double          | `std::stod`                                   |
| `MAX_TRIALS`          | `max_trials` (int)                      | integer              | integer                                       |
| `HEAD_TOLERANCE`      | `head_tol` (double, ft)                 | `%g` double          | `std::stod`                                   |
| `LAT_FLOW_TOL`        | `lat_flow_tol` (fraction, e.g. 0.05)    | `%g` double (fraction) | `std::stod` (fraction; GUI uses fraction in `readFromEngine`/`writeToEngine`) |
| `SYS_FLOW_TOL`        | `sys_flow_tol` (fraction)               | `%g` double (fraction) | same                                        |
| `MIN_SURFAREA`        | `min_surf_area` (ft²)                   | `%g` double          | `std::stod`                                   |
| `MIN_SLOPE`           | `min_slope` (ft/ft)                     | `%g` double          | `std::stod`                                   |

**Tab 4 — System / Performance**

| Key       | Storage                | `get` emits | `set` accepts |
|-----------|------------------------|-------------|---------------|
| `THREADS` | `num_threads` (int)    | integer     | integer       |

**Fraction-vs-percent note:** `LAT_FLOW_TOL` and `SYS_FLOW_TOL` are stored as fractions in `SimulationOptions` (parser divides input by 100). The legacy `.inp` format uses percent. We intentionally make the C API emit/accept **fractions** — that matches what `SimulationOptionsDialog::readFromEngine` already passes through (`getOption("LAT_FLOW_TOL", QString::number(sim.latFlowTolPct / 100.0, …))`) and what `writeToEngine` writes back. The `OptionsHandler` parser stays the sole place where the percent→fraction conversion happens on `.inp` ingest; `InpWriter` stays the sole place where fraction→percent happens on `.inp` emit. This keeps each surface using the encoding it natively uses without scattering 100× conversions through the C API switch.

#### Phase CY.2 — Implement `swmm_options_get` extensions

Single edit in `openswmm.engine/src/engine/core/openswmm_model_impl.cpp` adding the keys above to the existing `if/else if` chain before the final `else return SWMM_ERR_BADPARAM`. Helpers:
- Date emit: `datetime::decodeDate(std::floor(d), y, m, d)` then `snprintf("%02d/%02d/%04d", m, d, y)`.
- Time emit: `secs = (d - std::floor(d)) * SecsPerDay`; `snprintf("%02d:%02d:%02d", h, m, s)`.
- `SWEEP_START` / `SWEEP_END`: day-of-year (1–365) → calendar (year 2000) via `encodeDate(2000,1,1) + (doy-1)` then `decodeDate` → `MM/DD`.

#### Phase CY.3 — Implement `swmm_options_set` extensions (parity)

Single edit in the same file adding matching entries to the `swmm_options_set` switch. Fixes the secondary bug where `START_DATE` / `END_DATE` today call `std::stod` on `"MM/DD/YYYY"` and silently corrupt storage. Date set uses `datetime::parseDate(v)`; time set computes fractional-day from `parse_time_seconds(v) / SecsPerDay`. Date set preserves the existing time-of-day in storage (and vice versa for time set) so the dialog can write `START_DATE` and `START_TIME` independently — same composition rule the parser uses.

#### Phase CY.4 — §M.4 plan update

Once CY.2/CY.3 land, edit §M.4 of this document to:
- Move the §M.4 "deferred per user scope decision" paragraph into a fourth "Landed — gap 4 (engine: §M.4 deferred OPTIONS keys)" bullet under Slice CX phase CX.4.
- Update the §M.4 status table column "Options dialog (any tab)" to ✅ for the "Project open" trigger.

`include/ui/swmmvis_hydration_audit.h` is **not** extended in this slice — the audit array is for status-bar widgets (per §M.2 header comment); dialog-tab hydration is asserted by `tests/gui/test_simulationoptionsdialog.cpp` (parked under the `swmmvis_core` extraction).

#### Phase CY.5 — Regression test

New leaf test `openswmm.engine/tests/test_options_get_set_roundtrip.cpp`: for every key in the §CY.1 tables, drive `swmm_options_set(key, X)` → `swmm_options_get(key)` and assert byte-identical (or canonical-equivalent) round-trip on an empty engine. Also assert that after parsing a fixture `.inp` with non-default values, `get` returns the parsed values (not constructor defaults). ~35 cases, all self-contained.

- `openswmm.gui/docs/GUI_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` (§M.4 amendment after CY lands).

## §N — Context-Aware Styling Surface + Mesh Edges/Contours + Velocity/HGL Theming (DRAFT 2026-05-22, awaiting approval)

> **Status:** ⏳ architecture draft, awaiting approval. §N extends §J (theming / styling / legend architecture) with the four user-stated requirements raised 2026-05-22 that §J–§L do not currently close. Existing slice text is unchanged; new sub-phases land via the amendment blocks in §P. No code lands until the user approves §N–§P.
>
> **2026-05-27 status update.** Sub-sections **§N.2 / §N.2-bis / §N.4** (entry-point architecture, three-surface model, layer-kind → control matrix) are **superseded** by the Rule Model in [`RENDERING_RULE_MODEL_PLAN.md`](RENDERING_RULE_MODEL_PLAN.md). The single-dialog Active Rule combo + Rule List replaces the three-surface routing. Sub-sections **§N.5 (mesh edges) / §N.6 (contour generator) / §N.7 (engine velocity) / §N.8 (HGL/WSE) / §N.9 (labels)** survive intact — those are the rendering capabilities a Rule's Symbol + Decorations consume. §N.4's matrix is reframed in the Rule Model as "Default Rule List per layer kind" (see RENDERING_RULE_MODEL_PLAN.md §3.2 + §6).

### §N.0 Why this section exists

A user pass on 2026-05-22 against the styling surface surfaced four concrete requirements that §J–§L touch tangentially but do not actually deliver:

1. **Context-dependent styling UI.** The styling pane must follow the selected layer; the selected layer must be visibly highlighted so the user knows exactly what they are styling.
2. **Standard GIS styling for vector + raster, including terrain rendering and shading.** Vector covers `IFeatureRenderer` (§J.2) once 8.13.6.4 lands. Raster covers `IRasterRenderer` stub (8.13.6.7). What is **missing**: a stylable hillshade decorator (`MeshLayerItem` hardcoded brown-tan; `GISRasterLayer` has no hillshade at all — AU defers it to a non-existent "Slice AC.4"), and color-scale UI for graduated raster symbology.
3. **Mesh styling — edges, contours (filled + lines), terrain shading.** Today AZ.3 has fill + outline per category. There is no `showEdges` boolean. There is no contour generator at all — for raster, mesh elevation, or mesh result attributes.
4. **Mesh result animation styling — depth, velocity (computed by engine), HGL — color shades, efficient filled contours, contour lines, plus labels.** CF.MVP ships depth heatmap. CF.2 ships velocity arrows + path profile but velocity is GUI-side RT0-reconstructed. HGL is mentioned only for CF.3 plotting, not for theming. Neither velocity nor HGL is a first-class `SWMM2DResultVariable` that BA's per-attribute theming combo can drive. Labels associated with results / contours are not in any slice.

§N closes all four. §J's renderer + ramp + legend architecture is load-bearing for §N — every §N slice consumes it without modification.

> **Revised 2026-05-22 (post-implementation audit): three-surface entry-point architecture, not a unified dock.** The original §N.2 proposal called for a single `StylingDock` (QGIS-style) hosting tabs from every editor. An audit of the user's actually-committed code revealed a different, deliberate split: **`SymbologyDialog`** (per-layer vector renderer editor — Single / Graduated / Categorized / Labels / Arrows tabs — opened modally from the layer-tree's `layerStyleRequested` signal), **`LayerPropertiesDialog`** (per-layer Display state — mesh edges / hillshade / contours / opacity / CRS — opened from the layer-tree's `layerPropertiesRequested` signal), and **`LegendPanel`** (read-only legend dock that displays whatever the primary results layer is currently styled with). The §N follow-up slices shipped against this split — AZ.3.4 / AU.6.4-lite / BJ.2-lite / BJ.2-filled all wire into the `LayerPropertiesDialog` Mesh tab — and that has played out cleanly. **BI.4 (unified `StylingDock`) is therefore withdrawn** as a §N follow-up; see §P.BI.4 "Superseded" note below. §N.3 (selected-layer canvas affordance — pulsing extent / sibling dim / status-bar chip) remains in-scope as a future polish that can ride on whichever surface has focus.

### §N.1 The four requirements mapped onto §J / §P

| User requirement | Covered by today | §N delta |
|---|---|---|
| Single context-aware styling entry point | scattered dialogs (BB, BI, AZ.3, D-2) | **WITHDRAWN** — superseded by user's three-surface architecture (`SymbologyDialog` + `LayerPropertiesDialog` + `LegendPanel`). Layer-tree right-click routes to the right surface per concern. |
| Selected-layer visual highlight | Layer Tree only | **deferred to canvas-affordance follow-up** — pulse / sibling-dim / status-bar chip can ride on whichever surface has focus; not tied to a specific dock |
| Standard GIS vector styling + color scales | BB (ramps), BI (8.13.6 renderer + 8.13.8 symbol layers) | none — already covered when 8.13.6.4 paint-loop refactor lands |
| Raster color ramps + clamp + NoData | BI 8.13.6.7 (`IRasterRenderer` stub) | **AU amendment** — `RasterHillshadeRenderer` decorator (azimuth / altitude / z-exaggeration); promotes hillshade from "deferred to AC.4" |
| Mesh fill colour by category / feature | AZ.3 (`MeshSymbolDialog`) | **AZ.3 amendment** — `showEdges` toggle + per-edge pen style + per-feature `LabelConfig` |
| Mesh contours (filled + lines) on bed elevation | none | **new Slice BJ.2** — marching-triangles contour generator |
| Raster contours (filled + lines) on DEM | none | **BJ.2** — marching-squares contour generator |

| Mesh result theming: velocity (engine-computed) | CF.2 — GUI-side RT0 from edge fluxes | **CF.2 amendment** — add engine-side `swmm_2d_get_velocity_bulk` as canonical path; RT0 stays as fallback for older engines |

### §N.2 ~~Context-aware Styling Dock (the single entry point)~~ — WITHDRAWN

> **Status:** ⛔ withdrawn 2026-05-22. The original proposal (a single `StylingDock` hosting tabs per layer kind via a `LayerStyleEditorFactory`) competed with the user's actually-committed three-surface architecture. Superseded by §N.2-bis below. The original text is preserved at the end of §P.BI.4 for archaeology — readers chasing the dock pattern in the future should start there.

### §N.2-bis The actual entry-point architecture (three surfaces, layer-tree-routed)

The user's committed code splits per-layer styling across three coexisting surfaces. Each owns a distinct concern. The layer-tree's right-click context menu routes to the right surface per concern via existing signals; there is **no unified entry point**.

| Surface | Owns | Reached via | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`SymbologyDialog`** (`include/ui/dialogs/symbologydialog.h`) | Vector renderer config: SingleSymbolRenderer / GraduatedRenderer / CategorizedRenderer / RuleBasedRenderer + Labels expression + flow-direction Arrows. Drives the `IFeatureRenderer` interface from §J.2. | Layer-tree right-click → "Set Style…" emits `LayerTreePanel::layerStyleRequested(layer)`; `SWMMVis` opens the dialog. Animation toolbar's Set Style action routes through the same slot. | Shipped (BI 8.13.6 surface). |
| **`LayerPropertiesDialog`** (`include/ui/dialogs/layerpropertiesdialog.h`) | Per-layer display state that is **not** vector renderer config: name / CRS / opacity / visibility (existing); mesh edges / hillshade params / contour lines / filled isobands (AZ.3.4 + AU.6.4-lite + BJ.2-lite + BJ.2-filled); mesh statistics readout. | Layer-tree right-click → "Layer Properties…" emits `LayerTreePanel::layerPropertiesRequested(layer)`. | Shipped. Mesh-specific tabs added in §N follow-ups. |
| **`LegendPanel`** (`include/ui/panels/legendpanel.h`) | Read-only display of the primary results layer's active legend (colour ramp + variable label). Mirrors what `SymbologyDialog` configured for the active layer; updates live as the renderer changes. | Always visible as a dock; `View → Legend` toggles. | Shipped (BB 8.6.4 surface). |

The three surfaces are intentionally non-overlapping: a control that belongs in one does not appear in another. New §N follow-up controls go into whichever surface owns the concern (mesh display → `LayerPropertiesDialog`; vector renderer → `SymbologyDialog`; legend display → `LegendPanel`).

**Trade-offs vs. a unified dock:**
- **Pro:** Each surface is small and focused. No mega-tabbed `StylingDock` to wrestle with. Discoverability comes from the layer-tree right-click menu, not from a persistent panel.
- **Pro:** Each surface evolves independently. Adding mesh contours (BJ.2-lite) didn't touch `SymbologyDialog` or `LegendPanel`.
- **Con:** Users have to know which right-click entry leads to which dialog. The right-click menu wording matters — should be unambiguous (`Set Style…` for vector symbology, `Layer Properties…` for everything else).
- **Con:** No persistent canvas affordance for "you are styling this layer" — but §N.3 affordances (pulsing extent / status chip) can be wired to the active dialog's focus rather than to a dock, so this is not a hard regression.

**Future investigations** (out of scope for the §N batch but tracked for completeness):
- If a future user pass surfaces real pain about the three-surface split, revisit the unified-dock pattern as a separate slice (call it `BI.4-redux`) that wraps the three existing surfaces as embedded panels in one dock — without rewriting them. The §N.4 layer-kind → tab matrix (below) maps cleanly to that design.
- The selected-layer canvas affordance (§N.3) is orthogonal to the dock vs. dialog question and ships independently.

### §N.3 Selected-layer canvas affordance

When the user picks a layer to style, the canvas needs to say "you're styling **this**." Three subtle, non-blocking affordances ship together:

1. **Pulsing extent frame** — a `LayerSelectionOverlay` `QGraphicsItem` on `MapCanvas` draws the layer's full extent as a 2-px dashed rectangle in `MapCanvasTheme::selectionHighlight`, opacity 0.0 → 0.45 → 0.0 over 2.5 s, then settles at 0.20. Subsequent layer-tree selections retrigger the pulse. Auto-fades to 0 after 8 s of no interaction with the dock; reappears on dock focus or any styling edit. Setting cleared on layer deselect.
2. **Sibling dimming** — non-styled layers paint at `opacity * 0.55` while a styling tab is **focused** (dock visible but not focused = no dim). Resets immediately on focus loss. Skippable via `PreferencesManager → Styling/dimUnstyledLayersOnFocus` (default `true`).
3. **Status-bar chip** — a small persistent label `Styling: <LayerName>` in the status bar, colour-matched to the layer-tree row's category colour, click-target reveals the dock if hidden. Disappears when no layer is styled.

These three affordances combined: the user always knows which layer is being styled, without modal "you are now editing X" announcements that interrupt flow.

### §N.4 Layer-kind → control matrix (revised 2026-05-22 for three-surface architecture)

For each layer kind, which surface owns which control:

| Layer | `SymbologyDialog` (vector renderer) | `LayerPropertiesDialog` (display state) | `LegendPanel` (read-only display) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SWMMModelLayer` | **Per-kind via left-pane picker** (11 categories: Junctions / Outfalls / Storage / Dividers / Conduits / Pumps / Orifices / Weirs / Outlets / Subcatchments / RainGages — see §N.14) · Right-pane Single / Graduated / Categorized / Rules / Labels / Arrows tabs scope to the selected kind · Layer-scope `Apply to all kinds` button | Name · CRS · Opacity · Visibility | — (not a results layer) |
| `SWMMResultsLayer` (1D animation) | **Per-scope via left-pane picker** (3 scopes: Subcatchments / Nodes / Links — see §N.14) · Each scope picks one result variable + Graduated renderer config · Labels · Scale-visible | Name · Opacity · Visibility · Active-as-primary flag | Active legend for primary scope's variable |
| `SWMM2DMeshLayer` | — (mesh categories use the in-place AZ.3 `MeshSymbolDialog`, planned to fold into `SymbologyDialog`'s Categorized tab later) | Mesh tab: **Display** (showEdges + showMeshNodes — AZ.3.4) · **Hillshade** (azimuth / altitude / z-exag / shadow floor — AU.6.4-lite) · **Contours** (show lines + intervals + colour + width + filled bands + opacity — BJ.2-lite + BJ.2-filled) · **Statistics** (read-only) | — |
| `SWMM2DResultsLayer` (2D animation) — **BLOCKED on CF.MVP** | Attribute = Depth / Vmag / Vx / Vy / HGL ; ramp + binning + wet/dry threshold (future) | Visibility · Active-as-primary flag (future) | Active legend for primary 2D variable (future) |
| `GISVectorLayer` | Single / Graduated / Categorized / Labels (existing `SymbologyDialog` already covers) | Name · CRS · Opacity · Visibility | — |
| `GISRasterLayer` | — | Name · CRS · Opacity · Visibility · **Hillshade** (azimuth / altitude / z-exag — when AU.6.4 full lands) · **Contours** (when BJ.2-raster lands) | — |
| `WCSLayer` / basemap layers | — | Name · Opacity · Visibility · Blend mode (future) | — |

**Design rule:** Vector *renderer* config (symbol choice, ramp, classifier) lives in `SymbologyDialog`. Per-layer *display state* (opacity, mesh wireframe, hillshade params, contour params, terrain shading) lives in `LayerPropertiesDialog` as a layer-kind-conditional tab. The reasoning: renderer config is a per-feature-kind decision tree; display state is a flat scalar bag — they want different UI shapes.

**Where §N slices landed against this matrix:**
- AZ.3.4 mesh edges → `LayerPropertiesDialog` Mesh tab Display group ✓
- AU.6.4-lite tunable hillshade → `LayerPropertiesDialog` Mesh tab Hillshade group ✓
- BJ.2-lite mesh-bed contour lines → `LayerPropertiesDialog` Mesh tab Contours group ✓
- BJ.2-filled mesh-bed filled isobands → `LayerPropertiesDialog` Mesh tab Contours group (extends BJ.2-lite) ✓
- AZ.3.7 mesh-layer persistence → `ProjectSerializer` (no UI surface) ✓

Future slice destinations:
- AU.6.4 full (`RasterHillshadeRenderer`) → `LayerPropertiesDialog` for `GISRasterLayer` (new Hillshade tab) + reusing the mesh Hillshade group's widget shape
- BJ.2-raster (marching-squares for DEM) → `LayerPropertiesDialog` for `GISRasterLayer`
- BJ.2-results / CF.2 result-attribute theming → `SymbologyDialog` Graduated tab (when `SWMM2DResultsLayer` exists) + `LegendPanel` update path

### §N.5 Mesh edges + per-feature outlines — AZ.3 extension

AZ.3 today has fill / outline / width / opacity on `MeshFeatureSymbol`. The user wants a top-level **wireframe** view ("show edges") independent of per-feature outlines. `SWMM2DMeshLayer` gains:

- `bool m_edgesVisible` (default `false` — fills only); `setEdgesVisible(bool)`.
- `QPen m_edgePen` (default 0.5 px, `MapCanvasTheme::meshEdge` colour); `setEdgePen(QPen)`.
- `int m_edgeLodMinZoom` — below this canvas scale, edges paint decimated (every Nth edge) to keep fps stable on million-triangle meshes; auto-tuned by triangle count.

`MeshLayerItem::paint()` adds an edge pass after fills, before per-feature outlines, controlled by these settings. New Styling Dock **Edges** tab exposes: visibility checkbox, pen colour, pen width, zoom-LOD threshold (with a "current zoom" capture button). Persisted under the layer's `.oswp` block. Per §N.4 the existing AZ.3 `MeshFeatureSymbol::outlineColor / outlineWidth` remain — they are *per-feature outlines*, conceptually distinct from the *mesh wireframe*.

### §N.6 Contour generator — new Slice BJ.2

A single contour engine serves three data sources (raster DEM, mesh bed elevation, mesh result attributes). All three render the same two output kinds (filled isobands + isolines) with the same labelling. The engine is decoupled from data source via an `IContourSource` shim — adding a new source is one class.

```cpp
class IContourSource {
public:
    virtual QRectF      domainExtent() const = 0;
    virtual double      sampleAt(const QPointF &mapXY) const = 0;     // raster path
    virtual std::pair<QVector<Vertex>, QVector<Triangle>> triangulation() const = 0;  // mesh path
    virtual QPair<double,double> valueRange() const = 0;
};
```

Two algorithms ship:

- **Raster path — marching squares** for `IContourSource` implementations backed by gridded data (`GISRasterLayer`). Standard CGAL-free 16-case lookup; O(W·H) per redraw; suppressed when zoom-out exceeds a pixel-density threshold.
- **Mesh path — marching triangles** for `SWMM2DMeshLayer` (bed `z`) and `SWMM2DResultsLayer` (per-tri value). Per-triangle 8-case lookup; O(N_tri) per redraw. RT0 / piecewise-linear interpolation within the triangle yields C0 contours.

Both algorithms emit a `ContourPolygonSet` (filled isobands as `QPainterPath`s) and a `ContourLineSet` (isolines as `QVector<QPolygonF>`). Rendering is a single `QGraphicsItem` per data source, z-ordered above the base fill and below labels.

**`ContourSpec`** (per layer, per data source) controls the contour set:

```cpp
struct ContourSpec {
    enum Mode { Filled, Lines, Both, None };
    Mode               mode = Lines;
    IntervalBinner     binner;          // reuses §J.4 BB binning — Equal / Quantile / StdDev / Manual / Jenks / LogEqual / LogQuantile
    ColorRamp          ramp;            // reused from BB; isobands fill from ramp; isolines optional ramp or single colour
    QColor             lineColor;       // used when ramp-per-line is disabled
    qreal              lineWidth = 0.75;
    bool               labelEveryNth = true;
    int                labelStep = 5;
    LegendItemFormat   labelFormat;     // reused from BB Phase 8.6.9 (units / decimals / scientific)
    LabelExpression    labelExpression; // reused from BI.2 — default `format(value, decimals) || ' ' || units`
    LabelHalo          labelHalo;       // reused from BI.2
    qreal              minZoomToShow = 0.0;  // scale-visible
};
```

**Live updates during animation** (CF.MVP + CF.2 + BA cursor): when `SWMM2DResultsLayer::currentTimeChanged` fires, the layer's contour `QGraphicsItem` reruns marching-triangles on the now-current scalar field. Viewport culling + LOD decimation keep fps stable: at zoom-out, triangle merging coalesces sub-pixel contour segments; only iso-bands intersecting the viewport are rebuilt.

**Editor UI** lives in the Styling Dock's **Contours** tab: data-source picker (when multiple are available — e.g. bed-elevation vs depth on `SWMM2DResultsLayer`), mode combo (None / Lines / Filled / Both), binning combo (reused BB widget), interval-count or manual-breaks, ramp picker, per-line pen, "label every Nth" + format, scale-visible range.

**Engine prereqs:** none for raster / mesh-bed; for mesh-result contours, **canonical velocity** is via the engine bulk API added by CF.2 amendment (§N.7).

### §N.7 Engine-side velocity — CF.2.1 amendment

CF.2.1 today adds `swmm_2d_get_edge_flux_bulk` + edge geometry; the GUI reconstructs `(vx, vy)` via RT0 in CF.2.3. The user specifies velocity should be "**computed by the engine**." Add a sibling bulk accessor that returns per-triangle cell-centre velocity directly:

```c
SWMM_ENGINE_API int swmm_2d_get_velocity_bulk(SWMM_Engine engine, double* vx_vy);  // [nTri * 2], xy-major
```

Implementation in the engine reuses the existing `SurfaceFluxCalculator` + RT0 logic that the GUI replicates today, executed once per output write and cached on `SurfaceStateData::cell_velocity`. Default2DOutputPlugin emits `/Mesh2_velocity` `[nTime, nFace, 2]` alongside `/Mesh2_depth`. New engine gap entry **CF-04** filed; older engines + older `.h5` files degrade to the GUI-side RT0 path that CF.2.3 already builds, gated via `QLibrary::resolve` + HDF5-dataset-presence check.

Once landed, `SWMM2DResultVariable` gains `Vmag`, `Vx`, `Vy` enum entries (BA Phase 8.2 combo picks them up). The GUI no longer needs to invoke its RT0 reconstruction for theming purposes — only the streamline-integration tool (CF.2.5) still uses the local `(vx, vy)` field, and that field is now sourced from the engine cache.

### §N.8 HGL/WSE as a first-class 2D result attribute

HGL/WSE on the 2D mesh is `bed_z[i] + depth[i, t]` — fully GUI-derivable from existing engine outputs. No new engine API. Add a `Hgl` entry to `SWMM2DResultVariable`; `SWMM2DResultsLayer::sampleAttribute(tri, t)` computes `m_bedZ[tri] + m_depths[t, tri]` when the active variable is `Hgl`. BA Phase 8.2 combo lists it alongside Depth / Vmag / Vx / Vy. Same colour-ramp / contour / label code path as Depth.

### §N.9 Labels integrated with styling

BI.2 (§L.BI.2) already defines `LabelConfig` + `LabelExpression` + placement + halo + scale-visible + PAL-lite for vector layers. §N extends consumption to mesh + contour layers:

- `SWMM2DMeshLayer` gains a `labelConfig()` accessor (per-feature labels; placement = `InsidePolygon(centroid)`); Styling Dock **Labels** tab.
- `SWMM2DResultsLayer` gains a per-cell `labelConfig()` (sparse; placement = `InsidePolygon(centroid)` + `LabelScaleRange` so per-cell values only appear at high zoom).
- `BJ.2 ContourSpec::labelExpression` reuses the same `LabelExpression` parser; `LabelPlacement::AlongLine(RepeatEvery)` is the canonical contour-label mode; per-label rotation follows `pointAtPercent + angleAtPercent` (already a BI.2 capability).

No new parsing or rendering code — the consumers wire to the existing BI.2 engine. The BI.2 `Files` list grows by three layer-class touches.

### §N.12 Risk register (additions to §I)

| # | Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~~N-1~~ | ~~Dock + dialog duplication~~ | **Moot** | BI.4 withdrawn 2026-05-22; user's three-surface architecture has no dock to conflict with the dialogs. |
| N-2 | Contour generator at scale (>500k triangles) drops fps below 30 during animation. | High | Marching-triangles is O(N_tri) per redraw; viewport culling (skip tris fully outside `MapCanvas::exposedRect`) + zoom-LOD merge of sub-pixel segments + `QtConcurrent::map` per-tile parallelism. Benchmark target: 1 M triangles @ 60 fps redraw at full-extent on M2 Pro. Tracked in BJ.2 verification. |
| N-3 | Engine velocity API (CF-04) lands later than §N. | Low | CF.2's GUI-side RT0 reconstruction stays as the fallback path (`QLibrary::resolve` + HDF5-dataset-presence check). Themable Vmag/Vx/Vy works on day one against the GUI-side field; flips to engine field on engine upgrade with no GUI churn. |
| N-4 | Canvas affordance (pulsing extent + sibling dim) is intrusive on small maps or single-layer projects. | Low | Each affordance independently toggleable in `Preferences → Styling`. Defaults are conservative: pulse fades after 8 s; dim only while dock focused; chip is a 14 px label, not modal. |
| N-5 | Contour labels overlap at low zoom (BI.2 PAL-lite is point-oriented; contour labels are along-line). | Medium | BJ.2's contour labeller computes label slots at `LabelPlacement::AlongLine(repeatEvery_px)` *before* PAL-lite quad-tree dedup; only the surviving labels go into the shared dedup quad-tree. Falls back to "label every Nth contour only" at the lowest zoom. |
| N-6 | Vmag/Vx/Vy semantics drift between engine bulk API and GUI RT0 fallback. | Low | Engine RT0 implementation IS the same algorithm the GUI runs (`SurfaceFluxCalculator` is the shared math). Drift would be a bug in either; covered by parity test `test_velocity_engine_vs_rt0.cpp` in CF.2 amendment. |

### §N.14 Per-kind styling for multi-kind layers (added 2026-05-22)

**Problem discovered post-§N-revision:** the user's existing `SymbologyDialog` (`include/ui/dialogs/symbologydialog.h`) treats every layer as a *single renderer target* — its Single / Graduated / Categorized / Labels / Arrows tabs operate on "the layer's renderer" as if there were one. But the two SWMM-specific layer kinds are **multi-kind containers**:

- **`SWMMModelLayer`** owns **11 visually-distinct object categories** (per `enum Category`): `CatJunctions`, `CatOutfalls`, `CatStorage`, `CatDividers`, `CatConduits`, `CatPumps`, `CatOrifices`, `CatWeirs`, `CatOutlets`, `CatSubcatchments`, `CatRainGages`. Each has its own glyph shape (circle / square / triangle / diamond / line / polygon / etc.) and its own visual semantics; "set the layer's colour" is meaningless without saying *which category*.
- **`SWMMResultsLayer`** (when CF.MVP-resurrection ships) animates results across **3 broad attribute scopes**: `Subcatchments` (Runoff, Rainfall, GW flow, …), `Nodes` (Depth, Head, Total inflow, Flooding, Volume, …), `Links` (Flow, Velocity, Depth, Capacity, …). Per BA Phase 8.2 the status-bar combos are already grouped this way — same 3-scope split applies to the renderer per scope.

The §J.10 plan partially anticipated this via the `MultiKindRenderer` adapter ("wrapping 11 `SingleSymbolRenderer`s"), but the **UI surface for selecting which kind to edit was never specified**. The shipped `SymbologyDialog` therefore can't actually drive the multi-renderer layer.

#### §N.14.1 Kind enumeration per layer

| Layer | Kind scope | Enumeration (used by `SymbologyDialog`'s kind picker + persistence keys) |
|---|---|---|
| `SWMMModelLayer` | 11 fine-grained categories | Junctions, Outfalls, Storage, Dividers (point geometries with distinct glyphs) · Conduits, Pumps, Orifices, Weirs, Outlets (line geometries with distinct mid-glyphs and dash patterns) · Subcatchments (polygon) · RainGages (point) |
| `SWMMResultsLayer` | 3 broad attribute scopes | Subcatchments · Nodes · Links — matches BA Phase 8.2 status-bar combo grouping. Each scope picks one active result variable + one renderer config. |
| `SWMM2DMeshLayer` | 1 (single renderer for the whole mesh) | n/a — uses `LayerPropertiesDialog` Mesh tab, not `SymbologyDialog` |
| `SWMM2DResultsLayer` | 5 attribute scopes (per CF.2.7) | Depth · Vmag · Vx · Vy · HGL — picked from the BA combo, edited in `SymbologyDialog` Graduated tab |
| `GISVectorLayer` | 1 | n/a — single renderer applies |
| `GISRasterLayer` | 1 | n/a — single renderer applies |

#### §N.14.2 UI shape — kind-scoped `SymbologyDialog`

Two equivalent entry pathways (both reach the same dialog body):

1. **Layer-tree → category sub-row → right-click → "Set Style…"** *(preferred)*. The `LayerTreePanel` already shows `SWMMModelLayer` categories as sub-rows (via `SWMMObjectTreeModel`). Extend the category sub-row's context menu with `Set Style…` that emits a new `LayerTreePanel::layerKindStyleRequested(layer, kindEnumInt)` signal. `SWMMVis` opens `SymbologyDialog` with the kind argument pre-set.
2. **Layer-tree → layer row → right-click → "Set Style…" → dialog opens with kind picker visible**. The existing `layerStyleRequested(layer)` signal stays; for multi-kind layers the dialog adds a left-pane kind picker (defaults to whichever kind is "primary" — e.g., Junctions for `SWMMModelLayer`, Nodes for `SWMMResultsLayer`).

The dialog layout grows a 130-px-wide **left pane** with a `QListWidget` of kinds (icon + label, one row per enum value) when the layer is multi-kind. Single-kind layers (GIS / mesh) skip the pane entirely — backward-compatible. Changing the selection re-binds the right-pane tabs to that kind's per-kind `IFeatureRenderer`. The right pane (existing Single / Graduated / Categorized / Labels / Arrows tabs) is unchanged.

Mockup (multi-kind):

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Symbology — SWMM Model Layer (snoopy.inp)              [X]   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Object kind:          │ Symbol │ Graduated │ Categorized │…  │
│  ▸ Junctions  ●       │ ┌──────────────────────────────────┐ │
│    Outfalls           │ │ Colour:  [#1f77b4] [Pick…]       │ │
│    Storage            │ │ Size:    [4.0 px]                │ │
│    Dividers           │ │ Outline: [#000] [Pick…]  [0.5]  │ │
│    ──── Links ────    │ │ Shape:   [● Circle ▾]            │ │
│    Conduits           │ │                                  │ │
│    Pumps              │ │  [Live preview swatch]           │ │
│    Orifices           │ └──────────────────────────────────┘ │
│    Weirs              │                                      │
│    Outlets            │  [ Apply ]  [ Apply to all kinds ]   │
│    ──── Areal ────    │                                      │
│    Subcatchments      │                                      │
│    RainGages          │                                      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                              [ OK ]  [ Cancel ]  [ Apply ]   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The **Apply to all kinds** button writes the active right-pane config into every kind's renderer at once — useful for "make everything the same colour temporarily". `Apply` writes to the selected kind only.

Group separators in the left pane (`──── Links ────`, `──── Areal ────`) keep the list scannable; they're not selectable.

#### §N.14.3 Renderer storage — extends §J.2 `MultiKindRenderer`

`SWMMModelLayer` and `SWMMResultsLayer` each own a `MultiKindRenderer` (per §J.10). The dialog reads and writes to `multiRenderer->rendererFor(kind)`. Per-kind renderers default to sensible per-kind starting points (`SingleSymbolRenderer` with the kind's existing hardcoded glyph) so first-open shows the same visuals as today.

`IFeatureRenderer` per kind, JSON schema (extends BB Phase 8.6.13's `.swmm-style.json`):

```jsonc
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "layerKind": "SWMMModelLayer",
  "renderers": {
    "Junctions":  { "id": "single",    /* renderer-specific */ },
    "Conduits":   { "id": "graduated", "attribute": "max_flow", /* … */ },
    "Subcatchments": { "id": "categorized", "attribute": "land_use", /* … */ }
    // kinds without an entry use the layer's compiled default
  }
}
```

`LegendPanel` updates: instead of showing one legend, it shows one collapsible section per kind that has a non-default renderer (kinds using the compiled default are collapsed by default to save space).

#### §N.14.4 Persistence — extends `.oswp` session block

`ProjectSerializer` gains a `layerStyles` block on each layer's session record, carrying the per-kind renderer JSON for `SWMMModelLayer` / `SWMMResultsLayer`. Shape:

```jsonc
"layer": {
  /* existing fields … */
  "kindRenderers": {
    "Junctions":  { /* IFeatureRenderer JSON */ },
    "Conduits":   { /* … */ }
  }
}
```

Additive — older readers ignore `kindRenderers`; new readers tolerate missing entries (use compiled defaults).

#### §N.14.5 Sequencing — three sub-slices

This work is large enough to split:

- **BI-MK.1** — `SymbologyDialog` gains the kind-picker left pane + `MultiKindRenderer` wiring + per-kind read/write. Target: `SWMMModelLayer` (11 kinds). UI lands first; persistence in BI-MK.3. **Ships against existing code; no engine work.** Estimated ~400-500 lines.
- **BI-MK.2** — Layer-tree category-sub-row right-click + new `layerKindStyleRequested(layer, kindInt)` signal + `SWMMVis` slot opening `SymbologyDialog` pre-scoped to that kind. Touches `LayerTreePanel` + `SWMMObjectTreeModel` context-menu wiring. Estimated ~150-200 lines.
- **BI-MK.3** — `.oswp` persistence for per-kind renderer JSON (`ProjectSerializer` extension). Estimated ~100-150 lines.
- **~~BI-MK.4 (future)~~** **→ BI-MK.4-OUT (🔧 shipping 2026-05-25)** — Extend per-kind styling to `SWMMResultsLayer`. **Status correction**: the earlier "BLOCKED on CF.MVP-resurrection" note conflated `SWMMResultsLayer` (which DOES ship in tree today — concrete class at [src/layers/swmmresultslayer.h](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.h)) with `SWMM2DResultsLayer` (only the 2D variant was the CF.MVP blocker, and that too now ships per [src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.h](../src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.h)). **User-confirmed scope** (2026-05-25): 11 sub-rows matching the SWMMModelLayer pattern (Junctions / Outfalls / Storage / Dividers / Conduits / Pumps / Orifices / Weirs / Outlets / Subcatchments / RainGages) — not just 3 scopes — so the user can style Junctions vs Outfalls independently for the same NodeDepth variable. See §P.BI-MK.4-OUT for the slice definition. Estimated ~400 lines.
- **BI-MK.5 (future)** — Extend to `SWMM2DResultsLayer` (5 scopes — Depth/Vmag/Vx/Vy/HGL per CF.2.7). **BLOCKED on CF.MVP-resurrection + CF.2.7.** Estimated ~150 lines once unblocked.

Sequencing within the multi-kind batch: **BI-MK.1 first** (the dialog needs to know about kinds before anything else does), then **BI-MK.2** (entry-point), then **BI-MK.3** (persistence — last because schema settles after UI shape settles). BI-MK.4 and BI-MK.5 wait on CF.MVP-resurrection.

| N-7 | `MultiKindRenderer` per §J.10 was specced but not implemented; today's `SWMMModelLayer` paint loop reads per-kind `SWMMElementSymbol` directly. BI-MK.1 either has to ship `MultiKindRenderer` as a prereq (scope creep) or defer the multi-renderer indirection. | High | Land `MultiKindRenderer` as the first sub-phase of BI-MK.1; ~80 lines, isolated. Until then, dialog edits write through a shim that maps to the existing `SWMMElementSymbol` setters (BI Phase 8.13.6.4 paint-loop refactor finishes the architectural cleanup later). |

Per-kind labels defer to a future `BI-MK-labels` sub-slice if real demand surfaces. |
| N-10 | `LegendPanel` showing 11 sections per layer is too much. | Low | Only render legend sections for kinds that have a non-default renderer (default-renderer kinds collapse). Layer-level legend toggle to show / hide collapsed sections. |

### §P.BI.4 — ⛔ WITHDRAWN 2026-05-22 (Superseded note)

> **Status:** Withdrawn before any code landed. The audit during the BI.4-mini pre-flight step (2026-05-22 session) revealed that the user's committed code base had already adopted a different entry-point architecture for per-layer styling: three coexisting surfaces (`SymbologyDialog` for vector renderer config, `LayerPropertiesDialog` for non-renderer display state, `LegendPanel` for read-only legend display), routed from the layer-tree's existing `layerStyleRequested` and `layerPropertiesRequested` signals. The BI.4 unified-dock proposal would have competed with this. See **§N.2-bis** for the architecture description and **§N.4** for the layer-kind → control matrix mapped onto the three surfaces.
>
> **The §N follow-up slices that BI.4 was supposed to host** (AZ.3.4 mesh edges, AU.6.4-lite hillshade, BJ.2-lite/BJ.2-filled contours) **all shipped against `LayerPropertiesDialog`'s Mesh tab instead** — no dock needed. The pattern played out cleanly: one new control group per slice, no architectural surface area added.
>
> **What's preserved from the original BI.4 design:**
> - `§N.3` selected-layer canvas affordances (pulsing extent + sibling dim + status-bar chip) — orthogonal to the dock-vs-dialog question; tracked as a future "canvas-affordance" polish slice that rides on whichever surface has focus.
> - The §N.4 control matrix — recast as documentation of where each control lives across the three surfaces.
> - The dialog ↔ dock coexistence guard idiom — moot for now (no dock), but documented in case a future `BI.4-redux` slice revisits the unified-dock pattern.
>
> **For archaeology**, the original BI.4 design preserved in the git history at the parent commit of this revision (see `git log -- docs/GUI_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` for the 2026-05-22 revision commit that withdrew it). Future agents chasing a unified-dock pattern should start there and reconcile against the now-committed three-surface architecture before opening new work.

### §P.BI-MK.1 — New Slice **BI-MK.1** definition (insert after Slice BI block, before Slice BJ)

#### 🔧 Slice BI-MK.1 — `SymbologyDialog` per-kind left pane for `SWMMModelLayer` (Phase 8.13.40–43) — **8.13.40 shipped 2026-05-22, 8.13.41–43 awaiting SymbologyDialog WIP commit**

Closes the per-kind UI gap §N.14 surfaces. The existing `SymbologyDialog` is widened with a 130-px left pane listing the 11 `SWMMModelLayer::Category` values; the right pane re-binds its tabs to the active kind's per-kind `IFeatureRenderer` (managed via `MultiKindRenderer` per §J.10). Single-kind layers (GIS / mesh) skip the pane entirely — backward-compatible.

- ✅ **Phase 8.13.40 — `MultiKindRenderer` ships as a prerequisite (closes §J.10 N-7 risk)** *(shipped 2026-05-22)*: New `include/render/multikindrenderer.{h,cpp}` per §J.10 — an `IFeatureRenderer` adapter that holds `std::unordered_map<QString, std::unique_ptr<IFeatureRenderer>> m_perKind` keyed on the `FeatureRef::categoryHint` string (no enum coupling — renderer stays SWMM-agnostic). Container chosen over `QHash` because Qt6 `QHash` requires copyable mapped types and `unique_ptr`'s copy ctor is deleted; an `OpenSWMM::Render::detail::QStringHash` adapter (delegates to `qHash(QString)`) keeps `QString` as the key type. `symbolFor(feature, attrs)` dispatches on `feature.categoryHint`; empty-hint and missing-kind both fall through to a shared fallback (default `SingleSymbolRenderer`) so the renderer is never partial. `legendSymbolItems()` aggregates per-kind items in deterministic (sorted) order with a kind prefix on `userLabel` (combines with the inner renderer's `label` or `userLabel` when set: `Kind / Inner-label`; degrades to just `Kind` when the inner has no label). `rendererFor(kind)` / `setRendererFor(kind, std::unique_ptr<IFeatureRenderer>)` / `clearRendererFor(kind)` / `setFallback(std::unique_ptr<IFeatureRenderer>)` form the editor surface; null setter args are silently no-op'd (setFallback) or remove the entry (setRendererFor). `kinds()` returns sorted keys so legend + JSON output are reproducible across saves. JSON round-trip via a local factory in the .cpp that dispatches on the inner renderer's `"id"` field (`"single"` / `"graduated"` / `"categorized"` / `"rule"`) — unknown ids are silently skipped so old/new schemas tolerate each other. `clone()` deep-copies every per-kind entry + the fallback. Files: `include/render/multikindrenderer.h` (~95 lines), `src/render/multikindrenderer.cpp` (~155 lines), `tests/gui/test_multikindrenderer.cpp` (16 cases — default ctor, set/get/clear/null-remove, dispatch by category hint, unknown-kind/empty-hint fallback, null-fallback ignored, sorted kinds, legend aggregation with kind prefix, JSON round-trip, malformed JSON defaults, unknown inner id skipped, clone independence — **16/16 PASS in 2 ms**). CMake entries added to root `CMakeLists.txt` and `tests/gui/CMakeLists.txt`.
- ✅ **Phase 8.13.41 — `SymbologyDialog` left-pane layout (shipped 2026-05-24)**: New 150-px `QListWidget` (`m_kindList`) built only when `qobject_cast<SWMMModelLayer*>(layer)` succeeds — single-kind layers (GIS / mesh / raster) skip the pane entirely. Populated with 11 selectable rows (Junctions / Outfalls / Storage / Dividers / Conduits / Pumps / Orifices / Weirs / Outlets / Subcatchments / Rain Gages) plus 3 non-selectable bold separators (`── Nodes ──`, `── Links ──`, `── Areal ──`) for scannability. Default selection = `CatJunctions` (configurable via the new 3-arg ctor — see Phase 8.13.41-LT below). `currentRowChanged` → new `onKindChanged(int)` slot that updates `m_activeKind` and re-reads form fields from the now-active kind's renderer via `readFromLayer()`. The dialog also resizes to 820×540 (from 700×540) to accommodate the left pane without squeezing the right-pane tabs.
- ✅ **Phase 8.13.42 — Right-pane scoping + `Apply to all kinds` button (shipped 2026-05-24)**: New `m_activeKind` member (-1 = layer-scope, 0..10 = kind ordinal) scopes every read / write. `readFromLayer()` branches: kind-scoped → reads from `swmm->kindRenderer(activeKind)` (Slice 2-α slot) + also reads `swmm->linkArrowsEnabled(activeKind)` into the Arrows tab; layer-scoped → existing `currentRendererOf(layer)` path. `applyToLayer()` similarly branches: kind-scoped calls a new `applyCurrentTabToKind(activeKind)` helper that builds a renderer from the current tab via the extracted `buildRendererFromTabs()` free helper and routes it through `swmm->setKindRenderer(cat, ...)`; layer-scoped path unchanged. **Arrows tab special-cased**: when the active tab is Arrows and the dialog is kind-scoped, Apply writes through to `setLinkArrowsEnabled(cat, on)` instead of building a renderer. New `[ Apply to all kinds ]` button rendered to the left of the OK/Cancel/Apply button box (only visible when `isKindScoped()`) — iterates `0..NumCategories-1` calling `applyCurrentTabToKind` for each, so a Graduated config replicates to every kind at once.
- ✅ **Phase 8.13.43 — Per-kind defaults from Slice 2-α (shipped 2026-05-24)**: The "first-open seeds from compile-time defaults" promise is already provided by `SWMMModelLayer`'s ctor (Slice 2-α populates `m_kindRenderers[NumCategories]` from the existing `SWMMElementSymbol` glyphs), so the dialog gets sensible per-kind state without any extra seeding logic. `[ Reset Kind to Defaults ]` per-tab buttons deferred — the kind-row right-click menu's "Reset Kind to Defaults" item (Slice BI-MK.LT) already provides this entry point at the tree level.
- ✅ **Phase 8.13.41-LT — 3-arg constructor for context-menu pre-scope (shipped 2026-05-24)**: New `SymbologyDialog(layer, kindOrdinal, rendererId, parent)` overload sets `m_activeKind` from the kindOrdinal arg and (post-construction) flips the right-pane tab to the index matching `rendererId` ("single" → tab 0, "graduated" → tab 1, "categorized" → tab 2). The BI-MK.LT `SWMMVis::onLayerKindStyleRequested` slot now routes the empty-rendererId case ("Set Style…" menu item) through this overload so the user lands on a kind-scoped, current-renderer-class-matched dialog. **Graduated tab's Ramp combo** updated to enumerate `RasterColorRamp::builtinNames()` (the 13 Slice BB-α built-ins: Grayscale / Viridis / Plasma / Magma / Inferno / Cividis / Turbo / RdBu / RdYlGn / Spectral / BrBG / Legacy SWMM 5-interval / Legacy SWMM pollutant). `buildRendererFromTabs` calls `RasterColorRamp::builtin(name)` to materialise the ramp, sets `IntervalBinner` to `EqualInterval` with the user-picked bin count, and routes through `GraduatedRenderer::setRamp/setBinner` (the new Slice BB-α API).
- 🔧 **Deferred from this slice (per scope cut)**:
  - **Size/width-by-attribute controls** (Phase 8.13.43-α below) — `DataDefinedScalar` infrastructure not built; Single tab still has only static size/width spinboxes.
  - **Per-tab `[ Reset Kind to Defaults ]` button** — kind-row context-menu equivalent (Slice BI-MK.LT) covers the use case.
  - **Categorized per-value list editor** — defers to Slice BI.3-α (next).
  - **Live preview swatch + sample mini-map** in each tab — deferred to follow-up polish.
- ✅ **Phase 8.13.43-α — Size / width controls in Single + Graduated tabs (shipped 2026-05-24)**: Ships the full data-defined size pipeline end-to-end. **(1) Data type** — new `include/render/datadefined.h` defines `DataDefinedScalar { attribute, valueMin/Max, outMin/Max, curve (Linear/Sqrt/Log) }` with `evaluate(value)` (clamps + curve + linear-map), `isValid()` (non-empty attribute + finite ranges), JSON round-trip. 11-case `test_datadefinedscalar.cpp` covers curve correctness (Linear midpoint, Sqrt high-end compression, Log endpoints + monotonicity), clamping above/below range, NaN defensive default, degenerate input-range fallback, isValid rejection, JSON round-trip. **(2) Renderer extensions** — `SingleSymbolRenderer` gains `setSizeData(DataDefinedScalar)` + member `m_sizeData`; `symbolFor` evaluates the override against `attrs[m_sizeData.attribute]` and writes the resolved scalar into `props["size"]` AND `props["width"]` (whichever exists in the style). `GraduatedRenderer` gains `setOutputColorEnabled(bool)` / `setOutputSizeEnabled(bool)` / `setOutputSizeRange(min, max)` + `sizeForBin(int)` helper (linear interpolation across bin indices); `symbolFor` honours both axes independently. JSON round-trip extended on both renderers (`sizeData` on Single, `outputColorEnabled / outputSizeEnabled / outputSizeMin / outputSizeMax` on Graduated). **(3) Layer cache** — `SWMMModelLayer` gains parallel `m_kindFeatureSizes[NumCategories]` cache + `featureSize(c, idx)` accessor (negative sentinel = no override). `rebuildKindFeatureColors` extended to extract per-feature size from each `renderer->symbolFor` output; correctly flags overrides as active when EITHER per-feature colour OR per-feature size varies (so SingleSymbol + sizeData triggers the override paint path without needing a non-Single renderer). **(4) Painter integration** — node bucket loop (Junction/Outfall/Storage/Divider) and rain-gage bucket loop both read `featureSize(c, i)` per feature when overrides are active and scale the glyph radius accordingly (`r_eff = featureSize * 0.5 * invViewScale` when positive, else fall back to kind's static `markerRadius`). Link width-by-attribute deferred to a follow-up (would require sub-bucketing the sub-bucketing-by-colour idiom by (color, width) tuples — meaningful complexity for marginal value); subcatchment polygon outline-width deferred similarly. **(5) Dialog UI** — Single tab gains 7 new controls (`Size by attribute` checkbox + Attribute editable-combo + Value-range / Size-range spinbox pairs + Curve combo) revealed via `setEnabled(true)` when the checkbox toggles; defaults to attribute candidates `maxDepth/invertElev/geom1/maxFlow/area/length`. Graduated tab gains an `Output axes:` row with `[x] Color` (default on) + `[ ] Size` (default off) independent checkboxes. New `RenderConfig` struct encapsulates 13 dialog fields so `buildRendererFromTabs` stays a single small helper instead of a long arg list; both `applyCurrentTabToKind` and `applyToLayer` construct the config from member widgets. `readFromLayer` surfaces both the SingleSymbol `sizeData` round-trip and the Graduated output-axis toggles back into the form fields on dialog open. **Files added**: `include/render/datadefined.h` + `src/render/datadefined.cpp` + `tests/gui/test_datadefinedscalar.cpp`. **Files extended**: 8 (graduated/singlesymbol renderer h+cpp, swmmmodellayer h+cpp, swmmlayeritem.cpp, symbologydialog h+cpp). Tests stayed green (`test_ifeaturerenderer` 26 cases, `test_multikindrenderer` 16, `test_colorramp` 12, `test_intervalbinner` 8, `test_datadefinedscalar` 11 NEW, `test_irasterrenderer` 22 — total 95 cases). **Deferred / known gaps**: link width-by-attribute and subcatchment outline-width-by-attribute would require additional painter sub-bucketing — currently the painter for these kinds reads the kind's static pen, not per-feature; the renderer / dialog config persists correctly but those kinds visually fall back to the static width until the painter follow-up lands. "Use full range" button to auto-fill valueMin/valueMax from a layer scan is also deferred — the user types ranges manually for now.
>
> **2026-05-25 follow-up**: link width-by-attribute is **partially unblocked** by Slice BI-MK.4-OUT.2's per-feature size cache infrastructure (the same cache shape: per-kind × per-feature `QVector<double>`). The painter still needs cache-driven extension for link width — the existing color-sub-bucketing-by-`QRgb`-key idiom in the link bucket loop would extend to a (color, size) tuple key, where each unique tuple becomes its own batched `drawLines` call. ~50 lines of painter changes. Same idiom applies to subcatchment outline width. Treat as a 🔧 painter-extension follow-up rather than a fresh data-plumbing slice — the renderer + dialog already produce the right output values; only the painter needs to consume them.
- **Phase 8.13.41 — `SymbologyDialog` left-pane layout**: New `QListWidget` (`m_kindList`) in a 130-px-wide left pane built only when `qobject_cast<SWMMModelLayer*>(layer)` succeeds. Populated with 11 rows (icon + label) plus 3 non-selectable separator rows (`──── Nodes ────`, `──── Links ────`, `──── Areal ────`). Default selection = `CatJunctions`. `currentItemChanged` rebinds the right-pane tabs to `multiRenderer->rendererFor(activeKind)` via a new private slot `onKindChanged(int)`. Existing single-kind code path (GIS / mesh / WCS layers) skips the left pane and renders the right pane directly.
- **Phase 8.13.42 — Right-pane scoping + `Apply to all kinds` button**: All existing tabs (Single / Graduated / Categorized / Labels / Arrows) gain a `m_activeKind` member that scopes every read / write to that kind. New `[ Apply to all kinds ]` button under the right-pane tab strip writes the active right-pane config into every kind's renderer at once (calls `multiRenderer->setRendererFor(k, currentTabConfig.clone())` for each `k` in `Category`). Layer-scope `Apply` / `OK` / `Cancel` buttons unchanged — they commit / discard the staged edits across all kinds.
- **Phase 8.13.43 — Sensible defaults per kind**: First-open of the dialog seeds each kind's `MultiKindRenderer` slot with a `SingleSymbolRenderer` reflecting the kind's existing hardcoded glyph (`SWMMElementSymbol` defaults — circle for Junctions, square for Storage, triangle for Outfalls, line for Conduits, etc.). This means first-open shows visually the same as today; user edits diverge from there. A `[ Reset kind to defaults ]` button per right-pane tab restores the kind's compiled defaults.
- **Files**: new `include/render/multikindrenderer.{h,cpp}`; touches `include/ui/dialogs/symbologydialog.h` + `src/ui/dialogs/symbologydialog.cpp` (left-pane construction + kind scoping + Apply-to-all button), `include/render/ifeaturerenderer.h` (new `FeatureRef::kind()` accessor passed through to `symbolFor`), `include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h` (replace per-kind `SWMMElementSymbol` getters with `MultiKindRenderer` indirection via the existing renderer plumbing from Phase 8.13.6.5).
- **Engine APIs**: none.
- **Tests**: `test_multikindrenderer.cpp` (8 cases — empty, single kind, all 11 kinds, JSON round-trip, dispatch by kind, fallback to compiled default, legend section aggregation, clone independence). `test_symbologydialog_kindpicker.cpp` (5 cases — left pane builds for SWMMModelLayer, hidden for GIS layer, selection re-binds tabs, Apply writes selected kind only, Apply-to-all writes every kind).
- **Manual**: extend `docs/manual/21_symbology.md` with screenshots of the left-pane picker and the per-kind workflow; document the Apply-to-all button.
