### §P.BI-MK.3 — New Slice **BI-MK.3** definition (insert after BI-MK.2)

#### 🔧 Slice BI-MK.3 — `.oswp` persistence for per-layer renderer (Phase 8.13.46) — **first cut shipped 2026-05-22**

Generalized at first-ship from "per-kind renderer block" to **whole-renderer JSON per layer** because every concrete renderer (Single / Graduated / Categorized / Rule / MultiKind) round-trips via the same `IFeatureRenderer::toJson/fromJson` interface — duplicating logic per renderer type would have been busywork. MultiKindRenderer's per-kind dict is carried inside its own `toJson()` payload, so a single `"renderer"` key per layer covers the §N.14 use case once BI-MK.1.41 swaps the SWMMModelLayer default to a MultiKindRenderer.

- ✅ **Phase 8.13.46 — `ProjectSerializer` per-layer renderer round-trip** *(shipped 2026-05-22, first cut: `SWMMModelLayer` only)*: Added `kRenderer = "renderer"` key constant + a local `makeRendererFromJson(QJsonObject)` factory in `projectserializer.cpp` that dispatches on the renderer's `"id"` discriminator (`"single"` / `"graduated"` / `"categorized"` / `"rule"` / `"multikind"`). Serialize side appends `layerObj[kRenderer] = layer->renderer()->toJson()` right after the existing `hiddenObjects` block — additive, no schema version bump, older readers silently ignore the unknown key. Restore side calls `layer->setRenderer(makeRendererFromJson(...))` after the existing `hiddenObjects` restore — null factory result (unknown id, missing payload) is silently swallowed by `setRenderer`'s own contract so the layer keeps its compiled default. New includes pulled in for the factory: `render/ifeaturerenderer.h`, `render/multikindrenderer.h`, and the four concrete renderer headers. ~50 lines touched in `src/project/projectserializer.cpp`. Build green.
- ⏸️ **Phase 8.13.46-followup — extend to result-layer + 2D result-layer renderer persistence**: `SWMMResultsLayer` entries today serialize as bare path strings in the `resultLayers` array. Need to either (a) change array entries to objects `{path, renderer}` (back-compat by accepting both string and object forms in restore), or (b) add a parallel `resultLayerRenderers` map keyed by path. Same question for `SWMM2DResultsLayer` (no serialization at all today). Deferred to a follow-up sub-slice once the result-layers' renderer use is more settled (CF.MVP-fix work in flight per user's WIP — `LayerPropertiesDialog::buildResultsStylingTab` adds Color-ramp / Filled bands / Iso-lines controls for `SWMM2DResultsLayer`).
- **Engine APIs**: none.
- **Tests**: deferred (the round-trip is exercised indirectly by AZ.3.7's mesh round-trip + future BI-MK.1.41 manual save-reload verification once MultiKindRenderer wiring lands on `SWMMModelLayer`). A formal `test_projectserializer_renderer.cpp` (round-trip per concrete renderer type + factory-rejects-unknown-id + missing-key-keeps-default) should ship alongside the .41 wiring so it can exercise an actually-mutated renderer end-to-end.
- **Manual**: footnote in `docs/manual/21_symbology.md` that per-layer styles persist in `.oswp` (deferred until BI-MK.1.41 ships and the dialog actually lets users mutate renderers).
- **Dependencies**: BI-MK.1.40 (MultiKindRenderer + factory contract — shipped), X (`.oswp` schema).
- **Deferred**: per-kind style-import/export via `.swmm-style.json` (one entry per kind in the JSON; lands with BB Phase 8.6.13 once it covers the multi-kind case); result-layer + 2D-result-layer renderer persistence (see followup bullet).

### §P.BI-MK.LT — New Slice **BI-MK.LT** definition (insert after BI-MK.3) — **drafted 2026-05-24, subsumes BI-MK.2**

#### ✅ Slice BI-MK.LT — 3-level layer tree + per-sub-row right-click menu for multi-kind layers (Phase 8.13.47–49) — **shipped 2026-05-24**

**What landed**: `LayerTreeModel` extended to 3 levels using a `QHash<OpenSWMMVisLayer*, std::array<KindRow, 11>> m_kindRowStorage` + parallel `QSet<const void*> m_kindRowPtrSet` for O(1) discriminator checks (avoids scanning storage in `data()` / `parent()` per redraw). KindRow contains `{layer*, kindOrdinal}` and its address is the index `internalPointer` — stable across the model lifetime because `std::array` doesn't reallocate. Three new public helpers — `isKindIndex`, `kindParentLayer`, `kindOrdinal` — added for the context-menu code to consume. `index/parent/rowCount/data/setData/flags/layerForIndex/isCategoryIndex` all extended to honour the third level. Kind-row check-state toggles `SWMMModelLayer::setCategoryVisible(c, on)`. Right-click on a kind sub-row now opens a kind-scoped context menu with: **Zoom to Kind** (disabled v1 — no per-kind extent API yet), **Show/Hide *kind***, **Style ▸ Single symbol / Graduated (numeric) / Categorized (string / enum) / Rule-based (disabled v1)**, **Show flow arrows** (checkable, link kinds only — drives the Phase 8.13.8-mini toggle from BI-MK.LT instead of needing the dialog), **Set Style…**, **Reset *kind* to Defaults**. Each Style submenu item emits the new `layerKindStyleRequested(layer, kindOrdinal, rendererId)` signal. `SWMMVis::onLayerKindStyleRequested` swaps the kind's renderer class with sensible defaults — `"single"` calls `resetKindRendererToDefaults(c)`; `"graduated"` installs a `GraduatedRenderer` with a per-kind default `classifyAttribute` (maxDepth for nodes/storage, geom1 for conduits, maxFlow for active links, area for subcatchments) + Viridis ramp + EqualInterval 5-bin binner; `"categorized"` installs a `CategorizedRenderer` keyed on `"tag"`; empty `rendererId` falls back to opening the layer-scope `SymbologyDialog` (BI-MK.1 dialog still deferred). Each path ends with `MapCanvas::invalidate(Scene)` so the user sees the change immediately. **Visibility-checkbox toggle** path: per-kind checkbox in the tree drives `setCategoryVisible` which feeds the existing `hiddenCategoryCount` machinery — no new persistence keys needed. **Files**: `include/ui/panels/layertreepanel.h` (KindRow struct + kKindsPerSwmmModelLayer constant + m_kindRowStorage + m_kindRowPtrSet + 3 new public methods + new signal `layerKindStyleRequested`); `src/ui/panels/layertreepanel.cpp` (~150 lines: rebuildKindRows, model-method extensions, kind-row branch in onContextMenuRequested); `include/swmmvis.h` (forward-decl OpenSWMMVisLayer + new slot decl); `src/swmmvis.cpp` (~90 lines: connect + onLayerKindStyleRequested impl + 6 new render includes). **Tests**: existing render-test sweep (84 cases) stayed green; layertreemodel test parked alongside swmmvis_core extraction per existing comment in tests/gui/CMakeLists.txt — no new tests added in this slice. **Manual verification**: SWMMVis builds clean, launches with snoopy.inp; sub-row visibility + right-click menu surface drives end-to-end (single symbol roundtrips through write-through to legacy SWMMElementSymbol; graduated/categorized roundtrip through per-feature override cache from Phase 8.13.6.4; flow arrows toggle drives Phase 8.13.8-mini paint pass). **Deferred / known gaps**: kind icons currently a generic Layers glyph — replace with `LegendSymbolItem` swatch from the kind's renderer when a follow-up commit lands; per-kind "Zoom to Kind" requires a new `SWMMModelLayer::kindExtent(Category)` accessor; "Show Only This Kind" / "Show All Kinds" group-toggle convenience items deferred (single-row toggle covers basic case).

#### 🔧 Slice BI-MK.LT — original drafted spec (preserved below for archaeology):

The user's earlier ask ("sub-layers of visual element categories") and the §N.14.2 entry pathway #1 ("Layer-tree → category sub-row → right-click → Set Style…") need a real three-level tree, not just a signal that wires onto a non-existent sub-row. BI-MK.LT delivers the missing third level under `SWMMModelLayer` and **subsumes BI-MK.2** (signal-only entry point).

- **Phase 8.13.47 — `LayerTreeModel` 3-level extension**: `LayerTreeModel::rowCount(parent)` returns 11 when parent is a `SWMMModelLayer` row; new `enum class RowKind { Category, Layer, Kind };` discriminator on internal-pointer nodes. Kind sub-rows in fixed order (Junctions / Outfalls / Storage / Dividers / Conduits / Pumps / Orifices / Weirs / Outlets / Subcatchments / RainGages); icon per kind drawn via `LegendSymbolItem` from the kind's current renderer (updates live on `rendererChanged`). Per-sub-row visibility checkbox toggles the existing per-kind hidden-count machinery (`SWMMModelLayer::setCategoryVisible(int kindOrdinal, bool)` — add the setter if not already present, delegating to the per-category visibility tracking already in `swmmmodellayer.h`). Single-kind layers (GIS / mesh / WCS) skip the third level — `rowCount(layerIndex)` returns 0. **No new `.oswp` keys** — per-kind visibility piggy-backs on the existing `hiddenObjects` block.
- **Phase 8.13.48 — `LayerTreePanel` context menu on Kind rows**: `onContextMenuRequested` grows a third branch for Kind rows with this layout:
  ```
  Zoom to Kind
  Show Only This Kind   |   Show All Kinds
  ─────────────────────────────────────
  Style                              ►
     ▸ Single symbol
     ▸ Graduated   (numeric attribute)
     ▸ Categorized (string / enum attribute)
     ▸ Rule-based                       [disabled v1]
  ─────────────────────────────────────
  Show flow arrows           [checkbox] (link kinds only)
  ─────────────────────────────────────
  Set Style…
  Reset Kind to Defaults
  Properties…
  ```
  Each Style item emits a new signal `void layerKindStyleRequested(OpenSWMMVisLayer *layer, int kindOrdinal, QString rendererId)`. The `rendererId` parameter is the discriminator string the dialog uses to pre-select the matching right-pane tab (`"single"` / `"graduated"` / `"categorized"` / `"rule"`). `Set Style…` emits with `rendererId=""` (no class change — opens dialog without switching).
- **Phase 8.13.49 — `SWMMVis` slot wiring**: `SWMMVis::onLayerKindStyleRequested(layer, kindOrdinal, rendererId)` (a) when `rendererId` is non-empty, installs the matching renderer class (`SingleSymbolRenderer` / `GraduatedRenderer` / `CategorizedRenderer`) on the kind's `MultiKindRenderer` slot, preserving the kind's current color/glyph defaults where applicable; (b) opens `SymbologyDialog(layer, kindOrdinal, rendererId, this)` (new constructor overload — replaces the BI-MK.2 spec's two-arg overload with a three-arg version) so the dialog pre-scopes to the kind AND pre-selects the right-pane tab. The existing layer-row `Set Style…` continues through the layer-scope `layerStyleRequested(layer)` signal — backward-compatible. **Show flow arrows** toggle (link kinds only) inspects the kind's symbol-layer stack, adds or removes a `MarkerLine` (per Phase 8.13.8-α), and emits `rendererChanged`.
- **Files**: `include/ui/panels/layertreepanel.h` + `.cpp` (3-level model, new signal, new context-menu actions for Kind rows), `include/swmmvis.h` + `src/swmmvis.cpp` (`onLayerKindStyleRequested` slot — three-arg form), `include/layers/swmmmodellayer.h` + `.cpp` (`setCategoryVisible` setter if missing), `include/ui/dialogs/symbologydialog.h` + `.cpp` (new three-arg ctor overload that pre-selects the right-pane tab).
- **Engine APIs**: none.
- **Tests**: `test_layertree_kindrows.cpp` (8 cases — model exposes 11 sub-rows under SWMMModelLayer, GIS layer has 0 sub-rows, kind icon updates on rendererChanged, visibility checkbox toggles category visible flag, context menu items emit signal with correct rendererId, "Show flow arrows" toggles MarkerLine, "Show only this kind" hides others, model re-emits when a kind's renderer changes). Existing `test_symbologydialog_kindpicker.cpp` extended to verify the three-arg ctor pre-selects the right tab.
- **Manual**: extend `docs/manual/21_symbology.md` with the 3-level tree + per-kind right-click workflow.
- **Dependencies**: BI-MK.1 Phases 8.13.41-43 (dialog has the kind-picker pane), BI Phase 8.13.6.4 (per-kind renderer drives paint).
- **Deferred**: drag-from-Kind-row to dialog as a stretch idiom; per-kind ordering customization within the tree (current order is fixed).
- **Subsumes**: ~~BI-MK.2~~ (signal-only entry point — superseded; BI-MK.LT is the richer 3-level-tree replacement).

### §P.BI-MK.4-OUT — New Slice **BI-MK.4-OUT** definition (insert after BI-MK.LT2) — **drafted 2026-05-25, supersedes BI-MK.4 (BLOCKED) per §N.14 status correction**

#### 🔧 Slice BI-MK.4-OUT — `SWMMResultsLayer` per-kind renderer + per-feature override cache + paint refactor (Phase 8.13.6.4-OUT)

Parallel of Slice 2-α + Phase 8.13.6.4 + Phase 8.13.43-α for the output layer. End-to-end the user can right-click any of the 11 sub-rows on an output layer and pick Graduated → bin-mapped color + size driven by the active result variable per frame.

- **Phase 8.13.6.4-OUT.1 — Per-kind renderer slots on `SWMMResultsLayer`**: Add to `SWMMResultsLayer` ([include/layers/swmmresultslayer.h](../include/layers/swmmresultslayer.h)):
  - `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<IFeatureRenderer>> m_kindRenderers` (size `NumCategories`, indexed by `SWMMModelLayer::Category` — reuses the same enum + `kindKey(c)` helper).
  - Public API mirroring SWMMModelLayer's: `IFeatureRenderer *kindRenderer(Category)`, `void setKindRenderer(Category, std::unique_ptr<IFeatureRenderer>)`, `void resetKindRendererToDefaults(Category)`. Setter triggers `rebuildKindFeatureOverrides(c)` + emits `rendererChanged()` + `repaintRequested()`.
  - Seed defaults in the ctor: each slot gets a `GraduatedRenderer` with `classifyAttribute = first-variable-for-kind` (Junctions/Outfalls/Storage/Dividers → "depth"; Conduits/Pumps/Orifices/Weirs/Outlets → "flow"; Subcatchments → "runoff"; RainGages → "intensity") + Viridis ramp + `IntervalBinner` (EqualInterval, 5 bins).
- **Phase 8.13.6.4-OUT.2 — Per-feature override cache**: `QVector<QColor> m_kindFeatureColors[NumCategories]` + `QVector<double> m_kindFeatureSizes[NumCategories]` + `bool m_kindUsesOverrides[NumCategories]` — same shape as the SWMMModelLayer cache from Slice 2-α / Phase 8.13.43-α. New `rebuildKindFeatureOverrides(Category)` walks the kind's features, reads each feature's current result value from the existing `m_nodeResults` / `m_linkResults` / `m_subcatchResults` caches keyed by `kindRenderer(c)->classifyAttribute()`, builds an `attrs` map with one entry (`attrs[classifyAttribute] = resultValue`), calls `kindRenderer(c)->symbolFor(featureRef, attrs)`, extracts color from `props["color"]` and size from `props["size"]` / `props["width"]`.
- **Phase 8.13.6.4-OUT.3 — Animation hook**: Extend `SWMMResultsLayer::fetchResultsForStep` ([src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp:568](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp)). After the result-value caches refresh on `setVariable / setCurrentPeriod / animation tick`, call `rebuildKindFeatureOverrides(c)` for every kind in the scope of the active variable (Nodes scope → 4 kinds; Links scope → 5 kinds; Subcatch scope → 1 kind). This makes animation drive both color AND size per frame automatically, matching Phase 8.13.43-α's behaviour on the model layer.
- **Phase 8.13.6.4-OUT.4 — Paint loop refactor**: Refactor `populateScene`'s 3 paint branches at [src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp:730 (nodes) / 774 (links) / 825 (subcatchments)](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp). When `kindUsesOverrides(c)` is true: read per-feature `featureColor(c, idx) + featureSize(c, idx)` from the cache; scale node glyph radius / link line width / subcatchment polygon outline by `featureSize / staticSize`. When overrides off: fall back to today's `m_colorRamp.colorForValue(value)` direct path. Selection-highlight passes unchanged.
- **Phase 8.13.6.4-OUT.5 — JSON persistence**: Extend `ProjectSerializer`'s existing `kRenderer = "renderer"` per-layer round-trip ([src/project/projectserializer.cpp](../src/project/projectserializer.cpp)) to also handle `SWMMResultsLayer`'s 11 per-kind renderer slots. Add a `"kindRenderers": {"Junctions": {...}, "Conduits": {...}, ...}` object on each `SWMMResultsLayer` session record (additive; older readers ignore it). `setKindRenderer` is the restore-side entry point.
- **Files**: extends [include/layers/swmmresultslayer.h](../include/layers/swmmresultslayer.h) (~50 lines: cache fields + 5 new public methods + signal); [src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp) (~180 lines: seed defaults in ctor + rebuildKindFeatureOverrides + paint refactor + fetchResultsForStep hook); [src/project/projectserializer.cpp](../src/project/projectserializer.cpp) (~30 lines: per-kind renderer JSON).

Tests reuse `SWMMModelLayer::kindKey` for assertions on the kind names.

### §P.BJ.2 — New Slice **BJ.2** definition (insert after Slice BJ block, before Slice BK)

> **Lite cut shipped 2026-05-22 — mesh isolines only.** First-cut delivery covers the marching-triangles algorithm + a Pass 3 in `SWMM2DMeshQSGRenderer` that renders bed-elevation contour lines, controlled by `SWMM2DMeshLayer::showContours()`, `contourIntervalCount()` (default 10 evenly-spaced between zMin and zMax), `contourColor()`, `contourLineWidth()`. UI is a new **Contours (bed elevation)** group on the Mesh tab with a show-checkbox, intervals spinbox, colour picker (alpha-aware) and width spinbox. Files added: `include/contour/marchingtriangles.h` (header-only templated algorithm + `evenlySpacedLevels` helper), `tests/gui/test_marchingtriangles.cpp` (13 self-contained QtTest cases: case enumeration for all 6 non-trivial sign permutations + degenerate-triangle skip + multi-level + level-out-of-range early-out + 2-triangle independence + `evenlySpacedLevels` boundary cases — **13/13 green**). Files touched: `include/layers/swmm2dmeshlayer.h`, `src/layers/swmm2dmeshlayer.cpp`, `src/map/swmm2dmeshqsgrenderer.cpp` (Pass 3 added before transform; node tree grew to 4 children with empty-uploads in the cull early-out), `include/ui/dialogs/layerpropertiesdialog.h`, `src/ui/dialogs/layerpropertiesdialog.cpp`, `tests/gui/CMakeLists.txt`. Defaults: `showContours=false` (off by default — opt-in), `intervals=10`, `color=#C8 0x1a1a1a` (near-black 78% opacity), `width=1.0 px`. Defers to BJ.2 full: filled isobands (polygonisation between adjacent levels), per-level colour ramp (waits for BB ColorRamp + `IntervalBinner`), marching-squares for raster DEM, contour labels (waits for BI.2 `LabelExpression` + along-line placement), `MeshResultContourSource` for time-varying depth/Vmag/HGL (waits for CF.2.7 `SWMM2DResultVariable` enum), `ContourEditorPanel` as a reusable widget for the Styling Dock, viewport culling + LOD decimation (current Snoopy mesh ~5K tris × 10 levels is comfortable), `.oswp` persistence (bundled with AZ.3.7 mesh-layer block).

> **Filled-bands cut shipped 2026-05-22 — extends the lite cut.** Adds `marchingTrianglesIsobands` via Sutherland-Hodgman triangle-vs-half-plane clipping (50 lines in `include/contour/marchingtriangles.h`; convex-polygon output, ≤ 5 vertices, suitable for fan triangulation). Also adds `evenlySpacedLevelsInclusive` helper (N+1 break levels including endpoints, needed by the filled path) and `viridisAt` (5-stop Viridis palette sampler) as the temporary categorical colour source until Slice BB ships `ColorRamp`. New layer params on `SWMM2DMeshLayer`: `filledContours()` / `setFilledContours(bool)` (default `false`), `filledContoursOpacity()` / `setFilledContoursOpacity(double)` (default `0.55`). QSG renderer grows a 5th node — **Pass 4 isoband fills** — z-ordered between Pass 1 (hillshade) and Pass 2 (edges) so the underlying hillshade shows through the alpha and the wireframe + isolines stay crisp on top. Per-band colour computed by `viridisAt((bandIndex + 0.5) / nBands)` so adjacent bands are visually distinguishable; alpha from the layer's opacity setting. UI extension: two new rows in the existing **Contours** group on the Mesh tab — **Filled bands (Viridis palette)** checkbox + **Fill opacity** spinbox. Persistence extended in AZ.3.7's `meshLayers[].contours` block with `filled` + `filledOpacity` keys (additive, no schema bump). Tests: 10 new cases in `test_marchingtriangles.cpp` covering single-band full-coverage / single-band below-range / single-band partial / multi-band tiling / degenerate-triangle skip / single-level-empty / band-index-assignment + `evenlySpacedLevelsInclusive` boundary cases — **23/23 green**. Still defers (vs. BJ.2 full): user-pickable colour ramp (BB), per-band individual colour pickers (BB editor), raster marching-squares, contour labels (BI.2), result-attribute isobands (CF.MVP must ship `SWMM2DResultsLayer` first — currently absent from code despite the plan claiming it shipped; see §P.CF.MVP follow-up note below).

#### ⏳ Slice BJ.2 — Contour generator (raster + mesh, filled isobands + isolines + labels) (Phase 8.14.10–14)

Single contour engine driving three data sources per §N.6. Marching-squares for grids, marching-triangles for unstructured meshes; identical output shape (`ContourPolygonSet` + `ContourLineSet`) and identical labelling. Renders into a per-source `QGraphicsItem` z-ordered above the base fill, below labels. Live during animation for `SWMM2DResultsLayer` consumers.

- **Phase 8.14.10 — `IContourSource` + algorithms**: New `include/contour/icontoursource.h` per §N.6 signature. Two implementations: `include/contour/marchingsquares.{h,cpp}` (raster, 16-case LUT, sub-pixel suppression at low zoom), `include/contour/marchingtriangles.{h,cpp}` (mesh, 8-case LUT, piecewise-linear in-triangle interpolation). Both emit a `ContourResult { QVector<ContourBand> bands; QVector<ContourLine> lines; }`. Three concrete sources: `RasterContourSource` (wraps `GISRasterLayer`), `MeshBedContourSource` (wraps `SWMM2DMeshLayer` bed-z), `MeshResultContourSource` (wraps `SWMM2DResultsLayer` for current variable at current tick).
- **Phase 8.14.11 — `ContourSpec` + persistence**: Per §N.6 struct in `include/contour/contourspec.h`. Stored per (layer, dataSourceKey) in `.oswp` under `"contours": { "bedZ": {...}, "depth": {...} }`. `IntervalBinner` + `ColorRamp` are the same types as BB; `LabelExpression` + `LabelHalo` are the same as BI.2 — no parallel types.
- **Phase 8.14.12 — `ContourGraphicsItem` + viewport culling + LOD**: New `include/contour/contourgraphicsitem.{h,cpp}`. Per `paint()`: if `boundingRect()` does not intersect `exposedRect`, return early; if zoom-scale below `ContourSpec::minZoomToShow`, return early; else iterate `bands` (clipped to exposedRect) then `lines`. LOD: at zoom-out, sub-pixel segments are coalesced into the next-larger band before paint. `QtConcurrent::map` parallelism for marching-triangles batching by tile (each tile = a triangle range). Target: 1 M tris @ 60 fps on M2 Pro (asserted by perf test).
- **Phase 8.14.13 — `ContourEditorPanel` (Styling Dock tab)**: New `include/ui/widgets/contoureditorpanel.{h,cpp}`. Data-source picker (when layer offers multiple — e.g. `SWMM2DResultsLayer` offers bed + depth + vmag + HGL), mode combo, binning combo (reuses BB widget), interval-count or manual-break editor, ramp picker (reuses BB), per-line pen, label expression editor (reuses BI.2's editor) + format + halo, scale-visible range. Live preview thumbnail. Hosted in Styling Dock via `LayerStyleEditorFactory`; also reachable from right-click → "Edit Contours…" as a modal.
- **Phase 8.14.14 — Animation wiring for mesh result contours**: `SWMM2DResultsLayer::currentTimeChanged` triggers `MeshResultContourSource::invalidate()` → owning `ContourGraphicsItem::update()`. Re-computation is incremental: only the scalar field changes per tick, the triangulation is constant — `MarchingTriangles` caches the triangle list and recomputes only edge intersections.
- **Files**: new `include/contour/{icontoursource,marchingsquares,marchingtriangles,contourspec,contourgraphicsitem,contourbuilder}.{h,cpp}`, `include/contour/sources/{rastercontoursource,meshbedcontoursource,meshresultcontoursource}.{h,cpp}`, `include/ui/widgets/contoureditorpanel.{h,cpp}`; touches `GISRasterLayer`, `SWMM2DMeshLayer`, `SWMM2DResultsLayer` to register their contour sources + add `contourSpecs()` accessor; touches `ProjectSerializer` for `.oswp` round-trip.
- **Engine APIs**: none for raster + bed. For mesh-result velocity, consumes CF-04 (`swmm_2d_get_velocity_bulk`) via the same `SWMM2DResultsLayer::sampleAttribute` indirection — falls back to CF.2.3 GUI-side RT0 when the engine symbol is unresolved.
- **Tests**: `test_marchingsquares.cpp` (8 cases — single-cell saddle, monotonic ramp, NaN handling, sub-pixel suppression, ascending vs descending data, single-value collapse, golden image at 100×100, golden image at 1024×1024), `test_marchingtriangles.cpp` (10 cases — equilateral / right / degenerate triangle, edge-case all-equal / one-below-only / two-below, golden image on Snoopy mesh, RT0 in-triangle interpolation parity vs hand-calc, label-position parity), `test_contourspec.cpp` (4 cases — JSON round-trip per source kind, mode round-trip, label-format round-trip, missing-source-on-apply graceful skip), `test_contoureditorpanel.cpp` (5 cases — data-source picker round-trip, mode toggle, binning combo wired, label expression round-trip, live preview update), `test_contour_animation.cpp` (3 cases — recompute on `currentTimeChanged`, no recompute on `geometryChanged`, fps target on 100k-tri mesh).
- **Manual**: new `docs/manual/25_contours.md` — algorithm catalogue, performance notes, labelling examples, raster vs mesh idioms.
- **Dependencies**: BB (`ColorRamp`, `IntervalBinner`, `LegendItemFormat`), BI Phase 8.13.6 (paint-loop refactor for layer integration), BI.2 (`LabelExpression`, `LabelHalo`, `LabelPlacement::AlongLine`), AU (raster + mesh layers), CF.MVP (mesh result layer existence).
- **Deferred**: BJ.2-x — contour smoothing (Catmull-Rom or Chaikin) for visually crisp lines on coarse meshes; contour-driven flow-arrow placement (orthogonal to contour gradient); CGAL-based 2D natural-neighbour interpolation for irregular point data (1D node/link attribute contours — explicitly out of v1 scope per user 2026-05-22 answer).

### §P.CF.2 — Slice CF.2 amendment (append to CF.2.1 — Engine: bulk flux + edge geometry — as Phase CF.2.1b)

> **Amendment 2026-05-22 (§N integration — engine-side velocity is canonical, GUI RT0 becomes fallback):**
>
> - **Phase CF.2.1b — Engine cell-velocity bulk (`swmm_2d_get_velocity_bulk`, engine gap CF-04)**: New engine entry point `int swmm_2d_get_velocity_bulk(SWMM_Engine engine, double* vx_vy)` returning per-triangle cell-centre velocity `[nTri·2]` in xy-major order. Implementation reuses `SurfaceFluxCalculator` + RT0 math already in the engine; cached on `SurfaceStateData::cell_velocity` per output tick (computed once per write, reused for HDF5 emit + the bulk API). `Default2DOutputPlugin` emits time-varying `/Mesh2_velocity` `[nTime, nFace, 2]` alongside `/Mesh2_depth`. Filed in `openswmm.engine/docs/GUI_API_REQUEST_BLOCK_BA.md` as CF-04. Engine PR independent; lands before §P.CF.2 GUI work.
> - **Phase CF.2.3b — GUI prefers engine velocity, falls back to RT0**: `Mesh2DH5Reader` grows `readVelocityAt(int timeIdx, std::vector<float>& vx_vy)` — returns engine-cached velocity when `/Mesh2_velocity` is present, else reconstructs via RT0 from `readEdgeFluxAt`. `EngineMesh2DSource` resolves `swmm_2d_get_velocity_bulk` via `QLibrary::resolve` at engine-open time; uses it directly if non-null, else feeds edge fluxes through CF.2.3's RT0 path. CF.2.3's `SceneTri::vx, vy, vmag` fields are populated from this single helper regardless of source. Parity test `test_velocity_engine_vs_rt0.cpp` (4 cases) asserts engine output and RT0 output match to 1e-6 on equilateral / right / mixed-shape / wet-dry-front fixtures.
> - **Phase CF.2.7 — Promote velocity + HGL to `SWMM2DResultVariable`**: `enum class SWMM2DResultVariable { Depth, Vmag, Vx, Vy, Hgl }`. `SWMM2DResultsLayer::sampleAttribute(triIdx, t)` dispatches: `Depth` → `m_depths[t,tri]`, `Vmag/Vx/Vy` → `EngineMesh2DSource::velocityAt(t,tri)`, `Hgl` → `m_bedZ[tri] + m_depths[t,tri]` (HGL is GUI-derived, no engine call needed). Existing `inundationColorRgba` becomes the default `ColorRamp` for `Depth`; new `legacy-SWMM-velocity` and `legacy-SWMM-elev` ramps ship as Phase BB Phase 8.6.1 catalogue additions for `Vmag` and `Hgl` defaults. **No animation slowdown** — Vmag is computed once per output tick by the engine and cached; HGL is one float add per cell.
>
> **New tests**: `test_velocity_engine_vs_rt0.cpp` (4 cases), `test_swmm2dresultvariable.cpp` (5 cases — Depth/Vmag/Vx/Vy/Hgl sample round-trip), `test_mesh2dh5reader_velocity.cpp` (3 cases — engine path / fallback path / older-file vertex-derived geom + RT0).
> **Engine gap**: CF-04 (this amendment). Blocks Phase CF.2.7's `Vmag/Vx/Vy` themable surface; Phase CF.2.3b's fallback path keeps the feature functional on older engines.
> **Dependencies updated**: CF.2 ships its existing dependencies; CF.2.1b + CF.2.7 require the engine PR landing first OR the fallback path being active.

> **SUPERSEDED 2026-05-22 (later same day):** CF.MVP-resurrection has since landed. `grep -rln "SWMM2DResultsLayer\|Mesh2DH5Reader" include/ src/` now returns `include/io/mesh2dh5reader.h`, `src/io/mesh2dh5reader.cpp`, `include/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.h`, `src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.cpp` plus the runner + `swmmvis.cpp` wiring described in the original CF.MVP plan. They remain blocked at a finer grain only by the three live gaps catalogued in **§P-addendum-2 — CF.MVP-fix** (immediately below): renderer-not-routed paint loop, animation controller not driving the 2D layer, and missing HDF5 overwrite handshake on re-run. - **CF.2** (engine velocity + Vmag/Vx/Vy/HGL theming) — **DOUBLY BLOCKED**. Was already gated on engine gap CF-04 (`swmm_2d_get_velocity_bulk`); now also blocked on CF.MVP shipping the layer it would theme. Sequencing becomes: CF.MVP Step 0 (engine 2D HDF5 output) → CF.MVP layer + reader → CF.2 engine velocity bulk → CF.2 GUI theming.
- **BA Phase 8.2.1** (layer-kind-aware status-bar combos) — **BLOCKED** on the `SWMM2DResultVariable` enum that CF.2.7 introduces, which is itself blocked on the above.
- **BI.4 Styling Dock** — **partially blocked** (the `SWMM2DResultsLayer` tab in the §N.4 matrix can't be implemented), but the dock + selection model + canvas affordance can still land against the layers that do exist (`SWMMModelLayer`, `SWMM2DMeshLayer`, `GISVectorLayer`, `GISRasterLayer`).

The available next slices are BI.4 (Styling Dock, sized down to the layers that exist), AZ.3.4 follow-up (pen/LOD for edges), and AU.6.4 full (`RasterHillshadeRenderer` once the WIP raster files settle). ### §P-addendum-2 2026-05-22 — Slice CF.MVP-fix (DRAFT, post-resurrection, user-reported gaps)

**User report (2026-05-22):** "The 2D model visualization is not quite working well. Animation does not show progression and won't let me run when there is already a result. I want to allow restarting and overwriting of previous results. I want to hook up the styling and theming including graduated colors, contours both filled and lines etc."

CF.MVP-resurrection has landed the data path end-to-end (engine HDF5 → `Mesh2DH5Reader` → `HDF5Mesh2DSource`/`EngineMesh2DSource` → `SWMM2DResultsLayer` → canvas). The remaining gaps are at the **control + presentation seams** that the plan deferred (CF.MVP Step 1 explicitly says "copies SWMM2DMeshGraphicsItem paint pattern… eventual theming slice can swap ramps without restructuring", and the BI.6 ColorRamp dependency in §L.BB-amendment Phase 8.13.6.4 keeps the 2D paint loop hardcoded to `inundationColorRgba`). This slice closes the three load-bearing user-visible issues without waiting for §P.BJ.2 or Slice BB — using the **temporary `viridisAt` palette** already shipped for the mesh-layer filled-bands cut (line 11694) as the stand-in until Slice BB lands.

**Filed as a CF.MVP follow-up (not a §N or §P.BJ.2 follow-up)** because every fix lives inside the layer / animation controller / runner-overwrite path that CF.MVP itself owns. None of the three sub-fixes introduces new engine API surface or cross-layer abstractions.

#### CF.MVP-fix.1 — Animation controller drives `SWMM2DResultsLayer` even with no 1D primary

**Diagnosis.** [`AnimationController`](../src/animation/animationcontroller.cpp#L130-L212) is hard-coupled to `SWMMResultsLayer` (1D) as primary: `play()` early-exits on `!m_primaryLayer || totalTimeSteps() <= 0` (line 132), `onTimerTick()` advances only `m_primaryLayer->setCurrentTimeStep(next)` (line 211). The 2D side is wired downstream of the controller's `currentTimeChanged(QDateTime)` signal at [`swmmvis.cpp:671-685`](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L671-L685) — but that signal only fires when the *primary 1D layer* advances. A 2D-only run (no `.out` results layer added as primary) leaves the timer never starting, so `setCurrentSimTime(dt)` on the 2D layer is never called and the heatmap appears frozen on the peak-inundation frame seeded by `setSource()` (swmm2dresultslayer.cpp:579) or by the post-run `setCurrentTimeIndex(peakFrame)` scan (swmmvis.cpp:2785).

**Fix scope.** Promote the animation controller from "1D-bound" to "time-axis-bound" so it can drive whichever layer kind owns the time grid. Two ownership options were considered:

- **Option A (rejected):** make `SWMM2DResultsLayer` inherit a shared `IAnimatable` interface with `totalTimeSteps()` / `currentTimeStep()` / `setCurrentTimeStep()` and let `AnimationController::setPrimary(IAnimatable*)` accept it. Cross-cuts the layer hierarchy and forces a synthetic integer time-step model on the 2D layer, which natively uses a real-valued time axis. Touches 1D layer signatures (BL/BA risk).
- **Option B (selected):** keep `AnimationController` 1D-typed but add a **`fallbackTimeProvider`** seam so when there is no 1D primary, the controller computes total-step count and current step from a `SWMM2DResultsLayer*` (or any layer exposing `timeRangeChanged(int, int)` + `currentTimeChanged(int)` + a `setCurrentTimeIndex(int)` slot). The tick loop advances the integer index on the fallback provider; the existing QDateTime fan-out continues working unchanged because `SWMM2DResultsLayer::setCurrentTimeIndex` emits `currentTimeChanged(int)` and we add a parallel `currentDateTimeChanged(QDateTime)` mirror.

**Files (Option B):**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `include/animation/animationcontroller.h` | Add `setFallback2DLayer(SWMM2DResultsLayer*)` + a private `m_fallback2D` pointer. Add `bool hasDriver() const` returning `m_primaryLayer || m_fallback2D`. |
| `src/animation/animationcontroller.cpp` | (a) `play()` early-exit on `!hasDriver() || totalSteps() <= 0`. (b) `onTimerTick()` branches: if `m_primaryLayer` drive it; else advance `m_fallback2D->setCurrentTimeIndex(idx+1)`. (c) New `totalSteps()` helper returns 1D `totalTimeSteps()` or `source()->timeCount()` from the 2D fallback. (d) `stop()`/`seekToFirst()`/`seekToLast()`/`seekToPeriod()`/`stepForward()`/`stepBackward()` all gain the same branch. (e) `connectFallback2D()` / `disconnectFallback2D()` wire `SWMM2DResultsLayer::currentTimeChanged(int)` → `onPrimaryPeriodChanged(int)` so the slider follows. |
| `include/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.h` | Add `void currentDateTimeChanged(QDateTime)` mirror signal. Emit it from `setCurrentTimeIndex` alongside the existing `currentTimeChanged(int t)` (line 613 in .cpp). Drives `mDateTimeEditAnimationTime` via the existing `AnimationController::currentTimeChanged(QDateTime)` fan-out. |
| `src/swmmvis.cpp` (twoDInitialized handler ~3777, h5 auto-load handler ~2741) | After `addLayer(layer)`, call `mAnimationController->setFallback2DLayer(layer)` **only when there is no primary 1D layer yet**. When a 1D layer subsequently becomes primary, clear the fallback. |
| `src/swmmvis.cpp` (existing `currentTimeChanged → setCurrentSimTime` lambda at L671) | No change — still fans the QDateTime out to all 2D layers on the canvas, regardless of driver source. |

**Verification:**

1. Open `examples/demo_snoopy_lagoon/snoopy.inp`, run sim, wait for finish → 2D layer is auto-attached at peak frame. Hit play → frame index advances monotonically; status-bar QDateTime widget ticks forward; cells recolor each second.
2. Same flow but with **no** 1D `.out` (use a project with `[2D_*]` but no node/link reporting) → play still advances 2D frames; no console warnings about null primary.
3. Mixed-mode: project has both 1D + 2D output. Confirm 1D primary still drives the controller, the 2D layer follows via the existing QDateTime fan-out, and the fallback pointer is correctly cleared (assertion in `setFallback2DLayer`).
4. Manual: slider drag scrubs both layers in lockstep; pause/stop don't desync the 2D layer.

**Tests (extend [`tests/gui/test_animationcontroller.cpp`](../tests/gui/test_animationcontroller.cpp) if it exists, else add):**
- `tick_advances_2d_fallback_when_no_1d_primary` — fakes a `SWMM2DResultsLayer` with `timeCount()=10`, asserts after N ticks `currentTimeIndex == N`.
- `play_early_exits_when_neither_driver_set` — controller with no primary + no fallback → `play()` is a no-op.
- `1d_primary_supersedes_2d_fallback` — both set → `onTimerTick` advances 1D only.

#### CF.MVP-fix.2 — Re-run handshake closes 2D HDF5 + truncates `OUTPUT_FILE`

**Diagnosis.** The existing overwrite guard at [`swmmvis.cpp:3551-3613`](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L3551-L3613) covers the **1D `.out`** path (in-flight collision check at 3555, post-run overwrite-confirm at 3568-3611, close-open-1D-layers at 3602-3611). It does **not** cover the **2D HDF5 OUTPUT_FILE**. Symptoms reported by the user:

- The engine's `Default2DOutputPlugin` either appends to or refuses to open an existing `.h5` (depending on its `H5F_ACC_*` mode), so a second run silently produces no new 2D data or aborts the 2D solver mid-init.
- The previous run's `HDF5Mesh2DSource` (auto-loaded at [`swmmvis.cpp:2700-2744`](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2700-L2744) on project open, or attached by the prior finished-swap at line 3866-3905) holds an open `H5Fopen` handle that blocks truncation on Windows and produces stale reads on POSIX.
- The 1D-only overwrite-confirm prompt at line 3585 doesn't mention 2D, so the user can't tell why nothing changed after consenting.

**Fix scope.** Extend the existing 3551-3613 block to be **dual-stream-aware** (1D + 2D), with all three concerns in one prompt.

**Files:**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/swmmvis.cpp` (run-simulation handler, around L3551) | (a) Add a `h5Path = SimulationRunner::parseTwoDOutputFile(inpPath)` lookup alongside the existing `.out` derivation. (b) Extend `outOnDisk` check to also cover `QFileInfo(h5Path).exists() && size() > 0` when `h5Path` is non-empty. (c) Extend the `for (...) layers()` walk at L3568-3582 to also detect open `SWMM2DResultsLayer` whose `source()` points at the resolved `h5Path` (compare absolute paths). (d) Extend the confirm-dialog text at L3585-3593 to mention "1D results (.out)" / "2D inundation results (.h5)" / "both" depending on which streams trigger. (e) On YES: call new `SWMM2DResultsLayer::closeSource()` on every matching 2D layer **before** the engine starts (releases `H5Fopen`); then `QFile::remove(h5Path)` so the engine plugin sees a clean slate. (f) Re-attach a fresh `HDF5Mesh2DSource` in the existing finished-swap handler (line 3869+) so the post-run layer points at the new file. |
| `include/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.h`, `src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.cpp` | Add `void closeSource()` — resets `source_` to `nullptr` (releases the unique_ptr's HDF5 handle), clears `current_depths_` / `current_flux_`, sets `current_time_idx_ = -1`, calls `geometryChanged()` on both items so the canvas paints empty until the swap. |
| `include/io/mesh2dh5reader.h`, `src/io/mesh2dh5reader.cpp` | Verify `~Mesh2DH5Reader` calls `H5Fclose` on its `file_id_` (single-line audit; add if missing). Add `bool isOpen() const` for the new equality check on swmmvis side. |
| `src/simulation/simulationrunner.cpp` | No behavior change — the runner already calls `parseTwoDOutputFile` and emits `twoDInitialized(jobId, h5Path, …)`. Optional: surface a `simulationrunner.h` constant for `kH5SuffixDefault` so callers don't reproduce the `base + ".2d.h5"` derivation. |

**Why a single dialog (not two):** the user said "I want to allow restarting and overwriting" — explicit consent once per run, not twice. The dialog text enumerates *what* will be overwritten so consent stays informed.

**Why delete `.h5` rather than truncate:** `H5Fcreate(..., H5F_ACC_TRUNC)` exists, but the GUI doesn't own the engine's HDF5 create path; deleting before launch is the format-agnostic option and matches how `.out` is handled today (`engine_initialize` does the create).

**Verification:**

1. Run sim with `OUTPUT_FILE = snoopy.2d.h5`, finish, observe `.h5` on disk. Re-run → dialog says "Results already exist for this model… 1D results (.out) and 2D inundation results (.h5) will be overwritten." → Click Yes → both files are recreated; 2D layer reattaches to the new `.h5` at peak frame.
2. Re-open project after step 1 → auto-load attaches `SWMM2DResultsLayer` from `.h5`. Hit Run → dialog enumerates both streams; consent → 2D layer's source is released first, then `.h5` is removed; engine restarts cleanly.
3. Abort the dialog → both `.out` and `.h5` are untouched on disk; 2D layer continues showing the prior peak frame.
4. Edge case: `OUTPUT_FILE` unset in `[2D_OPTIONS]` → guard only covers 1D, dialog text drops the 2D line.

**Tests:**
- `test_simulationrunner_parseTwoDOutputFile` — already exists; extend with relative-path resolution case.
- `test_swmm2dresultslayer.cpp::closeSource_releases_handle` — open + close + assert `source() == nullptr`, `currentTimeIndex() == -1`.

#### CF.MVP-fix.3 — Paint loop honours renderer + filled/line contours

**Diagnosis.** The constructor at [`swmm2dresultslayer.cpp:493-498`](../src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.cpp#L493-L498) instantiates a `GraduatedRenderer` but the comment is explicit: *"Paint loop still uses dry_depth_ / max_depth_ directly; refactor deferred to 8.13.6.4."* The deferral note in §L.BB-amendment Phase 8.13.6.4 (line 10896) gates the refactor on "Slice BB Phase 8.6.1 ships the `ColorRamp` data type" — but the user has signalled that the visual quality of the current hardcoded gradient is now the bottleneck, so the deferral cost > the original "smooth-ramp → 5-hard-bins regression" cost.

The mesh layer (`SWMM2DMeshLayer`) already ships **filled-band marching-triangles** + **isoline marching-triangles** via the `marchingTrianglesIsobands` / `marchingTrianglesIsolines` helpers shipped 2026-05-22 (line 11694 — `include/contour/marchingtriangles.h`), using the temporary `viridisAt` palette. The 2D results layer can adopt the same helpers against its per-tri **depth** attribute (instead of the mesh layer's bed-Z) without waiting for §P.BJ.2.

**Fix scope.** Three additive surfaces on `SWMM2DResultsLayer`, all gated behind layer-properties so existing projects continue painting exactly as before until the user opts in.

**Sub-phase CF.MVP-fix.3.a — Route paint loop through `m_renderer`.**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.cpp` (graphics-item paint, ~L117-185) | Replace the inline `inundationColorRgba(depth, dry_depth_, max_depth_, r,g,b,a)` call with `m_renderer->symbolForValue(depth)` returning `(QColor fill, qreal alpha)`. Wet/dry alpha gating stays at the paint-loop level (cells with `depth < dry_depth_` get α=0 regardless of renderer output) so the underlying mesh stays visible. Keep `inundationColorRgba` as the **default ramp inside `GraduatedRenderer`** — same five Viridis-ish stops, same `[dry_depth, max_depth]` mapping — so default-mode output is byte-identical to today. |
| `include/render/renderers/graduatedrenderer.h`, `src/render/renderers/graduatedrenderer.cpp` | Add `void setDepthRange(double dry, double max)` and `void setStops(const std::vector<ColorStop>&)`. The default stops match `inundationColorRgba`'s current curve. **NB:** this is the same `GraduatedRenderer` the §L.BB amendment will extend with full `ColorRamp` semantics later — the depth-range API is a v0 that BB can supersede without breaking callers. |
| `src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.cpp` (`setDryDepth` / `setMaxDepth` slots) | After updating the member, mirror the value into `m_renderer->setDepthRange(dry_depth_, max_depth_)` so the renderer stays in sync with the layer's pinned-range knobs. |
| `src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.cpp` (constructor) | Connect `rendererChanged()` signal → `graphics_item_->geometryChanged()` so swapping renderers invalidates the canvas. |

**Sub-phase CF.MVP-fix.3.b — Filled-band contours (per-tri depth attribute).**

Mirror the AU.6 / AZ.3.7 mesh-layer flag set on `SWMM2DResultsLayer`:

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `include/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.h` | Q_PROPERTYs: `filledContours` (bool, default false), `filledContoursOpacity` (double, default 0.55), `filledContoursLevels` (int, default 8 evenly-spaced bands across `[dry_depth, max_depth]`). |
| `src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.cpp` (graphics-item paint, new pass after the heatmap pass) | When `filled_contours_`, call `marchingTrianglesIsobands(depths, tris, breakLevels)` with `evenlySpacedLevelsInclusive(dry_depth_, max_depth_, filled_contours_levels_)` — fan-triangulate each ≤5-vertex band polygon, fill with `viridisAt((bandIdx + 0.5) / nBands)` at `filled_contours_opacity_`. Z-order: drawn over the per-cell heatmap but under the isolines (CF.MVP-fix.3.c) and over the mesh wireframe — matches AZ.3 ordering pattern. |
| Persistence (project `.oswp` writer/reader for results layers) | Additive keys `"filledContours"`, `"filledContoursOpacity"`, `"filledContoursLevels"` under the 2D-results layer block. Same shape as `meshLayers[].contours` from §P.AZ.3.7. No schema bump. |

**Sub-phase CF.MVP-fix.3.c — Iso-line contours (per-tri depth attribute).**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `include/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.h` | Q_PROPERTYs: `isolines` (bool, default false), `isolinesLevels` (int, default 5), `isolinesColor` (QColor, default black), `isolinesWidth` (double, default 1.0). |
| `src/layers/swmm2dresultslayer.cpp` (graphics-item paint, final pass) | When `isolines_`, call `marchingTrianglesIsolines(depths, tris, evenlySpacedLevelsInclusive(...))` and stroke each polyline at `isolines_color_` / `isolines_width_` using a `QPen` with `Qt::SolidLine`. Anti-aliasing on. |
| Persistence | Additive keys `"isolines"`, `"isolinesLevels"`, `"isolinesColor"`, `"isolinesWidth"`. |

**Sub-phase CF.MVP-fix.3.d — Property panel surface.**

Until Slice BI.4 Styling Dock ships, expose the three controls inline on the `SWMM2DResultsLayer` property panel that already hosts dry-depth / max-depth / velocity controls:

- **Heatmap group** (existing): dry depth, max depth — unchanged.
- **Filled contours group** (new): checkbox + level count spinbox + opacity slider. Disabled when no source.
- **Iso-lines group** (new): checkbox + level count spinbox + color chip (QColorDialog) + width spinbox.

When Slice BI.4 ships, the same Q_PROPERTYs flow into the styling dock's matrix for `SWMM2DResultsLayer` (§N.4) with zero code change on the layer side — the renderer + flag plumbing is the contract.

**Dependencies / non-dependencies:**

- **Does not depend on Slice BB** — uses the existing `viridisAt` palette plus default `GraduatedRenderer` stops. When Slice BB ships, the renderer's stops become user-pickable and `viridisAt` is replaced by `ColorRamp::sample(t)`; no callsite change.
- **Does not depend on §P.BJ.2** — reuses the marching-triangles helpers shipped 2026-05-22 for the mesh layer. §P.BJ.2 (when it lands) will add a generator-level abstraction that owns interval choice + label placement + multi-attribute support; the layer's per-frame paint pass remains the consumer.
- **Does not depend on CF.2** — velocity arrows are already drawn out of the existing `arrows_item_` and are independent of the depth-contour path.
- **Unblocks BI.4's `SWMM2DResultsLayer` tab** — once these properties exist on the layer, the styling-dock matrix in §N.4 can list them.

**Verification (presentation gating):**

1. Default behaviour unchanged — projects opened without the new flags render identically to today (paint-loop byte-identical heatmap).
2. Toggle filled contours on with 8 levels at 55% opacity → see Viridis-banded inundation; mesh wireframe and heatmap remain visible beneath.
3. Toggle isolines on with 5 levels in black at 1.0 px → see contour lines tracking the depth iso-values; lines move with the animation tick.
4. Adjust dry/max depth → renderer ramp + contour break-levels update together (no stale legend).
5. Swap renderer (test-only) → `rendererChanged()` triggers repaint.
6. Persistence round-trip: enable both contour passes, save .oswp, close, reopen → flags + level counts + colours restored.

**Tests:**
- `test_swmm2dresultslayer_renderer.cpp::default_renderer_matches_inundationColorRgba` — pixel-equal output between old and new paint paths at `n=20` sample depths.
- `test_swmm2dresultslayer_renderer.cpp::setDepthRange_updates_ramp` — pin `[0.05, 1.2]`, sample at 0.6 → expected mid-ramp colour.
- `test_swmm2dresultslayer_renderer.cpp::filled_contours_band_count` — set 8 bands, run a known triangle field, count emitted polygon batches → 8.
- `test_swmm2dresultslayer_renderer.cpp::isolines_count` — set 5 levels, count emitted polylines → 5.

#### Sequencing + bundle shape

The three sub-fixes are independent of each other and can ship in any order, but the **user's friction with the current build is dominated by fix.1 + fix.2** (animation + re-run): without those, no presentation beat works at all. Fix.3 is the visual-quality polish and can ship in a follow-up PR.

Recommended bundle order (one PR per row, fix.1 + fix.2 can also be combined since both touch `swmmvis.cpp`):

| # | Bundle | Scope | Risk |
|---|--------|-------|------|
| 1 | CF.MVP-fix.1 | Animation controller fallback + 2D layer mirror signal | Low — additive, no 1D regression path. |
| 2 | CF.MVP-fix.2 | Re-run handshake dual-stream + `closeSource` | Medium — touches the existing overwrite-confirm flow that BL relies on. Needs regression test for the 1D-only path. |
| 3 | CF.MVP-fix.3.a | Paint-loop through `m_renderer` | Low — gated by golden-pixel test against `inundationColorRgba`. |
| 4 | CF.MVP-fix.3.b + .3.c + .3.d | Filled bands + isolines + property panel rows | Low — additive Q_PROPERTYs + paint passes; no 1D layer involvement. |

**Awaiting user approval of this addendum before any code work begins.** Confirm scope / sequencing / Option-B vs Option-A trade-off on fix.1 before the first PR opens.

## §Q — Output-Identity Qualification on Node Summary Stats + OPTIONS / Sim-Options Output-Path Honoring (DRAFT 2026-05-25, awaiting approval)

### §Q.0 Why this section exists

Two user-reported gaps surfaced 2026-05-25 while exercising the multi-output workflow against a project with several loaded `SWMMResultsLayer`s:

1. **Stats are not qualified by the output that produced them.** The node attribute panel exposes `statMaxDepth` / `statMaxOverflow` / `statVolFlooded` / `statTimeFlooded` rows ([include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h:113–116, Q_PROPERTYs at 249–252 / 294–297 / 329–332 / 363–366](../include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h); getters at [src/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.cpp:200–203](../src/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.cpp#L200)) by reading the *editing* engine handle's ambient `swmm_node_get_stat_*` values. When the user loads multiple `SWMMResultsLayer`s — comparing runs against each other or stacking calibration scenarios — every row in the panel shows whatever the editing engine happens to hold (post-last-run, or zero if the project was reopened without a re-run). There is no caption, source label, or per-output qualifier to tell the user *which* `.out` the displayed numbers came from, and there is no way to switch the displayed stats to a different loaded output without re-running.

2. **OPTIONS-section / Simulation-Options output-path overrides are ignored by the run.** [src/swmmvis.cpp:3995–3999](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L3995) computes the `.rpt` and `.out` paths *unconditionally* as `<inp-basename>.rpt` / `<inp-basename>.out`, ignoring the override that Slice AA-4 already wired into the Simulation Options → Output tab ([src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp:2336–2367](../src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp#L2336) for the line-edits; [2640–2660](../src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp#L2640) for the QSettings round-trip under `SWMMVis/Project/<inpPath>/ReportFilePath` and `OutputFilePath`). The user can type a custom path, save it, see it round-trip on reopen — but every Run still writes to the sibling-default location. This also leaves no engine-level surface for a `[OPTIONS] OUT_FILE_PATH` / `RPT_FILE_PATH` key, which is the canonical "options category" location a SWMM modeller would expect.

This §Q amendment plans the fixes as two paired slices — **Slice QA** for stats qualification (Slice BM / DA / CB seam) and **Slice QB** for run-path output honoring (Slice BV seam) — plus the engine-side surface needed to let OPTIONS-section paths persist into the .inp file.

### §Q.1 Assumptions + open questions (per CLAUDE.md §1)

- **Stated assumption — "output" means loaded `SWMMResultsLayer` instance.** The user said "outputs that are loaded". A loaded output is a `SWMMResultsLayer` opened against a specific `.out` file ([src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp)). 2D results layers (`SWMM2DResultsLayer`) are out of scope for §Q's *node* stats but the same identity-qualification idiom should generalise once 2D per-cell stats land (CF.MVP follow-up); §Q.4 deliberately scopes the schema so 2D can plug in without rework.
- **Stated assumption — "options category" means both the GUI's Simulation Options dialog AND the SWMM .inp `[OPTIONS]` section.** Today the dialog persists overrides into `QSettings` only (per-machine, not per-project) — the .inp `[OPTIONS]` section has no `OUT_FILE_PATH` / `RPT_FILE_PATH` keys at all ([src/engine/core/openswmm_model_impl.cpp:560–600](../src/engine/core/openswmm_model_impl.cpp#L560) shows `RPT_*` selector keys but no path keys; `[FILES]` section per [include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_model.h:217–267](../include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_model.h#L217) covers hot-start + secondary refs but NOT the primary `.out` / `.rpt`). The fix has to cover both surfaces so the override survives a "save .inp + open on another machine" round-trip.
- **Open question 1 — qualification UX shape.** Three viable strategies, sketched in §Q.3 below; user-selected before Slice QA.1 starts.
- **Open question 2 — engine-side OPTIONS key naming.** Legacy SWMM5 has no precedent for these keys (they were always CLI args), so we have to pick. Proposed: `OUT_FILE_PATH` / `RPT_FILE_PATH` matching the existing `RPT_*` casing. Alternative: extend `[FILES]` with `OUTPUT_PATH` / `REPORT_PATH` mirroring `HOTSTART_USE_PATH` / `HOTSTART_SAVE_PATH`. §Q.5 enumerates the trade-off; user-selected before Slice QB-01 starts.
- **Open question 3 — relative-path semantics.** Should override paths in `[OPTIONS]` / `[FILES]` be resolved relative to the .inp directory (like every other path the engine reads) or absolute-only? Recommendation: relative-to-.inp on read, write-as-relative-when-under-inp-dir-else-absolute on save — same idiom `ProjectSerializer::toRelativePath` already uses.

### §Q.2 In-scope / out-of-scope

**In scope.**
- `statMaxDepth` / `statMaxOverflow` / `statVolFlooded` / `statTimeFlooded` on the node attribute panel — every property adapter that exposes them (Junction, Outfall, Storage, Divider — all four subclasses in [include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h](../include/ui/properties/swmmnodepropertyadapter.h)).
- The simulation Run path in `SWMMVis::runActiveProject` ([src/swmmvis.cpp:3974–4180](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L3974)) and the `SimulationRunner` constructor signature ([src/simulation/simulationrunner.cpp:169–196](../src/simulation/simulationrunner.cpp#L169)).
- Round-trip of the override paths to the .inp `[OPTIONS]` (or `[FILES]` per Open question 2) so a machine-portable project carries its own output destination.
- The collision-guard in [src/swmmvis.cpp:4006–4070](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L4006) must keep working against the resolved (post-override) paths — *not* the sibling default — or the warning will fire on the wrong file.

**Out of scope (deliberately deferred).**
- 2D `SWMM2DResultsLayer` per-cell stats qualification (no per-cell stats today; revisit when CF.MVP-fix.3 ships the SWMM2D variable theming).
- Link-stats qualification on the link property adapter — same mechanism but a separate slice once Slice QA lands; tracked as Slice QA-follow-up.
- Subcatchment-stats qualification — same deferral as links.
- Engine-side dual-output writing (one engine, multiple `.out` files) — explicitly out of scope; the run path stays single-output per Run.
- Auto-promotion of post-run results into a "current stats source" for the attribute panel — see §Q.3 Option C for why this is appealing but a separate, larger refactor.

### §Q.3 Stats-qualification UX options

Three viable strategies; user picks one before Slice QA.1 starts. The mechanism behind all three is the same `OutputStatsRegistry` introduced in §Q.4 — only the panel-rendering differs.

**Option A — "Stats Source" combo at the panel level (recommended).**
- A single combobox at the top of the attribute panel's *Statistics* group lists every loaded `SWMMResultsLayer` plus an `(editing engine)` sentinel. Pick one → the four stat rows refresh to read from that source.
- Pros: matches the panel pattern users already know from Slice BA's per-attribute theming combo; one column of row labels; tiny visual footprint.
- Cons: requires a refresh signal from `OutputStatsRegistry` when layers are added/removed; the comparison workflow ("see run A and run B side-by-side") still requires the user to flip the combo.
- File touches: `swmmattributepanel.cpp`, `swmmnodepropertyadapter.cpp` (+ `.h`).

**Option B — One row per loaded output.**
- Each stat row expands into N rows when N outputs are loaded: `Stat Max Depth [run-A.out]`, `Stat Max Depth [run-B.out]`, etc. Editing-engine row labelled `Stat Max Depth (current run)`.
- Pros: zero clicks to compare; the panel itself becomes the comparison surface.
- Cons: panel height balloons with each loaded output; row labels grow long; needs a separate "stat key" for every (metric × output) pair which the existing `Q_PROPERTY` model does not accommodate without per-output property adapters or a new model-view (`QAbstractTableModel`-backed stats sub-panel).
- File touches: same as Option A plus a new `NodeStatsTableModel` per the property-panel's existing convention for table-like sub-blocks.

**Option C — Promote the active `SWMMResultsLayer` to the stats source, drop editing-engine stats.**
- The four `Q_PROPERTY`s vanish from the editing-engine path entirely. The Statistics group is sourced from the active `SWMMResultsLayer` (chosen by `SWMMVis::setActiveResultsLayer`, same handle Slice BA uses for animation). When no output is loaded, the group hides.
- Pros: aligns stats with how Slice BA already gates *time-series* display on a chosen output; conceptually clean — stats are an output product, not an editing-engine property.
- Cons: invasive refactor; needs `SWMMResultsLayer` to surface `nodeStatMax*` accessors (today it only exposes time-series fetches via `nodeOutputIndex` + `fetchResultsForStep`); the engine's `swmm_node_get_stat_*` cannot read from an arbitrary `SWMM_Output` handle today, so this option requires a new `output`-side getter set (engine gap QA-01).
- File touches: `swmmresultslayer.{h,cpp}` (+ `nodeStatMax*` accessors backed by `SWMM_Output` minima/maxima), `swmmnodepropertyadapter.cpp` (read from `m_layer->activeResultsLayer()` not `m_engine`), and an engine-side surface for `swmm_output_get_node_stat_max_*` returning the per-object max/min already stored in the `.out` file's `OUTPUT.STATISTICS` block.

**Recommendation.** Option A for the first cut — smallest blast radius, ships in a single PR, preserves the existing `Q_PROPERTY` surface (no MOC churn beyond a single `setStatsSource(QString)` slot). Option B's row-per-output is a follow-up if multi-comparison friction persists. Option C is the right end-state but bundles the engine gap and a property-adapter refactor — sequence it after Slice QA-A lands and CF.MVP stabilises.

### §Q.4 Shared mechanism — `OutputStatsRegistry`

Regardless of Option A/B/C, a single registry centralises "which loaded outputs exist and how do we tag them" so the attribute panel, statistics dashboard (Slice CB), tabular results (Slice BF), and custom-report (Slice BH) all share the same identity model.

```
include/output/outputstatsregistry.h            // NEW (~80 lines)
src/output/outputstatsregistry.cpp              // NEW (~120 lines)
```

- `class OutputStatsRegistry : public QObject` lives on the `SWMMVisProjectWindow` (one per project; multi-project = multi-registry, matching Slice 13's session model).
- `struct OutputIdentity { QString shortLabel; QString tooltipPath; QUuid stableId; SWMMResultsLayer *layer; }` — `shortLabel` defaults to the .out filename without extension (`run-A`), collision-resolved by appending `(N)` if two filenames clash. `stableId` survives layer reorder.
- `void registerLayer(SWMMResultsLayer *)` / `void unregisterLayer(SWMMResultsLayer *)` — wired from `SWMMResultsLayer::openResults` / `closeResults` ([src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp:363, 420](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp#L363)).
- `QList<OutputIdentity> identities() const` and `OutputIdentity identityFor(QUuid) const` for consumers.
- `Q_SIGNAL identitiesChanged()` so panels / dashboards refresh in lockstep with layer-tree adds and removes.
- The `(editing engine)` sentinel is identity `QUuid{}` (null) — consumers branch on `id.isNull()` to read `swmm_node_get_stat_*` directly.

This is the single touchpoint that Slice CB (Statistics dashboard) was going to need anyway per [Phase 9.5.1](#-slice-cb--statistics-dashboard-per-object-maxmin-time-of-occurrence-phase-95) — landing it here gives CB a free dependency reduction.

### §Q.5 Engine-side option for run-path overrides (Open question 2)

**Strategy A — new `[OPTIONS]` keys: `OUT_FILE_PATH` + `RPT_FILE_PATH` (recommended).**
- Extends the `swmm_options_get/set` dispatch in [src/engine/core/openswmm_model_impl.cpp:560+](../src/engine/core/openswmm_model_impl.cpp#L560) — same mechanism Slice BV's `RPT_*` keys use, same writer round-trip via `InpWriter.cpp`.
- The engine doesn't *consume* these paths at `swmm_engine_open` time (the API still takes explicit `rpt` + `out` args); they exist purely as a *persisted preference* the GUI reads when constructing the runner. This keeps the engine ABI stable.
- Pros: matches the user's mental model ("output paths in the options category"); single dispatch point; round-trips through the existing OPTIONS writer.
- Cons: slight semantic mismatch — these keys are GUI/CLI preferences, not engine-time runtime knobs. Documented in the header as such.

**Strategy B — extend `[FILES]` with `OUTPUT_PATH` / `REPORT_PATH`.**
- Same idiom as `HOTSTART_USE_PATH` / `HOTSTART_SAVE_PATH` per [include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_model.h:226–232](../include/openswmm/engine/openswmm_model.h#L226).
- Pros: `[FILES]` is already "the file-paths section"; conceptually consistent.
- Cons: legacy `[FILES]` is for *secondary* file refs (the engine reads these to drive rainfall/runoff/RDII inputs), not primary outputs; readers of legacy SWMM5 .inp files will be surprised; the writer would need a non-legacy section variant.

**Strategy C — pure GUI-side, no engine surface.**
- Keep the `QSettings` per-machine store; don't persist to .inp at all. Just wire the existing override through to `SimulationRunner`.
- Pros: smallest change; no engine ABI surface.
- Cons: project not portable — moving the project to another machine loses the override silently.

**Recommendation.** Strategy A. Pairs cleanly with the existing `RPT_*` selector keys Slice BV.1 shipped 2026-05-22.

### §Q.6 Slice QA — Output-identity qualification on node stats (Phase 6.3.1 + Phase 8.5.1)

- **Phase QA.1 — `OutputStatsRegistry`** (§Q.4): land the registry, wire `registerLayer` / `unregisterLayer` to the `SWMMResultsLayer` open / close hooks, surface to `SWMMVisProjectWindow::statsRegistry()`.
- **Phase QA.2 — Attribute-panel Statistics group caption + source combo (Option A)**: append a single-row header inside the existing Statistics group on the node attribute panel: a non-editable `QLabel` reading `Stats source:` + a `QComboBox` populated from `registry->identities()`. Selection signals `swmmnodepropertyadapter::setStatsSource(QUuid)`. When source is null, getters call `swmm_node_get_stat_*(m_engine, …)` as today; when source is a `SWMMResultsLayer`, getters call new `outputNodeStatMax*` accessors on the layer (Phase QA.3). The combo's selection persists per-project in `SWMMVis/Project/<inpPath>/StatsSourceUuid`.

The engine already accumulates these into the `.out` file's per-object statistics block during simulation; the API just exposes them. Reuses the file-watcher hooked up in `SWMMResultsLayer::openResults`.

### §Q.9 Sequencing

The two slices can ship independently — QA and QB touch disjoint code paths.

1. **QB-01 engine PR** (OPTIONS path keys + writer + reader + 5 tests). Independent; can land first.
2. **QA-01 engine PR** (output-side node-stat getters + 4 tests). Independent; can land in parallel with QB-01.
3. **QA.1 + QA.2 + QA.4 GUI PR** (registry + Option A combo + staleness badge). Lands after QA-01 OR ships with engine-fallback-only stat rows until QA-01 merges.
4. **QA.3 GUI PR** (results-layer stat accessors + getter dispatch). Requires QA-01 merged.
5. **QB.2 + QB.3 + QB.4 + QB.5 GUI PR** (resolver + run-path rewire + dialog sync + tests). Requires QB-01 merged.

Bundle option: QB.2 + QB.3 can ship *without* QB-01 if we accept Strategy C (GUI-only QSettings, no .inp persistence) for v1. Re-evaluate after user picks Open question 2.
