## §R — Save-Extension Double-Suffix Fix + .oswp Auto-Create on .inp Save + GeoPackage-as-Plugin Clarification (DRAFT 2026-05-25, awaiting approval)

### §R.0 Why this section exists

Three user-reported items surfaced 2026-05-25 while exercising the Save / Save As flow against a project with the GeoPackage writer installed:

1. **Save is appending an extra `.inp` to a filename that already ends in `.inp`** — yielding `model.inp.inp` (or `model.inp.oswp` for the sidecar). Root-cause analysis below.
2. **No corresponding `.oswp` project file is created on every `.inp` save path** — the user expects: *"if there does not exist a corresponding project, create one with the same name by default."* Today `SWMMVis::onSaveProject` and `SWMMVis::onSaveAs` *do* write the sidecar, but several adjacent save paths skip it; the double-extension bug above also causes the sidecar to land at the wrong filename, making it appear that no sidecar was created.
3. **GeoPackage is now showing up in the "available plugins" list** — the user wants a clarification of *why* (intended? side-effect?).

Items 1 + 2 are fixes (Slice **RA**, Slice **RB**). Item 3 is a diagnosis the user needs before deciding whether to fix it (Slice **RC** is the optional fix). All three are bundled here because they share the same Save-flow code surface ([src/swmmvis.cpp:2761–2867](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2761), [src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp:666–741](../src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp#L666)) and the same `FileFilterRegistry` plumbing.

### §R.1 Item 1 — root cause of the double-`.inp` extension bug

`SWMMVis::onSaveAs` at [src/swmmvis.cpp:2826–2839](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2826) reads the dialog's selected path then computes the .inp path two different ways depending on the chosen extension:

```cpp
const QString path = dlg.selectedFiles().value(0);
const QString ext = QFileInfo(path).suffix().toLower();
const bool isProject = (ext == QStringLiteral("oswp"));
const QString inpPath = isProject
    ? QFileInfo(path).absolutePath() + QChar('/')
          + QFileInfo(path).completeBaseName() + QStringLiteral(".inp")  // ← LINE 2838
    : path;
```

**The bug.** `QFileInfo::completeBaseName()` strips **only the last** extension. So if the dialog returns `model.inp.oswp` (a real possibility — see scenarios below), `completeBaseName()` returns `model.inp`, and `inpPath` is computed as `model.inp.inp`. The downstream sidecar then computes `ProjectSerializer::sidecarPathFor("model.inp.inp")` ([src/project/projectserializer.cpp:170–176](../src/project/projectserializer.cpp#L170)) which uses the *same* `completeBaseName()` → `model.inp.oswp`, perpetuating the double extension into the sidecar filename too.

**How `model.inp.oswp` gets into the dialog return value (three paths):**

- **Path A — Qt's default-suffix behavior + macOS dialog.** [src/swmmvis.cpp:2818](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2818) calls `dlg.setNameFilter(kFilters->saveAsFilter())` but *never* calls `dlg.setDefaultSuffix(...)`. On macOS the native dialog will silently append the *first matching filter pattern's extension* when the user types a bare basename (`model`) and picks a different active filter — leading to chains like `model.inp` (typed/suggested) → user changes filter to ProjectWrite (`.oswp`) → dialog appends `.oswp` → `model.inp.oswp`.
- **Path B — `selectFile()` pre-populates with the existing extension.** [src/swmmvis.cpp:2822](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2822) pre-fills the dialog with `QFileInfo(suggested).fileName()` — for a loaded project this is `model.inp`. If the user then switches the filter to `.oswp` without clearing the basename, the dialog can produce `model.inp.oswp` on accept (Qt 6 native dialog behavior on Linux + macOS).
- **Path C — Plugin-supplied writer extensions are not de-duplicated.** `saveAsFilter()` ([src/plugins/filefilterregistry.cpp:180–211](../src/plugins/filefilterregistry.cpp#L180)) concatenates ProjectWrite + InputRead-writable entries with no preference order beyond the "All Supported" combined line. The active filter therefore drifts with each open of the dialog and doesn't preserve the *file-format-of-record* the user picked last time. Combined with Path A, this produces unpredictable extension stacking.

**The fix (Slice RA).** Three small, additive changes — none of them refactor the existing flow:

- **Phase RA.1 — Normalize the dialog result.** Replace [src/swmmvis.cpp:2830–2839](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2830) with a small helper `normalizeSaveAsPath(const QString &dialogPath, bool &isProject)` that:
  1. Computes `ext = QFileInfo(dialogPath).suffix().toLower()`.
  2. If `dialogPath` ends with `.inp.inp` / `.oswp.oswp` / `.inp.oswp` / `.oswp.inp` / any `<ext>.<ext>` duplication where both halves are known writable kinds — strip the *outer* duplicate.
  3. For `isProject` case, use `QFileInfo::baseName()` (strips *all* extensions: `foo.inp.oswp` → `foo`) NOT `completeBaseName()` (which keeps the inner `.inp`).
  4. Returns the canonical `inpPath` (`<stem>.inp`) and sets `isProject` from the *original* dialog extension, not the post-strip one.
  Helper lives in a new `include/project/saveaspathnormalizer.{h,cpp}` so the unit test in Phase RA.4 can call it without spinning up the dialog.
- **Phase RA.2 — Set the default suffix from the active filter.** Add immediately after [src/swmmvis.cpp:2818](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2818):
  ```cpp
  // Default suffix follows the currently-selected filter. Qt re-emits
  // filterSelected() on every filter change, so we keep the suffix in
  // lockstep — preventing macOS's native-dialog "append the first filter's
  // extension" surprise when the user switches filters mid-flow.
  connect(&dlg, &QFileDialog::filterSelected,
          &dlg, [&dlg](const QString &filter) {
              // Extract the first "*.<ext>" token from the active filter and
              // strip the leading "*." — that becomes the default suffix.
              static const QRegularExpression re(QStringLiteral(R"(\*\.([A-Za-z0-9]+))"));
              const auto m = re.match(filter);
              if (m.hasMatch()) dlg.setDefaultSuffix(m.captured(1));
          });
  // Seed once for the initial filter selection (signal fires only on change).
  dlg.setDefaultSuffix(QStringLiteral("inp"));
  ```
- **Phase RA.3 — Preserve last-used filter.** Persist the user's last-selected filter per-project under `SWMMVis/Project/<inpPath>/LastSaveAsFilter` (matches Slice AA-4's QSettings idiom). On open, restore via `dlg.selectNameFilter(...)`. This kills Path C drift — once the user picks "SWMM Input File (*.inp)" once, every subsequent Save As starts there. Also kept in sync per-project to handle the multi-instance case (per-project filter memory) and prevent cross-instance bleed.
- **Phase RA.4 — Tests.** `tests/gui/test_saveaspathnormalizer.cpp` (8 cases — bare `.inp` passes through, `model.inp.inp` collapses to `model.inp`, `model.inp.oswp` produces `model.inp` as inpPath + `model.oswp` as project, `model.oswp.inp` round-trip, `model.gpkg.gpkg` collapses to `model.gpkg`, `model.inp` with non-writable extension passes through verbatim, empty path returns empty, deeply duplicated like `foo.inp.inp.inp` collapses to `foo.inp`). Plus `tests/gui/test_onsaveas_extension.cpp` (3 cases — Save As `.inp` from a `.inp`-loaded project writes single `.inp` + single `.oswp` sidecar; Save As `.oswp` writes `<stem>.inp` + `<stem>.oswp`; filter switch mid-flow doesn't double-suffix). The dialog-level cases use `QFileDialog::testOption` injection per the existing pattern in `tests/gui/test_swmmvis_save_*.cpp`.

**Files (Slice RA).** New `include/project/saveaspathnormalizer.{h,cpp}`; touches `src/swmmvis.cpp` (Save As dialog setup + result normalization), `tests/gui/test_saveaspathnormalizer.cpp` (new), `tests/gui/test_onsaveas_extension.cpp` (new), `docs/manual/03_projects.md` (Save As extension semantics note).

**Risk.** Low. The change is additive: existing well-formed paths (`model.inp`, `model.oswp`) flow through `normalizeSaveAsPath` unchanged. The only behavioral change is the stripping of duplicate extensions, which is the desired fix. The `setDefaultSuffix` addition is forward-only — existing test fixtures pass empty default suffix and remain valid.

### §R.2 Item 2 — `.oswp` auto-create on every `.inp` save (Slice RB)

**Current behavior (good but incomplete).** The two GUI menu handlers already create the sidecar:
- `SWMMVis::onSaveProject` ([src/swmmvis.cpp:2761–2795](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2761)) — writes `.oswp` via `ProjectSerializer::sidecarPathFor` after a successful `pw->save(...)`.
- `SWMMVis::onSaveAs` ([src/swmmvis.cpp:2797–2867](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2797)) — writes `.oswp` when `writeSidecar` ([line 2850](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2850)) is true, which it is for `.inp` and `.oswp` saves.

**Gaps that bypass sidecar creation.**
- **`SWMMVisProjectWindow::saveAs` is callable directly** ([src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp:679–741](../src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp#L679)) from non-menu paths (auto-save before run at [src/swmmvis.cpp:3982–3993](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L3982), `combineProjects` flow, plugin-driven save). It only writes the `.inp` and does **not** touch the sidecar. The auto-save-before-run path in particular is the most user-visible: hit Run on an unsaved project, the .inp gets saved, but no `.oswp` is created beside it.
- **The double-extension bug (§R.1)** causes `sidecarPathFor("model.inp.inp")` to compute `model.inp.oswp` — which exists on disk but the user (looking for `model.oswp`) thinks no project file was created. Once Slice RA lands, this part resolves naturally.
- **Plugin-backed writes (e.g. `.gpkg`)** are deliberately excluded from sidecar creation per [src/swmmvis.cpp:2850 comment](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L2850): *"Plugin-backed export formats (.gpkg, …) are standalone — they carry no project sidecar."* The user wants this *retained* — see §R.4 for the discussion.

**The fix (Slice RB).**

- **Phase RB.1 — Move sidecar creation into `SWMMVisProjectWindow::saveAs`.** Refactor [src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp:679–741](../src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp#L679) to, on successful write, *unconditionally* call `ProjectSerializer::saveToFile(ProjectSerializer::sidecarPathFor(newPath), this, ...)` **when the chosen plugin id is empty (built-in `.inp` writer)**. Plugin-driven writes (non-empty `pluginId`) skip sidecar — preserves the `.gpkg` standalone-export semantics. The two menu-handler sites in `swmmvis.cpp` then drop their duplicate sidecar logic and become trivially correct.
- **Phase RB.2 — "Auto-create on first save" sentinel.** Add a tiny pre-check inside `SWMMVisProjectWindow::saveAs`: if the resolved sidecar path does *not* exist on disk AND `pluginId.isEmpty()`, log a one-line `Creating sibling project file: <oswp>` at Information severity so the user sees the project file being created the first time. Subsequent saves are silent. This addresses the user's exact phrasing — *"if there does not exist a corresponding project, create one with the same name by default"* — by making the auto-create visible.
- **Phase RB.3 — Plumb through every non-menu save site.** Audit and remove now-redundant duplicate sidecar writes from `SWMMVis::onSaveProject` and `SWMMVis::onSaveAs` (since `SWMMVisProjectWindow::saveAs` now owns the responsibility). Confirm the auto-save-before-run path at [src/swmmvis.cpp:3982–3993](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L3982) now writes the sidecar (free win — same call site, no new code).
- **Phase RB.4 — `.oswp` auto-create on `.inp` *open*, when no sidecar exists.** Optional polish per the user's "by default" phrasing: at the end of `SWMMVis::openSingleINP`, if no sidecar exists at `sidecarPathFor(inpPath)`, immediately write one capturing the current canvas state (default layer order, default CRS, no result layers). Cost is one write per first-time open; the alternative (lazy creation on first save) is what RB.1 already does, so RB.4 is purely UX: the user sees `model.oswp` in their file manager the moment they open a project. **Recommendation: ship RB.4 OFF behind a preference (`Preferences/AutoCreateOswpOnOpen`, default `true`) so the user can disable if they want to keep folder contents minimal until they actually save.**
- **Phase RB.5 — Tests.** `tests/gui/test_sidecar_autocreate.cpp` (7 cases — `saveAs(.inp)` writes sidecar; `saveAs(.gpkg)` does NOT write sidecar; auto-save-before-run creates sidecar; first-save sentinel message fires once and only once; sidecar path uses corrected `baseName` so `model.inp.inp` is impossible after Slice RA; `openSingleINP` creates sidecar when RB.4 enabled; `openSingleINP` skips sidecar when RB.4 disabled).

**Files (Slice RB).** Touches `src/swmmvisprojectwindow.cpp` (move sidecar to `saveAs`), `src/swmmvis.cpp` (drop duplicate sidecar logic from menu handlers, add `openSingleINP` auto-create path), `tests/gui/test_sidecar_autocreate.cpp` (new), `docs/manual/03_projects.md` (auto-create behavior note).

**Dependencies.** Slice RA (the path-normalizer) must land first or in the same PR, else the sidecar path computation still produces `model.inp.oswp` on double-extension paths.

### §R.3 Item 3 — Why GeoPackage shows up in the available-plugins list (DECISION APPROVED 2026-05-25 — RC-2 path)

> **User decision (2026-05-25):** "I want the GeoPackage to be discoverable and available." Interpreted as: GeoPackage must appear in `openswmm::discover_plugins_by_id()` output (so the Simulation Options writer combos + Plugins tab list it) and must be selectable as the active Input / Output / Report writer at runtime. This is achieved by **Option RC-2** (explicit built-in registration + symbol-leak hygiene); RC-1 (separate `.so`) and RC-3 (docs-only) are ruled out for this iteration. Rationale recorded below.

**Diagnosis.** GeoPackage is built as a **STATIC** library ([src/engine/input/geopackage/CMakeLists.txt:31](../src/engine/input/geopackage/CMakeLists.txt#L31): `add_library(openswmm_geopackage STATIC …)`) that links into the engine's main library. It exports a global C symbol `openswmm_plugin_info()` ([src/engine/input/geopackage/GeoPackagePluginInfo.cpp:39](../src/engine/input/geopackage/GeoPackagePluginInfo.cpp#L39)) that returns the `GeoPackagePluginInfo` singleton.

Now look at `PluginFactory::discover()` ([src/engine/plugins/PluginFactory.cpp:163–178](../src/engine/plugins/PluginFactory.cpp#L163)). It scans:
1. The engine's library directory (`get_library_directory()`).
2. `<libdir>/plugins/` if it exists.
3. `<libdir>/components/` if it exists.

`scan_directory` opens every shared library it finds via `platform_lib_open`, resolves `openswmm_plugin_info` via `platform_sym` ([line 228](../src/engine/plugins/PluginFactory.cpp#L228)), and if non-null registers the returned info pointer as a plugin.

**The leak.** Because GeoPackage's `openswmm_plugin_info` is a non-`static`, non-namespaced, `extern "C"` symbol exported by the engine's *main* shared library (since the static GeoPackage lib was linked into it), the discovery scan finds this symbol in `libopenswmm_engine.dylib` (or `.so` / `.dll`) and registers GeoPackage as if it were a discovered external plugin. This is **unintentional** — the symbol leak makes a statically-linked component look like a dynamically-loaded plugin.

Notice that `PluginFactory::register_builtin_infos()` ([src/engine/plugins/PluginFactory.cpp:563–588](../src/engine/plugins/PluginFactory.cpp#L563)) explicitly registers only `BuiltinDefault{Input,Output,Report,StateIO}PluginInfo`. GeoPackage is NOT in that list — so its appearance in the plugin enumeration is purely the side-effect described above, not a deliberate registration.

**This is a real bug, not just a UX quirk.** Three concrete problems flow from it:
- The plugin row in the Simulation Options → Plugins tab can be Add/Remove-edited, but removing it has no effect (the singleton remains alive in-process). The user gets misleading UI feedback.
- The "Single container" combobox in the Output sub-tab ([src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp:2310–2318](../src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp#L2310)) explicitly references GeoPackage as the canonical tri-role example — implying GeoPackage is *expected* to be discoverable, which conflates "available via static link" with "available as a runtime plugin".
- The discovery scan picks up the same `openswmm_plugin_info` symbol in the engine binary regardless of which directory the binary lives in, so deploying without `.gpkg` support requires a separate CMake variant rather than a clean "drop the plugin .so to disable" model that the discovery API otherwise affords.

**Why RC-2 over RC-1 / RC-3 (decision rationale, recorded for traceability).**

The user's "discoverable AND available" requirement is satisfied identically by RC-1 and RC-2 at the UI surface — both leave GeoPackage listed in `discover_plugins_by_id()` output, both keep it selectable from the Input / Output / Report writer combos and the Plugins tab. The difference lives below the line:

| Aspect | RC-1 (SHARED `.so` / `.dylib` / `.dll`) | RC-2 (explicit built-in, this slice) | RC-3 (docs-only) |
|--------|-----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|------------------|
| Listed in writer combos | yes — via discovery scan | yes — via `register_builtin_infos` | yes — via leaked symbol |
| Selectable as Input / Output / Report writer | yes | yes | yes |
| Add/Remove on Plugins tab does something | yes (the `.so` is dlopen-able / dlclose-able in principle) | no — correctly disabled (built-in) | no — silently misleading |
| Ships an extra deployment file | yes (one per platform, codesigned on macOS) | no — single engine binary | no |
| Windows DLL placement / RPATH / SIP concerns | yes — non-trivial | none — static link | none |
| Symbol-leak hygiene | clean (separate library) | clean (symbol hidden) | broken |
| Drop-the-`.so`-to-disable workflow | supported | not supported (CMake gate only) | not supported |
| Risk if engine is statically linked into a host binary | adds shared-lib dep | none | none |

RC-1's only unique advantage is the drop-the-`.so`-to-disable deployment model, which the user did NOT ask for — they explicitly want GeoPackage available. RC-3 leaves a misleading UX (Add/Remove pretends to work) and the symbol leak; the user's question itself was prompted by that misleading appearance.

**RC-2 ships the chosen behavior: GeoPackage is a first-class built-in, listed and selectable everywhere a third-party plugin would be, but accurately flagged as a built-in so the UX is honest.**

**Slice RC scope (chosen RC-2 path, APPROVED).**

- **Phase RC.1 — Explicit registration in `PluginFactory::register_builtin_infos`** ([src/engine/plugins/PluginFactory.cpp:563–588](../src/engine/plugins/PluginFactory.cpp#L563)). Add immediately after the four existing `register_one(...)` calls:
  ```cpp
  #ifdef OPENSWMM_HAS_GEOPACKAGE
      register_one(&openswmm::gpkg::GeoPackagePluginInfo::instance());
  #endif
  ```
  Pulls the header transitively via a forward declaration so we don't add a public-header dependency on the geopackage internal lib. The `#ifdef` keeps static-binary builds without geopackage compiling clean (matches the existing `OPENSWMM_HAS_GEOPACKAGE` gate from [src/engine/input/geopackage/CMakeLists.txt:60–62](../src/engine/input/geopackage/CMakeLists.txt#L60)).
- **Phase RC.2 — Hide the leaked C symbol** so the discovery scan can't double-register. On the GeoPackage static-lib CMake target, set:
  ```cmake
  set_target_properties(openswmm_geopackage PROPERTIES
      CXX_VISIBILITY_PRESET hidden
      C_VISIBILITY_PRESET   hidden
      VISIBILITY_INLINES_HIDDEN ON
  )
  ```
  Add `__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))` to the `openswmm_plugin_info` definition in [GeoPackagePluginInfo.cpp:39](../src/engine/input/geopackage/GeoPackagePluginInfo.cpp#L39) so the symbol stays internal to the geopackage TU; remove the prototype from the public-facing `GeoPackagePluginInfo.hpp:163` since no external consumer should resolve it. On MSVC, no `.def` change is needed (the symbol was never declared `__declspec(dllexport)`); the visibility properties harmonise behavior across compilers.
- **Phase RC.3 — Surface `is_builtin` through the discovery API.** `openswmm::discover_plugins_by_id()`'s returned struct currently lacks an `is_builtin` flag. Add it to the struct definition (in the plugin SDK header) defaulting to `false`. `PluginFactory::register_builtin_infos` sets it to `true` on the four Default plugins and on GeoPackage; dynamic discovery in `scan_directory` leaves it `false`. Single source of truth for "this row is a built-in".
- **Phase RC.4 — GUI: Plugins tab honours `is_builtin`.** In [src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp](../src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp) `readPluginsFromEngine` ([line 2477+](../src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp#L2477)), tag each row with the `is_builtin` flag from `discover_plugins_by_id`. The Plugins-tab Remove button greys out when the selected row is built-in; the Add button works as today (you can still add third-party plugins). The writer combos in the Output sub-tab are unaffected — built-in plugins remain freely selectable. Add a small "(built-in)" suffix to the plugin caption in the Plugins-tab table column so the user can see at a glance which rows are baked in.
- **Phase RC.5 — Tests.**
  - engine: `tests/unit/engine/test_pluginfactory_builtins.cpp` (5 cases): (a) GeoPackage registered as built-in when `OPENSWMM_HAS_GEOPACKAGE` defined; (b) NOT registered when undefined; (c) `openswmm_plugin_info` symbol no longer publicly visible from the engine library — assert via `dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "openswmm_plugin_info") == nullptr` on Linux / macOS, skip on MSVC; (d) discovery scan no longer double-registers (count of GeoPackage rows in `registry_` is exactly 1); (e) `is_builtin` flag is `true` on GeoPackage row and `false` on a hypothetical dropped-in shared-lib plugin (test fixture builds a minimal `.so` in a tmp dir).
  - GUI: extend `tests/gui/test_simulationoptionsdialog.cpp` with 2 cases — Remove button disabled when GeoPackage row selected; Remove button enabled when a non-builtin row selected.

**Files (Slice RC, APPROVED).**

| Repo | File | Change |
|------|------|--------|
| engine | [src/engine/plugins/PluginFactory.cpp](../src/engine/plugins/PluginFactory.cpp) | `register_one` call for GeoPackage under `#ifdef OPENSWMM_HAS_GEOPACKAGE`. |
| engine | [src/engine/input/geopackage/CMakeLists.txt](../src/engine/input/geopackage/CMakeLists.txt) | `*_VISIBILITY_PRESET hidden` + `VISIBILITY_INLINES_HIDDEN ON` on `openswmm_geopackage` target. |
| engine | [src/engine/input/geopackage/GeoPackagePluginInfo.cpp](../src/engine/input/geopackage/GeoPackagePluginInfo.cpp) | `__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))` on the `openswmm_plugin_info` definition. |
| engine | [src/engine/input/geopackage/GeoPackagePluginInfo.hpp](../src/engine/input/geopackage/GeoPackagePluginInfo.hpp) | Remove the public prototype for `openswmm_plugin_info` (line 163). |
| engine | plugin-SDK header for `discover_plugins_by_id` return struct | Add `bool is_builtin = false;` field. |
| engine | `tests/unit/engine/test_pluginfactory_builtins.cpp` (new) | 5 cases per Phase RC.5. |
| GUI | [src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp](../src/ui/dialogs/simulationoptionsdialog.cpp) | Plumb `is_builtin` into the Plugins-tab model; grey Remove; add "(built-in)" suffix. |
| GUI | `tests/gui/test_simulationoptionsdialog.cpp` | +2 cases for Remove gating. |
| docs | `docs/PLUGINS.md` (new, engine repo) | Built-in vs discovered taxonomy; current built-ins list (Default I/O/Report/StateIO + GeoPackage); how to author a third-party plugin. |
| docs | `docs/manual/10_simulation_options.md` (GUI repo) | Plugins-tab section: built-in rows explanation + screenshot. |

**Dependencies (Slice RC).** Independent of Slices RA and RB. Can ship before, in parallel with, or after them. The engine PR (Phases RC.1–RC.3 + RC.5 engine tests) lands first; the GUI PR (Phase RC.4 + GUI tests) lands once the engine bump propagates.

**Open follow-up (not blocking RC):** Slice CG's "engine plugin manager UI" eventually wants a richer plugin-row inspector (capabilities, version, registration status). The `is_builtin` flag landed here is one field; capabilities-bitset, version-string, and registration-info follow when CG ships. RC's slice intentionally adds *only* the `is_builtin` field so the smaller PR can ship now without waiting on CG's broader design.

### §R.4 Cross-slice ownership table

| Concern | Owner | Reads | Writes |
|---------|-------|-------|--------|
| Save-As dialog default-suffix tracking | `SWMMVis::onSaveAs` (Slice RA.2) | active filter from `QFileDialog::filterSelected` | `QFileDialog::setDefaultSuffix` |
| Save-As path canonicalization | `normalizeSaveAsPath` (Slice RA.1) | raw dialog result | (none — pure function) |
| Last-used filter memory | `SWMMVis::onSaveAs` (Slice RA.3) | `QSettings` per-project | same |
| Sidecar auto-create | `SWMMVisProjectWindow::saveAs` (Slice RB.1) | `pluginId` (empty = built-in `.inp` writer) | `<stem>.oswp` via `ProjectSerializer::saveToFile` |
| First-time sidecar log message | `SWMMVisProjectWindow::saveAs` (Slice RB.2) | sidecar mtime / existence | log surface only |
| On-open sidecar creation | `SWMMVis::openSingleINP` (Slice RB.4, preference-gated) | `Preferences/AutoCreateOswpOnOpen` | `<stem>.oswp` |
| GeoPackage as explicit built-in | `PluginFactory::register_builtin_infos` (Slice RC) | `OPENSWMM_HAS_GEOPACKAGE` define | `registry_` |
| GeoPackage symbol visibility | GeoPackage static lib (Slice RC) | (none) | (symbol hidden) |
| Plugins tab Add/Remove gating | `SimulationOptionsDialog` (Slice RC, GUI) | `is_builtin` flag from discovery | row UI state |

### §R.5 Sequencing

The three slices can ship in any order; the recommended bundle order minimises user-visible breakage windows:

1. **Slice RA PR** (path normalizer + default-suffix + last-filter memory + 11 tests). Independent; ships first because every later test relies on the correct path math.
2. **Slice RB PR** (sidecar auto-create in `SWMMVisProjectWindow::saveAs` + remove duplicated logic from menu handlers + 7 tests). Requires RA merged (so the sidecar path doesn't inherit the double-extension bug).
3. **Slice RC PR** (APPROVED RC-2 path — engine: explicit GeoPackage builtin registration + symbol-visibility hardening + `is_builtin` flag on discovery API + 5 engine tests; GUI: Plugins tab honours `is_builtin` flag + 2 GUI tests). Independent of RA/RB — can ship before, in parallel with, or after them.

Alternative bundle: RA + RB ship as one PR (they touch overlapping code in `swmmvis.cpp` Save handlers); RC ships separately because it lives almost entirely in the engine repo.

### §R.6 Risk register additions (extends §I)

| ID | Risk | Mitigation |
|----|------|-----------|
| R-R1 | Path normalizer strips a legitimate `<name>.inp.inp` filename a user created on purpose (e.g., a backup convention) | Normalizer only collapses when *both* halves are known writable kinds from `FileFilterRegistry`. A user-coined name with a custom kind passes through unchanged. |
| R-R2 | `setDefaultSuffix` on macOS still appends the suffix when the user types a name that already contains it (Qt behavior on native dialog) | Path normalizer in Phase RA.1 is the defense-in-depth: even if the dialog returns `model.inp.inp`, the normalizer collapses it. The default-suffix change is the *prevention* layer; the normalizer is the *correction* layer. |
| R-R3 | Moving sidecar creation into `SWMMVisProjectWindow::saveAs` causes the auto-save-before-run path to now write a sidecar — slowing Run startup by one disk write | One small disk write (a few KB JSON) on a save the user already initiated; benign. Profile in the existing `test_swmmvis_runactive_perf.cpp` if it exists. |
| R-R4 | Hiding GeoPackage's `openswmm_plugin_info` symbol breaks an external consumer that resolves it directly via `dlsym` | The symbol is undocumented (not in any public header beyond the geopackage internal lib's own `.hpp`) and Slice AA-3's plugin discovery is the only known consumer. Hide is safe; tests assert no external linkage breaks. |
| R-R5 | Slice RB.4 (auto-create on open) writes `.oswp` for every drive-by .inp open the user does — clutters folders with stub project files | Gated behind `Preferences/AutoCreateOswpOnOpen` (default `true` per the user's "by default" request, but easily flipped). Stub `.oswp` is small (<2 KB) and harmless. |

### §R.7 Manual / docs impact

- `docs/manual/03_projects.md` — extend the Save / Save As section with: (1) extension-canonicalization note, (2) sidecar auto-create on every .inp write, (3) plugin-backed exports skip sidecar by design.
- `docs/manual/10_simulation_options.md` — Plugins-tab section: note that GeoPackage is a built-in (Slice RC), is selectable in the Input / Output / Report writer combos like any other plugin, but the Remove button is greyed out for built-in rows (you can't dlclose a static library); the row caption gains a `(built-in)` suffix.
- `docs/PLUGINS.md` (new, in the engine repo) — describe the static-vs-dynamic plugin distinction, list which plugins ship statically (Default Input/Output/Report/StateIO, GeoPackage), and document the discovery surface for third-party plugin authors.

**End of §R. RC's resolution is APPROVED (RC-2 path, see §R.3). Awaiting user approval on RA + RB before code work begins.** Open confirmations: (1) RA's normalizer strategy + default-suffix wiring matches expectations; (2) RB.4's on-open auto-create default (`true` per user phrasing vs `false` to keep folders clean) — recommendation is `true`. RC ready to enter the engine-PR queue (Phases RC.1–RC.3 + RC.5 engine tests) once RA / RB confirmations land.

## §S — Link Attribute Parity + Cross-Section Compound Editor (DRAFT 2026-05-25, awaiting approval)

### §S.0 Why this section exists

The node side of the Property Browser was deepened in Slice DB / DB.2 / DA.4.3: per-type subclasses, tag, coords, computed read-outs (`crownElev`, `fullVolume`, `degree`), post-run stats (`statMaxDepth`, …), and the four compound-edit cells (`Inflows`, `DWF`, `RDII`, `Treatment`) routed through `NodeCompoundEditRef` + `NodeCompoundEditButton` + `NodeCompoundEditDialog`. Subcatchment has the same shape via `SWMMSubcatchPropertyAdapter`.

Links lag behind. `SWMMLinkPropertyAdapter` today exposes only the universal scalars (`name`, `fromNode`, `toNode`, `length`, `roughness`, `offsetUp`, `offsetDn`, `flapGate`) plus a small per-type slice (`crestHeight` / `dischargeCoeff` / `endContractions` on weirs, `pumpCurve` + `initState` on pumps, `offsetUp` aliased as `offset` on orifice/outlet). There is no `tag`, no `Q_PROPERTY` for the **cross-section** (the legacy `Shape` compound-edit row in `objprops.txt:ConduitProps[5]`), no loss-coefficient rows, no seepage / culvert / barrel / initial-flow / max-flow rows, and no compound-edit refs for **Inlet Usage** or the orifice / weir / outlet conditional sub-forms.

Slice **BN** (Phase 6.4) is scoped to land the full modal-dialog editors (`ConduitEditor` / `PumpEditor` / `OrificeEditor` / `WeirEditor` / `OutletEditor` + the deep `XSectionEditor` with the 26-shape live-preview palette + `StreetEditor` / `StandardSizeDialog`). §S sits **between Slice DA and Slice BN** as a *horizontal* first cut: it widens the Property-Browser surface to full legacy parity for every link kind via `Q_PROPERTY` additions + a `LinkCompoundEditRef` family that mirrors the node compound-edit pattern, so the user can edit every legacy `ConduitProps` / `PumpProps` / `OrificeProps` / `WeirProps` / `OutletProps` field inline today, and BN replaces the placeholder cross-section / inlet-usage sub-dialogs with the richer multi-pane variants later.

Per CLAUDE.md §4.01 (`openswmm.gui/CLAUDE.md`) — when in doubt, the legacy SWMM-GUI Delphi sources (`Epaswmm5/objprops.txt` + `Epaswmm5/Dxsect.pas` + `Epaswmm5/Dculvert.pas` + `Epaswmm5/Dinlet*.pas`) are the parity source of truth.

### §S.1 Assumptions + open questions (per CLAUDE.md §1)

**Assumptions (calling out so the user can challenge):**

1. The horizontal first-cut goal is **inline parity in the Property Browser** + a functional but bare-bones modal for the cross-section row. The full live-preview / 26-shape icon palette / `StandardSizeDialog` / `StreetEditor` redesign stays in Slice BN.
2. The XSection cell uses the same compound-edit pattern as the four node cells (`LinkCompoundEditRef` ↔ `LinkCompoundEditButton` ↔ `LinkCompoundEditDialog`), not a custom inline `QComboBox + QSpinBox` strip — this keeps the QPropertyModel / delegate plumbing uniform and reuses the existing metatype + USER-property + `valueChanged()` wiring exactly as Slice DB.2 does for nodes.
3. Round-trip-only fields with a missing engine *getter* (today: `initial_flow`, `max_flow` per `openswmm_links.h:218,227`) ship as Q_PROPERTY *after* the engine getters land — listed as engine gaps **BN-LINK-01a** / **-01b** below.
4. Type-toggle fields (Orifice `SIDE`/`BOTTOM`, Weir `TRANSVERSE`/…/`ROADWAY`, Outlet `FUNCTIONAL`/`TABULAR` × `DEPTH`/`HEAD`) need new engine accessors — listed as **BN-LINK-02..-04**. §S can ship the Q_PROPERTYs with engine setters/getters stubbed (read-only display + grayed-out cells) until the engine work lands, then flip the cells editable in a one-line follow-up.
5. The `applyLink*` family in `SWMMModelLayer` is the single write path. Every new setter slot on the adapter routes through a new `applyLink<Field>` helper on the model layer, which calls `swmm_link_set_*` and emits `attributeChanged(linkName)`. The Property Browser, Attribute Table, Map symbology layer, and (future) profile plot all subscribe to that single signal — no per-view polling.
6. The cross-section sub-dialog mutates the engine *while open* (same as `NodeCompoundEditDialog`'s Apply-as-you-go for `[INFLOWS]` rows); committing the cell back via `setModelData` is purely a "refresh summary" trigger, mirroring `NodeCompoundEditButton::onClicked` line-for-line. Cancel-with-unsaved-edits is handled by the dialog's own Apply / Revert button row, not by a deferred-commit model layer.

**Open questions (please answer before §S enters the build queue):**

- **Q-S1.** Do we want Slice BN's `XSectionEditor` to *supersede* §S.SC entirely (i.e. §S.SC is a 30-day placeholder that gets ripped out when BN lands), or does §S.SC remain the engine-coupled core that BN's live-preview / icon-palette UI *wraps*? Recommendation: the latter — §S.SC's `LinkCompoundEditDialog`'s XSection page is built so BN replaces only the left pane (shape picker → icon view) and the parameter widget bank, leaving the engine-call surface and `LinkCompoundEditRef` plumbing intact.
- **Q-S2.** For the IRREGULAR cross-section shape (transect reference), do we ship a read-only display + "Edit transect…" hand-off to the (already-implemented) `TransectEditorDialog` in §S, and defer the inline read-only profile preview to BN? Recommendation: yes — the inline preview widget already lives in BQ.6.7.4 as a reusable `TransectProfileWidget`, so §S.SC just embeds it.
- **Q-S3.** Should §S land tag-editing parity for links **first** as a tiny isolated Slice SA (mirror of the existing node tag wiring) so the user gets immediate visible benefit while §S.SB / §S.SC are still in code review? Recommendation: yes — §S.SA is one engine-API call (`swmm_link_get_tag` / `_set_tag` already exist per `openswmm_links.h:922,926`) and one `Q_PROPERTY(QString tag …)` on every link adapter subclass.
- **Q-S4.** Loss coefficients (entry / exit / avg) — legacy shows them as **three separate rows** in `ConduitProps[13..15]`. The engine setter/getter `swmm_link_set_loss_coeff` / `_get_loss_coeff` takes all three in one call (`openswmm_links.h:514,525`). Recommendation: three separate `Q_PROPERTY` rows on `SWMMConduitPropertyAdapter` (`lossInlet`, `lossOutlet`, `lossAvg`); each setter reads the other two from the engine first then writes the triple. Confirms with the legacy editing UX; alternatively a `LinkCompoundEditRef::LossCoefficients` cell — but three plain rows are simpler and still propagate through the same `attributeChanged` signal.

### §S.2 In-scope / out-of-scope

**In scope (§S):**

- Tag row on every link subclass adapter.
- Scalar `Q_PROPERTY` additions per link kind to reach legacy parity per `objprops.txt`. Read-only display until the engine getter exists; editable as soon as the round-trip is complete.
- `LinkCompoundEditRef` metatype + `LinkCompoundEditButton` cell widget + `LinkCompoundEditDialog` host (mirror of `NodeCompoundEdit*` triple).
- **XSection** compound-edit row on `SWMMConduitPropertyAdapter` (and the `Orifice` / `Weir` subclasses that share the cross-section concept — orifices use `CIRCULAR` / `RECT_CLOSED`; weirs use TRANSVERSE / SIDEFLOW / TRAPEZOIDAL / V-NOTCH).
- **Inlet Usage** compound-edit row on `SWMMConduitPropertyAdapter` — placeholder dialog hosting a `QTableWidget` for `[INLETS]` rows; BO Phase 6.5.8 replaces with the rich `InletUsageEditor`.
- **Culvert Code** compound-edit row on `SWMMConduitPropertyAdapter` — single combo over the 6 legacy FHWA chart codes + "None" sentinel; engine getter/setter pair already exists.
- `applyLink*` helpers on `SWMMModelLayer` for every new setter (one helper per field; all emit `attributeChanged(name)`).
- MVC verification: Property Browser ↔ Attribute Table ↔ Map symbology ↔ (existing) hover-tooltip layer all refresh off the single `attributeChanged` signal — no view-side polling.

**Out of scope (deferred to Slice BN):**

- Multi-pane modal `XSectionEditor` with live parametric figure, 26-shape SVG palette, debounced redraw, dimension arrows, design-flow water surface overlay.
- `StandardSizeDialog` (legacy `Darchpipe.pas` size table).
- `StreetEditor` + `STREET` xsection branch (Slice BN Phase 6.4.6).
- `CUSTOM` xsection inline shape-curve preview.
- Variable-speed pump fields (Slice BN Phase 6.4.5).
- Right-click "Change Type…" on links (Slice BN Phase 6.4.1 — engine gap AG.1 needed first).

### §S.3 MVC architecture (the engineering invariant)

The legacy SWMM-GUI `Fproped.pas` reads engine state straight into the form on open and writes it straight back on close — a one-shot dialog model with no live propagation. The user explicitly called out (CLAUDE.md `openswmm.engine/CLAUDE.md` §5.1) that the modern GUI must use Qt MVC so the same data edited from one surface (Property Browser) propagates to every other viewer (Attribute Table, Map, Profile Plot, future scripting console). §S inherits and reinforces the pattern already established by Slice DA / DB:

```
┌───────────────────────────┐    every getter round-trips
│       SWMM_Engine         │ ←── into the engine; no view-
│   (single source of truth)│    side cache of attributes.
└───────────────▲───────────┘
                │ swmm_link_set_*  /  swmm_link_get_*
                │
┌───────────────┴───────────┐
│      SWMMModelLayer       │   single write path; emits
│  applyLink<Field>(idx,v)  │── attributeChanged(name) on
│  → swmm_link_set_<Field>  │   every successful mutation.
└───────────────▲───────────┘
                │ attributeChanged(name)
                │
   ┌────────────┼──────────────┬────────────────┬───────────────┐
   │            │              │                │               │
┌──┴──┐  ┌──────┴────────┐ ┌──┴────────┐ ┌─────┴────┐  ┌────────┴────────┐
│ Map │  │ Property      │ │ Attribute │ │ Profile  │  │  Future:        │
│ ren-│  │ Browser       │ │ Table     │ │ Plot     │  │  Scripting cons-│
│ der │  │ (QPropMod +   │ │ (Object   │ │ (BC)     │  │  ole, REST API, │
│ er  │  │ Q_PROPERTY    │ │ Browser)  │ │          │  │  results panes  │
│     │  │ adapter)      │ │           │ │          │  │                 │
└─────┘  └───────────────┘ └───────────┘ └──────────┘  └─────────────────┘
```

Concretely:

1. **Adapter (Model):** `SWMMLinkPropertyAdapter` subclasses. **No state on the adapter** — every `Q_PROPERTY` getter calls `swmm_link_get_*`; every WRITE slot calls *(via the model layer)* `swmm_link_set_*` and re-emits `changed()`. Matches `SWMMNodePropertyAdapter` exactly.
2. **Model layer (Controller):** `SWMMModelLayer::applyLink<Field>(int idx, ValueType v) → bool`. Validates, calls `swmm_link_set_*`, returns false on engine error, on success emits `attributeChanged(linkName)`. No view-side knowledge.
3. **Views (Property Browser, Attribute Table, Map):** subscribe to `attributeChanged(QString)`. Property Browser calls `adapter->refresh()`; Attribute Table re-reads the affected row; Map calls `update()` on the affected link's bbox. **No view talks to another view directly.**
4. **Compound-edit dialogs (e.g. XSection):** mutate the engine *during* the dialog (via the same `applyLink*` helpers), so every keystroke propagates in real time. Cancelling reverts via a dialog-internal snapshot taken on open (mirrors `NodeCompoundEditDialog::reject` ↔ `restoreSnapshot`). **No "save on OK" — Apply-as-you-go.**

Two visible consequences:

- Editing a conduit's cross-section in the Property Browser repaints the map symbology (line width if styled by capacity / depth) and refreshes the Attribute Table's `Shape` column in the same paint tick.
- Selecting a link in the Object Browser, opening the XSection dialog, dragging Geom1 → the map redraws live as the user drags; cancelling the dialog reverts both the Property Browser row and the map.

### §S.4 Current state — what `SWMMLinkPropertyAdapter` exposes today

Source-of-truth: [include/ui/properties/swmmlinkpropertyadapter.h](../include/ui/properties/swmmlinkpropertyadapter.h).

| Link kind | Common Q_PROPERTY (base) | Per-kind Q_PROPERTY (subclass) |
|-----------|--------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **(all)** | `name`, `linkKind`, `fromNode`, `toNode` | — |
| **Conduit** | ↑ | `length`, `roughness`, `offsetUp`, `offsetDn`, `flapGate` |
| **Pump** | ↑ | `pumpCurve` (DataObjectRef), `initState` |
| **Orifice** | ↑ | `offset` (= offsetUp), `dischargeCoeff`, `flapGate` |
| **Weir** | ↑ | `offsetUp`, `offsetDn`, `crestHeight`, `dischargeCoeff`, `endContractions`, `flapGate` |
| **Outlet** | ↑ | `offset` (= offsetUp), `flapGate` |

No tag. No xsection. No loss coeffs. No barrels / seepage / culvert / max-flow / init-flow. No orifice type / shape / time-to-open-close. No weir type / road weir extras / coeff curve / can-surcharge. No outlet rating type / coeff / exponent / curve.

### §S.6 Slice SA — Link tag parity (Phase 6.2.6 / DA companion)

**Engine prerequisites:** none (`swmm_link_get_tag` / `_set_tag` already in `openswmm_links.h:922,926`).

**GUI work:**

- `SWMMLinkPropertyAdapter`: add `tag()` getter + `setTag(QString)` slot in base class (mirror of `SWMMNodePropertyAdapter::tag` / `setTag` at `swmmnodepropertyadapter.h:93,158`).
- Each of the 5 subclasses (`Conduit` / `Pump` / `Orifice` / `Weir` / `Outlet`): one new `Q_PROPERTY(QString tag READ tag WRITE setTag NOTIFY changed)` row (placed right after `name` to match the node convention).

**Cost:** ~80 LOC across 3 files. Lands first; lowest risk.

### §S.7 Slice SB — Scalar attribute parity (`Q_PROPERTY` additions)

Adds all the "no engine gap, single scalar" fields from §S.5. Mirrors `SWMMNodePropertyAdapter`'s straightforward `Q_PROPERTY` + getter + setter slot pattern; each setter goes through a new `applyLink<Field>` helper on `SWMMModelLayer`.

**Engine prerequisites (verify at slice-start; if missing, file as engine gaps):**

- **BN-LINK-01a** `swmm_link_get_initial_flow(SWMM_Engine, int idx, double* flow)` — symmetric getter for the existing setter. Engine implementation: read `Link[idx].q0` field. ~6-line patch + 1 test.
- **BN-LINK-01b** `swmm_link_get_max_flow(SWMM_Engine, int idx, double* flow)` — symmetric getter for the existing setter. Read `Conduit[Link[idx].subIndex].qMax` (conduit-only). ~10-line patch + 1 test.

**GUI work (after engine gaps land):**

- `SWMMConduitPropertyAdapter` adds: `initialFlow`, `maxFlow`, `lossInlet`, `lossOutlet`, `lossAvg`, `seepRate`, `barrels`. Seven new `Q_PROPERTY` rows. Loss-coeff setters internally read the other two via `swmm_link_get_loss_coeff` before writing the triple — see §S.1 Q-S4.
- `SWMMLinkPropertyAdapter` (base): add the accessor methods (one per field) using the GETTER_D macro pattern already in `swmmlinkpropertyadapter.cpp:90`.
- `SWMMModelLayer`: `applyLinkInitialFlow`, `applyLinkMaxFlow`, `applyLinkLossCoeffs` (one helper writing the triple — atomic from the model layer's view), `applyLinkSeepRate`, `applyLinkBarrels`. All emit `attributeChanged(linkName)`.
- `displayLabelFor` additions with unit suffixes (`(cfs)` / `(cms)` for flow, `(in/hr)` / `(mm/hr)` for seepage, dimensionless for the rest).
- Tests: `tests/gui/test_conduit_scalar_roundtrip.cpp` — 14 cases (2 per field: set+read, plus loss-coeff triple-write atomicity).

**Cost:** ~250 LOC across 3 files. Conduit-only; pump / orifice / weir / outlet scalar additions are blocked on engine gaps **BN-LINK-02..-10**.

`LinkCompoundEditDialog`:

- Host with a `QStackedWidget` page-per-kind, exactly like `NodeCompoundEditDialog`.
- Apply-as-you-go via the `applyLink*` helpers; dialog-internal snapshot on open + restore on `reject()` so cancel is non-destructive.
- "Edit transect…" / "Edit shape curve…" buttons on the XSection page hand off to the (already-implemented) `TransectEditorDialog` / `CurveEditorDialog` (BQ.6.7.1 / .4 — landed 2026-05-24 per the file-header note).

**§S.SC.1.a — XSection page layout (amended 2026-05-25):** The shape picker on the XSection page is a horizontal `QSplitter` (`Qt::Horizontal`, user-resizable) rather than a single `QComboBox`. **Left pane:** a `QListWidget` in `IconMode` with `flow=LeftToRight`, `wrapping=true`, `viewMode=IconMode`, and the label below the icon — one row per allowed shape (filtered by link type as today: 20 for Conduit, 2 for Orifice, 3 for Weir). Each item's icon is rendered from a user-supplied SVG asset under `:/swmmvis/xsects/<basename>` (25 files registered in `resources/swmmvis.qrc` — 20 cover today's `kShapes` set; 5 — `baskethandle_xsect.svg`, `custom_xsect.svg`, `dummy_xsect.svg`, `forcemain_xsect.svg`, `street_xsect.svg` — are pre-staged for Slice BN.6.4.4). The engine-id → basename map lives in `xsectSvgBasenameFor()` in `linkcompoundeditdialog.cpp`. A procedural colored-tile placeholder (`makePlaceholderShapeIcon()`) is retained as the fallback for `QIcon::isNull()` (e.g. when the test binary doesn't compile `swmmvis.qrc`, or when a future shape id has no asset yet) so the palette is never blank. **Right pane:** the existing contextual params form (per-shape `Geom1..4` `QDoubleSpinBox` rows with shape-aware labels, `Barrels` `QSpinBox`, live summary `QLabel`). Selection on the left drives `updateXsectFieldVisibility()` + `applyXsect()` exactly like the combo did. The splitter persists no state across sessions in §S.SC.1.a — that lands with BN.6.4.4's preferences integration. This is a leaf-widget rewrite inside the page, so the `LinkCompoundEditButton` ↔ `LinkCompoundEditRef` ↔ delegate plumbing is untouched and the §S.SC tests continue to pass without modification. See [R-S5](#S13) for the contract Slice BN.6.4.4 inherits.

**SWMMModelLayer additions:**

```
bool applyLinkXsect(int linkIdx, int shape, double g1, double g2, double g3, double g4);
bool applyLinkBarrels(int linkIdx, int n);              // shared with §S.SB
bool applyLinkCulvertCode(int linkIdx, int code);
bool applyLinkInletUsage(int linkIdx, …);                 // shape TBD by BO 6.5.8 contract
```

All emit `attributeChanged(linkName)`. The xsect mutation additionally invalidates the link's full-flow capacity cache; the symbology renderer recomputes on the next paint tick triggered by the same signal.

**Tests:**

- `tests/gui/test_linkcompoundeditref.cpp` (4 cases — metatype converter, USER-property round-trip, Apply / Revert on dialog, attributeChanged emitted once per Apply).
- `tests/gui/test_link_xsect_roundtrip.cpp` (19 cases — one per `SWMM_XSectShape` value, set + read-back + delegate cell summary text).
- `tests/gui/test_link_culvert_code.cpp` (7 cases — 6 codes + None sentinel).

**Cost:** ~600 LOC across 9 new files + ~80 LOC in `swmmlinkpropertyadapter.{h,cpp}` + ~50 LOC in `swmmmodellayer.cpp`.

### §S.12 Sequencing

1. **Slice SA (lands first; ~80 LOC):** Link tag parity. No engine work. Visible benefit immediately.
2. **Engine PR — gaps BN-LINK-01a / -01b only** (initial-flow / max-flow getters). Lowest-risk additions; ~30 LOC engine-side + 2 tests.
3. **Slice SB:** Conduit scalar parity (init flow, max flow, loss coeffs, seepage, barrels). Depends on step 2.
4. **Slice SC.1 (XSection compound cell — conduit only):** `LinkCompoundEditRef` + `LinkCompoundEditButton` + `LinkCompoundEditDialog` (XSection page only). Uses existing `swmm_link_get_xsect` / `_set_xsect`.
5. **Slice SC.2 (Culvert + Inlet-Usage compound cells):** Add `CulvertCode` and `InletUsage` pages to the dialog. Inlet-Usage page is a placeholder QTableWidget — BO Phase 6.5.8 replaces.
6. **Engine PR — gaps BN-LINK-02..-10 bundle:** Full conditional-field set. ~600 LOC engine-side + 11 tests.
7. **Slice SD:** Conditional-field GUI follow-up (orifice type / weir type / outlet rating / pump startup-shutoff / weir extras / roadway weir).
8. **MVC verification pass:** end-to-end test that edits made in the Property Browser propagate to the Attribute Table + Map + (existing) hover-tooltip + cell-editor cancel reverts everything. New `tests/gui/test_link_mvc_propagation.cpp` (8 cases).
9. **Slice BN (downstream, not part of §S):** rich modal editors replace the §S.SC pages' inner bodies.

Total §S delivery — without the engine PRs: **~1100 LOC GUI + ~50 cases of test parity**. With the full engine PR bundle: **+~700 LOC engine + 11 tests**.

### §S.13 Risk register (additions to §I)

| ID | Risk | Mitigation |
|----|------|-----------|
| R-S1 | Apply-as-you-go on the XSection dialog leaves the engine in a half-valid state if the user changes shape (e.g. CIRCULAR → TRAPEZOIDAL) without filling in the new shape's geom3/geom4 — engine may reject the partial set | Dialog's shape combo writes a *complete* default set on shape change (legacy `DefConduit` defaults seeded from `objprops.txt:436`); a single `applyLinkXsect` call is the smallest atomic mutation. |
| R-S2 | Conduit `Max Depth` shown in the inline property row + inside the XSection dialog will go out of sync between the two surfaces during edit | Both surfaces are bound to the same adapter Q_PROPERTY; the dialog mutates the engine via `applyLinkXsect`, which emits `attributeChanged`; the adapter re-emits `changed()`; the property browser's `maxDepth` cell re-reads. No second source of truth. |
| R-S3 | The `LinkCompoundEditRef` metatype collides with `NodeCompoundEditRef`'s registered string converter | Distinct `Q_DECLARE_METATYPE` types; converters are keyed by metatype id, not by ref-struct name. Test `test_metatype_no_collision.cpp` asserts both converters live side-by-side. |
| R-S4 | Round-trip getter for `initial_flow` / `max_flow` (engine gaps BN-LINK-01a/b) is a surprising omission — there may be a structural reason in the engine (e.g. these are write-once at simulation start) | Verify at slice-start: read `solver/swmm_links.cpp` to confirm `Link[i].q0` and `Conduit[Link[i].subIndex].qMax` are stored as engine state across the simulation. If not, document as runtime-only and ship the Q_PROPERTY as a write-only cell that displays "—" on read. |
| R-S5 | Slice BN replaces §S.SC's XSection page body — risk of breaking the metatype contract during the swap | §S.SC's dialog defines a stable widget contract: page exposes `setRef(LinkCompoundEditRef)` / `commit() → bool` / `revert()`. BN's rich page implements the same three methods and slots into the same `QStackedWidget` index. No metatype or model-layer changes; BN is a leaf-widget replacement. |
| R-S6 | Inlet-usage placeholder dialog ships before the engine accessors (BN-LINK-11) are confirmed | Placeholder is read-only display only; the "Edit…" button on the row is disabled with a tooltip naming Slice BO Phase 6.5.8. Same gating pattern as `SWMMRainGagePropertyAdapter`'s sub-table fields in Slice DA.2. |

| R-S9 | Splitter geometry doesn't restore across sessions (project save / load round-trip). | Splitter state isn't part of `.oswp` today (see Phase 12 — Project File Persistence); the dialog is modal and its layout resets on each open. No persistence required at the §S.SC.1.a stage; BN may layer a per-user QSettings restore later. |

**Engine gaps newly identified by §S.SC.1.a:**

- **BN-XS-01** — sidewalls for `RECT_OPEN` cross-section. The legacy SWMM-GUI exposes a 4-value combo (`BOTH` / `LEFT_ONLY` / `RIGHT_ONLY` / `NONE`) used by the 2D-coupling overland-flow path; the engine doesn't have an accessor today. File alongside the BN-LINK-07..-10 weir bundle since both touch the same hydraulics path. Estimated effort: ~40 LOC engine + 2 unit tests. Defer until BN Phase 6.4.4 starts.

**Sequencing fit:** §S.SC.1.a slots between §S.SC.1 (compound-edit plumbing, landed) and Slice BN Phase 6.4.4 (full rich editor). It's a one-PR widget rework — no engine work, no metatype changes, no plan-doc churn beyond this subsection. The cpp follow-up is the immediate next item on the build queue.

## §T — Subcatchment Attribute Parity + Compound Editors (DRAFT 2026-05-25, awaiting approval)

### §T.0 Why this section exists

Nodes (Slice DA / DB / DB.2 / DA.4.3) and links (Slice §S, drafted) have a deepened Property Browser surface — per-type subclasses, tags, computed read-outs, post-run stats, compound-edit cells routed through `NodeCompoundEditRef` / `LinkCompoundEditRef` + button + dialog triples. Subcatchments lag substantially: `SWMMSubcatchPropertyAdapter` ([include/ui/properties/swmmsubcatchpropertyadapter.h](../include/ui/properties/swmmsubcatchpropertyadapter.h)) exposes only eight hydrology scalars — `name`, `area`, `width`, `slope`, `impervPct`, `nImperv`, `nPerv`, `dsImperv`, `dsPerv`. No tag, no rain-gage assignment, no outlet, no infiltration model picker / params, no groundwater, no LID group, no snowpack, no land-use coverages, no initial pollutant buildup, no curb length, no subarea routing, no n-perv / Dstore / infiltration patterns, no rainfall / runoff / evap / infil / snow-depth post-run summary, no `xCoord`/`yCoord` centroid, no `Description` (comment) plumbing.

Legacy `SubcatchProps` (`SWMM-GUI/Epaswmm5/objprops.txt:704–736`) defines **28 rows** that the Property Browser is supposed to surface, half of which open the seven sub-dialogs `Dinfil.pas` (infiltration), `Dgwater.pas` (groundwater per-subcatch), `Dsubland.pas` (land-use percentages), `Dloads.pas` (initial pollutant loads), `Dlidgroup.pas` + `Dlidusage.pas` (LID assignment), and `Dsnow.pas` (snowpack — referenced by name only here; the editor itself lives in §T's companion Slice BP).

§T sits between Slice DA / §S and Slice BO (Phase 6.5 — the full modal `SubcatchmentEditor` plus the rich LID / land-use / infiltration / pollutant-loads sub-editors) as a **horizontal first cut** that widens the Property Browser surface to full legacy parity via Q_PROPERTY additions + a `SubcatchCompoundEditRef` family that mirrors `NodeCompoundEditRef` / `LinkCompoundEditRef`. The user can edit every legacy `SubcatchProps` field inline today; Slice BO replaces the placeholder sub-dialogs with the richer multi-pane editors later.

Per `openswmm.gui/CLAUDE.md` §4.01 — when in doubt, the legacy SWMM-GUI Delphi sources (`Epaswmm5/objprops.txt` + `Epaswmm5/Dsubland.pas` + `Epaswmm5/Dinfil.pas` + `Epaswmm5/Dgwater.pas` + `Epaswmm5/Daquifer.pas` + `Epaswmm5/Dsnow.pas` + `Epaswmm5/Dlidgroup.pas` + `Epaswmm5/Dlidusage.pas` + `Epaswmm5/Dloads.pas`) are the parity source of truth.

### §T.1 Assumptions + open questions (per CLAUDE.md §1)

**Assumptions (calling out so the user can challenge):**

1. The horizontal first-cut goal is **inline parity in the Property Browser** + functional but bare-bones modal pages for the six compound rows (Infiltration / Groundwater / LID Group / Land Uses / Initial Buildup / Snowpack). The full multi-tab `SubcatchmentEditor` modal with the live runoff-routing diagram, the LID library picker with cross-section preview, and the per-pollutant treatment grid stays in Slice BO Phase 6.5.x.
2. Subcatchments are a **single object kind** — unlike nodes (4 subclasses) and links (5 subclasses), there is no `SubcatchKind` discriminator. Q_PROPERTY rows live directly on `SWMMSubcatchPropertyAdapter`; no subclassing. Object-Browser per-type grouping (Slice S virtualised tree) is unaffected.
3. The six compound-edit cells use the same compound-edit pattern as the four node cells and the three link cells — a new `SubcatchCompoundEditRef` metatype + `SubcatchCompoundEditButton` cell widget + `SubcatchCompoundEditDialog` host. This keeps the QPropertyModel / delegate plumbing uniform and reuses the metatype + USER-property + `valueChanged()` wiring exactly as Slice DB.2 / SC.1 do.
4. Apply-as-you-go: the compound dialogs mutate the engine *during* the dialog (every keystroke propagates), and Cancel reverts via a dialog-internal snapshot taken on open. Same contract as `NodeCompoundEditDialog` and `LinkCompoundEditDialog`.
5. The `applySubcatch*` family on `SWMMModelLayer` is the single write path. Today only `applySubcatchAdd`, `applySubcatchDelete`, `applySubcatchVertices`, `applySubcatchArea` exist (see `swmmmodellayer.h:1039–1126`). §T adds one helper per new scalar setter; every helper emits `attributeChanged(subcatchName)`. Property Browser, Attribute Table, Map symbology layer, and (future) profile / runoff-time-series plot all subscribe to that single signal — no view-side polling.
6. Round-trip-only fields with missing engine getters (e.g. infiltration **Pattern** assignment, **Snow Pack** assignment, **Aquifer** assignment, **Subarea Routing** direction + percent, **Curb Length**, **Initial Buildup** per-pollutant loadings) ship Q_PROPERTY *after* the engine getter/setter pair lands. The engine gap list (`§T.10`) sequences them as one bundle (**BO-SUB-01..-12**) that the GUI slices in §T.SU consume.
7. Coordinates: legacy `SubcatchProps[1..2]` are X/Y of the centroid, which the engine computes from the polygon — they're read-only in the property browser. Polygon vertex edits route through the already-implemented `applySubcatchVertices`; the centroid Q_PROPERTY is computed live from `swmm_spatial_get_polygon` + a centroid pass. Editing X/Y inline (drag the centroid label) is out of scope for §T — that lives in Slice AU's polygon-edit map tool.
8. The legacy `Description` (`SubcatchProps[3]`) is a free-form comment; the engine currently has no per-subcatchment comment storage (same gap as conduit `Description` in §S). Defer to Slice BV/BM (comment-storage engine surface).

**Open questions (please answer before §T enters the build queue):**

- **Q-T1.** Six compound cells is a lot of rows compared to the four on a node and three on a link. Recommendation: ship them in **two visual groups** in the Property Browser — *Hydrology subforms* (Infiltration, Groundwater, Snowpack) and *Water-quality subforms* (Land Uses, Initial Buildup, LID Group) — using the existing `setRowEditable` / heading-row mechanism (Slice DA.4.3) so a single non-editable heading row separates each group. Confirm grouping or pick alternate ordering.
- **Q-T2.** Subarea Routing (`SubcatchProps[16..17]` — direction enum + percent routed) is a two-field tuple that legacy edits as two adjacent rows. Recommendation: two **separate** Q_PROPERTY rows on the adapter (`subareaRouting` Q_ENUM + `pctRouted` double), each routed through its own `applySubcatchSubareaRouting` / `applySubcatchPctRouted` helper. Alternative: a `SubcatchCompoundEditRef::SubareaRouting` cell — but two plain rows are cheaper and propagate through the same `attributeChanged` signal. Recommendation: two plain rows.
- **Q-T3.** Should §T land tag-editing parity for subcatchments **first** as a tiny isolated Slice TA (mirror of node Slice DB tag + §S.SA) so the user gets immediate visible benefit while §T.TB / §T.TC are still in code review? Recommendation: yes — `swmm_subcatch_get_tag` / `_set_tag` already exist (`openswmm_subcatchments.h:682,686`); one Q_PROPERTY + one `applySubcatchTag` helper + 1 test = ~60 LOC.
- **Q-T4.** Infiltration model is a **per-subcatchment override** of the project-wide `INFIL_MODEL` option. The engine exposes `swmm_subcatch_get_infil_model` / `_set_infil_*_param` triples for HORTON / GREEN_AMPT / CURVE_NUMBER, but the active model is changed by writing the corresponding parameter set (no scalar setter for "switch model only"). Recommendation: the §T.TC Infiltration page shows a 4-radio selector (HORTON / MODIFIED_HORTON / GREEN_AMPT / MODIFIED_GREEN_AMPT / CURVE_NUMBER — 5 values, not 4; legacy `Dinfil.pas` ComboBox1 has 5 entries) plus a parameter block whose visible rows depend on the model selection. Switching model writes the new model's default parameter set via the corresponding `_set_infil_*` accessor; the previous model's parameters are not destroyed (legacy SWMM-GUI preserves the most-recently-edited per-model set in its own in-memory cache — replicate this on the dialog, not the engine). The Property Browser row summary reads `model name + key params`. Confirm Q-T4 or pick alternate UX.
- **Q-T5.** Groundwater (`Dgwater.pas`) couples a subcatchment to an aquifer **plus** 12 per-subcatchment GW-flow parameters (A1/B1, A2/B2, A3, surface elev, threshold, override of aquifer bottom / water table / unsat moisture, custom lateral / deep equations). The engine today exposes only `swmm_aquifer_count` / `_index` / `_id` / `_add` — no aquifer **parameter** setters and no per-subcatch **GW-flow** parameter setters. Recommendation: §T.TC's Groundwater page ships as **placeholder** (aquifer name picker + an "Edit GW flow params…" button that is disabled with tooltip naming Slice BO Phase 6.6 + Slice BP `AquiferEditor`); the inline cell summary shows just the assigned aquifer name. The engine today exposes only `swmm_lid_usage_add` (no count / get / set / remove). Recommendation: §T.TC's LID page ships as **placeholder** read-only display only; the "Edit…" button is disabled with tooltip naming Slice BO Phase 6.5.7. The cell summary reads `N LIDs assigned`. Engine gap **BO-SUB-09** opens up the full CRUD surface so Slice BO can deepen the page.
- **Q-T7.** Land Uses (`Dsubland.pas`) is a stringgrid of `(landuse_name, percent)` rows that must sum to 100. The engine has `swmm_subcatch_set_coverage(sc_idx, lu_idx, fraction)` / `_get_coverage` — symmetric pair already exists. §T.TC's Land Uses page can ship **fully editable** today: a `QTableWidget` rebuilt from `swmm_landuse_count` rows × the percent per subcatch. Apply-as-you-go writes each cell on commit. Recommendation: ship full edit in §T (not placeholder); Slice BO Phase 6.5.6's deepening is the live-validation "must sum ≤ 100" feedback strip + per-pollutant land-use breakdown links. Confirm Q-T7.
- **Q-T8.** Initial Buildup (`Dloads.pas`) is a grid of `(pollutant_name, initial_load lb/ac or kg/ha)` rows — one row per pollutant. Engine today exposes `swmm_pollutants_set_init_conc` for runoff *concentration*, but not the per-subcatchment initial *surface buildup* loads. Recommendation: §T.TC's Initial Buildup page ships as **placeholder** read-only display; the "Edit…" button is disabled with tooltip naming Slice BO Phase 6.5.9. ### §T.3 MVC architecture (the engineering invariant)

Same invariant as §S, reinforced for the subcatchment surface. Per `openswmm.engine/CLAUDE.md` §5.1, every viewer/editor must stay synchronized through the engine + a single write path + a single `attributeChanged` signal — no view-side caches.

```
┌───────────────────────────┐    every getter round-trips
│       SWMM_Engine         │ ←── into the engine; no view-
│   (single source of truth)│    side cache of attributes.
└───────────────▲───────────┘
                │ swmm_subcatch_set_*  /  swmm_subcatch_get_*
                │ swmm_subcatch_set_coverage / _set_infil_horton / _set_infil_green_ampt / …
┌───────────────┴───────────┐
│      SWMMModelLayer       │   single write path; emits
│  applySubcatch<Field>(…)  │── attributeChanged(name) on
│  → swmm_subcatch_set_<…>  │   every successful mutation.
└───────────────▲───────────┘
                │ attributeChanged(name)
                │
   ┌────────────┼──────────────┬─────────────────┬──────────────────┐
   │            │              │                 │                  │
┌──┴──┐  ┌──────┴────────┐ ┌──┴────────┐  ┌─────┴────────┐  ┌──────┴─────────┐
│ Map │  │ Property      │ │ Attribute │  │ Runoff       │  │  Future:       │
│ pol-│  │ Browser       │ │ Table     │  │ time-series  │  │  scripting /   │
│ ygon│  │ (QPropMod +   │ │ (Object   │  │ plot (CF)    │  │  REST API /    │
│ ren-│  │ Q_PROPERTY    │ │ Browser)  │  │              │  │  result panes  │
│ der │  │ adapter)      │ │           │  │              │  │                │
└─────┘  └───────────────┘ └───────────┘  └──────────────┘  └────────────────┘
```

Concretely:

1. **Adapter (Model):** `SWMMSubcatchPropertyAdapter`. **No state on the adapter** — every Q_PROPERTY getter calls `swmm_subcatch_get_*`; every WRITE slot calls *(via the model layer)* `swmm_subcatch_set_*` and re-emits `changed()`. Matches `SWMMNodePropertyAdapter` / `SWMMLinkPropertyAdapter` exactly.
2. **Model layer (Controller):** `SWMMModelLayer::applySubcatch<Field>(int idx, ValueType v) → bool`. Validates, calls `swmm_subcatch_set_*`, returns false on engine error, on success emits `attributeChanged(subcatchName)`. No view-side knowledge.
3. **Views (Property Browser, Attribute Table, Map):** subscribe to `attributeChanged(QString)`. Property Browser calls `adapter->refresh()`; Attribute Table re-reads the affected row; Map polygon renderer calls `update()` on the affected subcatchment's bbox. **No view talks to another view directly.**
4. **Compound-edit dialogs (Infiltration / Groundwater / LID Group / Land Uses / Initial Buildup / Snowpack):** mutate the engine *during* the dialog (via the same `applySubcatch*` helpers), so every keystroke propagates in real time. Cancelling reverts via a dialog-internal snapshot taken on open (mirrors `NodeCompoundEditDialog::reject` ↔ `restoreSnapshot` and `LinkCompoundEditDialog`). **No "save on OK" — Apply-as-you-go.**

Two visible consequences:

- Editing a subcatchment's `%Imperv` in the Property Browser repaints the map polygon (fill color if styled by `pct_imperv`) and refreshes the Attribute Table's `%Imperv` column in the same paint tick.
- Selecting a subcatchment, opening the Infiltration dialog, dragging the Horton `MaxRate` slider → the map polygon fill (when styled by `max_rate`) redraws live; cancelling the dialog reverts both the Property Browser row and the map polygon fill.

| Q_PROPERTY today |
|-------------------|
| `name`, `area`, `width`, `slope`, `impervPct`, `nImperv`, `nPerv`, `dsImperv`, `dsPerv` |

Total: **8 editable scalars**. No tag. No xCoord/yCoord. No raingage. No outlet. No infiltration. No groundwater. No LID. No snowpack. No land-use coverages. No initial buildup. No curb length. No subarea-routing. No pct-zero-imperv. No patterns. No post-run stats.

### §T.12 Sequencing

1. **Slice TA (lands first; ~60 LOC):** Subcatchment tag parity. No engine work. Visible benefit immediately.
2. **Slice TB (~200 LOC):** Centroid X/Y (RO) + rain-gage picker + outlet picker (node-or-subcatch) + 3 read-only post-run stats. No engine work.
3. **Slice TC.1 (Infiltration compound cell — fully wired):** `SubcatchCompoundEditRef` + `SubcatchCompoundEditButton` + `SubcatchCompoundEditDialog` (Infiltration page only). Uses existing `swmm_subcatch_get_infil_*` / `_set_infil_*` triples.
4. **Slice TC.2 (Land Uses compound cell — fully wired):** Add Land Uses page; uses existing `swmm_subcatch_get_coverage` / `_set_coverage`.
5. **Slice TC.3 (placeholder compound cells: Groundwater + Snowpack + LID Group + Initial Buildup):** Add 4 placeholder pages with "Edit…" disabled + tooltips naming the Slice BO / BP phases that deepen them.
6. **Engine PR — gaps BO-SUB-01..-12 bundle:** 12 accessor pairs across 3 headers + python + MCP tool surface.
7. **Slice TD:** Engine-gap-gated GUI follow-up — `pctZeroImperv`, `subareaRouting`, `pctRouted`, `curbLength`, 3 pattern pickers. Then deepen 4 placeholder compound pages into fully wired pages (Groundwater consumes BO-SUB-04..-08; LID Group consumes BO-SUB-09; Initial Buildup consumes BO-SUB-10; Snowpack consumes BO-SUB-11).
8. **MVC verification pass:** end-to-end test that edits made in the Property Browser propagate to the Attribute Table + Map polygon + (existing) hover-tooltip + cell-editor Cancel reverts everything. New `tests/gui/test_subcatch_mvc_propagation.cpp` (10 cases).
9. **Slice BO / BP (downstream, not part of §T):** rich modal editors (`SubcatchmentEditor`, `LidUsageEditor`, `AquiferEditor`, `SnowpackEditor`, `InitialPollutantLoadsEditor`) replace the §T.TC pages' inner bodies via the stable page contract (`setRef` / `commit` / `revert`).

Total §T delivery — without the engine PRs: **~1300 LOC GUI + ~40 test cases**. With the full engine PR bundle: **+~1000–1200 LOC engine + 12 tests** (plus companion bundle for Slice BP, ~400 LOC + 2 tests).

### §T.13 Risk register (additions to §I)

| ID | Risk | Mitigation |
|----|------|-----------|
| R-T1 | Apply-as-you-go on the Infiltration dialog leaves the engine in a half-valid state if the user switches model (HORTON → GREEN_AMPT) without filling in the new model's parameters — engine may reject the partial set | Dialog's model combo writes a *complete* default set on switch (seeded from legacy `DefSubcatch` infiltration block); a single `applySubcatchInfil<Model>` call is the smallest atomic mutation. Per-model parameter cache lives on the dialog so re-selecting a previously-edited model restores its parameters. |
| R-T2 | Outlet picker accepts both node and subcatchment id spaces; collision when a node and a subcatchment share the same id | Picker shows two grouped sections (Nodes / Subcatchments) so collision is visually disambiguated. Setter validates by checking which id space the picked entry came from (carried on the DataObjectRef as a `kindHint` field, similar to `SWMMNodePropertyAdapter::OutfallType`). |
| R-T3 | Land Uses page's percentage column has a "must sum to 100" invariant that legacy SWMM-GUI enforces at OK-click; Apply-as-you-go conflicts with this if a user is mid-typing | Sum-validator runs on every edit and surfaces a non-blocking warning bar at the bottom of the page (not a modal). Engine accepts partial coverages (legacy CN-aware infiltration ignores rows with fraction = 0); commit only blocks if a single row > 100. Same pattern as `NodeCompoundEditDialog`'s DWF base-value validator. |
| R-T4 | The `SubcatchCompoundEditRef` metatype collides with `NodeCompoundEditRef` and `LinkCompoundEditRef`'s registered string converters | Distinct `Q_DECLARE_METATYPE` types; converters keyed by metatype id, not by ref-struct name. New test case in `test_metatype_no_collision.cpp` asserts all three converters live side-by-side. |
| R-T5 | Slice BO replaces §T.TC's page bodies — risk of breaking the metatype contract during the swap | §T.TC's dialog defines a stable widget contract (per §S precedent): page exposes `setRef(SubcatchCompoundEditRef)` / `commit() → bool` / `revert()`. BO's rich page implements the same three methods and slots into the same `QStackedWidget` index. No metatype or model-layer changes; BO is a leaf-widget replacement. |
| R-T6 | Engine gap **BO-SUB-09** (full LID-usage CRUD) is the biggest engine PR in §T.10 and the highest-risk: `Tlid_usage` storage lives in the subcatchment struct as a linked list in the legacy engine | Verify at engine-PR-start: read `solver/swmm_lid.c` to confirm the linked-list shape. Worst-case, add a parallel SoA index alongside the legacy linked list (same approach as `swmm_inflow_*` CRUD pattern). |
| R-T7 | Centroid X/Y read-only display drifts from the polygon when the user drags vertices via `applySubcatchVertices` | The X/Y Q_PROPERTY getters compute the centroid live (no cache); `applySubcatchVertices` emits `attributeChanged(name)` which re-reads the centroid on the next paint. No second source of truth. |
| R-T8 | Six placeholder compound cells visibly under-deliver vs the full legacy `Dsubcatch.pas` UX | §T's manual update calls out the placeholder set explicitly and links each placeholder to the Slice BO / BP phase that deepens it. Cell tooltips name the slice ID so a user inspecting a disabled "Edit…" button knows exactly what unblocks it. |
| R-T9 | The outlet picker has to enumerate `swmm_node_count + swmm_subcatch_count` candidates on every cell open; large models slow open | Use the existing `DataObjectPickerEditor`'s lazy-population pattern (Slice DB.4); enumerate on first open + cache + invalidate on `objectsAddedOrRemoved` signal from the model layer. |

### §T.14 Manual / docs impact

- `docs/manual/27_subcatchment_lid.md` — extend with the new Property Browser parity row inventory + the six compound-cell surface. Defer the rich `SubcatchmentEditor` / `LidUsageEditor` modal walkthrough to Slice BO's manual update.

Awaiting user approval before code work begins.** Open confirmations from §T.1: (Q-T1) two visual groupings in the Property Browser tree (Hydrology subforms / Water-quality subforms) — recommendation: yes; (Q-T2) Subarea Routing direction + percent as two plain rows, not a compound cell — recommendation: yes; (Q-T3) Slice TA (tag-only) ships first as a no-engine-work warm-up — recommendation: yes; (Q-T4) Infiltration model switch writes new-model defaults via `applySubcatchInfil<Model>`, per-model parameter cache lives on the dialog — recommendation: yes; (Q-T5) Groundwater ships as placeholder behind aquifer name picker; full per-subcatch GW params land with BO-SUB-04..-08 — recommendation: yes; (Q-T6) LID Group ships as placeholder until BO-SUB-09's full CRUD lands — recommendation: yes; (Q-T7) Land Uses ships fully wired in §T (engine pair exists) — recommendation: yes; (Q-T8) Initial Buildup ships as placeholder until BO-SUB-10 lands — recommendation: yes; (Q-T9) Snowpack ships as placeholder until BO-SUB-11 lands — recommendation: yes; (Q-T10) Post-run stats (`statPrecip`, `statRunoffVol`, `statMaxRunoff`) ship as read-only Q_PROPERTYs mirroring node `statMax*` block — recommendation: yes. ## §U — Comprehensive QSG (Qt Scene Graph) Migration Strategy (DRAFT 2026-05-25, awaiting approval)

### §U.0 Why this section exists

User direction (2026-05-25): perform a comprehensive review of rendering in the GUI, identify which elements are **not** currently being rendered through Qt Scene Graph (QSG), and capture a migration strategy that closes those gaps to improve rendering performance.

Per CLAUDE.md §5.0 ("follow preconfigured work plans … and not implement whole new strategies that have not been vetted"), this section does **not** invent a new rendering architecture. It is a **coordination layer** that triages every renderable element in the codebase against the QSG seams already established by the four vetted rendering plans:

- [`docs/RENDERING_5M_PLAN.md`](RENDERING_5M_PLAN.md) — Phases A (CPU foundation, ✅ shipped) + B.RHI (Qt Quick Scene Graph pivot — B.RHI.1/.2 shipped, B.RHI.3/.4 outstanding).
- [`docs/QSG_PAN_ZOOM_OPTIMIZATIONS.md`](QSG_PAN_ZOOM_OPTIMIZATIONS.md) — Stages 1–7 on the `SWMMLayerQSGRenderer` (all ✅ shipped).
- [`docs/RENDERING_OUTPUT_SUBLAYERS_PLAN.md`](RENDERING_OUTPUT_SUBLAYERS_PLAN.md) — `ISublayer` / `ISublayerHost` scaffolding (S1–S2.5a shipped; S2.5b/c, S3, S5 paint wiring outstanding).
- [`docs/RENDERING_STATIC_STYLING_PLAN.md`](RENDERING_STATIC_STYLING_PLAN.md) — Static-attribute styling on `SWMMModelLayer` + `GISVectorLayer` (T1–T11 drafted, none shipped). Note: §6 of that plan explicitly defers QSG migration of static sublayers to "a separate workstream under `RENDERING_5M_PLAN.md`" — §U.4 below names which RENDERING_5M_PLAN.md slice covers it.

This section is the missing index that ties those plans together at the **element level**, and surfaces the elements none of them yet cover.
