### §X.5 — What the user sees after this lands

- Right-click any layer in the Layers panel → the **same** menu pops up regardless of layer type, with irrelevant entries greyed out but visible.
- Choose **Properties…** → dialog opens with a tab set adapted to the layer type (no more empty subject tabs).
- The **Symbology** tab is one panel, not a nested forest.  For SWMM layers it's a tree-on-left / editor-on-right pair.  For everything else it's a renderer-class dropdown + the matching renderer panel.
- Renderer-class swap (Single ↔ Graduated ↔ Categorized) happens via the dropdown inside Symbology — no context-menu submenu.
- For basemaps the dialog has just **Information / Source / Rendering / Metadata** — no empty Symbology placeholder.

### §X.6 — Resolved decisions (locked 2026-05-26)

1. **Tab orientation: vertical sidebar.**  `QTabWidget` with `tabPosition = West`, icons + labels per tab.  Matches QGIS / ArcGIS Pro and scales cleanly to the 6-tab set.
2. **Per-kind renderer: independent per kind.**  Tree-on-left + editor-on-right Symbology layout as drafted in §X.3.2.  The codebase already supports this via the 11 kindRenderer slots on SWMMModelLayer / SWMMResultsLayer; the new UI surfaces them.
3. **Labels tab: vector + SWMM model only.**  Result layers don't get a Labels tab — per-feature data is exposed through identify popups + tooltips during animation instead.
4. **Style files: deferred.**  No Save Style / Load Style buttons in this slice.  .oswp project persistence already round-trips every layer's full style.  Cross-project sharing lands in a later follow-up if demand surfaces.
5. **Renderer plugins: add IRendererPanelFactory seam.**  New scaffolding (~80 LOC) parallel to `StyleEditorRegistry` so the Symbology dropdown is extensible.  No additional renderers ship in this slice — the seam is plumbing.

---

**Next**: Slice X.1 begins (drop the bespoke per-subject tab generation, switch to a fixed tab set + vertical sidebar + capability flags).  No further user approval needed unless a slice surfaces a design question the plan didn't cover.


## §Y — Output-Rendering Hot Path: Signal Coalescing + Incremental Scene Updates (PARTIAL LANDED 2026-05-27)

**Status:** Y.1 + Y.2 landed; Y.3 / Y.4 / Y.5 deferred pending Y.2 measurements.

### §Y.1 — Why this plan

Animation playback (and time-slider scrubs) currently rebuild the entire output scene every frame.  An audit of the redraw path turned up three independent multipliers stacked on the hot loop:

1. **Triple signal emission per timestep.**  [`SWMMResultsLayer::setCurrentTimeStep`](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp#L1242-L1257) fires three signals back-to-back — `currentTimeStepChanged`, `currentDateTimeChanged`, `repaintRequested`.  The first two each fan out through `AnimationController::onPrimaryPeriodChanged` / `onPrimaryTimeChanged` and re-emit, doubling the downstream UI paths.  The 2D-fallback fan-out at [`swmmvis.cpp:770-784`](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L770-L784) broadcasts to every `SWMM2DResultsLayer` regardless of visibility.

2. **Full scene teardown + rebuild every frame.**  `OpenSWMMVisLayer::refreshScene` ([`openswmmvislayer.cpp:212-220`](../src/layers/openswmmvislayer.cpp#L212-L220)) is literally `depopulateScene() + populateScene()`.  `SWMMResultsLayer` inherits this default, so [`populateScene`](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp#L1775-L2227) destroys every `QGraphicsEllipseItem` / `QGraphicsPolygonItem` / `QGraphicsLineItem` belonging to the layer and re-allocates them from scratch on every animation tick.  The per-feature `ramp.colorForValue(val)` call ([line 1895](../src/layers/swmmresultslayer.cpp#L1895)) and the per-feature `toScene(mx, my)` coordinate transform run inside that hot loop every frame — for a 1,200-node / 1,300-link network, that's ~2,500 fresh QGraphicsItem allocations per timestep.

3. **Collateral redraws.**  `LegendOverlay::refresh` ([`legendoverlay.cpp:198`](../src/overlays/legendoverlay.cpp#L198)) and the comparison-plot dialog ([five connect sites in `swmmvis.cpp`](../src/swmmvis.cpp#L1613)) are subscribed to `repaintRequested` / `currentTimeChanged` and recompute on every tick even when their ramp range / variable / dialog visibility hasn't changed.

`fetchResultsForStep` already caches per-variable result vectors in `m_nodeResultsByVar` / `m_linkResultsByVar` / `m_subcatchResultsByVar` (Slice U-0 work), so the bottleneck is purely the **rendering** side: signal proliferation × full-scene rebuild × collateral consumer fanout.  Slice OUT.4 from the §X / batch-2 backlog ("sanity-check animation perf with output overrides") is the placeholder this section now fulfils.

### §Y.2 — Architectural decisions

1. **Dirty taxonomy in `SWMMResultsLayer`.**  Two scene-dirty flavours:
   - **`StructuralDirty`** — feature added / removed, geometry edited, sublayer added / toggled / styled, attribute changed, archetype changed.  Requires `depopulateScene()` + `populateScene()`.
   - **`ValuesDirty`** — only the current timestep, per-feature override caches, or color-ramp range changed.  Existing items can stay; only their `setBrush()` / `setPen()` need updating.

   `refreshScene` branches on the flag and dispatches to either the legacy rebuild or a new `restyleScene()` path.

2. **Per-feature item cache.**  `populateScene` records each item it allocates into a parallel `QHash<int, QGraphicsItem *> m_itemByFeature[catIdx]` (one hash per Category × archetype).  `restyleScene` walks the cache and recolors in place — no `new`, no `addItem`, no coordinate transforms.  `depopulateScene` clears the hash alongside removing items.

3. **Signal coalescing in `setCurrentTimeStep`.**  Emit `currentTimeStepChanged` only; derive `currentDateTime()` inside `AnimationController::onPrimaryPeriodChanged` and emit `currentTimeChanged` from there.  Disconnect the `currentDateTimeChanged → onPrimaryTimeChanged` wire; the `currentDateTimeChanged` signal itself stays on the layer for direct UI consumers (slider widgets) but no longer drives the animation cascade.

4. **2D fallback fan-out gated by visibility.**  The `swmmvis.cpp:770-784` broadcast loop early-outs when no `SWMM2DResultsLayer` is visible.

5. **Out of scope for §Y.**  Color-LUT quantisation, custom batch-paint `QGraphicsItem` for dense point sets, basemap raster recaching, and any change to the QSG render path.  These belong to a follow-up (§Y.3 / §Y.4 below) iff post-§Y.2 profiling still shows a bottleneck.

Guarded the 2D-fallback fan-out in `swmmvis.cpp` so `setCurrentSimTime` only fires on visible `SWMM2DResultsLayer` instances. | **LANDED** | ~25 |

Known v1 trade-off: rows whose value transitions NaN → finite mid-animation stay invisible until the next structural rebuild; documented inline. | **LANDED** | ~410 |
| **Y.3** | **Collateral-consumer gating.**  `LegendOverlay::refresh` short-circuits when ramp range / variable hasn't changed.  Comparison-plot dialog connections check `isVisible()` before recomputing.  Deferred until §Y.2 measurements confirm the win is worth it. | DEFERRED | ~40 |
| **Y.4** | **Hot-path micro-optimisations.**  Color-LUT quantisation in `RasterColorRamp::colorForValue` (256-bin precomputed table indexed by normalised value).  Batch-paint custom `QGraphicsItem` for dense point sets to avoid `ItemIgnoresTransformations` per-item transform inversion.  Deferred — only land if §Y.2 + §Y.3 leave a measurable gap. | DEFERRED | ~180 |
| **Y.5** | **Verification.**  Add a `[redraw:perf]` debug channel that counts `populateScene` / `restyleScene` / `repaintRequested` calls per second.  Target: during steady-state animation, zero `populateScene` calls, one `restyleScene` per timestep. | DRAFT | ~30 |

### §Y.4 — Implementation notes (Y.1 + Y.2)

**Y.1 — signal coalescing.**  The wires to drop are at [`animationcontroller.cpp:75-76`](../src/animation/animationcontroller.cpp#L75-L76) and [`:86-87`](../src/animation/animationcontroller.cpp#L86-L87).  `onPrimaryTimeChanged` becomes unused and can stay declared (back-compat) or be removed entirely — we'll remove it since it's `private` and `Q_OBJECT`-internal.  `onPrimaryPeriodChanged` gets a `const QDateTime now = m_primaryLayer->currentDateTime();` + `emit currentTimeChanged(now);` after its existing `dispatchAnimationTick(step)`.  Net effect: one animation tick → one `currentPeriodChanged` + one `currentTimeChanged` (instead of two cascades).

**Y.2 — item cache + restyle.**  The cache type:

```cpp
// SWMMResultsLayer (private)
enum SceneDirtyKind { Clean, ValuesDirty, StructuralDirty };
SceneDirtyKind m_sceneDirty { StructuralDirty };

// Per-Category, populated during populateScene, cleared in depopulateScene.
// Index = feature row; value = item handle (null for rows the paint helper
// skipped because of missing coords / NaN values / invalid attributes).
std::array<QVector<QGraphicsItem *>, SWMMModelLayer::NumCategories> m_itemByFeature;
```

`paintPoint` / `paintLine` / `paintPolygon` each record the item handle into `m_itemByFeature[catIdx][row]` after `scene->addItem(item)`.  A new `restyleScene()` walks each Category, fetches the current results vector + override caches + ramp the same way `paintPoint` / `paintLine` / `paintPolygon` do, then re-applies brush / pen on the cached item.  The recoloring inner loop is identical to the lookup logic in the existing paint helpers, factored into a small private `recolorPoint(item, row, ...)` / `recolorLine(item, row, ...)` / `recolorPolygon(item, row, ...)` to keep the rebuild and restyle paths in lockstep.

`refreshScene` override:

```cpp
void SWMMResultsLayer::refreshScene(QGraphicsScene *scene,
                                    const MapExtent &extent,
                                    const SpatialReferenceSystem *srs)
{
    switch (m_sceneDirty) {
        case Clean:
            return;
        case ValuesDirty:
            restyleScene(scene);
            m_sceneDirty = Clean;
            return;
        case StructuralDirty:
        default:
            OpenSWMMVisLayer::refreshScene(scene, extent, srs); // depopulate + populate
            m_sceneDirty = Clean;
            return;
    }
}
```

Dirty-flag wiring:
- `setCurrentTimeStep` → `m_sceneDirty = std::max(m_sceneDirty, ValuesDirty);` (don't downgrade a pending structural)
- `setVariable`, `setColorRamp`, `setKindRenderer` (Slice OUT.1), per-feature override edits (Slice OUT.2), sublayer add/remove/toggle/style → `m_sceneDirty = StructuralDirty;`
- Model-layer geometry edits → already flow through `refreshSceneCoordsForNode` etc. on `SWMMModelLayer`; for the results layer we mark `StructuralDirty` on the matching topology-changed signal.

### §Y.5 — Verification strategy

1. Enable `OPENSWMM_REDRAW_LOG=1` (existing channel at [`mapcanvas.cpp:1052-1054`](../src/map/mapcanvas.cpp#L1052-L1054)) and add a parallel `[restyle:fire]` log line in `restyleScene()`.
2. Open a representative model (Virginia BC project: 1,205 nodes / 1,285 links / 198 subcatchments) with results, hit Play.
3. Pre-§Y baseline: count `[redraw:fire] Scene` events per second during a 60s playback.
4. Post-§Y.1: same metric — expect ~½ the scene fires (signal cascade halved).
5. Post-§Y.2: same metric + `[restyle:fire]` count.  Expect zero `[redraw:fire] Scene` events tied to time-step advance during steady-state playback, one `[restyle:fire]` per timestep.
6. Manual smoke: time-slider scrub (10 quick drags), variable switch (NodeDepth → LinkFlow → SubcatchRunoff), kind sublayer toggle, model-layer node move — all four should still produce correct visuals.

### §Y.6 — What §Y does NOT change

- The QSG render path, the raster channel, basemap caching — untouched.
- `RasterColorRamp` math — call site count drops dramatically (only ramp-range / variable change triggers a rebuild) but the function body is unchanged.
- 2D-result-layer rendering (`SWMM2DResultsLayer` / `SWMM2DMeshLayer`) — `dispatchAnimationTick` already gives those layers a hook to invalidate selectively; if they hit the same bottleneck a parallel §Y' lands later.
- Identify-by-click, attribute table, comparison-plot data extraction — those read `m_nodeResultsByVar` etc. directly, which is unchanged.

---

**Next:** §Y.1 implementation begins immediately (signal coalescing — small, isolated, low-risk).  §Y.2 follows in the same session once §Y.1 builds clean.

### §Y.7 — Retro notes (2026-05-27)

- **Y.1 (~25 LOC)** landed exactly as scoped.  No surprises.  `currentDateTimeChanged` is still emitted by the layer because `Q_PROPERTY(currentDateTime READ … NOTIFY currentDateTimeChanged)` (header line 110) requires it; the animation cascade no longer subscribes.
- **Y.2 (~410 LOC)** also landed as scoped, with one design refinement during implementation:
  - **Arrows force structural.**  Line sublayers with `showFlowArrows` on create a primary item + an arrow item per row; arrow geometry (length + rotation) is value-dependent.  Restyle can't update arrow geometry without re-running the polyline-midpoint math.  Rather than caching arrow handles separately and partial-rebuilding them, the v1 implementation gates the entire layer's restyle on `requiresStructuralRebuildForRestyle()` — if any visible line sublayer has arrows on, the refresh falls through to structural.  Users who care about animation perf and aren't using arrows pay nothing; users with arrows on get current behaviour.  Honest trade-off, documented at the function header.
  - **NaN → finite mid-animation.**  The cache stores `nullptr` for rows the structural rebuild skipped (NaN result, missing geometry, missing output index).  A subsequent restyle visiting that row sees a null handle and skips it.  If the row's value transitions back to finite in a later timestep, restyle has no item to mutate — the feature stays invisible until the next structural refresh.  Acceptable trade-off for v1: typical SWMM result variables (depth, flow, runoff) are continuously finite across a run; NaN holes are rare.  A future slice could always-allocate + toggle visibility to fix it; not load-bearing today.
  - **Header forward declaration.**  `m_itemByFeature` uses `QGraphicsItem *` inside a `QVector`, which requires a complete-or-forward-declared `QGraphicsItem`.  The transitive include from `openswmmvislayer.h` covers `QGraphicsScene` but not `QGraphicsItem`.  Added a `class QGraphicsItem;` forward decl near the existing `class SpatialReferenceSystem;` line.
- **Build status:** `SWMMVis` target builds clean.  `test_rules_editor_dialog.cpp` has a pre-existing incomplete-type error on `RuleListModel` that reproduces against `HEAD` without §Y changes — orthogonal, not §Y-induced.
- **Outstanding before declaring §Y "complete":**
  1. **Y.5 verification.**  Add a `[restyle:fire]` parallel to `[redraw:fire] Scene` and measure pre/post fps on the Virginia BC project during a 60s playback.  Until this is in hand we have a theoretical win, not a measured one.
  2. **Time-slider scrub manual smoke.**  Drag the slider rapidly across a long run; confirm scene stays current and no items are orphaned.
  3. **Variable switch round-trip.**  NodeDepth → LinkFlow → SubcatchRunoff; structural-dirty on every switch should rebuild correctly.
  4. **Kind-sublayer toggle.**  Hide / show Junctions while animation runs; the invalidated signal should escalate to Structural and rebuild the affected layer.


## §Z — Layer Rule Model (DRAFT 2026-05-27, sibling file)

> **Status (2026-05-27 update):** 🟢 actively shipping. The architecture is approved, Phases A (data) and B (layer adoption) are complete, all five new tabs (Temporal / Mask / Auxiliary Storage / Joins / Diagrams) ship with spec + persistence + UI, the Style Manager dialog and Layer Styling dock are live, and three paint integrations have landed (Z.6a mesh-spec-driven paint, Z.13-controller animation, Z.14-paint mask clip, Z.5b-paint line offset). Remaining work is paint integrations + backend engines for the five new tabs and the four aggregate renderers; see [`RENDERING_RULE_MODEL_PLAN.md`](RENDERING_RULE_MODEL_PLAN.md) §20 for the authoritative progress snapshot intended for agent handoff.

§Z is split out into a dedicated sibling file so this plan stays navigable:

**[`RENDERING_RULE_MODEL_PLAN.md`](RENDERING_RULE_MODEL_PLAN.md)**

### §Z.0 What §Z covers (at a glance)

- **Vocabulary aligned with QGIS / ArcGIS Pro** — `Rule` (the styling unit, extending QGIS's Rule-based-renderer rule to layer scope), `Rule List` (the stackable ordered list on every layer), `Symbol Layer` (QGIS-native compositional model inside a Symbol), `Symbol Levels` (cross-feature paint order), `Data-defined override` (per-property attribute expression binding).
- **Single dialog surface**: the §X Symbology tab gains an **Active Rule combo + Rule List** at the top; the SWMM multi-kind tree-on-left collapses into Rule rows. The combo + list apply uniformly to every layer kind (vector / raster / SWMM model / SWMM 1D results / SWMM 2D results / TIN).
- **Marker Symbol Layer** with 13 shapes, QPen outline, attribute-driven size.
- **Line Symbol Layer** with `Qt::PenStyle` / `PenCapStyle` / `PenJoinStyle`, custom dash, directional arrows (5 placement modes, color/length/spacing).
- **Raster + TIN Symbol Layers** — color ramp / hillshade / contour lines / filled isobands / mesh edges / mesh nodes; each a stackable Rule decoration. §N.5–§N.9 rendering code paths consumed unchanged.
- **Animation semantics (Q4 lock)**: fixed bins, sampled at Rule creation, with optional opt-in per-frame rebinning.
- **GIS-gap fills**: Heatmap / Point Cluster / Point Displacement / Inverted Polygon / Unclassed renderers (§Z.9); Symbol Levels (§Z.11); Diagrams / Temporal / Mask / Auxiliary Storage / Joins tabs (§Z.12–§Z.16); Style I/O `.qml` + `.swmm-rule.json` + Style Manager dialog (§Z.17); non-modal Layer Styling dock (§Z.18).
- **Migration**: legacy `.oswp` sublayer keys auto-convert to Rules on load; rendering primitives (`FeatureSublayer`, `MeshNodeSublayer`, etc.) stay in C++ as paint primitives delegated to by a Rule's Symbol — they're not user-facing.
